articles.title: Escape from flatland: Strained-ring linchpins for 3D heterocyclic scaffolds in drug discovery
articles.abstract: Strained rings offer an escape from flat chemical space, enabling access to three-dimensional bridged heterocycles. This perspective examines two complementary strategies—introducing heteroatoms through reaction partners or embedding them within strained precursors—and links precursor design and activation mode to topology, stereochemistry, and substituent orientation. It highlights how heteroatom identity and placement tune molecular properties and outlines advances in stereocontrol, precursor accessibility, and medicinal-chemistry validation needed to make strain-release synthesis a practical tool for drug discovery.

articles.title: Photoinduced Charge Separation via Symmetry-Breaking
articles.abstract: Photoinduced symmetry-breaking charge separation (SB-CS) is a fundamental process in molecular photophysics that underpins energy and charge transport in reaction centers and organic, supramolecular, and hybrid materials. Despite extensive investigations across diverse systems, SB-CS is often described in system-specific terms, obscuring the underlying unifying principles. In this Review, we establish a coherent framework demonstrating that SB-CS can be understood within a multidimensional parameter space defined by electronic coupling, energetic driving force, and nuclear reorganization. We critically analyze how the interplay between locally excited and charge-transfer states governs charge separation and recombination dynamics, highlighting the existence of an optimal intermediate coupling regime that enables efficient symmetry-breaking while suppressing nonproductive decay pathways. By integrating insights from solution, solid-state, and single-molecule measurements, we show that environmental fluctuations and structural heterogeneity play a central role in driving charge localization rather than merely acting as spectators or perturbations. Importantly, we distinguish universal physical principles from system-specific manifestations, allowing the formulation of transferable design rules for achieving efficient and long-lived charge-separated states. Finally, we outline emerging directions toward predictive, data-driven models that link molecular structure to SB-CS dynamics, providing a foundation for the rational design of next-generation optoelectronic and energy-conversion materials.

articles.title: Ultrafast Nonlinear Vibrational Spectroscopy of Aqueous Solutions at Surfaces and in Heterogeneous Environments
articles.abstract: Water and aqueous electrolytes at surfaces, interfaces, and in confinement behave differently from the bulk, yet linear spectroscopy rarely combines the chemical specificity, surface selectivity, and temporal resolution needed to resolve electric double-layer formation, specific-ion adsorption, and hydration at interfaces and under nanoconfinement. This review assesses how ultrafast nonlinear vibrational spectroscopy, comprising two-dimensional infrared spectroscopy, vibrational sum-frequency generation (SFG), and time-resolved SFG, probes the hydrogen-bond network and the dynamics of interfacial water and electrolytes on femtosecond-to-picosecond timescales. We first establish vibrational benchmarks for bulk water and simple electrolytes, then treat soft aqueous boundaries, including air–water, hydrophobic and hydrophilic, lipid, surfactant, and nucleic acid interfaces. We next examine solid–liquid and electrochemical systems, spanning metal oxides, minerals, and field-induced effects, before turning to water and proton dynamics in nanoconfined geometries and complex architectures. Throughout, experimental results are set against theoretical and computational frameworks, from polarizable force fields to machine-learning potentials. Our aim is to identify which molecular-level features of interfacial water are now firmly established, where the prevailing mean-field description of the electric double layer breaks down, and which experiments would resolve the outstanding discrepancies.

articles.title: Bifunctional Electrocatalysts
Cation Radius Engineering of d10 Metal Hybrid Halides toward Coordination Modulation for Giant Optical Anisotropy
articles.abstract: Birefringent crystals are core materials for polarization modulation in optical devices, yet commercial crystals generally suffer from low birefringence values. In this work, three hybrid halide crystals, (C5H5NS)2ZnCl2, (C5H5NS)2CdCl2, and (C5H5NS)HgCl2, were successfully prepared by combining 4-mercaptopyridine unit with d10 metal chlorides to further modulate the metal coordination environments. For (C5H5NS)2ZnCl2 and (C5H5NS)2CdCl2, two π-conjugated units directly coordinate to one metal-centered tetrahedron, which further assembles into a one-dimensional structure via hydrogen-bond interactions. For (C5H5NS)HgCl2, two π-conjugated units coordinate to two metal-centered tetrahedra, forming the isolated (C5H5NS)2Hg2Cl4 dimer, and the complete crystal framework is stacked by intermolecular forces. The birefringence of the three compounds exhibits diversity with the variation of d10 metal ions. Notably, (C5H5NS)2CdCl2 sets records among cadmium-based hybrid halides with metal−halogen−organic functional groups. Structural analyses and theoretical calculations demonstrate that the birefringence of the three crystals is jointly contributed by the organic part and inorganic composition. This study verifies that modifying the coordination environment by tuning the ionic radii of metal center ions is an effective strategy for birefringence modulation and advances the research on hybrid halides for birefringent crystal applications.

articles.title: Dynamic Poly(disulfide) Interphase Enhances Ductility and Toughness of Covalent Adaptable Network Composite without Loss of Stiffness
articles.abstract: Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) offer recyclability and reprocessability, yet bond-exchange dynamics can reduce mechanical strength and toughness. Although the composite formation of CAN provides benefits in both aspectsstrengthening the CAN and adding recyclability to the compositeit still faces a stiffness−ductility trade-off that limits material usefulness. Here, we demonstrate a CAN composite design in which silica nanoparticle incorporation, combined with interfacial chemical structure, enhances ductility and toughness in a highly crosslinked matrix without compromising the high elastic modulus. Introducing poly(disulfide) dynamic covalent bonding chains into the network and at the filler interface significantly increases ductility, toughness, and stress at break. Together with a comparison to composites with permanent interfacial bonding, these results underscore the important role of interfacial chemistry. Based on these comparative experiments, the observed toughness enhancement is proposed to arise from energy dissipation via reorganization at the interphase through stress-activated disulfide exchange and network topological rearrangement. The resulting stress-responsive viscoelasticity enables stable deformation and allows CAN-based composites to overcome the stiffness−ductility trade-off.

articles.title: Heteroanionic Tuning of Cooperative Ta Off-Centering in Quasi-One-Dimensional CsTaS3− x Cl x Semiconductors
articles.abstract: The structural behavior of CsTaS3 was investigated alongside that of the new heteroanionic compound CsTaS2.16Cl0.84, synthesized via the reaction of Ta and S in a CsCl flux. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that both compounds are isostructural, crystallizing in the centrosymmetric hexagonal space group P63/mmc with split Ta positions along the face-sharing octahedral chain direction. Pair distribution function analysis of both compounds, supported by STEM imaging of CsTaS3, identifies the local intrachain displacement motif as cooperative Ta sliding rather than alternating Ta−Ta dimerization. While X-ray absorption near-edge spectroscopy (XANES) confirms the decrease of the average oxidation state in CsTaS2.16Cl0.84, the same structural distortion persists, albeit now with a reduced magnitude. Both materials are semiconducting, and Cl incorporation increases the band gap from ∼1.00 eV in CsTaS3 to ∼1.12 eV in the heteroanionic phase. Single-crystal detectors fabricated from CsTaS2.16Cl0.84 exhibit high resistivity, which effectively suppresses dark current and enhances signal-to-noise performance. These devices deliver an X-ray sensitivity of 7470 μC Gyair−1 cm−2, demonstrating efficient charge generation and collection under irradiation.

articles.title: Interplay of Synthesis, Structure and Thermoelectric Properties in Two Families of Silicide Zintl Phases Grown in Magnesium-Rich Flux
articles.abstract: Large crystals of metal silicide Zintl phases with general formula (Ca/Eu/Mg)2Si were grown from reactions of silicon with varying amounts of europium and calcium in magnesium/zinc flux. The Eu/Ca reactant ratio determined the structure type of the products. Calcium-rich reactions yielded Ca1−xEuxMgSi (0 < x < 0.7) compounds adopting the orthorhombic TiNiSi structure type in space group Pnma. Increasing europium content led to the prevalence of Eu8−yCayMg16Si12 (0 < y < 3.4) products with the hexagonal Ho5Ni19P12 structure type in space group P6̅2m. Single crystal X-ray diffraction studies indicate mixing of Zn on one Mg site in the hexagonal structures; thus, the formula can be expressed as Eu8−yCayMg16−αZnαSi12. Magnetic susceptibility data indicate europium is divalent in all of the compounds, with low-temperature magnetic ordering transitions. Density of states calculations show a pseudogap at the Fermi level for both structures, indicating semimetallic character; transport measurements indicate p-type behavior. Ca/Eu mixing and higher ratios of Eu2+ suppress lattice thermal conductivity in both structure types. In Ca1−xEuxMgSi, Eu-substitution lowers resistivity but yields minimal Seebeck enhancement; in Eu8−yCayMg16Si12 (Eu8−yCayMg16−αZnαSi12), Ca-substitution increases resistivity and markedly improves the Seebeck coefficient, with Eu7.59Ca0.41Mg15.62Zn0.36Si12 reaching S ≈ 150 μV K−1 at 300 K.

articles.title: Nonclassical Dihydrogen Bond-Directed Assembly of o -Carborane-Based Molecules into Macroscopic Architectures with Circularly Polarized Luminescence
articles.abstract: Hierarchical architectures are ubiquitous in nature; however, the bottom-up construction of multilevel chiral macroscopic assemblies from small organic molecules remains highly challenging. Herein, we report an unprecedented assembly strategy for constructing hierarchically organized particles (HOPs) through the co-assembly of achiral o-carborane-based molecules (C-1 and C-2) with chiral (R/S)-limonene. Intriguingly, C-1-(S)-limonene forms microscale cocoon-like superstructures, whereas C-1-(R)-limonene undergoes self-assembly into fibrous architectures that ultimately evolve into random aggregates at the micrometer scale. In contrast, C-2-(R/S)-limonene assembles into bowtie-shaped microarchitectures. Graph Theory (GT) analysis reveals structural complexity indices (CIs) of 5.5 and 54 for the C-1-(S)-limonene- and C-2-(S)-limonene-based HOPs, respectively, indicating significantly higher architectural complexity for the latter. These assemblies exhibit distinct circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) properties: C-1-(S)-limonene displays intense CPL emission at 504 nm with a high luminescence dissymmetry factor (glum) of +0.006, whereas C-2-(S)-limonene exhibits CPL emission at 560 nm with a glum value of +0.002. These results demonstrate that chirality signals are transferred across multiple length scales from the molecular level to macroscopic architectures. The observed structural divergence originates from the synergistic effects of nonclassical dihydrogen bonding (Bδ+−Hδ−···Hδ+−Cδ−) between achiral o-carborane derivatives and chiral limonene, together with molecular polarity and elasticity effects. This study establishes a paradigm for fabricating chiral o-carborane-based hierarchical aggregates with programmable architectures and tailored chiroptical properties.

articles.title: Progressive Fluorination-Controlled Steric Effects in Low-Dimensional Bismuth Bromides
articles.abstract: Although fluorination introduces tunable lattice rigidity and steric matching that influence molecular dynamics, the use of progressive fluorination as an effective method for structure−property tuning remains limited. Here, we report structural, thermal, dielectric, vibrational, and optical investigations of two members of zero-dimensional (0D) hybrid bismuth bromides with the general formula A3BiBr6, where A denotes 2,2-difluoroethylammonium and 2,2,2-trifluoroethylammonium cations. Differential scanning calorimetry reveals that the difluorinated compound undergoes a first-order phase transition at 184.3/177.5 K (heating/cooling), similar to the monofluorinated analogue, whereas its trifluorinated counterpart exhibits no structural phase transitions within the studied temperature range. A single-crystal X-ray diffraction study shows that the trifluorinated compound adopts trigonal symmetry (space group P3̅). In contrast, the difluorinated analogue crystallizes in the orthorhombic space group Pnnm at room temperature and transforms upon cooling into a monoclinic phase described by the P21/n space group. Temperature-dependent infrared and Raman spectroscopies indicate that the phase transition mechanism is governed by order−disorder processes. The noncovalent interaction calculations support that the F···F intermolecular interactions originate from sterically constrained packing rather than attractive interactions, contributing to dense crystal arrangement. Optical studies reveal that band gap energies correlate with octahedral deformation and level of fluorination. The difluorinated compound exhibits orange luminescence of excitonic origin, which is still observable at room temperature. The presented data demonstrate that degree of fluorination is a versatile design strategy for tuning dipolar degrees of freedom, intermolecular interactions, the strength of organic−inorganic coupling, and optical properties in hybrid halides.

articles.title: Reductive Electrodeposition of Cationic Polymer Networks for Conformal Permselective Interphases
articles.abstract: The integration of ultrathin and conformal interphases onto electrodes can lead to advanced electrochemical systems with control over the near-surface nanoenvironment impacting the double layer, electrode stability, reagent access, and solvation. However, the precise fabrication of nanometric interphases with tailored thickness and composition without blocking active surface sites is challenging, especially on porous application-relevant electrodes. Here, we report the reductive and self-limiting electrodeposition of polymer networks (EPoN) as a versatile and tunable method to uniformly coat non-planar and porous electrodes with physically adhered ultrathin functional polymer networks. The deposition chemistry is based on cathodically mediated methylpyridinium crosslinking and achieves the fabrication of polymer thin films on oxidation-sensitive catalytic metals. Our reductive EPoN process follows a self-limiting growth mechanism, yielding uniform and defect-correcting coatings with tunable nanometric thickness and charge density. The polymer network interphase is permselective, retaining molecular access to the functional surface, but modulates its permeation and activity based on charge and size, as demonstrated with a positively charged nanometric interphase as a functional barrier for regulating the hydrogen evolution reaction on copper. Our reductive EPoN strategy establishes a robust platform to tailor catalytic interphases for precise control over the electrochemical nanoenvironment.

articles.title: Structure-Directing Agents of Chaordic Materials Using High-Entropy Alloying
articles.abstract: For nearly a century, alloy design has been guided by the Hume-Rothery rules, which describe the conditions required for solid solution formation and have traditionally constrained the compositional space available to materials scientists. The emergence of high-entropy alloys fundamentally altered this paradigm by demonstrating that configurational entropy can stabilize compositions that would otherwise be thermodynamically unfavorable. Since their discovery, high-entropy concepts have expanded beyond metallic systems into ceramics, including oxides, carbides, silicides, nitrides, and borides, creating new opportunities to access unconventional chemistries and local atomic environments. This review examines how high-entropy alloying can be used to transcend classical alloying limitations and stabilize elements in coordination environments that are inaccessible in conventional materials. Particular emphasis is placed on high-entropy borides, where ordered boron frameworks provide a structural scaffold that accommodates chemically disparate elements while preserving phase stability. Recent examples, including Pt- and Si-containing high-entropy diborides, demonstrate how entropy stabilization enables the incorporation of elements that do not form stable binary diborides (MB2), resulting in unique electronic structures, bonding environments, and functional properties. More broadly, these systems illustrate how the interplay between disorder and local order can be leveraged to design next-generation materials beyond the boundaries imposed by traditional alloying rules.

articles.title: Symmetry-Broken Co3O4 via Site-Selective Pd Substitution for Bifunctional Water Electrolysis
articles.abstract: Spinel oxides generally show subpar activity for electrochemical water splitting because of low electronic conductivity, suboptimal adsorption energies, and poor operational stability. To overcome these limitations, Pd2+ is introduced to induce lattice strain in a metastable Co3O4 phase featuring off-centered cobalt and oxygen atoms. While pristine Co3O4 typically crystallizes in the centrosymmetric Fd3̅m space group, 1.2 at % Pd transforms it to the dominant non-centrosymmetric F4̅3m space group. This unconventional lattice contains two non-equivalent tetrahedral sites and one octahedral site. Pd2+ preferentially substitutes the Co1 atom at the (0, 0, 0) 4a tetrahedral position, with a relative stabilization of −1.02 eV. Pd2+-induced enhancement of the density of states near the Fermi level tunes the d-band center, while Co-to-Pd charge redistribution activates the otherwise less active tetrahedral site alongside the intrinsically active octahedral site, thereby enhancing alkaline water electrolysis. For oxygen and hydrogen evolution, this bifunctional catalyst delivers mass activities of 60.6 and 31.0 A/g and turnover frequencies of 0.32 and 0.28 H2 s−1 at 300 and 250 mV overpotentials, respectively. In a two-electrode configuration, it reaches 50 mA/cm2 at an iR-uncorrected cell voltage of 1.85 V, while at 200 mA/cm2, it produces 25.4 mL/h H2 at a cell voltage of 2.31 V.

articles.title: The AtomicLimits Database: Towards Artificial Intelligence as a Research Assistant for Atomic Layer Deposition and Etching
articles.abstract: The AtomicLimits ALD/ALE database is a community resource that catalogues atomic layer deposition (ALD) and atomic layer etching (ALE) processes reported in the literature. While widely used, it currently captures only a small fraction of the available information, with limited process information per entry, and relies on manual curation. As ALD/ALE process development grows in demand and complexity, with many interdependent parameters and increasingly sophisticated chemistries such as for multicomponent films, decades of experimental and simulation knowledge remain locked across publications, supplementary files, and lab notebooks. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML) and large language models (LLMs), offer a path to unlock this knowledge for data-driven analysis and process design, but realizing this potential depends on structured, machine-readable data. In this perspective, we propose a framework to evolve AtomicLimits into an AI-ready knowledge infrastructure that integrates literature-extracted, experimental, and simulation data through a community-defined schema, a structured template that specifies which data fields to capture and how to organize them. We outline the AI capabilities this enables, from structured querying to autonomous experimentation, and discuss the coordinated community effort required to realize this vision for the atomic-scale processing field.

articles.title: Unraveling the Correlation between Crystallite Orientation in Conjugated Polymer Thin Film and Charge Transport Properties
articles.abstract: Despite great progress in tailoring the molecular structures of donor−acceptor (D−A) copolymers, the ability to precisely tailor their solid-state chain packing and establish a comprehensive structure−property relationship remains a grand challenge. Here, three diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP)-based copolymers adjusting alkyl side chains with various lengths are developed to control their aggregation behavior in different solvents and the corresponding crystallite orientation in thin films, establishing the structure−charge -transport −property relationship and elucidating the underlying mechanism. Specifically, DPPs with longer side chains exhibit weaker solution aggregation, favoring the formation of a face-on orientation in as-cast films, where the face-on to edge-on orientation can be further achieved by strengthening their solution aggregation via changing the solvent from chloroform to chlorobenzene and xylene. Remarkably, by using a floating-film transfer method, the initially face-on crystallites in as-cast DPP films can be transformed into narrower distributed edge-on crystallites, resulting in the charge mobility being nearly tenfold higher than that of the corresponding as-cast sample. This study highlights how molecular engineering and processing strategies collaboratively guide the aggregation and packing of DPPs in the solution and solid state, offering key insights into the structure−processing−property relationship of D−A copolymers for high-performance optoelectronic devices.

articles.title: Unravelling the Role of Stacking Disorder on the Optoelectronic Properties of Zn3P2
articles.abstract: Zinc phosphide (Zn3P2) is a promising photovoltaic absorber for thin-film and flexible solar cells due to its earth-abundant composition and favourable optoelectronic properties. Recent advances in epitaxy have enabled the growth of high-quality Zn3P2 thin films despite the challenges posed by its incompatible lattice parameter and thermal expansion coefficient. However, Zn3P2 remains prone to intrinsic extended defects, such as rotated domains, that can limit device performance. Here, using (scanning) transmission electron microscopy, we identify a class of extended defects that appear as planar faults described by displacement vectors lying in the (001) plane. Within a pseudo-cubic description of Zn3P2, we establish a direct correspondence between planar faults and rotated domains, showing that both arise from the flexible ordering of vacant sites in the Zn sublattice. First-principles calculations reveal an extremely low planar-defect formation energy of 2.5 mJ m−2, demonstrating that these defects form at essentially negligible energetic cost, in excellent agreement with their high experimentally observed occurrence. Additional density functional theory calculations show that the studied intrinsic planar defects neither introduce mid-gap electronic states nor significantly perturb the local electrostatic potential, indicating that they are electronically benign. Our results suggest that any connection between the observed planar defects and a reduction in device performance must therefore involve indirect mechanisms, such as strain effects or interactions with other defects.

Medicinal plants in a changing climate: evolutionary genomics for resilience and conservation
articles.abstract: Medicinal plants face growing threats from climate change, habitat fragmentation, selective harvesting, and other human-induced pressures that may diminish genetic diversity and weaken evolutionary resilience. Recent studies in population genomics and landscape genomics indicate that resilience is influenced not just by diversity across a species, but also by how adaptive variation is distributed among populations and its connection to environmental gradients. In medicinal plants, factors such as geographic isolation, precipitation, temperature, salinity, and demographic history have been linked to population differentiation and potential adaptive loci. Genomic methods can thus shift conservation from outlining neutral diversity to pinpointing populations and alleles that may be significant for upcoming climates. Simultaneously, transcriptomic, metabolomic, and epigenetic research shows that genetic adaptation is enhanced by phenotypic plasticity and environmental modulation of stress and specialized metabolism pathways. Nevertheless, direct evidence linking adaptive genomic variation to fitness in wild medicinal plant populations is still scarce, and numerous at-risk taxa are deficient in genomic resources. In this study, we integrate recent findings that connect genetic variability, regional adaptation, molecular stress responses, and conservation strategies for medicinal plants. We emphasize landscape genomics and genomic vulnerability as tangible connections between evolutionary ecology and conservation, stressing the importance of incorporating adaptive variation, epigenetic plasticity, demographic history, ecological interactions, and habitat preservation. Future research should emphasize non-model medicinal species, wider geographic sampling, temporal genomic tracking, and field validation of potential adaptive loci.

articles.title: AI-Powered Clinical Decision Support Tools
articles.abstract: To the Editor The Viewpoint article by Drs Singh and Mello provides a balanced discussion of advertising in artificial intelligence (AI)–powered clinical decision support (CDS). It is worth highlighting that the authors state that AI-powered CDS often is free. Did we not say the same about drug company–sponsored lunches and so-called “free” pens and other giveaways in the 1990s? Some will recall when drug companies sponsored lunches for faculty and trainees, gave away pens and other branded items, and sometimes accompanied physicians on rounds. For those who trained more recently, please know that this practice was widely accepted; however, we eventually learned that there is, in fact, no free lunch. Now, we must learn there is no free CDS. Singh and Mello note that while “some products operate on a subscription model, others such as OpenEvidence use advertising revenue to offer access without charge.” It is surprising and disappointing that clinicians may think they are receiving CDS for free. Perhaps they have forgotten—or may have never learned—that drug company advertisements influence prescribing behavior when they appear alongside information intended to educate physicians and support clinical practice. Clearly the drug companies themselves have not forgotten. Twenty years ago, the International Federation of Pharmaceutical Manufacturers and Associations revised its code of ethics and barred gifts or money that could influence prescribing behavior. CDS companies that embed pharmaceutical advertisements in their products should end this practice and, if they do not, the pharmaceutical industry should do so. Better yet, clinicians should recognize they have other options without industry advertisements and should choose such CDS tools.

articles.title: AI-Powered Clinical Decision Support Tools—Reply
articles.abstract: In Reply We appreciate the thoughtful letters in response to our Viewpoint. We agree with Dr Ziegelstein that the simplest solution to the ethical quandaries of advertising in AI-powered CDS tools would be for the AI-powered CDS companies that use advertisements and/or the pharmaceutical companies that partner with them to end this practice altogether. However, this is unlikely to happen, given that advertising is a potentially more lucrative revenue source than other options such as subscriptions. Ziegelstein’s suggestion that clinicians recognize they have other options and choose CDS tools that do not embed advertisements seems more realistic, particularly if their organizational employers nudge them in this direction. Historically, once Epocrates (a free drug information app) began supporting ads at the point of care, its credibility with its physician users eroded and other services such as UpToDate ultimately won out.

articles.title: Asymptomatic Carotid Revascularization May Be Justified, but Not to Improve Cognition
articles.abstract: Stroke is a feared complication of atherosclerotic carotid artery stenosis. After years of debate regarding the value of revascularizing asymptomatic carotid stenosis in the modern era of intensive medical prevention with antiplatelet therapy and high-intensity statins, the CREST-2 trial revisited this question in a pair of randomized clinical trials: one trial comparing carotid endarterectomy plus best medical management vs medical therapy alone and the other comparing carotid artery stenting plus best medical management vs medial therapy alone. The topline findings showed that carotid artery stenting, but not carotid endarterectomy, significantly reduced the risk of the primary outcome of a composite of stroke or death within 44 days or ipsilateral stroke within up to 4 years compared with medical therapy alone among patients without contralateral stenosis who were good procedural candidates.

articles.title: Blood Pressure Targets in Critically Ill Children
articles.abstract: “Do I need to treat this blood pressure?” is one of the most common questions to pass through the minds of acute care pediatricians during a typical day in the hospital. Blood pressure generally increases with somatic growth, reflecting developmental changes in stroke volume, vascular structure and function, and neurohumoral regulation. As a result of interindividual variation across the developmental stages of childhood, there is a wide range of acceptable blood pressure values. There is also long-standing ambiguity about what should be considered the limits of acceptable blood pressure, particularly among hospitalized children. Age-based reference values offer a starting point, although the threshold used to identify an unusually low blood pressure may differ from the pressure needed to maintain adequate organ perfusion. This uncertainty can create substantial tension when a clinician faces the decision whether to manage potentially low blood pressure in a child. Treatments for potentially low blood pressure can also vary widely, from temporary stimulation to administration of vasopressor and inotropic medications through a central vascular catheter. The clinical question of whether to manage low blood pressure is driven by concern that withholding treatment could cause harm that is hard to measure.

Co-testing with HPSA and FIT may offer a promising and economically attractive strategy in populations with high incidence of both gastric and colorectal cancers. Beyond demonstrating the potential value of this approach, the Taiwanese experience may also provide valuable lessons for countries seeking to strengthen cancer prevention programs.

articles.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Fecal Immunochemical Testing—Reply
articles.abstract: In Reply We thank Dr Huynh and colleagues for their thoughtful comments on our economic evaluation of HPSA-FIT co-testing. Rather than modeling a program developed de novo, we evaluated the incremental value of integrating HPSA testing into an established colorectal cancer screening program. Accordingly, infrastructure development costs were not included in our analysis; however, this should not be interpreted as suggesting implementation requires only minimal investment. Health system readiness varies considerably across countries, but we regard such heterogeneity as support for a staged implementation strategy rather than a limitation: countries with established FIT programs can readily add HPSA testing to existing stool-based testing pathways, whereas those with less mature systems may need to strengthen registries, laboratory networks, referral pathways, and treatment capacity.

articles.title: Fixed Pupils: Neurologic Finality vs Poetic Repair
articles.abstract: In “Holding Hope,” the poem’s crux is not simply the devastating neurologic sign of “fixed pupils,” but also the way this medical phrase is transformed in the ear of the shocked sibling of a mortally wounded patient into the impossible mercy of healing: “[t]hey fixed his pupils.” The clinical distancing inherent in a bedside case presentation, reflexively performed before a disbelieving family member, is translated by a kind of poetic mishearing from incomprehensible loss into hopeful repair. The patient’s sibling seems to only grasp fragments of reality, while the physicians only offer partial truths. Even the clinician-speaker of the poem struggles with what can be held medically vs emotionally, the gasping lines and broken-up stanzas structurally reflecting the patient’s wounded brain and body and the heartbreak of both family member and physician. Yet poetry here does not really restore hope like some kind of harmless magic bullet, nor does it heal the lethal real-world gunshot wounds; more painfully, perhaps, it tries to reconcile brutal finality with the disconsolate wish it were not so. Thus the poem ultimately becomes an “antipresentation” of sorts, in which medical facts are melded with human truths, words can have double meanings, and what can be held is both the obligatory, dire prognosis and its denial. The insistence on what poetry can hear, and what no case presentation could ever convey, is reiterated in the poem’s final lines, expressed in the importunate paradox of the patient’s sibling’s repeated words: “…you heard/‘They fixed his pupils.’”

articles.title: Licensure Framework for Autonomous Clinical Artificial Intelligence
articles.abstract: To the Editor A recent Perspective proposed a federal licensure framework for autonomous clinical artificial intelligence (AI) modeled on physician credentialing. We disagree with the analogy. Medical licensure regulates a professional actor with fiduciary duties, moral agency, personal accountability, and the ability to refuse unsafe action. A software product has none of these. It is deployed by identifiable commercial and institutional actors. Granting it professional standing does not create accountability; it obscures it.

articles.title: Licensure Framework for Autonomous Clinical Artificial Intelligence—In Reply
articles.abstract: In Reply We thank the correspondents for their Letters to the Editor, which converge on 1 concern—that autonomous clinical AI is not a person—and we agree. Our proposal never attributes moral agency to software, and licensure does not require it. Drs Ferguson and Telemi and Dr Jiang argue that a product cannot be a practitioner. But we do not license software as a moral actor; we authorize a defined clinical function and attach accountability to identifiable human parties. Developers bear primary responsibility and deploying institutions secondary responsibility precisely because the model cannot. Licensure here is a mechanism for ongoing, outcome-based authorization, not a claim of personhood.

articles.title: The Physician of The Future
articles.abstract: In the midst of the present social upheaval, one may well wonder the position physicians will eventually occupy in the cosmic scheme. Intelligent observers inform us that the answer depends entirely on our own conduct—the mass conduct inherent in intelligent organization. If physicians are to assume that leadership essential to sane medical progress, they must evolve an outline of purposes, a constructive forward-looking program of things to be done, of channels through which cooperation must flow toward their leadership. This constructive program must be so wisely planned and so faithfully followed by all worth-while physicians that at least the intelligent element of public opinion will go with it.

articles.title: A Photosensitizer Bearing an Asymmetric “Push-Pull” Bipyridine Ligand Enhances Excited State Electron Transfer
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Herein we report RuII photosensitizers that bear a single “push-pull” ligand designed to polarize charge on a single pyridine ring of 2,2′-bipyridine (bpy) in the metal-to-ligand charge-transfer (MLCT) excited state for enhanced excited state electron transfer. The photosensitizers have the general structure [Ru(dtb)2(4-CO2H,4′-R-bpy)]2+, where R is –H (RuHcb), −CF3 (RuFcb), and −CH3 (RuMcb) and dtb is 4,4′-(tert-butyl)2-bpy. These photosensitizers were synthesized, characterized spectroscopically and electrochemically, and contrasted with [Ru(dtb)2(dcb)]2+ (RuDcb) that bears the more common dicarboxylic acid ligand, Dcb = 4,4′-(CO2H)2-bipyridine. When anchored to mesoporous TiO2 thin films in a 0.1 M LiClO4/CH3CN electrolyte, RuMcb|TiO2 displayed the largest excited state electron injection yield ϕinj = 0.90 and, generally, ϕinj decreased as R became more electron withdrawing. RuDcb|TiO2 displayed a significantly lower ϕinj = 0.80. Transient absorption spectra recorded on ps and ns time scales and spectroelectrochemical data revealed that ∼70% of the total ϕinj for RuMcb occurred on a sub ps time scale that could not be kinetically resolved, only 20% occurred on this same time scale for RuDcb. Quantum chemical simulations were utilized to characterize the charge transfer excited states, the surface binding, and the interfacial electron transfer kinetics. Apart from RuFcb, the data reveal that the push–pull ligand had little impact on the ground state and a significant one on the MLCT excited state, polarizing charge on a sub-ps time scale for more efficient interfacial electron transfer. More broadly, the data reveals that push–pull ligands can be optimized for excited state electron transfer reactivity.

articles.title: Assisted Tandem Catalysis with M–M Bonded Heterobimetallic Pd–Pt Complexes: Accessing Both Pd and Pt Catalytic Cycles
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: We report the synthesis of M–M bonded Pd–Pt complexes at the Pd(I)/Pt(I) and Pd(I)/Pt(III) oxidation states. These bimetallic complexes act as a reservoir for catalytically active Pd and Pt centers, and catalysis is observed in a variety of Pd- and Pt-catalyzed reactions. We demonstrate that tandem catalytic reactions with our Pd(I)/Pt(I) complex can capitalize on both Pd and Pt catalytic cycles to enable multistep processes. These include tandem hydrosilylation/Hiyama coupling, Suzuki coupling/amide reduction, Buchwald–Hartwig amination/amide reduction, and Heck coupling/amide reduction. Tandem cycloisomerization/Heck coupling is also observed with our Pd(I)/Pt(III) complex. Control studies demonstrate that homobimetallic Pd–Pd and Pt–Pt complexes do not perform the tandem catalytic reactions and that the Pd–Pt complex is stable under air and moisture for at least 9 months. The M–M bond in these complexes enables access to unique Pd and Pt oxidation states and facilitates M–M communication, both of which can have an impact during catalysis.

articles.title: Beyond Linker Length: Three-Dimensional Linker Geometry Governs Flexibility in Zn–Triazolate MOFs
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Flexible metal–organic frameworks undergo cooperative structural transformations that underpin applications in molecular separations, sensing, and gas storage; however, the molecular origins of framework flexibility remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the role of linker geometry in directing the structural response of a family of isoreticular Zn–triazolate pillared-layer MOFs incorporating cubane (cdc), bicyclo[1.1.1]pentane (pdc), and bicyclo[2.2.2]octane (boct) dicarboxylate linkers. Variable-temperature and in situ CO2 powder X-ray diffraction, variable-temperature single-crystal X-ray diffraction, gas adsorption measurements, and machine-learning-enabled atomistic simulations reveal fundamentally different mechanical responses despite the frameworks possessing closely related architectures. The cdc framework exhibits reversible cooperative breathing, the pdc analogue undergoes pathway-dependent structural reorganization consistent with kinetic trapping following cooling of the activated framework to 77 K, whereas the boct framework accommodates deformation through continuous elastic distortion without discrete phase transitions. Computational analysis demonstrates that these contrasting behaviors arise primarily from the manner in which linker geometry governs strain accommodation within the flexible Zn–triazolate sheets, rather than from the deformation of the linker itself. These results establish structure–mechanics relationships across this family of flexible MOFs and demonstrate that subtle changes in molecular geometry provide a powerful strategy for programming cooperative structural behavior.

articles.title: Catalytic Asymmetric Diels–Alder Reaction of β,β-Disubstituted Enals with Cyclopentadiene: Syntheses of (−)-Camphene, (−)-β-Santalene, and (−)-( Z )-β-Santalol
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Despite the long and rich history of the Diels–Alder reaction, certain aspects of its scope still remain remarkably underexplored. Most prominently, reactions with β,β-disubstituted enals as dienophiles are scarcely represented in the literature. The first general and highly enantioselective method, enabled by a strongly acidic and confined imidodiphosphorimidate organocatalyst, is reported here. The reaction tolerates a broad range of enals, including substrates with functional groups and complex alkenyl substituents, delivering the corresponding cycloadducts in good yields and excellent enantioselectivity. The synthetic utility of the method is further highlighted by concise asymmetric total syntheses of (−)-camphene, (−)-β-santalene, and (−)-(Z)-β-santalol from inexpensive starting materials.

articles.title: Catalytic Uncaging of Anticancer Drugs via a Buchner Ring Expansion
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Selective drug activation in living systems remains a central challenge in targeted cancer therapy. Bioorthogonal catalysis addresses this by using abiotic transition-metal catalysts to unmask prodrugs at the tumor site, but the repertoire of suitable reactions remains limited. Here, we exploit the Buchner ring-expansion as a new uncaging strategy, in which a metal-carbene catalyzes a regioselective intramolecular ring-expansion followed by spontaneous 1,6-elimination to release a caged payload─a cascade with no biological equivalent. The iridium porphyrin complex [Ir(mPIX)Me] catalyzes this reaction at nanomolar concentrations, and the platform can accommodate structurally diverse payloads. As a proof of concept, functionalization with a bivalent human carbonic anhydrase IX (hCA IX) inhibitor enabled tumor-selective release of epirubicin (Epi) in a cancer cell model. This work thus delineates a new reaction class to the growing toolkit of transition-metal-mediated bioorthogonal chemistry.

articles.title: Continuous-Flow Irradiation Facilitates Catalyst-Free Methane-to-Methanol Conversion
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Converting methane to methanol (MTM) holds far-reaching practical implications, yet achieving both high productivity and high selectivity remains a longstanding challenge owing to the inertness of methane and the susceptibility of methanol to overoxidation. Here, we propose a continuous-flow irradiation system (CIS) by coupling radiation technology and flow chemistry for efficient MTM under ambient conditions. High-energy radiation promises direct methane activation in an oxidant-independent and catalyst-free manner with high efficiency, which enables its integration with continuous-flow synthesis that decouples CH4 activation from methanol formation in time and space, thereby preventing overoxidation and undesirable cascade side reactions. The CIS–MTM achieves a superior methanol production rate (68.3 μmol·h–1, at a dose rate of 7.2 kGy·min–1, 83.2 RH%, CH4 flow rate 60 mL·min–1) than most existing indirect activation routes, with economic scalability comparable to industrial methods. This work introduces radiation technology as a potential direct activation method for methane conversion.

articles.title: Cryogenically Flexible Organic Single-Crystal Heterostructures via Molecular Alloying for Advanced Optical Tuning
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Organic single-crystal heterostructures (OSCHs) constitute a promising platform for advanced flexible optoelectronics, yet imparting mechanical flexibility to these multiblock systems, especially given the susceptibility to failure at the interfaces between individual crystal segments, remains challenging. This obstacle is particularly aggravated at cryogenic temperatures, where the freezing of vibrational motion may cause brittleness and lead to mechanical failure. Herein, we describe an epitaxial growth strategy using molecular alloys for the fabrication of crystals of cryogenically flexible two-color (blue–cyan–blue) triblock heterostructures, prepared by growing triphenylene (TP) segments onto perylene (PER)-doped alloy seed crystals via crystallization under controlled cooling. The compatibility between the host and guest molecules provides interfaces with low defect densities. Analysis of the crystal structure reveals an abundance of weak intermolecular interactions that are thought to enable the reversible elastic deformation observed at both 298 and 77 K, thereby preventing cracking. Simultaneously, efficient Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) between TP and PER enables continuous emission tuning and doping-ratio-controlled programmability of the optoelectronic properties. The resulting heterostructures not only support low-loss active optical waveguiding and programmable multichannel optical logic and information encoding but also remain fully operational for optical transduction during bending under cryogenic conditions. This work establishes a general molecular alloying approach to structures that integrate low-temperature mechanical compliance with sophisticated photonic functionalities, providing a pathway to deformable, multiemissive optoelectronics elements that remain operational in extreme environments.

articles.title: Discovering Underpotentially Deposited Crystalline Sodium Metal Nanoparticles on the Surface of Hard Carbon Anodes
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Sodium-ion batteries are attractive candidates for low-cost and scalable energy storage in which hard carbon (HC) anodes are used. However, sodium (Na) metal plating in HC anodes at voltages above the plating potential remains a critical problem. The location and spatial distribution of crystalline sodium (c-Na) metal nanoparticles, the clusters associated with Na storage in HCs, are important for understanding this underpotential plating behavior but remain unclear. Here, we implement a cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and electron tomography (cryo-ET) workflow that directly localizes c-Na metal clusters in sodiated HC samples: cryo-ET maps nanoscale three-dimensional (3D) distributions, while cryo-EM resolves local structure and chemistry. Our workflow reveals that c-Na metal clusters reside predominantly on the surfaces or near surfaces of individual HC particles. This finding challenges existing interpretations in the literature that locate the c-Na metal clusters within closed nanopores in the bulk of the HC, presumably because prior characterization using nonimaging techniques and two-dimensional (2D) projection images associated with traditional transmission electron microscopy (TEM) lacks the spatial 3D information necessary to resolve the full spatial distribution. Our discovery is an important step toward explaining the underpotential plating phenomenon of Na metal in HC anodes, suggesting that particle-level surface and near-surface interfaces are relevant targets to mitigate plating alongside bulk-pore, electrode, and electrolyte/interphase design.

articles.title: Electroenzymatic Cascade Enables Amino Acid Synthesis through Simultaneous Nitrite Reduction and NADH Regeneration
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Amino acids are central to life and the chemical industry, yet their sustainable synthesis remains a challenge. An electroenzymatic cascade offers a promising alternative by combining the electron/proton transfer capability of electrocatalysis with the exceptional specificity of biocatalysis. Here we present a conceptually distinct electroenzymatic cascade platform that integrates electrocatalytic nitrogen oxide reduction, NADH regeneration, and enzymatic reductive amination. Using l-glutamate (l-Glu) as a model, we demonstrate that with Cu nanowires as the bifunctional electrocatalyst, the system generates NH4+ and biologically active NADH in situ, driving the production of l-Glu under mild conditions. The coupled cascade not only shifts the reaction equilibrium forward but also provides a favorable orientation and a proton-rich environment for the bioactive cofactor, boosting overall selectivity of bioactive NADH. The modular design allows straightforward adaptation to diverse substrates and electrodes, demonstrating the broad generality of this platform. This work establishes a sustainable and versatile strategy for amino acid synthesis and opens new directions for electroenzymatic production of nitrogen-containing chemicals.

articles.title: Extended Active Learning-Guided Design of Multi-Component Electrolytes with Opposing Cosolvent Properties for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Multi-component electrolytes offer expanded tunability over electrochemical properties, yet their rational design is constrained by a lack of generalizable principles. Intricate intercomponent interactions obscure the relationship between the molecular properties and battery performance, rendering material selection and compositional optimization intractable. Here, we present an extended active learning-guided framework to efficiently navigate the vast materials space and refine formulations for tri-solvent-based electrolytes in aqueous zinc-ion batteries with minimal experimental workload. Specifically, co-solvent candidates are clustered by molecular properties; co-solvents are then selected, and their pairwise combinations undergo rigorous formulation optimization. Our data-driven approach discovered a nonintuitive electrolyte composition: combining co-solvents with fundamentally opposing properties. This unique formulation, which disrupts the hydrogen-bonded network while reconstructing the solvation structure, enables Zn||NH4V4O10 full-cells to retain 90.2% capacity after 1,000 cycles. This study unveils the possibility of using active learning to discover unconventional electrolyte formulations that would otherwise be infeasible to identify through human insights.

articles.title: Living Spatially Organized Hybrid Condensates for Efficient Light-Driven CO2-to-Chemical Conversion
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Light-driven CO2-to-chemical conversion presents a sustainable route for biomanufacturing, yet the performance of photosynthetic biohybrid systems remains fundamentally constrained by disorganized biotic–abiotic interfaces, which result in inefficient photoelectron transfer, low carbon production, and substantial cellular toxicity. Here, we report a spatially organized intracellular biohybrid system that enables the light-powered conversion of CO2 to 2,3-butanediol inEscherichia coli. Inspired by the algal pyrenoid, we constructed a TiO2/RuBisCO hybrid condensate (TRHC) by integrating protein liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) with in situ biomimetic mineralization. This spatially defined condensate physically clusters light-harvesting and carbon-fixing modules, thereby facilitating direct photoelectron transfer and contributing to improved long-term cellular robustness under continuous illumination. The TRHC achieved an apparent quantum yield of 12.4% and reduced the light-induced cellular mortality by 64%. By providing a robust photoelectron supply for CO2 assimilation, the integrated system attains a 2,3-butanediol yield of 1.38 mol/mol from the consumed glucose. Moreover, under illuminated fed-batch fermentation, the platform maintains sustained biosynthetic activity over 5 days, producing 62.11 g/L of 2,3-butanediol. This LLPS-guided strategy offers a generalizable framework for engineering efficient biotic-abiotic interfaces in solar-driven biomanufacturing.

articles.title: Molecular Diversity Generation via Selective Enzymatic C–CN Bond Scission
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Selective removal of functional groups offers a powerful route to streamline molecular design and generate structural diversity. The use of such deletion strategies has surged in organic synthesis, yet achieving these transformations with high selectivity remains a formidable challenge. Here, we present a photoenzymatic platform for stereocontrolled C–CN bond cleavage of malononitriles, enabling access to diverse chiral nitriles. Directed evolution of the flavin-dependent enzyme OYE1 yielded a variant that efficiently converted a wide range of geminal dinitriles, affording products in high yields (up to >99%) and enantioselectivities (up to 3:97 e.r.). The platform was further extended to a one-pot cascade combining Michael addition with enzymatic decyanation. Mechanistic studies revealed a pathway involving a benzyl radical intermediate (Int1), followed by a carbanion species (Int2). This work establishes the first photobiocatalytic cyano group deletion strategy and provides a modular approach for sustainable synthesis of valuable chiral nitrile scaffolds.

articles.title: Pressure-Induced Single-Crystal-to-Single-Crystal Dimerization and Irreversible Optical Reconstruction in a 2D Hybrid Lead Halide
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: External pressure is a powerful tool for tuning hybrid metal halides (HMHs), yet the resulting structural and optical changes are usually reversible upon decompression. Locking pressure-accessed states through covalent bond formation, particularly while preserving single-crystallinity and optical functionality, remains challenging. Here, we report a pressure-induced single-crystal-to-single-crystal (SC-SC) [2 + 2] dimerization in a two-dimensional lead halide, (S-MAMBA)2PbBr4, which contains acrylate-functionalized S-MAMBA+ cations. This process yields a stable dimerized single-crystal phase upon decompression. The topochemically preorganized arrangement of S-MAMBA+ enables irreversible cyclobutane formation while preserving the crystallinity. High-pressure vibrational and diffraction measurements, together with recovered single-crystal structure determination, establish the pressure-induced bond-forming transformation. During compression, the emission evolves from self-trapped exciton (STE)-dominated to free-exciton (FE)-dominated recombination near the dimerization threshold, indicating a reconstructed excitonic pathway. After decompression, the dimerized phase shows irreversible optical reconstruction, characterized by opposite absorption and emission shifts. Density functional theory (DFT) reveals that this chemical transformation perturbs the inorganic-framework band-edge electronic structure through changes in organic–inorganic interactions and interlayer coupling. This work demonstrates that pressure can be used as a novel and powerful trigger for permanent bond and electronic structure reconstruction in hybrid materials.

articles.title: Regioselective Growth of Mesoporous Metal–Organic Frameworks for the Construction of Anisotropic Nanohybrids
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Mesoporous anisotropic nanohybrids (m-ANHs) have attracted growing interest because their structural asymmetry enables unique advantages in applications such as multidrug co-delivery and cascade catalysis. However, anisotropic growth in mesoporous systems has thus far been largely confined to an amorphous framework. Achieving regioselective growth of crystalline functional units integrated with mesoporous frameworks remains highly challenging, primarily because of the intrinsic competition at the heterointerface between crystal nucleation/deposition and micelle-directed mesostructural coassembly. Herein, we report an acidity-gated interfacial crystallization-coassembly switching strategy to construct single-crystalline mesoporous MOF (meso-MOF)-based ANHs. This strategy enables the site-selective growth of a new single-crystalline meso-MOF compartment at predefined heterointerfaces, yielding a diverse family of well-defined frame-like, dumbbell-like, and ternary spiny nanohybrids. Mechanistically, precise regulation of the HCl/CH3COOH ratio modulates the nucleation kinetics of MOF precursors, generating localized supersaturation that is sufficient to trigger site-selective heterogeneous nucleation. Concurrently, synchronization of MOF nucleation/growth with interfacial micelle-directed coassembly allows crystallization and mesopore organization to proceed cooperatively. The applicability of this interfacial regulation is demonstrated in several lattice-compatible and chemically stable MOF systems with different compositions and hybrid configurations. As a proof of concept, the hierarchical spiny topology significantly enhances physical bacteria–material interactions, endowing the ternary ANHs with superior antibacterial performance. Remarkably, even in the absence of any drug loading, the ANHs achieve an approximately 90% inhibition efficiency against drug-resistant bacteria. This work establishes a versatile route to regioselectively integrate single-crystalline mesoporous domains into complex anisotropic nanohybrids and highlights the functional potential of structurally programmed crystalline mesoporous interfaces.

articles.title: Stable N-Heterocyclic Carbene-Derived α-Diimine Radical Cations with Anionic Nitrogen Character
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Nitrogen-centered radicals possessing substantial anionic character have remained highly challenging to isolate because of their intrinsic electronic instability in the absence of metal coordination. Herein, we report a family of stable N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC)-derived α-diimine radical cations that constitute a rare class of persistent organic radicals featuring pronounced anionic nitrogen-centered radical character. Combined crystallographic, EPR, electrochemical, spectroscopic, and computational studies reveal an unusual electronic structure in which the molecular framework is formally cationic whereas both the unpaired electron and substantial negative charge are predominantly localized on the α-diimine nitrogen atoms. These radicals exhibit remarkable stability, undergo selective proton- and hydrogen-atom-transfer reactions, and participate in fully reversible, stepwise interconversion among dicationic, radical cationic, and neutral redox states without degradation of the molecular framework. Two-electron reduction induces reversible C–N bond formation to generate either an azetidinimine or a zwitterionic structure, with their relative stability governed by remote electronic substituents. Variable-temperature spectroscopy, UV–Vis analysis, and DFT calculations reveal dynamic solution-state equilibria that can be thermodynamically tuned through peripheral electronic modulation. These findings establish a new design principle for persistent nitrogen-centered radicals and reveal how redox state, charge distribution, spin localization, and reversible covalent bond reorganization can be coupled within a metal-free molecular framework.

SLIP coatings achieve superhydrophobic performance matching that of PFAS materials. Additionally, the SLIPs are demonstrated to be biodegradable and tolerant to abrasion and UV light exposure. Exciton Recycling as a Strategy for Controlling Energy Transfer in Doped Perovskite Nanocrystals
articles.abstract: Controlling interfacial energy transfer is central to hybrid optoelectronic and light-harvesting systems but is often limited by the short lifetime of donor excitations. Here, we show that dopant-induced exciton reservoirs regulate energy transfer. In Mn2+-doped CsPbX3 (X = Br, Cl) nanocrystals, vibrationally assisted delayed fluorescence (VADF) enables exciton capture, storage, and repopulation. This exciton recycling sustains energy transfer to molecular acceptors through Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET). Ultrafast transient absorption and time-resolved photoluminescence measurements reveal a nonmonotonic dependence of FRET efficiency on Mn concentration, consistent with an optimal regime of Mn-mediated exciton recycling. By tuning halide composition and temperature, we establish a correlation between VADF strength and energy-transfer efficiency, achieving up to a 4-fold enhancement in FRET. These findings identify exciton availability as a key control parameter for interfacial energy transfer and highlight exciton-reservoir engineering as a strategy for controlling energy flow in semiconductor nanostructures.

articles.title: Helical Photonic Confinement of Narrowband-Emissive Carbon Quantum Dots Enables Amplified and Stimulus-Responsive Circularly Polarized Luminescence
articles.abstract: Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) materials that simultaneously exhibit large luminescence dissymmetry factors (glum), high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs), and dynamic optical addressability remain highly sought after yet challenging to realize. Here, we establish a CQDs-CLCs photonic coupling platform via helical photonic confinement of narrowband-emissive carbon quantum dots (CQDs) in a chiral liquid crystal (CLC) host, enabling controlled emitter-photonic bandgap (PBG) spectral engineering. This yields amplified chiroptical signals with a glum of up to 1.12 and a figure of merit (FM = glum × PLQY) of 0.67. Beyond static performance, the helical photonic architecture allows dynamic CPL modulation by multiple stimuli, including temperature, light, electric field, mechanical pressure, viewing angle, and polarization. This work establishes helical photonic confinement as a material-photonic coupling strategy for decoupling dissymmetry amplification from emission efficiency while enabling multimodal stimulus-responsive modulation, offering potential applications in optical encryption, smart textiles, and photonic devices.

articles.title: Nanoscale Mapping of Internal Magnetization Dynamics Reveals How Disorder Shapes Heat Generation in Magnetic Particle Hyperthermia
articles.abstract: Magnetic particle hyperthermia relies on the efficient conversion of magnetic field energy into heat, yet the microscopic mechanisms governing this process within individual particles remain poorly understood. Here, we combine AC magnetometry experiments with dynamic micromagnetic simulations to connect microstructural features, magnetization dynamics, and macroscopic heat dissipation. We resolve heat generation at the intraparticle level, uncovering heterogeneous nanoscale heat-generation bursts with nanometer and nanosecond resolution. At a given particle size, grain size acts as an experimentally tunable parameter, balancing anisotropy disorder and pinning strength, thereby controlling both the magnitude and spatiotemporal distribution of heat release. Experiments show that flux-closure-dominated nanoflower architectures composed by larger grains generate more heat than their smaller-grain counterparts, whose deeper intraparticle pinning landscape redistributes heat generation over extended time windows. Together, our results provide a mechanistic framework linking nanoparticle microstructure to magnetic heating and establish design principles for optimizing nanoflowers as magnetic hyperthermia transducers.

articles.title: Oriented Spiral Growth of Two-Dimensional Materials
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) spiral growth is crucial for scalable moiré superlattices, yet controlled large-area synthesis remains an outstanding challenge. Here, we report a rational epitaxial strategy for synthesizing oriented spiral WS2 films on a-plane sapphire, where unidirectionally aligned R-stacked domains serve as templates and substrate tilting acts as the key trigger for spiral growth. Comprehensive characterization confirms high density, identical crystallographic orientation, zero interlayer twist, well-defined R-stacking, and excellent crystalline quality across these structures. We propose a two-stage growth model: dual-coupling-guided formation of aligned R-stacked domains transitions into a dual-mode process for simultaneous lateral coalescence and vertical screw-dislocation-driven growth. The unique configuration of these oriented-spiral films endows photodetectors with superior performance and an extended spectral response. Our work represents a significant advance in 2D spiral materials, establishing a key step toward robust and scalable twistronics.

articles.title: Shear Assisted Diamond Formation in Cold-Compressed HOPG
articles.abstract: Diamond synthesis from a graphite precursor is primarily constrained by the requirement for the simultaneous application of extreme pressures and temperatures. We explore the microstructural changes in highly oriented pyrolytic graphite subject to shear during room temperature compression. Using a diamond anvil cell, nonhydrostatic pressures of up to 160 GPa were applied, resulting in an optically transparent, diamond-like material above 80 GPa that reverted to an opaque, largely graphite-like material upon decompression. Detailed microstructural analysis of the recovered sample revealed nanoscale diamond-like domains embedded within a graphitic matrix containing shear bands and localized basal slip features consistent with a high shear environment. Employing a rotational diamond anvil cell greatly enhanced these shear-induced features, producing significant amounts of diamond in samples recovered from applied pressures as low as 15 GPa. These findings demonstrate that shear can facilitate the graphite-to-diamond transformation, enabling sp3 bond formation under conditions where extreme temperatures are not required.

articles.title: Tailored Dissipation for Directional Transport in Plasmonic Ratchets
articles.abstract: Ratchets provide directed transport without global biased forces via parity-breaking combinations of nonequilibrium driving with dissipation or nonlinear dynamics. They play a central role down to the quantum level in molecular motors, colloidal particles, microbiological processes, semiconductor devices, optical lattices, and photonic structures, where nonequilibrium is usually achieved by dynamic potentials or couplings. Here, we address the question of whether transport can be achieved by only using time-dependent dissipation while keeping all potentials and couplings static. In this experiment-theory collaboration, we construct such non-Hermitian ratchets that solely rely on time- and space-periodic dissipation. Notably, the rectified transport increases with larger local dissipation. Floquet theory uncovers low-loss directional transport at suitable driving frequencies, which is linked to linear quasienergy bands. These regions are separated from nonresonant behavior by sharp transitions with characteristic exceptional points in the spectrum. A plasmonic Floquet-dissipative ratchet is studied experimentally by using real- and Fourier-space leakage radiation microscopy.

articles.title: Crystalline neutral and cationic oxoboranes
articles.abstract: The isolation of oxoboranes (RB≡O) featuring a genuine B–O triple bond has remained an outstanding challenge owing to the electron deficiency of boron and the intrinsic instability of the B≡O linkage. So far, direct evidence for such species has been largely limited to gas-phase and matrix-isolation studies and only recently inferred in solution. Here we report the isolation of a stable, free oxoborane generated via a carbon-monoxide-triggered transformation of a heterocumulene. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction establishes a terminal B≡O unit, while electronic structure analyses reveal two orthogonal π bonds consistent with a highly polarized triple bond. Mechanistic studies support a carbon monoxide coordination–insertion–isomerization pathway. The resulting oxoborane exhibits ambiphilic reactivity, enabling access to both neutral and cationic derivatives. These findings establish free oxoboranes as isolable species under condensed-phase conditions and provide a platform for exploring low-coordinate boron–oxygen multiple bonds. The isolation of oxoboranes featuring a genuine B–O triple bond is challenging owing to the instability of the B≡O linkage. Now stable crystalline oxoboranes have been prepared through a carbon-monoxide-triggered transformation, revealing a highly polarized B–O triple bond and enabling access to both neutral and cationic derivatives through ambiphilic reactivity.

articles.title: Synthesis and isolation of stable oxoboranes
articles.abstract: Oxoboranes, molecules bearing a triple bond between a dicoordinate boron atom and a monocoordinate oxygen atom, are some of the longest-sought reactive main-group species. Their syntheses have been the subject of a series of documented attempts dating back to at least the early 1960s, leading to gas-phase/matrix isolation and evidence of chemical trapping, as well as isolation of oxoborane derivatives with reduced B–O bond orders. However, their detection or isolation of base-/acid-free oxoboranes in the condensed phase remains challenging. Here we present a remarkably simple synthesis of three oxoboranes that are stable as crystalline solids at room temperature. These species feature exceptionally short (1.208(4)–1.217(4) Å) and strong B–O bonds. Their properties are elucidated by both experimental and computational methods, and an explanation for their unusual stability is provided. Oxoboranes are among the longest-sought species in main-group chemistry. Now, stable crystalline oxoboranes with exceptionally short and strong B–O bonds have been prepared through the reaction of a diboracumulene with carbonyl-bearing compounds.

articles.title: A SARS-CoV-2 entry inhibitor trimerizes to lock the spike protein in a closed conformation
articles.abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 spike protein binds its receptor ACE2 to initiate target-cell infection. To engage ACE2, at least one of the three receptor-binding domains (RBDs) of the spike must adopt the up orientation. Here, we describe S22, a potent, bioavailable, and non-toxic inhibitor of BA.2 and all subsequent Omicron variants. Cryo-EM analyses showed that S22 assembled as a trimer in the central cavity of the spike apex, stabilizing all three RBDs in the down orientation, thereby preventing ACE2 association. Binding studies, especially those using mixed S22-sensitive and -resistant spikes, imply a cooperative assembly of three S22 molecules with three RBDs, resulting in an unusually slow S22 off-rate. Consistent with its slow dissociation and favorable pharmacokinetics, S22 suppressed viral replication and inflammation in the lungs of XBB.1.5-infected female mice. Thus, S22 potently inhibits Omicron entry through a distinct mechanism whereby a small compound assembles cooperatively as a trimer to stabilize spike in an inactive conformation. In this study, the authors identify S22 as a potent inhibitor of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variants and use structural analysis to show that it prevents infection by assembling as a trimer into a trimeric spike protein cavity, locking the spike in a closed, inactive state.
