A multi-attention mechanism-improved ResNet18 approach for lithology identification and classification
articles.abstract: Lithology identification is vital for improving geological exploration accuracy, optimizing petroleum exploration schemes, and ensuring construction engineering safety. Traditional identification methods suffer from low efficiency, high cost, and heavy dependence on domain expertise. This study proposes a lithology identification approach based on the ResNet18 backbone, in which five lightweight attention mechanisms, namely CBAM, channel-only attention, ECA, SE, and spatial-only attention, are systematically compared, and the best-performing CBAM module is embedded to strengthen feature extraction and discrimination capacity. The Open-Source Computer Vision (OpenCV) library is adopted for dataset preprocessing, where raw images are converted to grayscale to suppress interference from irrelevant information. Comparative experiments demonstrate that CBAM outperforms the other evaluated attention modules and is therefore incorporated into the final network architecture. A hyperparameter sensitivity analysis of the CBAM-based model demonstrates that the model performance varies with different combinations of learning rate and batch size. When trained with a learning rate of 0.0001 and a batch size of 16, the model achieves a lithology identification accuracy of 86.36%, substantially improving overall recognition performance. By integrating CBAM into ResNet18, the proposed method enables accurate recognition to support multi-field engineering applications, reduce risks, and promote intelligent precision.

articles.title: A qualitative exploration of variations in social prescribing in primary care for people living with dementia in England: Barriers and enablers to positive service experiences
articles.abstract: The number of people living with dementia and related costs continue to grow worldwide. Although generally associated with memory difficulties, non-cognitive symptoms of dementia are common and usually stem from unmet needs. Evidence emerging suggests that social prescribing improves the wellbeing of people living with dementia. This study explored adaptations to key elements of social prescribing for people living with dementia, as well as barriers to and enablers of positive experiences among people living with dementia and service providers. The qualitative study engaged people living with dementia (n = 8), carers (n = 9) and service providers (n = 17) involved in social prescribing through primary care. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, and the essential ingredients of social prescribing schemes comprised the initial organising categories for template analysis. The final template included four integrative themes: unique challenges of dementia; interpretations of the social prescribing role; integration of social prescribing into dementia care; and evaluation, improvement and sustainability. Positive workplace cultures and skills in dementia care and support enabled multidisciplinary collaborations and the successful adaptations of the generic social prescribing model to improve the experiences among people living with dementia and service providers. Resistance to and confusion about the social prescribing link workers’ role, and inappropriate referrals were barriers to positive experiences and bottom-up feedback. Primary care networks’ agreements on core outcomes within proactive systems of dementia care and support may promote meaningful bottom-up feedback on the effectiveness of social prescribing for people living with dementia, guiding service improvements.

articles.title: A qualitative study of the barriers and facilitators to adopting a sustainable diet among adolescents in Ireland
articles.abstract: An increasing body of evidence indicates that systemic changes to the food system are necessary to mitigate ongoing environmental degradation. The adoption of sustainable dietary practices is an actionable individual-level strategy that may benefit both human health and environmental sustainability. This paper aimed to explore the barriers and facilitators to adopting a sustainable diet among adolescents in Ireland. The data from this research seeks to clarify the steps needed to support this dietary transition. Data were collected from four sites, involving 48 participants aged 15–17 years in seven semi-structured focus groups. Non-probability convenience sampling was employed. Transcripts were audio-recorded, transcribed, and inductively coded to identify barriers and facilitators, which were then deductively mapped onto the Theoretical Domains Framework and presented on the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation – Behaviour model. Barriers (n = 33) were more frequent than facilitators (n = 8) in the adoption of a sustainable diet. Prominent barriers to adopting a sustainable diet included a lack of knowledge about the characteristics of a sustainable diet, a current diet that does not align with a sustainable diet, a lack of practical skills for preparing a sustainable diet, unaccommodating school canteens, and cultural influences such as a strong attachment to meat. Facilitators to the adoption of a sustainable diet were the view that this diet promotes human health, and the acknowledgement of the changes required to make their diet more sustainable. However, although participants could identify changes to make their diets more sustainable, most were unwilling to transition at present. This research is important because it provides insights into the design of future interventions using the Behaviour Change Wheel intervention framework to facilitate behaviour change to support adolescents’ transition to a sustainable diet.

articles.title: Airway management and anaesthetic interventions for children with cleft lip and/or palate undergoing general anaesthesia: Protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis
articles.abstract: Background Children with cleft lip and/or palate may present unique challenges during perioperative airway management because of altered upper-airway and craniofacial anatomy. These children frequently undergo surgical procedures requiring general anaesthesia and airway instrumentation. Several airway-management and anaesthetic techniques have been evaluated to facilitate tracheal intubation and reduce perioperative airway complications, but the comparative evidence from randomised controlled trials has not been systematically evaluated. Methods This systematic review and meta-analysis will include randomised controlled trials involving children < 18 years with cleft lip and/or palate undergoing general anaesthesia. Eligible studies will compare alternative techniques or devices for airway management or other anaesthetic strategies between two groups of cleft lip/palate patients. The primary outcome will be difficulty in tracheal intubation. Where definitions vary substantially, outcomes will be analysed separately or synthesised narratively. Secondary outcomes will include difficult mask ventilation, oxygen desaturation, airway obstruction, difficult laryngoscopy, first-attempt intubation success, number of intubation attempts, time to successful intubation or airway establishment, failed intubation and other perioperative airway or respiratory adverse events. Two reviewers will independently select RCTs, extract data and assess risk of bias. Risk of bias will be evaluated using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Random-effects meta-analysis will be performed where clinically appropriate. Risk ratios will be used for dichotomous outcomes and mean differences or standardized mean differences for continuous outcomes. Certainty of evidence for important outcomes will be assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Registration and review status The review was prospectively registered in PROSPERO on 10 March 2026 (CRD420261326076). Full-text screening and data extraction are ongoing and not yet complete. Protocol amendments are documented transparently in PROSPERO.

articles.title: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi and mycorrhizal helper bacteria co-inoculation alters drought-associated physiological traits and leaf abscisic acid concentration in citrus rootstocks
articles.abstract: Plants rely heavily on root-associated microflora to mitigate various environmental stresses such as drought and the use of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) as a biological instrument to enhance plant drought tolerance, through the formation of mutualistic associations, seems like a novel strategy for sustainable agriculture. Thus, a glasshouse study was undertaken with two citrus rootstocks (Troyer citrange and Cleopatra mandarin) under 20 days of differential moisture regimes (well-watered and water-stress condition), after 270 days of inoculation with two AMF strains (Glomus intraradices and mixed strains of Gigaspora decipiens + Glomus mosseae) alone or in combination with mycorrhizal helper bacteria (MHB), i.e., phosphate solubilising bacteria (PSB), Azospirillum or Providencia, with an objective of testing the hypothesis that AMF and MHB might influence ABA accumulation in citrus leaves, thereby altering physio-biochemical response to declining soil water status. The seedlings dually inoculated with AMF and MHB exhibited significantly higher relative water content of leaf as well as rhizospheric soil. Glomus intraradices in association with PSB or Azospirillum accumulated higher concentrations of osmolytes (phenols, proline and total soluble sugars) and antioxidant metabolites (glutathione and carotenoids) in leaves under WS condition. Significantly altered leaf tissue ABA accumulation was noticed in dual inoculated treatment of Glomus intraradices and Azospirillum for Troyer citrange (3.517 µg g-1 F.W.) and G. intraradices and PSB for Cleopatra mandarin seedlings (3.079 µg g-1 F.W.), under water-stress condition, as compared to other microbial inoculants including control. Thus, water deficit stress induced physiological and biochemical response pathways could be modified by AMF and MHB. Under these experimental conditions, Troyer citrange exhibited higher relative water content, photosynthetic activity, and stomatal conductance under drought conditions than Cleopatra mandarin seedlings, offering a potential microbial intervention strategy for mitigating osmotic stress in semi-arid environments.

articles.title: Atrial fibrillation is independently associated with impaired myocardial perfusion
articles.abstract: A characteristic feature of obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) is impaired myocardial blood flow (MBF). Previous studies have shown that atrial fibrillation (AF) is also associated with reduced hyperemic MBF. However, it is unknown whether an independent association exists between AF and MBF in symptomatic patients with suspected obstructive CAD. We studied 874 patients at Kuopio University Hospital (Finland) who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) and [15O]H2O myocardial perfusion positron emission tomography due to suspected obstructive CAD in 2017–2023. The final cohort comprised 31 AF patients and 120 propensity score-matched sinus rhythm (SR) patients. The matching criteria were age, sex, body mass index, number of traditional risk factors for CAD (0–5), calcium score, and total CCTA status (i.e., the overall severity of CCTA findings). Global hyperemic MBF was lower in AF patients than in SR patients (median 1.9 mL/g/min [IQR 1.4–2.6 mL/g/min] vs. 3.0 mL/g/min [IQR 2.4–3.6 mL/g/min], p < 0.001). Impaired hyperemic MBF (< 2.3 mL/g/min in ≥ 1 segment) was more frequent in AF patients (n = 25/31, 81%) than in SR patients (n = 50/120, 42%, p < 0.001). Furthermore, the presence of AF was independently associated with reduced hyperemic MBF in three multivariate general linear models (p < 0.001 in each model). To summarize, AF was independently associated with impaired hyperemic MBF in patients with suspected obstructive CAD. This association should be considered in clinical practice when interpreting the results of myocardial perfusion imaging in patients with AF.

articles.title: Beyond mid-thigh: Ultrasound assessment of hamstring muscle architecture at multiple muscle lengths in relation to strength
articles.abstract: Objectives To investigate the relationship between ultrasound-based muscle architecture parameters and isometric knee flexor muscle strength in healthy individuals, and to evaluate whether distal (25%) and proximal (75%) measurement sites differ in their ability to reflect muscle strength compare to the commonly used mid-thigh (50%) region. Methods Isometric muscle strength was measured in 20 healthy (22.15 ± 2.41 y; 8 females, 12 males) participants using a hand-held dynamometer. Ultrasound parameters (cross-sectional area, muscle thickness, pennation angle) of the biceps femoris-long head, semitendinosus, and semimembranosus were measured at 25%, 50%, and 75% of thigh length. Associations between strength and ultrasound-based parameters were examined using multiple linear regression analysis. Results Moderate-to-high correlations (r = 0.615–0.815) were observed between muscle strength and cross-sectional area for all muscles at 50%. The regression model explained 89% of the variance in muscle strength (p < 0.001). Notably, the cross-sectional area of the semimembranosus and the total hamstring cross-sectional area at 25% length demonstrated strong correlations with muscle strength (r = 0.907 and 0.802, respectively). At 75%, the cross-sectional area of the semimembranosus showed a non-significant association with strength, while it could not be measured for the semitendinosus and biceps femoris-long head due to anatomical limitations. Muscle thickness showed significant correlations for the semitendinosus and semimembranosus (r = 0.702 and 0.698, respectively), whereas pennation angle demonstrated weaker and inconsistent relationships. Conclusions The cross-sectional area of the semimembranosus at 50% of muscle length showed the strongest ultrasound-based predictor of isometric muscle strength. However, measurement at the distal site demonstrated robust associations, suggesting this region may serve as a practical alternative. In contrast, proximal measurements were limited and showed non-significant associations with strength. These findings can help expand the clinical and research applications of ultrasound imaging for assessing hamstring strength. Given the exploratory nature of this study, these findings should be interpreted cautiously.

articles.title: Comparative genomics of seven Tenacibaculum maritimum isolates from farmed Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar), Atlantic halibut (Hippoglossus hippoglossus), and lumpfish (Cyclopterus lumpus) in Canada and Norway reveals conserved features
articles.abstract: Tenacibaculum maritimum is a major bacterial pathogen of marine fish responsible for ulcerative disease outbreaks and high mortality in numerous fish species and represents an important challenge in aquaculture worldwide. In this study, we characterized seven newly sequenced T. maritimum isolates recovered from farmed Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar), Atlantic halibut (Hippoglossus hippoglossus), and lumpfish (Cyclopterus lumpus) in British Columbia (Canada) and Norway, including the first complete genome of T. maritimum isolated from Atlantic salmon in Norway. Comparative genomic analysis revealed the presence of a complete Type IX secretion system (T9SS) and the canonical gliding-associated machinery. We also identified a largely conserved repertoire of candidate T9SS substrates and several major host-interaction proteins. Phylogenetic analysis placed the isolates in several well-supported clades comprising strains from different geographic origins and host species. Characterization of the O-antigen gene clusters identified three different types (1−0, 2−1, and 4−0), whose distribution was not congruent with the phylogenetic relationships among isolates. Colony development of the four Norwegian isolates on agar was strongly influenced by incubation temperature, with rapid growth at 20–24°C, slower growth at 12–16°C, and only limited growth at 8°C. This study expands the available genomic resources for T. maritimum and highlights the importance of integrating genomic and environmental surveillance to improve tenacibaculosis management in aquaculture systems.

articles.title: Comparison of IOL power calculation formulas in short eyes using ESCRS calculator and eyetemis: Influence of anterior segment biometry
articles.abstract: This study compared the refractive prediction accuracy of seven contemporary intraocular lens (IOL) power calculation formulas in eyes with short axial length and assessed the influence of anterior chamber depth (ACD) and lens thickness (LT) on prediction error (PE). A total of 124 eyes with an axial length ≤22.0 mm that underwent uncomplicated phacoemulsification with implantation of a Tecnis ZCB00 IOL were included. Predicted postoperative refractions were obtained using the ESCRS calculator for Barrett Universal II, Cooke K6, EVO 2.0, Hill-RBF 3.0, Hoffer QST, Kane, and Pearl-DGS. Formula performance was evaluated using robust trimmed-mean analyses of trueness, precision, and accuracy implemented in the Eyetemis platform, along with conventional PE metrics and the proportions of eyes within predefined error thresholds. The mean axial length was 21.67 ± 0.31 mm, and the mean implanted IOL power was 25.2 ± 1.6 D. Kane showed a lower trimmed-mean absolute PE than Hoffer QST (0.376 vs. 0.445 D; p = 0.014). No significant inter-formula differences were observed at clinically relevant error thresholds. ACD and LT showed weak, formula-specific associations with PE; however, these findings were exploratory and not clinically actionable. Overall, contemporary formulas provided broadly comparable refractive accuracy in short eyes, although small formula-specific differences were observed.

articles.title: Disparities in screening participation and stage at diagnosis for breast and bowel cancers among individuals with pre-existing mental health disorders: A population-based study
articles.abstract: People with pre-existing mental health disorders (PMHD) often have lower cancer screening uptake and later-stage diagnoses. It remains unclear whether these disparities persist within highly accessible universal healthcare systems without strict gatekeeping. We simultaneously investigated the associations between PMHD and both screening participation and stage at diagnosis of breast and bowel cancers within the Taiwan health service. Using nationwide National Health Insurance and Cancer Registry data covering over 99% of the population, we compared outcomes between individuals with and without PMHD. Propensity score matching was applied for the screening cohort. Adjusted odds ratios were estimated using logistic regression, with subgroup analyses for severe PMHD. Overall, PMHD was associated with higher screening participation (adjusted odds ratios [aOR]: breast = 1.04, bowel = 1.12) and reduced odds of metastatic disease at diagnosis (breast = 0.72, bowel = 0.93), although the magnitude of these associations was modest, particularly for bowel cancer. Conversely, individuals with severe PMHD had significantly lower odds of screening (breast = 0.81, bowel = 0.88) despite high outpatient use. Furthermore, while the severe group retained reduced odds of metastatic breast cancer at diagnosis (aOR = 0.79), they showed no staging advantage for bowel cancer. While Taiwan’s highly accessible universal healthcare system may contribute to a surveillance effect benefiting the general PMHD population, significant disparities persist for individuals with severe illnesses. Targeted interventions, procedural simplifications for self-administered tests, and multidisciplinary person-centred care models, may be needed to ensure health equity.

articles.title: Erector spinae plane block added to intercostal nerve block versus intercostal nerve block alone for postoperative analgesia in video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery: A randomized controlled trial
articles.abstract: Objective The aim of the study was to investigate whether the addition of an erector spinae plane block (ESPB) to surgical intercostal nerve block (INB) provides additional postoperative analgesic benefits in patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS). Methods This prospective, randomized controlled trial included 60 adult patients undergoing elective three-port VATS. Patients were randomly assigned to receive either combined ESPB plus INB (EI) or INB alone. Patients, surgeons, ward nurses, postoperative outcome assessors, and data analysts were blinded to group assignment, whereas the anesthesiologists performing the intervention were unblinded. The primary outcome was pain intensity at 1 hour postoperatively, assessed using the Numerical Rating Scale (NRS). Prespecified secondary outcomes included repeated postoperative NRS pain assessments through 48 hours and cumulative opioid consumption at 24 hours. Results The NRS pain score at 1 hour postoperatively was 5.83 ± 2.86 in the EI group and 5.52 ± 3.10 in the INB group (mean difference 0.31, 95% confidence interval [CI], −1.25 to 1.87, p = 0.691). In a post hoc exploratory longitudinal analysis, a linear mixed-effects model demonstrated no significant group-by-time interaction in postoperative NRS pain scores (F[7, 401.2] = 0.81, p = 0.581). Cumulative opioid consumption at 24 hours, expressed as intravenous morphine equivalents, was 41.0 mg (interquartile range [IQR], 31.0–58.5) in the EI group and 40.0 mg (IQR, 29.1–48.3) in the INB group (between-group difference, 3.0 mg; 95% CI, −6.2 to 12.0; p = 0.501). Conclusions Adding single-injection ESPB to surgical INB did not significantly reduce 1-hour postoperative pain scores or 24-hour opioid consumption following VATS. Larger adequately powered studies are required to determine whether smaller clinically relevant incremental benefits exist. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03949790

articles.title: Experiences and challenges of healthcare professionals in oncological surgery during the COVID-19 pandemic: A qualitative study
articles.abstract: by Antonia L. Stengler, Elke Mattern, Ulrich Ronellenfitsch, Anke Steckelberg Introduction The COVID-19 pandemic posed significant challenges not only to healthcare systems but also to healthcare professionals. This study explores the experiences, perceptions, and perceived burdens of healthcare professionals involved in the care of patients undergoing oncological surgery during the pandemic, with a particular focus on clinical staff working in hospital-based care in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. Methods A qualitative, interpretive-hermeneutic approach was employed using one focus group and one individual semi-structured interview. Participants were healthcare professionals involved in the care of patients undergoing oncological surgery. The focus group included 12 participants, and one additional participant took part in an individual interview. The transcripts were independently coded and analytically annotated by two researchers and systematically analyzed in an iterative process using MAXQDA. The analysis combined deductively informed codes derived from the interview guide with inductively developed codes emerging from the data. The study was reported in accordance with the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) reporting statement. Results In September 2024, one focus group and one individual interview were conducted with a total of 13 participants, predominantly nurses and nursing assistants. Nine categories were identified. Participants described substantial emotional, professional, and organizational burdens during the COVID-19 pandemic, including stress, anxiety, increased demands, uncertainty, and difficulties in maintaining usual standards of patient care. Participants also reported challenges related to postponed or adapted oncological treatments, communication with patients under infection-control measures, postoperative care under capacity constraints, team collaboration, and the availability and use of personal protective equipment. Political measures, changing regulations, and the occupational vaccination mandate were perceived by participants as sources of uncertainty, frustration, and reduced autonomy. Despite these challenges, participants also described experiences of team cohesion and professional commitment. Participants expressed a need for clearer guidance, accessible contact persons, psychosocial support, supervision, and greater involvement in decision-making. Conclusion The findings suggest that healthcare professionals involved in hospital-based oncological surgical care experienced substantial emotional, ethical, and organizational challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic. Participants’ accounts indicate that pandemic preparedness should extend beyond infection control and include clear communication, consistent guidance, psychosocial support, supervision, and adequate organizational resources. Given the small, convenience-based, and predominantly nursing sample, these findings should be interpreted as context-specific accounts rather than as representative of healthcare professionals in oncological surgery as a whole.

articles.title: Factors associated with mortality among critically ill pediatric patients referred to a tertiary hospital in Indonesia
articles.abstract: Background An efficient referral system is an important but often under-recognized determinant of survival in critically ill children. Previous studies have reported high mortality rates among pediatric patients transferred to tertiary care facilities. This study aimed to identify factors associated with Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) mortality among critically ill children transferred and admitted to a tertiary-level referral hospital in Yogyakarta, Indonesia. Material and methods This prospective cohort study was conducted over a 12-month period (July 1, 2023, to June 30, 2024) and included all critically ill children admitted to the PICU following interhospital referral. Demographic, clinical, referral, and transport data were prospectively collected. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with PICU mortality. Results A total of 334 children were included, with a median age of 6 years. PICU mortality was 25.4%. The most common referral indication based on the Pediatric Assessment Triangle (PAT) was central nervous system dysfunction. Pre-referral management most commonly included oxygen therapy, antibiotic administration, and fluid resuscitation. Compared with survivors, non-survivors had higher PELOD-2 scores and were more likely to require intubation, mechanical ventilation, and vasoactive support before referral. In the multivariable analysis, pre-referral vasoactive support (adjusted OR 2.23, 95% CI 1.20–4.15; P = 0.011) and higher PELOD-2 scores within the first 24 hours after PICU admission (adjusted OR 1.32 per 1-point increase, 95% CI 1.20–1.45; P < 0.001) were independently associated with PICU mortality. Referral distance, decision time, and transfer time were not independently associated with mortality. Conclusion PICU mortality among critically ill children transferred and admitted to a tertiary-care hospital in Indonesia remains high. Pre-referral vasoactive support and higher PELOD-2 scores at PICU admission were independently associated with PICU mortality. These findings generate the hypothesis that improvements in early stabilization and communication may improve outcomes, warranting prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Fluid-layer-assisted mold temperature control for injection-molded bridge-type compliant mechanisms: Experimental thermal validation and simulation-based benchmarking against conventional cooling channels
articles.abstract: The injection molding of bridge-type compliant mechanisms is sensitive to non-uniform mold temperature because the thin flexure hinges are prone to premature solidification and incomplete filling. This study evaluates a fluid-layer-assisted mold temperature-control architecture using experimental thermography, transient thermo-fluid simulation, a representative straight-channel thermal baseline, melt-filling analysis, and displacement testing of molded HDPE mechanisms. The fluid-layer thermo-fluid model was validated against infrared measurements, yielding a mean absolute error (MAE) of 5.01 °C and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 6.44 °C across six validation points. Under the numerical benchmark condition of an 80 °C inlet temperature, a mass flow rate of 59.5 g/s, and 40 s heating, the fluid-layer architecture was predicted to increase the average cavity-surface temperature by approximately 4.0 °C and reduce the maximum longitudinal temperature difference by 28.6% relative to the straight-channel model. Independent thermography of a representative steel straight-channel insert under the same inlet-temperature and flow-rate conditions showed a lower and more non-uniform surface-temperature field than the steel fluid-layer configuration, confirming the direction of the predicted thermal advantage. Melt-filling simulations subsequently predicted incomplete filling at the thin flexure region for the straight-channel configuration and complete filling for the fluid-layer configuration; this filling comparison remains simulation-based. For HDPE blends containing 0–25 wt% recycled material, the molded mechanisms retained an approximately linear input–output displacement response over the investigated range. At an input displacement of approximately 175 µm, the mean output displacement decreased from 857 µm for virgin HDPE to 745 µm at 25 wt% recycled HDPE. The results support the fluid-layer architecture as a conventionally machinable approach for improving mold-surface thermal control, while polymer morphology, fatigue durability, and experimental straight-channel filling remain subjects for future work.

articles.title: From accounting systems to business performance: A serial mediation model with IPMA evidence from Vietnamese SMEs
articles.abstract: This study examines how organisational and technological antecedents shape management accounting information quality and adoption level among Vietnamese small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), and how these characteristics influence decision quality and business performance, with business environment uncertainty as a moderator. Using a cross-sectional survey of 503 Vietnamese SME managers, the study applies partial least squares structural equation modelling and importance-performance map analysis to test a five-antecedent serial mediation model grounded in contingency theory and information processing theory. All ten hypotheses were supported. Information technology capability was the strongest driver of accounting information quality (β = 0.508), and market competition intensity was the strongest driver of adoption level (β = 0.385). Decision quality was the strongest direct driver of business performance (β = 0.558), and business environment uncertainty positively moderated this relationship (β = 0.238). All five serial indirect paths to business performance were statistically significant. The importance-performance analysis identified information technology capability as the highest-priority investment area, combining high importance with low realised performance (52.01 out of 100). To our knowledge, this study offers one of the first comprehensive tests of a serial mediation model linking these antecedents to business performance through accounting characteristics and decision quality in Vietnamese SMEs, one of the first importance-performance prioritisation maps for managers in this context, and extends contingency theory by identifying business environment uncertainty as a pure moderator rather than a direct antecedent. Findings suggest Vietnamese SME managers should prioritise digital accounting infrastructure investment ahead of expanding accounting tool adoption, and that government support for digital accounting tools may be warranted. The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, partly addressed through theoretically grounded antecedent ordering, predictive validity testing, and multi-method bias assessment; the single-country scope reflects Vietnam's structural representativeness of wider ASEAN transition economies.

articles.title: From public digital discourse to sustained engagement: Digital cultural translation of the Twenty-Four Solar Terms
articles.abstract: Digital media can increase the visibility of living heritage without securing understanding or sustained engagement. We examined how public digital discourse about the Twenty-Four Solar Terms can be translated into an interpretive stimulus and how users evaluate it. We collected 3,433 publicly visible online text units and retained 1,101 after cleaning and anonymisation. The retained corpus informed collaborative thematic reading; 1,089 texts met the token threshold for keyword extraction and auxiliary topic-model inspection. Thematic analysis identified six cultural theme categories. They covered seasonal diet and bodily care; temporal order and heritage knowledge; and natural phenology and seasonal perception. They also covered folk customs and ritual life; aesthetic imagery and digital creative expression; and agricultural production and everyday practice. These categories informed a five-page storyboard through theme-design mapping and expert-assisted review. Survey data from 350 valid respondents were analysed with covariance-based structural equation modelling (CB-SEM) and supplementary fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA). Information clarity, visual aesthetics, perceived explorability and perceived authenticity were positively associated with perceived cultural value. Perceived explorability had the largest standardised path estimate for cultural value, and perceived authenticity was also associated with cultural identity. Perceived cultural value and cultural identity were associated with sustained cultural engagement intention. Configurational analysis identified four sufficient configurations for high engagement and four for low engagement. The two solution sets were asymmetric rather than mirror images. These findings link perceived interpretive qualities, cultural value and cultural identity with sustained cultural engagement intention.

articles.title: Heart rate and blood pressure variability, and baroreflex sensitivity, during heat exposure in persons with type 2 diabetes and hypertension
articles.abstract: The autonomic nervous system regulates cardiovascular homeostasis during stressors such as heat, but the effects of type 2 diabetes (T2D) with hypertension on such responses are unclear. Twenty male participants (10 with type 2 diabetes and hypertension and 10 age-matched healthy controls; mean ages 64 ± 4.14 and 63 ± 5.42 years) underwent a 90-minute whole-body heat exposure at 40 °C and 50% relative humidity. Heart rate variability (HRV), baroreflex sensitivity (BRS), and blood pressure variability (BPV) were assessed before, during and after the heat exposure. Heat exposure increased heart rate in both groups but this response was less in T2D (5.43 bpm; ~ 7% increase) versus controls (13.96 bpm; ~ 22% increase; p = 0.014). Similarly, reductions in HRV indices to heat stress were generally smaller in magnitude among participants with T2D. For example, high-frequency power (HF RR) decreased by 31.21 ms² (~54.5% reduction) in T2D because of heat exposure, compared with a reduction of 179.35 ms² (~74% reduction) in controls (p = 0.038). Further, LF BRS decreased by 1.07 ms/mmHg (~25% reduction) vs. 3.96 ms/mmHg (~51% reduction) (p = 0.021), HF BRS by 1.58 ms/mmHg (~35% reduction) vs. 4.15 ms/mmHg (~62% reduction) (p = 0.034), and mean BRS by 1.18 ms/mmHg (~26% reduction) vs. 4.16 ms/mmHg (~58% reduction) (p = 0.010) in those with T2D versus controls, respectively. Low-frequency power (LF RR), LF/HF ratio and BPV parameters also showed smaller (though nonsignificant) changes in T2D. Overall, combined T2D and hypertension produced blunted autonomic responses to short-term heat exposure, potentially increasing vulnerability to temperature extremes.

articles.title: Linking academic stress to loneliness, anxiety, and depression: The association of problematic micro-drama use among Chinese university students
articles.abstract: Objective Problematic micro-drama use (PMDU) has received increasing attention as micro-dramas have become widely consumed among young adults in China. This study examined the associations between academic stress and PMDU among Chinese university students, explored which dimensions of academic stress were uniquely associated with PMDU, and examined the associations between PMDU and loneliness, anxiety symptoms, and depressive symptoms. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 510 Chinese university students. Participants completed measures of academic stress, PMDU, loneliness, anxiety symptoms, and depressive symptoms. Multiple linear regression analyses were conducted while controlling for gender and age. The Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure was applied to relevant families of multiple tests. Results Higher academic stress was associated with greater PMDU (β = .447, p < .001). Among the five dimensions of academic stress, learning effectiveness pressure remained significantly associated with PMDU after correction for multiple comparisons (β = .292, FDR-adjusted p < .001), whereas the other dimensions did not show statistically significant unique associations after correction. PMDU was positively associated with loneliness (β = .331), depressive symptoms (β = .323), and anxiety symptoms (β = .305), and all three associations remained significant after FDR correction (all FDR-adjusted p < .001). Conclusions Academic stress, particularly stress related to perceived learning effectiveness, was associated with greater problematic micro-drama use among Chinese university students. Higher PMDU was also associated with greater loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. These findings identify PMDU as a media-use behavior relevant to both academic stress and psychological well-being, although the cross-sectional design does not establish the direction of these associations.

articles.title: Microbial community structure of Penaeus vannamei post-larvae naturally infected with multiple viruses in hatchery tanks
articles.abstract: Background This study offers an observational evaluation of how viral and bacterial infections co-occur with alterations in the microbiome and survival of Penaeus vannamei post-larvae, one of the most economically important species in global aquaculture. Methods Eleven commercial larval production tanks were classified into three distinct infection scenarios using histology and PCR: Baculovirus penaei (BP) monoinfection, mixed infections (BP, white spot syndrome virus [WSSV], and acute hepatopancreatic necrosis disease [AHPND]-causing bacteria), and non-infected controls. High-molecular-weight DNA was subjected to shotgun metagenomic sequencing on the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform, followed by evaluation of microbial diversity, community structure, and infection-associated microbial signatures. Results Although BP was the most abundant viral genus across infected groups, severe mortality was observed only under mixed-infection conditions, which were closely associated with AHPND-causing bacteria presence and microbiome disruption rather than with BP alone. Deep metagenomic sequencing revealed reduced, distinct microbiome structures in shrimp infected with BP and in those with mixed infections, compared to non-infected individuals. Non-infected post-larvae maintained complex and well-balanced bacterial communities, predominantly composed of Donghicola and Muricauda. Nudiviridae and Oscillospiraceae showed comparable relative abundances in BP-only and mixed-infection groups. In contrast, mixed infections were characterized by a relative increase in Vibrio, together with the PCR-detection of PirAB toxin genes, whereas WSSV remained detectable in the metagenomic dataset despite its comparatively low relative abundance, while the infection remained thermally suppressed and asymptomatic in the larvae. Functionally, infected larval microbiomes were enriched for transposases, retrotransposons, and virulence-factor genes. The near-complete BP-GR25 genome (119,245 bp) was assembled and annotated from larval metagenomes. Conclusion These results highlight the value of high-throughput sequencing in the early detection of pathogens in aquaculture, where subtle microbial shifts during postlarval stages can be valuable indicators of health status for production.

articles.title: Paradoxical hepcidin–iron dysregulation in primary sclerosing cholangitis
articles.abstract: Background Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic, progressive liver disease characterised by biliary inflammation. Its exact aetiology remains unclear. This study aimed to use a combination of diagnostic methods and blood analysis to better understand the metabolic changes accompanying PSC. Methods PSC patients (n = 60) and healthy controls (n = 60) were evaluated by magnetic resonance imaging and spectroscopy (hepatic fat and iron content), ultrasonography, standard blood analysis expanded with markers of iron metabolism, and colonoscopy. Results PSC patients exhibited significant liver fibrosis and elevated liver enzymes. Serum hepcidin was increased (p p p p < 0.0001). Conclusion PSC patients demonstrated an atypical pattern of iron metabolism: elevated circulating iron and depleted liver iron stores despite increased hepcidin levels. This paradox suggests a disruption of hepcidin-mediated iron regulation, potentially sustaining a proinflammatory environment. Further investigation is warranted to clarify underlying mechanisms and therapeutic implications. Trial Registration Clinical Trials I.D.: NCT06026449

articles.title: Pathways to the emergence of online group polarization in sports events
articles.abstract: Online group polarization surrounding sports events has emerged as a significant challenge for digital public opinion governance. Drawing on social combustion theory, the study identifies seven explanatory conditions: political triggers, news narrative frames, opinion leaders, capital intervention, first media, event attributes, and stakeholder participation. Using a sample of 24 recent high-profile sporting events, the study employs crisp-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (cs QCA) to investigate the configurational pathways leading to online group polarization and to generate insights for its mitigation. The findings identify five distinct pathways through which online group polarization in sports events emerges, revealing two underlying generative mechanisms. The first is the “sensitive issues–emotional narrative” mechanism, while the second is the “non-sensitive issues–capital involvement” mechanism.

articles.title: Practice-dependent changes in body representation but not in reaching distance following virtual tool-use
articles.abstract: Previous research has shown that tool-use can modify neural representations of our body and the space surrounding us. Furthermore, virtual tools can become incorporated into the user’s body representation after training. However, the extent to which such changes depend on the amount of sensorimotor experience remains unclear. In the present study, we investigated whether different amounts of virtual tool-use training (30, 60, 90 and 120 trials) influence body and action-oriented spatial representations. Participants completed a tactile distance judgment (TDJ) task, indexing body representation; and a reaching distance estimation (RDE) task, indexing perceived actionable space, before and after virtual tool-use training. Virtual tool-use produced an overall decrease in TDJ responses, indicating plastic changes in the forearm tactile distance perception. Although the magnitude of change varied across training conditions, the strongest and most reliable evidence for TDJ change emerged following 120 trials of practice, suggesting that extended sensorimotor experience may be required for stable modifications of body representations. In contrast, RDE changed modestly from pre-test to post-test but did not vary systematically with training duration, suggesting that perceived reaching distance may adapt more rapidly and with less dependence on additional practice. Arm length was a significant predictor of RDE error, indicating that stable anatomical constraints continue to influence reachability judgments despite tool-use experience. Together, these findings suggest a dissociation between body representation and perceived reaching distance, with each exhibiting distinct temporal dynamics following tool-use training. More broadly, the results demonstrate that virtual tool-use can induce changes that transfer to subsequent physical assessment, highlighting virtual environments as a valuable framework for investigating body representation plasticity and tool embodiment.

articles.title: Reduced cognitive empathy and differences in EEG activity in low-achieving adolescents
articles.abstract: Students with low academic achievement tend to display more maladaptive behaviours in interactions with peers and teachers. Empathy plays a key mediating role in these interactions and is also linked to academic performance. In particular, facial emotion recognition is one component of socioemotional processing that may contribute to empathic responding. To explore the relationship between empathy, emotion recognition, and academic achievement, a comparative study was conducted with 40 students aged 14–17, divided into two groups: one with low academic achievement enrolled in a school support programme, and a control group with adequate academic performance. A multimethod approach was applied, including the Basic Empathy Scale, a facial expression recognition test, and electroencephalographic (EEG) recordings. Results showed significantly lower cognitive empathy in the low-achieving group in the primary between-group analysis. The overall between-group difference in facial emotion recognition accuracy was not statistically significant. EEG analyses identified exploratory between-group differences in source-level oscillatory activity estimates during facial-expression processing. These electrophysiological findings provide complementary information about task-related activity patterns but should not be interpreted as specific neural markers of empathy or as confirmation of a behavioural facial emotion recognition deficit. Overall, the multimethod approach offers complementary perspectives on socioemotional functioning in low-achieving adolescents, although the exploratory EEG findings require cautious interpretation and replication in larger, independent samples.

articles.title: Research on strengthening of T-shaped reinforced concrete simply supported beams with U-shaped jackets to enlarge the cross-section: Theoretical analysis, experiments, and finite element analysis
articles.abstract: To promote the reuse of existing beams, an experimental investigation was conducted on T-shaped reinforced concrete (RC) beams strengthened with U-shaped RC jackets. Three specimens were tested: one unstrengthened T-shaped control beam and two strengthened beams. Each jacket comprised additional reinforcing bars and higher-strength concrete cast along both sides of the web and the beam soffit, transforming the original T-shaped cross-section into a rectangular section. All three specimens were subjected to cyclic loading, and corresponding finite element simulations were performed to investigate their hysteretic response, skeleton response, flexural deformation, and failure modes. The strengthened beams exhibited load-carrying capacities more than twice that of the unstrengthened beam, and the finite element simulations generally reproduced the experimental responses. Based on truss–arch synergy, an analytical model was developed to predict the load-carrying capacity of RC beams. The predictions agreed well with the experimental results, supporting the reliability of the proposed model.

articles.title: SIRT5 deficiency exacerbates sepsis acute renal injury by activating ACSL4/FTH1 axis dependent ferroptosis
articles.abstract: Sepsis‑associated acute kidney injury (S‑AKI) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in critically ill patients, yet effective targeted therapies remain lacking due to an incomplete understanding of its pathogenesis. Ferroptosis, an iron‑dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, has recently been implicated in AKI, but the upstream regulators of this process in sepsis remain undefined. Here, we identify SIRT5, a mitochondrial NAD ⁺ ‑dependent desuccinylase, as a critical endogenous suppressor of ferroptosis in S‑AKI. Using a cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) murine model and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)‑stimulated HK‑2 proximal tubular cells, we show that SIRT5 expression is significantly downregulated in septic kidney injury. Renal tubular‑specific ablation of Sirt5 exacerbated CLP‑induced renal dysfunction, structural damage, and tubular cell death, whereas AAV9‑mediated SIRT5 overexpression attenuated these pathological changes. Mechanistically, SIRT5 deficiency tipped the balance of the ACSL4/FTH1 axis toward ferroptosis: it increased ACSL4‑dependent membrane lipid remodeling and reduced FTH1‑mediated iron sequestration, accompanied by suppression of the antioxidant enzyme GPX4. Consequently, lipid peroxidation, iron overload, and mitochondrial damage were markedly amplified. Notably, knockdown of ACSL4 in SIRT5‑deficient HK‑2 cells effectively reversed lipid peroxidation, iron accumulation, and cell death, establishing ACSL4 as a key downstream effector of SIRT5‑mediated ferroptosis suppression. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized SIRT5–ACSL4/FTH1 regulatory axis that governs ferroptotic susceptibility in renal tubular cells during sepsis, and suggest that pharmacological restoration of SIRT5 activity or blockade of ACSL4‑driven ferroptosis may offer novel therapeutic avenues for S‑AKI.

articles.title: Sound and music in video games: A systematic review of player engagement and a meta-analysis of positively valenced player experience
articles.abstract: Video game sound and music have previously been found to influence player engagement and affective responses during gameplay. However, a systematic investigation into the full extent of these effects has not been conducted. This review examined the influence of music and sound on players’ affective responses and engagement during video game play, with a meta-analysis of positively valenced experience (enjoyment, fun or positive affect). Fourteen studies met the inclusion criteria, six of which provided data for the meta-analysis. Game audio was associated with more positively valenced experience than silence (g = 0.48, 95% CI [0.22, 0.74]; small-sample adjusted 95% CI [0.14, 0.82]). Heterogeneity (I² = 58%) was accounted for by one self-selected music condition; without it, the effect was smaller and homogeneous (g = 0.34, 95% CI [0.18, 0.50]; I² = 0%). In exploratory subgroup analyses, sound effects showed a consistent benefit (g = 0.46), whereas the added effect of music over game sound was uncertain (g = 0.31, adjusted 95% CI [−0.07, 0.68]). In the narrative synthesis, music and sound were often associated with higher immersion, flow and motivation. Thirteen of the 14 studies were rated at low risk of bias. Evidence that game audio improves players’ affective experience is promising but preliminary; its effect on engagement has not yet been tested quantitatively, and further research and standardisation of methods are needed.

articles.title: The lived experience of intimate partner violence among first-generation latino immigrants in Southern New Mexico
articles.abstract: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a significant public health concern that disproportionately affects immigrant populations. First-generation Latino immigrants in the United States experience IPV within complex cultural, relational, and structural contexts that remain underexplored. This study aimed to explore and describe how first-generation Latino immigrants in Southern New Mexico experience and make meaning of IPV and to examine the cultural and relational influences shaping these experiences. A qualitative phenomenological design was used, and reporting followed the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) guidelines. Twenty-four first-generation Latino immigrants were interviewed; two who described observing rather than personally experiencing IPV were excluded, yielding an analytic sample of 22 who participated in in-depth, semi-structured interviews conducted in English or Spanish using a trauma-informed and culturally responsive approach. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and translated where necessary. Data was analyzed using thematic analysis informed by phenomenological principles, supported by Intellectus® Qualitative software and manual coding to ensure rigor and depth. Data saturation was reached during data collection. Six major themes emerged: cultural factors, abuse, culture of silence, control, universal factors, and systemic barriers to legal and support resources. Participants described IPV as shaped by cultural norms, normalization of violence, fear, dependency, and limited access to resources. A pervasive culture of silence, reinforced by stigma, immigration-related fears, and social isolation, constrained help-seeking behaviors. Structural barriers further limited access to legal protections and support systems, exacerbating vulnerability. Findings highlight the need for culturally responsive, multilevel interventions that address the social, cultural, and structural determinants of IPV among Latino immigrant populations. Efforts to improve access to support services and reduce systemic barriers are critical to enhancing safety and positive health outcomes.

articles.title: Excitonic Stark Response Induced by Quantum Capacitance in van der Waals Heterostructures
articles.abstract: Precise electrostatic control in van der Waals heterostructures is commonly described by a geometric capacitor model, which assumes that the internal electric field is fully determined by external gate voltages. Here, we show that this description breaks down in the presence of interfacial charge tr…

articles.title: Local Obstructions to Trapped-Region Escape in Modified Gravity
articles.abstract: Energy conditions in modified gravity are commonly imposed on an “effective” stress tensor that mixes physical matter with additional gravitational degrees of freedom, obscuring which sector actually controls null focusing, horizon multiplicity, and the disappearance of trapped regions. We develop a…

articles.title: Biodegradable batteries power technology you can swallow
articles.abstract: Tested in pigs, a new battery design offers a safer, more reliable alternative to standard power sources for ingestible medical devices.

articles.title: A ceasefire in name only: Gaza’s healthcare system still faces catastrophic destruction and shortages
articles.abstract: In April the United Nations, European Union, and World Bank published their Final Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment for Gaza.1 The report estimates that Gaza’s development has been set back by 77 years and that healthcare is one of the worst affected sectors.It is projected to need more than $10bn to rebuild and recover from the Israeli military’s systematic campaign of destruction. Since October 2023, approximately 14% of the healthcare workforce has been killed, died, been detained by Israeli forces, left the profession, or fled.2 However, the notion that Gaza has entered a phase of recovery is inaccurate and dangerous—we are still very much in a state of emergency.The UN report documents the immense barriers to delivering even the most basic medical care that my colleagues at Medical Aid for Palestinians and our partner organisations in Gaza have experienced daily for more than three years. We are witnessing the consequences...

articles.title: Active verification of AI input in articles
articles.abstract: Clark discusses The BMJ’s AI policy.1 I think academic publishing is in a deep crisis. Virtually any neural network can quickly bypass standard quality filters. These models easily adjust text length, mimic flawless academic style, and format bibliographies without errors.The current strategy adopted by publishing houses—relying on superficial declarations—seems ineffective. They simply ask authors to disclose usage—something along the lines of “Yes, I used ChatGPT.”But this rests solely on the honour system. Recent data on publication ethics confirm that such declarations are often futile: they cannot stop covert plagiarism, detect hidden data hallucinations, or verify the actual authorship of an article.234We must move away from the outdated “take our word for it” approach and implement tools for active verification.Cardiology offers an excellent benchmark here. Flagship journals have long maintained a zero tolerance policy regarding the transparency of raw data. Publishing a clinical trial requires the submission of anonymised patient datasets.56...

articles.title: [Correspondence] Super El Niño threatens a public health emergency in Africa
articles.abstract: Africa stands on the cusp of an El Niño-driven public health emergency, superimposed on an increasingly unpredictable and extreme climate. The projected toll of heat-related deaths in Africa in the coming months will dwarf that in the northern hemisphere during the summer of 2026.1,2 Equally concerning are heightened risks for floods in the Greater Horn and Central Africa, droughts in southern Africa, and rainfall anomalies across the Sahel.3,4 Compounding hazards converge around water insecurity, wildfires, infectious disease outbreaks, and disrupted health care.

articles.title: Behavioral diversity knowledge shortfall in biodiversity conservation
articles.abstract: Behavior is a critical but underexplored component of biodiversity, often overlooked in conservation science, ecological restoration, and biodiversity management. We argue that behavioral diversity needs to be formally recognized as a distinct facet of biodiversity, given its critical value as a reservoir of adaptive potential, and that current gaps in knowledge should be acknowledged as what we formally define to be a behavioral diversity knowledge shortfall. Present knowledge shortfalls need to be confronted by establishing standardized behavioral diversity indicators, harnessing recent technological developments and large databases, building capacity, promoting interdisciplinary collaboration, and setting research priorities. Recognizing and reducing the behavioral diversity knowledge shortfall will help better explain existing biodiversity patterns and improve the outcomes of conservation actions.

articles.title: A Cell-Autonomous Cold Sensor Promotes Lipolysis Through Phase Separation
articles.abstract: Temperature is a fundamental determinant of mammalian metabolism. The canonical cold-adaptation pathway involves cold sensing by peripheral sensory neurons, which activate sympathetic outflow, {beta}-adrenergic signaling, and lipolysis in adipose tissue. In contrast, we report here a cell-intrinsic mechanism by which physiologically relevant cooling temperatures (27-31 oC) enhance lipolysis in subcutaneous adipose tissue. Mechanistically, cooling drives liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) of perilipin 1 (PLIN1), the dominant lipid droplet coat protein, promoting its condensation and the local recruitment of PKA to the droplet surface. This spatial reorganization selectively amplified PKA-mediated perilipin 1 phosphorylation, CGI-58 release, and ATGL-dependent lipolysis. The process depends on the intrinsically disordered region (IDR) of perilipin1, where four aromatic residues, conserved in endotherms but not in ectotherms, are required for cooling-induced LLPS and lipolysis in vivo. Notably, targeted delivery of an LLPS-competent perilipin 1 variant to the inguinal adipose tissue of mice enhanced local lipolysis and reduced depot mass. Together, these findings uncover a cell-intrinsic thermosensitive mechanism that can tune lipolytic responsiveness, offering a possible strategy for targeted depot-selective fat reduction.

articles.title: A canonical input to the head direction compass carries predominantly eye movement signals
articles.abstract: The mammalian head direction (HD) system is thought to update its internal compass using angular head velocity (AHV) signals relayed from the brainstem. We tested this canonical interpretation by recording from the nucleus prepositus hypoglossi (NPH), a proposed AHV relay known to be important for accurate HD tracking, while simultaneously measuring eye and head movements in mice. Neurons classified as AHV-tuned instead predominantly encoded eye movements: most showed saccade-related bursts or pauses, and apparent AHV tuning was largely explained by eye rather than head motion. Optotagging showed that even NPH neurons projecting directly to the HD circuit predominantly encoded eye movements. Empirically constrained population models reconstructed eye position and gaze direction, but head-direction readouts failed when eye and head motion were dissociated. These findings overturn the canonical view of NPH as a dedicated AHV relay, revealing eye movements as a major, previously unmeasured component of the signals entering the mammalian HD circuit and thereby changing the computational problem that the HD system must solve to maintain a stable representation of heading.

articles.title: A direct RPA-Polθ interaction licenses theta-mediated end joining
articles.abstract: DNA double-strand break repair often involves end resection, yet how resected ends are directed toward distinct repair pathways remains poorly understood. Here, we identify replication protein A (RPA) as an unexpected essential factor for cellular polymerase theta-mediated end joining (TMEJ). Using MUSIC-MAP, a newly developed platform linking endogenous sequence variants to DNA repair outcomes, we map a discrete functional interface between RPA2 and polymerase theta (Polθ). Disrupting this interface in RPA2 abolishes TMEJ without impairing cell viability or homologous recombination. Mutations in the complementary Polθ surface likewise impair TMEJ, whereas reciprocal charge-reversal mutations in RPA2 and Polθ restore TMEJ, providing genetic evidence for a direct physical interaction. Structural modeling suggests that the Polθ-binding surface becomes accessible at RPA-coated ssDNA termini, positioning RPA as a docking platform for Polθ engagement. These findings reveal how RPA, previously considered a barrier to TMEJ, instead functions as a molecular platform that translates the organization of ssDNA into selective enzyme engagement, enabling mutagenic repair without compromising homologous recombination. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Dutch Cancer Society, https://ror.org/0368jnd28, 2021-2/13905, 2024-3/16583

articles.title: A minimal model of a forest after neutral theory
articles.abstract: Community ecology seeks the mechanisms underlying biodiversity, and simplified models can reveal them. Neutral ecology exemplifies this approach, but it doesn't distinguish species, limiting its capability for forecasting and prediction. We address this by developing a predictive, minimal model for forest dynamics. We show in a neotropical forest plot that environmental variation couples to the community as a single common effect on all species' growth rates. Life history acts on that variation, forecasting species' gains and losses a decade ahead. Finally, immigration, coupled to competition and life history, allows us to predict long-run species abundances. Simple rules thus govern the dynamics of this forest: competition, immigration, and the effect of the environment on growth. Beyond that, species are set apart by their life histories alone.

articles.title: A pump-leak model of epithelia reveals the roles of paracellular pathways in water transport & the importance of boundary conditions
articles.abstract: We develop a pump-leak model of epithelial transport, where the flux of water through the epithelium is modeled as a compartment, or sink, whose volume grows linearly with time. A method is described for calculating the voltage in the sink compartment, as well as analytical solutions to the system of equations. We show how growing boundary conditions can be used to model a scenario where water and ion fluxes are possible in the steady state. It is possible to drive a continuous flux of water through an epithelium that is powered by the Na+ pump establishing small osmotic gradients between compartments. We show that paracellular pathways play a crucial role in the operation of epithelial transport by ensuring that the flux through the epithelium is electroneutral. For the Na+ pump situated on the basolateral membrane, water fluxes can be directed in the same direction as the Na+ ion by having a high Na+ conductance on the apical membrane and high K+ conductance on the basolateral membrane. Flipping these conductances changes the direction of water fluxes. We introduce a graphic formalism that makes clear the precise mechanism of water transfer, showing the osmotic and electrical constraints. We demonstrate that it is possible when the extracellular osmolarity is low (~10mOsm) for the intracellular osmolarity to exceed that of the former considerably and produce a hyperosmolar solution.

articles.title: A vagal-to-sympathetic reflex controls lung vascular leak
articles.abstract: Dynamic regulation of the vascular barrier is required for an effective inflammatory response, allowing delivery of plasma proteins and immune cells to sites of insult. Although normally protective, sustained leak becomes costly in organs like the lung, where swelling stiffens tissue and impairs breathing, yet many upstream regulators remain unidentified. Using a chemogenetic screen of vagal afferent subtypes, we identify a neural reflex that drives lung vascular leak. The reflex originates in an orphan population of neurons expressing Cysltr2 that innervates alveolar capillary beds and senses both mechanical and inflammatory stimuli, fitting classic definitions of pulmonary 'J' receptors, an afferent subtype described anatomically since the 1950s whose function has remained speculative. Activating CYSLTR2 neurons increases lung vascular leak within minutes and causes perivascular edema and respiratory dysfunction, whereas silencing them during inhaled allergen challenge reduces leak and improves lung mechanics. Rather than acting locally through antidromic peptide release, this reflex engages brainstem relays and sympathetic efferents to broadcast its effects throughout lung vasculature. Vagal control of the vascular barrier thus forms an axis of organ defense that can go awry in disease, revealing new ways to regulate organ fluid balance upstream of the endothelium

articles.title: Additive and dominance gene effects described by a logistic function in concentration-limited metabolic pathways at steady state out of equilibrium
articles.abstract: Additive (a) and dominance (d) gene effects are key to phenotype manifestation. We investigated the relationship between these effects and gene-encoded enzyme rates in an n-step linear metabolic pathway with mass limitation at stationary state out of equilibrium, where internal flux depended on internal enzyme concentrations (Ei, i=1 to n) and external flux on input/output enzyme/transporter concentrations (Ee). Using coupled reversible Michaelis-Menten (MM) equations for Ei rates and irreverisble MM for Ee rates we found that stationary-state metabolite concentration (Si) was a logistic function of Ei. Its inflection point (S0i, E0i) depended on the total mass of the system ({Sigma} Si) and on Ee saturation, shifting from negative to positive values as reaction kinetics transitioned from first to mixed or zero order. Moreover, {Sigma} Si and Ee saturation explained negative, partial, and complete dominance in this metabolic system, provided phenotypic value of trait T is linearly dependent on Si at certain sink. The system was unstable when approaching closure (Ee=0). In this condition, asymptotic Smax equaled equilibrium concentration, being equilibrium displacement the driving force of flux. In pathways with n>1 reaction steps there was a change of regime in early reactions when increments in En passed E0n. This change of regime led to peaks raising at some Si previous to Sn and Sn+1 that were modeled by adding a Gaussian component to the logistic equation. Therefore, if T is determined by some of these Si, overdominance and dominance reversals may be explained. We obtained a good fit when applied this equation to Ei and Si data obtained from silicon-cell models developed with specific kinetic equations and experimentally determined kinetic parameters. In addition, we applied this framework to experimental data on amylose accumulation in starch granules catalyzed by granule-bound starch synthase I, and found that the logistic function fitted data from six plant species. This framework may contribute a partial explanation of the non-linearity between genotype and phenotype from the metabolic standpoint, which may be useful in the future for plant or animal breeding technologies.

articles.title: An ITK - SLP-76 Y173 Axis Regulates TCR Signal Persistence and Thymic Development
articles.abstract: The TCR-induced tyrosine kinase cascade results in ITK-mediated phosphorylation of at least two substrates: PLC-{gamma}1 Y783, an essential mediator of TCR signaling, and SLP-76 Y173. We previously provided evidence that SLP-76 Y173 supports proximal TCR and Fc{varepsilon}RI signaling; but its role in thymocyte development was never explored. Here we demonstrate that SLP-76 Y173 was required for TCR/CD28-induced degradation of I{kappa}B; moreover, both ITK and SLP-76 Y173 were required for persistent TCR-induced phosphorylation of PLC-{gamma}1, ERK and p38. To explore whether SLP-76 Y173 may mediate ITK-dependent events in vivo, we replaced SLP 76 Y173 with phenylalanine in a mouse model. Like ITK-deficient thymocytes, SLP-76 Y173F thymocytes exhibited reduced thymic cellularity, reduced CD4/CD8 ratios, and reduced surface expression of CD5. In ex vivo-stimulated thymocytes, mutation of SLP-76 Y173 or inhibition of ITK reduced the persistence of TCR-induced calcium flux; moreover, TCR-induced phosphorylation of ERK and p38 depended on SLP-76 Y173. Like ITK-deficient thymi, SLP-76 Y173F thymocytes exhibited decreased production of CD4- iNKT1 thymocytes, coupled with increased production of innate-like CD4+ and CD8+ SP thymocytes. Our results provide strong evidence that the ITK substrate site, SLP-76 Y173, promotes TCR signal persistence that is required to mediate the thymic developmental effects of ITK.

articles.title: An improved CRISPR-LICHT screen of 120 Tdark genes illuminates new biologically relevant SOX2 targets in human brain organoids
articles.abstract: SOX2 is a transcription factor and central regulator of neural progenitor identity, yet the downstream molecular networks through which it supports human brain development remain incompletely characterized. Here, we applied CRISPR-lineage tracing at cellular resolution in heterogeneous tissue (CRISPR-LICHT) to human cerebral organoids to functionally interrogate SOX2-dependent regulatory networks. Using a SOX2-focused library targeting SOX2 together with conserved neurodevelopmental regulators expressed in neural progenitor cells, we showed that CRISPR-LICHT detects reproducible lineage- depletion phenotypes across genes already known to be involved in progenitor maintenance, fate specification, glial differentiation and neuronal maturation. This extends the application of CRISPR-LICHT beyond the severe neural progenitor phenotypes previously characterized for microcephaly-associated genes and demonstrates its ability to detect perturbation effects across a broader set of neurodevelopmental regulators, involving SOX2 targets previously defined in mouse and now open to further understanding in a human model setting. We further screened 120 evolutionarily conserved, poorly characterized SOX2-dependent genes classified as Tdark within the Illuminating the Druggable Genome framework and identified 28 candidate hits whose disruption impaired neural progenitor lineage expansion and/or survival. These candidates included proteins associated with cytoskeletal organization, membrane dynamics and intracellular architecture, suggesting that SOX2-dependent developmental programmes may engage cellular processes beyond transcriptional regulation. Individual downregulation of CDC42EP4, a poorly characterized CDC42 effector linked to cytoskeletal organization, revealed altered distribution of targeted progenitors between ventricular- and subventricular- like compartments, with changes consistent with altered progenitor-state progression. Together, these findings expand the functional landscape of SOX2-dependent regulation in human neural progenitors and identify cellular architecture as a potential component of SOX2-associated developmental programs.

articles.title: Asking the Data: Conversational Interrogation of LC-MS/MS Proteomics Data Sets with an LLM Agent
articles.abstract: Proteomics workflows are designed to answer predefined questions, leaving analytical problems that emerge after first results difficult to investigate without additional bioinformatics work. We introduce data set interrogation, a conversational framework in which a researcher uses a large language model (LLM) agent to translate emerging questions into executable tests, check the answers against controls, and keep the code, inputs, and decisions in a dated record. Applied retrospectively to four LC–MS/MS data sets, the framework exposed problems that changed the interpretation of three in-house studies: a search database lacking one of two symbionts, a swapped pair of tandem mass tag (TMT) channels, statistics inflated by non-host proteins, and false deamidation assignments caused by selection of the 13 C isotope peak as monoisotopic; the same question asked of every data set revealed failed or partial cysteine alkylation in all three. A public TMT data set was reanalyzed from raw files in 24 min, a feasibility measure without a human comparison; among spectra identified by both workflows, 99.2% received the same peptide assignment as in Proteome Discoverer, and protein fold changes correlated (r = 0.93). In seeded tests, a purpose built channel assignment check detected all 216 between strain channel swaps and none of 90 within-strain swaps. The framework couples natural language interaction with executable analyses, explicit controls, and traceable decisions, enabling researchers to investigate questions not anticipated by the original pipeline. These results establish feasibility in a limited retrospective setting with one researcher; broader evaluation across users, models, and data sets is required to determine general performance.

articles.title: Astatine-211 injury induces an immunostimulatory melanoma-cell state and promotes systemic antitumor immunity
articles.abstract: Targeted alpha therapy is generally evaluated by absorbed dose and direct tumor-cell killing, but whether alpha-particle-injured tumor cells can induce systemic antitumor immunity remains poorly defined. We investigated the immunogenic consequences of astatine-211 (211At) injury in a prophylactic melanoma vaccination-challenge model. B16F10 cells were exposed ex vivo to 211At, etoposide, or ultraviolet irradiation under conditions that reduced viable-cell counts at 24 hours to approximately 40% of untreated controls. Injured cells were administered subcutaneously to syngeneic C57BL/6J mice before intravenous challenge with viable B16F10 cells. Vaccination with cells exposed to 1 MBq/mL 211At suppressed pulmonary metastasis, reduced regulatory T-cell proportions, and elicited tumor-reactive interferon-{gamma} responses and antibodies. Transcriptomic profiling revealed enrichment of type I interferon, inflammatory, and chemokine-related signatures, together with suppression of cell-cycle, translation, and metabolic programs. At the cellular level, 211At injury was accompanied by {gamma}H2AX accumulation, G2/M arrest, increased reactive oxygen species and cytosolic double-stranded DNA, and senescence-like changes. These features arose without consistent increases in classical damage-associated molecular patterns or prominent induction of senescence-associated secretory phenotype factors at 1 MBq/mL. In vivo pharmacologic inhibition of stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling attenuated the antimetastatic effect of vaccination. Together, these findings demonstrate that 211At injury can generate an immunostimulatory tumor-cell state characterized by DNA damage and altered inflammatory signaling. STING contributes to the resulting immune protection, highlighting immunogenic tumor-cell conversion as a consideration in the design of targeted alpha therapies.

articles.title: Auditory tracking magnitude, temporal alignment, and anatomical distribution during wakefulness and propofol-based anesthesia in human sEEG
articles.abstract: General anesthesia attenuates auditory responses, but response magnitude alone does not describe how residual activity aligns with sound over time or varies across the brain. We jointly characterized these aspects of auditory tracking using stereoelectroencephalography (sEEG) in 13 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy during wakefulness and clinically defined unresponsiveness under propofol-based anesthesia. The same rhythmic humming sequences were presented at approximately 1.61 Hz in both sessions. During anesthesia, stimulus-rate power showed widespread reductions and phase alignment with the stimulus rhythm was less consistent, although responses remained detectable at some recording channels. During wakefulness, response strength decreased with cortical surface distance from posteromedial Heschl's gyrus; this distance-response relationship was weaker during anesthesia. In a contrastive learning analysis (CEBRA), low-dimensional embeddings derived from anesthesia recordings yielded lower acoustic-envelope decoding accuracy on held-out data and lower consistency across model fits. Together, these findings characterize how attenuated auditory tracking is expressed jointly in response magnitude, temporal alignment, and anatomical distribution.

articles.title: Autonomous sampling and eDNA metabarcoding for offshore biodiversity monitoring: a pilot study around an FPSO in the Southwestern Atlantic
