The recurrent CBP–ID4 variant R1868W activated the formation of low-mobility aberrant nuclear condensates, whereas the C–terminal, truncating variant C1723fs, impaired condensate formation and showed diffuse nuclear localization. Treatment with the selective p300/CBP HAT inhibitor A485 partially restored condensate dynamics and fusion-relaxation behavior in R1868W. Furthermore, R1868W recruited BRD4 around condensates in an acetylation-dependent manner, which was suppressed by the BET inhibitor JQ1. Together, these findings suggest that aberrant condensate material properties arising from disrupted CREBBP IDR-dependent regulation play a critical role in the molecular pathogenesis of MKHK.

articles.title: Clinical Significance and Distribution of Cerebrospinal Fluid Type IV Oligoclonal Band Pattern in Neurological Disorders: A Retrospective Analysis
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: To characterize the clinical features and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings of patients exhibiting a type IV oligoclonal band (OCB) pattern, defined by the presence of identical IgG bands in both CSF and serum. Methods: This retrospective observational study included all consecutive adult patients with a type IV pattern detected during routine CSF analysis at Geneva University Hospitals in 2023. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were collected through chart review. Results: A total of 178 patients were included. The mean age was 60.2 years (SD 16.5), and 51.7% were female. The type IV pattern was most frequently observed in non-inflammatory neurological diseases (NIND) (n=103, 57.9%). Other inflammatory neurological diseases accounted for 37 cases (20.7%), multiple sclerosis was identified in 8 patients (4.5%), and peripheral nervous system disorders were present in 20 patients (11.2%). Systemic inflammatory comorbidities were observed in 40 patients (22.5%). An elevated albumin quotient was present in 73 patients (41%) and was most common among those with CNS infections, aseptic meningitis, CNS neoplastic diseases, and peripheral nervous system disorder. Repeated CSF analyses demonstrated temporal fluctuations in the type IV pattern in some patients, without corresponding changes in diagnosis. Discussion: The type IV pattern is predominantly associated with NIND and is relatively uncommon in multiple sclerosis. Although it may reflect systemic immune activation and/or blood brain barrier dysfunction in certain inflammatory conditions, its clinical significance remains nonspecific. These findings support cautious interpretation of the type IV pattern in routine clinical practice.

articles.title: Comparing the Phenotypic and Genetic Differences Between Autistic Regression and Autism Without Regression Using the SPARK Cohort
articles.abstract: The biology of autistic regression (Autreg) remains poorly understood. We investigated Autreg's phenotypic and genetic landscape in 51 633 individuals from the SPARK cohort. We calculated the frequencies of parental-reported language regression and regression affecting social, play, toileting, and/or other developmental domains, and ages at skill regression and regain within SPARK. We compared developmental milestones, quantitative developmental measures, and selected other phenotypes in Autreg and autism without regression (Autnreg). Rare damaging coding variants and polygenic scores (PGS) in Autreg and Autnreg were compared using genome sequencing data. Rare variants were analyzed using the Transmission And De novo Association (TADA) framework in 1 107 Autreg and 974 Autnreg individuals, followed by pathway enrichment analysis. PGS for autism, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, epilepsy, and schizophrenia were initially compared. PGS validation was conducted in 14 001 Autnreg and 11 638 Autreg individuals using larger SPARK genotyping data. We identified regression in 43% of autistic individuals. Other regression occurred later than language regression, and 60% of skill regain occurred within two years. Autreg was associated with lower Vineland-3 Adaptive Behavior Composite scores (p<0.001) and >twofold increased odds of epilepsy and intellectual disability (p<0.001). Developmental milestones and quantitative measures had modest differences. TADA analysis highlighted genes involved in nucleotide catabolism, transcription, and focal adhesion, with PTEN emerging as a strong candidate for Autreg. Schizophrenia PGS explained 0.087% of variance in liability to regression among autistic individuals. In conclusion, Autreg was associated with increased neurodevelopmental morbidity. Schizophrenia PGS and rare variants explained a minimal fraction of its etiology.

articles.title: Cross-Sectional Study of Periodontal Oral Dental Foci of Infection (PODFI) in Medically Compromised Patients at Lille University Hospital
articles.abstract: Oral dental foci of infection (ODFI), particularly those of periodontal origin, can trigger systemic inflammatory responses that may cause bacteraemia for medically compromised patients. Although guidelines recommend detection and elimination of these foci, precise data on the distribution of periodontal oral dental foci of infection (PODFI) risk within these populations remain scarce. This study aimed to describe periodontal sources of infection in medically compromised patients using a periodontal examination and follow-up form and a recently developed PODFI risk levels classification. This observational, retrospective, cross-sectional, single-center study evaluated medically compromised patients with periodontitis in the dental surgery department of the Lille University Hospital between September 2024 and September 2025. Periodontitis was diagnosed according to the 2017 Classification of Periodontal Diseases established at the 2017 World Workshop. The primary outcome was the distribution of PODFI risk levels (moderate, high, very high). Secondary outcomes aimed to describe periodontal conditions in a specific population of medically compromised patients. Thirty-nine patients were included in this study. Evaluation of PODFI risk (n = 34) revealed a predominance of moderate-risk profiles (67.6 %) and a significant proportion of high-risk profiles (32.4 %); no low-risk or very high-risk profiles were observed. Generalized periodontal inflammation was very common (92 %), with a median of 26 bleeding on probing (BOP) sites and 71 plaque-positive sites, showing a positive correlation (R = 0.52, p = 0.002). Severe and active forms of periodontitis predominated (n = 39), with 74.4 % of cases classified as stage III (28.2 %) or stage IV (46.2 %), and grade B was the most common (56.4 %), followed by grade C (38.5 %) (p = 0.025). Medically compromised patients have a high prevalence of severe and active periodontitis, with nearly one-third of them classified as being at high risk for infection. The recently developed periodontal oral dental foci of infection (PODFI) classification provides a structured and clinically relevant tool for stratifying infection risk and guiding treatment decisions. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to confirm the validity of these PODFI risk levels.

articles.title: Educational expectations and needs of individuals scheduled for breast surgery within the Primary Nursing Model: a qualitative study
articles.abstract: Background. A diagnosis of breast cancer may represent a potentially destabilizing event, with significant physical, psychological, and social implications. Individuals scheduled for breast surgery require clear, understandable, and personalized information to prepare for surgery and manage the postoperative period. However, a discrepancy may arise between perceived informational needs and the information actually received. The Primary Nursing model, based on continuity of care and the presence of a designated primary nurse, may promote greater personalization of nurse-led patient education. Aim. To explore the experiences of individuals scheduled for breast surgery in relation to the nurse-led patient education received throughout the perioperative pathway, in order to understand their educational expectations, informational needs, and perceptions of the usefulness of the educational interventions provided within the Primary Nursing model. Design. A qualitative study with a phenomenological orientation. Methods. The study will be conducted at the European Institute of Oncology. Participants will be recruited through convenience sampling among individuals diagnosed with breast cancer who have undergone surgery and received the nurse-led discharge education routinely provided. Approximately 20 participants are expected to be enrolled; the final sample size will be determined according to the principle of data saturation. Data will be collected through semi-structured interviews conducted approximately two weeks after discharge by a member of the research team who is not involved in the participants Clinical care. The interviews, lasting approximately 30-40 minutes, will be audio-recorded with prior consent, transcribed verbatim, and assigned a sequential identification code. Sociodemographic data and clinical information extracted from the medical records will also be collected. The transcripts will be analyzed using thematic analysis according to Braun and Clarke, with a phenomenological orientation. Expected contribution. The study may contribute to understanding potential discrepancies between educational expectations, informational needs, and the perceived usefulness of the information received, thereby informing clinical practice toward personalized educational interventions consistent with continuity of care.

articles.title: Familial factors inflate the estimated effects of genetic liability to ADHD on behavioural outcomes
articles.abstract: Background: People with ADHD have worse health, behavioural and social outcomes, widely interpreted as evidence that ADHD causes these harms, justifying early identification and treatment. But ADHD clusters in families, and conventional studies cannot separate the effect of a person's own ADHD from the family environment in which it arises. We used a family-based genetic design to distinguish the two. Methods: We used up to 22 genome-wide significant variants associated with ADHD (38,691 cases, 186,843 controls) to estimate effects of genetic liability to ADHD on 16 health and behavioural outcomes. We compared population-based estimates with family-based estimates from within-sibship analyses of up to 164,220 siblings. We tested for heterogeneity between the designs, and applied sensitivity analyses. We involved individuals with lived experience of ADHD in interpreting the findings and shaping how the clinical/public-health implications were described. Findings: Population-based analyses implied that greater genetic liability to ADHD increased smoking, alcohol use and depressive symptoms, and reduced educational attainment, age at first child and cognitive performance. In family-based analyses, these effects attenuated. For example, the effect on number of depressive symptoms fell from 0.059 SD (95% CI 0.039, 0.080) to 0.002 SD (-0.052, 0.055), and age at first child increased from -0.045 SD (-0.058, -0.033) to 0.003 SD (-0.040, 0.047), with significant differences between designs (p=0.048 and p=0.034). Findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses. Interpretation: Much of the excess health and behavioural burden attributed to ADHD may reflect the family and environmental context in which ADHD occurs, rather than an individual's own ADHD. Interventions targeting the individual might not reduce these outcomes as much as expected. Distinguishing such effects requires family-based designs. Funding: Medical Research Council, UK Research and Innovation, Research Council of Norway, US National Institute of Mental Health, and Australian National Health and Medical Research Council.

articles.title: From non-uptake during early adolescence to acceptance during a catch-up campaign: a qualitative study of changing HPV vaccination decisions across two life stages among young women in Amsterdam, the Netherlands
articles.abstract: Background: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination effectively prevents HPV-related disease, but its population-level impact depends on sufficient coverage. In 2023-2024, the Netherlands offered free HPV vaccination to individuals aged 19-27 years through a national catch-up campaign. For women, this was a second opportunity, as they had been offered vaccination at ages 9-13 through the National Immunisation Programme (NIP). Back then, uptake was relatively low (46-57% in these birth cohorts), but uptake increased to 55-63% following the catch-up vaccination. This campaign provided an apt opportunity to explore the factors underlying previous and current HPV vaccination decisions among the same women across two life stages. Methods: Between May 2023 and May 2024, 16 semi-structured interviews were conducted in Amsterdam with women who accepted HPV vaccination during the catch-up after non-uptake during early adolescence. Interviews explored factors influencing non-uptake and later acceptance, guided by the Health Belief Model and additional sociocultural constructs. Data were analysed using thematic analysis with open and theory-guided coding in MAXQDA. Results: Non-uptake during early adolescence was primarily shaped by parental decision-making, cultural and religious norms, fear of side effects, low perceived susceptibility to HPV and limited self-efficacy. Acceptance in young adulthood was driven by greater autonomy, higher perceived susceptibility, increased trust in accumulated vaccine evidence and accessible vaccination infrastructure. Peer influence replaced parental influence as the dominant social factor. Conclusion: HPV vaccine decision-making is a dynamic process rather than fixed. Permanent catch-up HPV vaccination opportunities would enable young adults to make autonomous vaccination decisions as their circumstances change.

articles.title: Stage-dependent associations of Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome with Cognitive Decline, Depression, and Neuroimaging Signatures in multi-regional older adults
articles.abstract: Background Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic (CKM) syndrome is a multisystem condition associated with adverse outcomes, yet its impact on age-related cognitive health remains understudied. We examined associations of CKM with neurocognitive and neuropsychiatric outcomes, modifiable physical and psychosocial factors contributing to cognitive impairment across CKM stages, and neuroimaging correlates. Methods Global aging cohorts (mean follow-up 6.5 years) and the Cohort Studies of Memory in an International Consortium (5.4 years) were used. CKM stages (0-4) were defined according to AHA framework. Longitudinal domain-specific cognitive changes were assessed using linear mixed-effects models, and depressive symptoms using generalized linear regression with individual participant data approach. Population-attributable fractions were estimated for six modifiable factors associated with cognitive impairment across CKM stages. Cross-sectional associations with 34 neuroimaging biomarkers were examined in UK Biobank. Results Among 28,242 participants, advanced CKM stages (3-4) were associated with accelerated cognitive decline, particularly in attention, executive function, and language. Associations were stronger in younger individuals, men, and those with less education, but not modified by APOE 4 status. Advanced CKM stages were associated with depressive symptoms among cognitively unimpaired individuals. Modifiable factors accounted for 24.8% of cognitive impairment risk across CKM stages, mainly social isolation (7.0%), depressive symptoms (5.2%), and physical inactivity (5.2%). Advanced CKM stages were linked to widespread MRI alterations (27 biomarkers), especially white matter hyperintensity. Conclusion Advanced CKM stages are associated with accelerated cognitive decline and greater cerebrovascular burden. Addressing psychosocial factors and physical inactivity, alongside management of CKM risk factors, may help reduce cognitive impairment.

articles.title: Statistical Analysis Plan for the REDEP study: Effectiveness of dual-mobility cups for preventing dislocation after primary total hip arthroplasty by a posterolateral approach compared to unipolar cups in elderly patients
articles.abstract: Periprosthetic hip dislocation is a frequent complication after primary total hip arthroplasty. Observational studies suggest that dual mobility cups may reduce dislocation risk to approximately 1%, but definitive randomized evidence supporting their routine use in primary total hip arthroplasty is absent. The REDEP trial is the first prospective, randomized controlled trial that compares dual mobility cups with unipolar cups in patients [≥]70 years who electively undergo primary total hip arthroplasty via a posterolateral approach. The primary objective of the trial is to determine the difference in the number of patients who suffer a periprosthetic dislocation of the hip within 1 year after primary total hip arthroplasty in this population. Other outcomes include the difference in the total number of hip dislocations (including recurrent dislocations within patients), differences in patient-reported outcome measures, and differences in the incidence of (serious) adverse events. This statistical analysis plan describes the primary statistical analysis for the REDEP study. The analyses described herein were defined prior to database lock and unblinding. Secondary analyses will be described in subsequent versions of this statistical analysis plan.

articles.title: Favorable Carrier Dynamics in a Narrow-Gap Layered Oxynitride Enable Efficient Molecular Hybrid CO2 Photoreduction
articles.abstract: Efficient interfacial electron transfer from light-harvesting semiconductors to molecular catalysts remains a major challenge in molecular–semiconductor hybrid photocatalytic CO2 reduction, particularly for narrow-bandgap semiconductors, whose reduced thermodynamic driving force often requires assistance from metallic electron-transfer mediators such as Ag. Here, we show that, despite its narrow bandgap of 2.1 eV, the layered perovskite oxynitride K2LaTa2O6N (KLTON) functions as an effective semiconductor support for a supramolecular RuRu′ CO2-reduction catalyst without relying on Ag nanoparticles. The RuRu′/KLTON hybrid selectively converted CO2 to formate under visible-light irradiation with >99% selectivity, a turnover number of 691, and an apparent quantum yield of 6.1 ± 0.6% at 420 nm. Loading a small amount of Ag further increased the turnover number to 1077, but this 1.5-fold enhancement was modest compared with the larger Ag-induced activity enhancements reported for several conventional oxynitride-based hybrids, highlighting the weak Ag dependence of the KLTON-based system. Spatial photodeposition of Ag and MnOx revealed spatially differentiated surface redox reactivity on the terraced layered structure of KLTON, while time-resolved microwave conductivity and transient infrared absorption measurements showed favorable photogenerated-carrier dynamics and demonstrated that Ag loading modifies the electron dynamics of KLTON. Time-resolved emission measurements further revealed an additional nonradiative decay pathway at the Ru(II) photosensitizer/KLTON interface, consistent with interfacial electronic interaction without uniquely assigning its microscopic origin. These results identify favorable carrier dynamics and weak Ag dependence as key features of the KLTON-based molecular hybrid and highlight layered narrow-bandgap mixed-anion semiconductors as promising support materials for visible-light-driven molecular photocatalysis.

articles.title: Kinetic Limitations of Single-Atom Catalysts in Hydrazine Oxidation
articles.abstract: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) have attracted considerable interest, displaying impressive performance for a wide plethora of electrocatalytic reactions. However, the important question whether isolated sites are always beneficial remains unresolved. Here, by using the hydrazine oxidation reaction (HzOR) as a model reaction, we examine how isolated single-atom metal sites restrict the adsorption mode of intermediates to the monodentate configuration, which leads to weak intermediate stabilization and poor reaction kinetics. This contrasts with bulk metal sites where availability of the bidentate adsorption configuration offers better intermediate stabilization and dehydrogenation kinetics. As a result, Ir, Pt, and Pd SACs were found to require high HzOR overpotentials of 0.90, 1.21, and 1.19 V at 3 mA cm–2, respectively. Comparatively, their Ir, Pt, Pd nanoparticle counterparts with similar metal loading exhibit considerably lower overpotentials of only 0.35, 0.83, and 0.64 V at 3 mA cm–2, respectively. Taken together, our work contributes towards a more complete understanding of SACs, emphasizing the importance of considering site structure and the mechanistic demands of the reaction.

articles.title: Mechanism-Driven Size Optimization of Fully Exposed Rh Cluster Catalysts for Butane Dehydrogenation
articles.abstract: Nonoxidative butane dehydrogenation offers a direct route to C4 olefins, yet it remains challenged by the need to promote C–H activation while ensuring olefin desorption and suppressing C–C cracking. Here, we report a mechanism-guided study that combines density functional theory calculations with experimental validation to rationally design Rh-based catalysts for butane dehydrogenation. A series of Rh models with distinct geometric configurations on a graphene surface, including isolated Rh atom, fully exposed Rh2 and Rh3 clusters, and extended Rh surfaces, were constructed to elucidate the structure–activity relationship. The calculations reveal a volcano-type dependence of dehydrogenation activity on the Rh geometric configuration. Fully exposed Rh3 clusters exhibit optimal energetics for sequential C–H activation, whereas isolated Rh atoms and Rh nanoparticles show inferior activity. Experimental studies on Rh/nanodiamond@graphene catalysts confirm the prediction, demonstrating that fully exposed Rh clusters with an average Rh–Rh coordination number of approximately 1.9 achieve the best balance between C–H activation, olefin desorption, and C–C bond cleavage suppression. This study highlights highly efficient Rh active sites by regulating the geometric configuration and electronic property and provides a general strategy for designing dehydrogenation catalysts.

articles.title: Multiplexed Ultrahigh-Throughput Evolution for Esterase Selectivity across a Broad Substrate Scope
articles.abstract: Directed evolution of enzymes is generally performed toward a specific substrate, which predictably improves enzyme activity toward the probe substrate. However, it is difficult to predict whether evolved enzymes will be selective or promiscuous toward other substrates. Multiplexed directed evolution can identify enzyme variants with selectivity/promiscuity across multiple substrates, but is typically performed using plate-based screening assays that are limited to testing a few hundred mutants. Combining substrate multiplexing with ultrahigh-throughput evolution technologies is a promising avenue for deeper exploration of the mutational landscape, but it has not been investigated whether enzymes evolved using multiplexed ultrahigh-throughput methods exhibit selectivity/promiscuity toward a broader scope of small-molecule substrates beyond the probes used during evolution. Here, we performed multiplexed ultrahigh-throughput evolution of Bacillus subtilis (BS2) esterase, merging yeast surface display with masked acid chloride probes, to identify a panel of mutants with improved selectivity toward the phenylcyclopropyl (pCP) ester protecting group relative to not only the probe substrate, but also a broad panel of 90 additional esters. Additionally, we applied the platform to identify a promiscuous mutant with improved activity across a broad substrate scope. Finally, we applied the highly pCP-selective BS2 variant, together with a selective variant for the methylcyclopropyl (mCP) ester protecting group, to demonstrate proximity labeling in mammalian cells with two orthogonal enzyme/probe systems, opening new opportunities in multiplexed proximity labeling. Overall, this study presents an efficacious method to identify enzyme variants with desired selectivity profiles that may be extended to multiple applications in chemical biology and synthesis.

articles.title: Nickel-Catalyzed Electroreductive Cross-Electrophile Coupling of Aryl/Alkenyl Triflates with Alkyl Bromides Assisted by an Organo-Mediator
articles.abstract: Given the thermodynamic stability of the C(sp2)–O bond, the development of simple and efficient strategies for its functionalization holds significant practical value. In this study, we report an electroreductive, one-pot nickel-catalyzed cross-electrophile coupling (XEC) of aryl/alkenyl triflates with diverse (1°, 2°, and 3°) alkyl bromides. Rapid in situ generation of Ni0 species enables efficient activation of the C(sp2)–O bond, yielding a broad range of C(sp2)–C(sp3) coupling products. Notably, the ligand functions as an organo-mediator to assist alkyl halide activation and prevent the over-reduction of substrates. This protocol is distinguished by its broad substrate scope, scalability, and mild reaction conditions.

articles.title: Regulated Density of Atomic Cu Sites Dictates Switching from C1 to C2+ Products in CO Electroreduction
articles.abstract: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) are generally considered C1-selective in CO2/CO electroreduction, as spatially isolated sites cannot efficiently sustain adjacent CO-derived intermediates required for C─C coupling. Here we show that this selectivity bias is not intrinsic to atomically dispersed Cu, but depends on single-atom site density. Across a series of Cu–N3O catalysts with different Cu site densities, increasing site density drives a clear selectivity crossover from H2 and CH4 formation to C2+ products. The total C2+ Faradaic efficiency (FE) rises from 9.6% on the low-density to 78.1% on the high-density at 1 bar CO, and further reaches 87.7% at 7 bar CO, whereas the low-density remains C1-selective. In situ attenuated-total-reflection surface enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) reveals that dense Cu single atoms sustain a larger *COatop population and simultaneously shift interfacial water from strongly hydrogen-bonded species towards free-water-rich configurations. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that higher site density stabilizes CO-containing surface states and lowers the barrier of the acetate-forming pathway. These findings identify a CO-rich and proton-accessible interfacial state that favors C─C coupling over C1 hydrogenation, establishing site density as a structural descriptor for multicarbon electrosynthesis on single-atom catalysts.

articles.title: Synergistic Facet Engineering and Axial Asymmetric Coordination of Single-Atom Cu Polarize Nitric Oxide Intermediates to Boost Photocatalytic Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia
articles.abstract: Sluggish charge dynamics and poor *NO polarization at active sites hinder the efficiency of photocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia (PcNRA). To address these issues, an atomic-level regulation strategy synergizing facet engineering with axial coordination was developed. Specifically, isolated Cu sites were anchored onto an electron-rich, ultrathin BiVO4 substrate exposing (040) facets. Functionalized ligands featuring distinct donor heteroatoms (S, N, O) were then systematically introduced, yielding a series of single-atom catalysts (S/N/O-Cu/BVO) with tailored axial microenvironments. A comprehensive methodology combining multidimensional spectroscopy and computational chemistry was established to verify this single-atom axial coordination. Detailed analyses of characteristic binding energies and absorption edge shifts via X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and synchrotron X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) identified localized coordination field effects. Crucially, these effects are distinct from conventional electronic metal-support interactions (EMSI), providing spectroscopic confirmation of successful axial ligand incorporation and guiding the prediction of their configurations. Building upon these spectral findings, density functional theory (DFT) models were constructed and optimized, conclusively validating the asymmetric axial coordination configurations within the system, specifically Cu-S2O1, Cu-N2O1, and Cu-O4. Catalytic evaluations demonstrated that S-Cu/BVO achieves the highest ammonia yield at 435 μmol·h–1·g–1. In-situ spectroscopy and DFT calculations elucidated the multidimensional synergistic mechanism driving this enhanced activity: (1) The prominently exposed (040) facets act as an interfacial electron sink, efficiently directing photogenerated electrons toward the Cu sites; (2) The axial S ligands reconstruct the electronic structure of the Cu centers via strong orbital coupling, thereby improving effective orbital overlap with nitrate; (3) The resulting asymmetric Cu-NO-S bridging configuration polarizes the critical *NO intermediate, substantially lowering the kinetic barrier for the rate-determining step.

articles.title: The Emerging Potential of Janus-Type Di-N-heterocyclic Carbene Transition Metal Complexes in Homogeneous Catalysis
articles.abstract: The article explores the catalytic potential of the emerging class of Janus-type di-N-heterocyclic carbenes that have attracted attention in recent times. The article details different aspects of these Janus-type di-N-heterocyclic carbenes particularly from their classifications, expansion in synthesis approaches, to finally their utility in different homogeneous transformations.

articles.title: Operando X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy Reveals Oxide Solid Electrolyte Stability against Electrochemically Plated Lithium
articles.abstract: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) has revealed many possible Li-induced interfacial reactions in solid-state electrolytes (SSEs), but most in situ studies form Li|electrolyte interfaces through non-electrochemical Li deposition, including evaporation, sputtering, or electron-beam-induced deposition. These routes may introduce additional energy that activates reaction pathways not accessed during electrochemical Li plating. Here, we use lab-based operando XPS to directly evaluate oxide solid-state electrolyte stability during electrochemical Li formation. Using this approach, we find sharply different responses for two representative oxide SSEs: NASICON-type Li1+xAlxTi2–x(PO4)3 (LATP) is reduced upon Li plating, forming a Li+/Ti3+-rich mixed-conducting interphase that partially relaxes through coupled ionic–electronic redistribution, whereas garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) shows no spectroscopically resolvable Zr or La reduction. This work represents the first direct operando XPS evaluation of SSE stability against electrochemically plated Li metal.

articles.title: Au Nanoparticle-Functionalized Antheraea pernyi Silk Nanofibrils: A Spatially Adaptive Anti-Inflammatory and Pro-Regenerative Paradigm for Disparate Chronic Epithelial Diseases
articles.abstract: Management of disparate chronic epithelial diseases relies on fragmented site-specific protocols yet remains hindered by common pathological barriers and sustained inflammation. Herein, we developed a top-down strategy to exfoliate short nanofibrils from Antheraea pernyi silk fibers featuring inherent Arg-Gly-Asp (RGD) motifs, followed by in situ growth of Au nanoparticles. The resulting platform (Au@ASFs) achieved superior spatial adaptability via catalytic oxygen propulsion, navigating across barriers to reach deep-seated lesions. Once localized, Au@ASFs provided phase-spanning multifunctional therapy through near-infrared (NIR)-triggered photothermal sterilization. Through RGD–integrin interactions, they also promoted hemostasis and M2 macrophage polarization to resolve persistent inflammation while enhancing fibroblast migration, angiogenesis, and neuronal differentiation. In vivo, Au@ASFs (+NIR) significantly improved closure of infected diabetic oral ulcers from 43.1 to 95.5% by day 7 and restored colon length in ulcerative colitis from 66.3 to 97.7% of healthy controls. In infected diabetic wounds, Au@ASFs (+NIR) increased closure from 63.8 to 89.1% by day 14. Transcriptomic analysis of wound tissues revealed reprogramming through suppressed NF-κB inflammatory signaling, activated Wnt5a/GSK-3β signaling for neuronal differentiation, and modulated PI3K-Akt signaling for tissue regeneration. Collectively, Au@ASF (+NIR) consistently resolves chronic epithelial diseases across disparate anatomical sites, establishing a unified drug-free paradigm that transcends site-specific constraints.

articles.title: Chirality-Functionalized Covalent Organic Frameworks for Enantioselective Neuroprotection with Restored Neuroactive Signaling in Alzheimer’s Disease
articles.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is driven by amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation and a cascade of interconnected neurotoxic events, including oxidative stress, glutamate excitotoxicity, calcium dysregulation, and impaired neuroactive ligand–receptor signaling. To address the multifactorial nature of AD pathology, chiral d- or l-cysteine-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) nanoparticles are developed as a multitarget nanotherapeutic platform. Both enantiomers effectively inhibit Aβ aggregation, scavenge reactive oxygen species, reduce extracellular glutamate levels, and attenuate calcium dysregulation. In parallel, d/l-Cys-COFs rescue compromised neuroactive ligand–receptor signaling, as evidenced by normalized expression of neuropeptide Y and brain-derived neurotrophic factor. In transgenic AD mice, d/l-Cys-COF treatment significantly improves memory and cognitive performance. Notably, the d-enantiomer affords superior neuroprotection through enhanced suppression of pathological intracellular calcium overload, whereas restoration of neuroactive ligand–receptor signaling remains chirality-independent. These findings identify chirality as a key design element for multitarget nanotherapeutics against AD, with enantioselective efficacy arising primarily from differential regulation of calcium dysregulation and shared restoration of neuroactive signaling contributing to the overall therapeutic benefit.

articles.title: Emergent Higher-Order Optical Nonlinearity in Self-Assembled Polar Supertextures
articles.abstract: Giant optical nonlinearities enable advanced materials control and bridge exotic light-matter phenomena to next-generation photonics. However, materials exhibiting strong higher-order optical nonlinearity beyond the second order are typically rare. Here, we report the discovery of a giant and ultrafast second-harmonic generation (SHG) in self-assembled polar skyrmions under mid-infrared excitations. The transient SHG intensity exhibits a distinctive power dependence originating from higher-order nonlinearity. More generally, we show that large higher-order nonlinearity emerges across diverse domain structures in polar superlattices. Phase-field simulations demonstrate a strong and periodic local permittivity variation within each polar texture at equilibrium, and further confirm the fast polarization oscillation in polar skyrmions with mid-infrared excitations. This intense local permittivity modulation can satisfy epsilon-near-zero conditions, unlocking dramatically enhanced nonlinear optical responses without photonic engineering. Consequently, the self-assembled polar topologies with strong inherent optical nonlinearity could establish a platform for quantum information processing and high-speed optical communications.

articles.title: Ion Transport Enhancement in Charge-Regulating Hydrogels
articles.abstract: Weak polyelectrolyte hydrogels are emerging as a versatile platform for ion transport and separation, desalination, and energy applications. However, a predictive understanding of how dynamic charge regulation at the nanoscopic scale influences ionic mobility in these polymer networks remains elusive. Here, using large-scale molecular simulations, we dissect the coupled mechanisms governing small-ion transport in weak polyelectrolyte hydrogels, and reveal how charge density, competitive binding, and dynamic charge regulation jointly control ion mobility. By systematically isolating these effects, we uncover a pronounced nonmonotonic dependence of ion self-diffusion on hydrogel pKa and salt concentration for multivalent ions. Strikingly, allowing the hydrogel backbone to dynamically regulate its charge eliminates this nonmonotonicity and leads to dramatic enhancements in ion mobility, with diffusion coefficients increasing by more than a factor of 2 for trivalent ions. We attribute this effect to a protonation-assisted hopping mechanism that continuously remodels the local electrostatic landscape, providing an additional molecular-scale pathway for ion unbinding beyond translational escape and accelerating ion-pair kinetics without affecting the fraction of free ions. Our results demonstrate that dynamic nanoscale charge regulation can decouple ion mobility from equilibrium binding strength, offering a powerful design lever unavailable in fixed-charge materials. Building upon these insights, we propose simple molecular design principles for next-generation ion-conducting hydrogels and suggest alternative strategies for nanostructured membranes, energy materials, and biologically inspired charge-adaptive soft matter.

articles.title: Strain-Engineered Deterministic Quantum Dots for Telecom O-Band Emission Using Buried Stressors
articles.abstract: The deterministic realization of quantum light sources operating at telecom wavelengths is essential for long-distance fiber-based quantum communication and distributed quantum computing. In this work, we demonstrate that telecom O-band emission can be achieved from site-controlled InGaAs/GaAs quantum dots (QDs). Our concept utilizes a buried AlAs/AlOx stressor layer with the unique feature of inducing a well-defined and controllable tensile strain field at the growth surface, enabling both site-selective nucleation at the mesa’s centers and a redshift of QD emission to the ∼1.3 μm wavelength range. This concept not only eliminates the need for strain-reducing layers (SRLs), which are known to degrade optical coherence, but also provides spatial control and spectral tunability. The grown telecom QDs show single-photon emission with g(2)(0) = (5.0 ± 1.0) × 10–2 at 4 K and (2.8 ± 0.3) × 10–1 at 77 K, demonstrating the quantum nature and thermal stability of the emitters. The emission characteristics of complex excitonic states are analyzed using 8-band k·p and configuration-interaction modeling, which quantitatively reproduces the experimental observations. Finally, we present a theory-supported strategy to further redshift the emission toward the center of the O-band and beyond by employing a multiburied stressor approach. This combined framework of experiment and theory establishes the buried stressor concept as a scalable route toward highly coherent, position-controlled O-band quantum emitters compatible with scalable photonic integration.

articles.title: Ultrasensitive Enantioselective Chiroptical Sensing with Large-Area Twisted Aligned Carbon Nanotube Films
articles.abstract: Enantioselective chiroptical sensing is gaining traction across various applications. However, intrinsic molecular chiroptical responses are weak, and existing amplification approaches add synthesis, manufacturing, or operational complexity that limits sensitivity and scalability. Here, we present an enantioselective sensing paradigm merging adsorption-driven chirality induction with large-scale optical transduction in twisted stacks of aligned carbon nanotube (CNT) films. Chiral molecules adsorb onto CNTs to form chiroptically active composites that are macroscopically assembled by alignment and rotational stacking, yielding large ultraviolet circular dichroism (CD). We resolve enantiomer handedness and quantify concentration in single-enantiomer aqueous solutions using a single sensor without lithography, hotspot delivery, or a paired opposite-handed reference. We achieve high sensitivity with estimated sub-μM minimum detectable concentrations for glucose and provide a proof-of-concept demonstration with alanine. Neither analyte-only solution shows detectable CD under the present measurement conditions. We demonstrate Langmuir-type adsorption behavior using molecular dynamics simulations and reproduce experimental results using optical simulations. This platform provides a foundation for future development toward cost-effective in situ enantiomer monitoring in aqueous environments.

articles.title: Regioisomerism‐Guided Molecular Passivation for 26.05%‐Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Defect‐mediated nonradiative recombination remains a major barrier to efficient and stable perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Although considerable advances have been made with molecular additives, how the spatial arrangement of functional groups affects device performance remains largely unexplored. Here, we present a regioisomerism‐guided molecular design strategy using fluorinated aniline as a well‐defined model system to incorporate into the lead iodide (PbI2) precursor solution during two‐step sequential perovskite deposition. By systematically comparing ortho‐, meta‐, and para‐fluoroaniline, we demonstrate that the ortho isomer, 2‐fluoroaniline (2‐FA), affords the most effective regulation of defect states and device performance. This superiority arises from the formation of an intramolecular hydrogen bond, which redistributes the molecular electrostatic potential and confers stable bidentate coordination with the perovskite lattice. Additionally, 2‐FA facilitates high‐quality α‐FAPbI3 films and aligns the energy level favorably with the hole transport layer, yielding a champion efficiency of 26.05% for the n‐i‐p PSCs. Moreover, the 2‐FA‐containing device exhibits superior operational stability. This regioisomerism‐guided design works universally across n‐i‐p and p‐i‐n architectures, irrespective of one‐step or two‐step fabrication. Our work establishes regioisomerism as a simple yet powerful molecular design principle for molecular engineering and provides new insight into the rational development of efficient and stable PSCs.

articles.title: Resolving the Structural Origin of Lattice Oxygen Release across Scales in Practical Lithium‐Manganese‐Rich Electrodes
articles.abstract: Gas evolution from lattice oxygen release is a major obstacle to deployment of high‐energy‐density cathodes, yet its structural origin within dense electrodes remains challenging to resolve across multiple length scales. This difficulty arises because gas evolution is the collective outcome of oxygen release from numerous grains and particles, whose environments can vary across electrode, secondary‐particle, and grain scales. Here, by integrating online electrochemical mass spectrometry with synchrotron X‐ray and electron microscopy, this study resolves the spatial origin of O2 evolution through mapping Mn reduction, a chemical fingerprint of oxygen release, across four orders of magnitude in length scale. Two lithium‐manganese‐rich layered oxide (LMR) electrodes that vary only in secondary‐particle size are employed as a model system, and their O2 evolution differs twofold. Spatially resolving Mn oxidation state distribution reveals no detectable Mn‐reduction gradient across the electrode thickness or within particles, indicating that the difference does not originate from electrode‐ or particle‐scale heterogeneity. Instead, frontal facets (lithium‐intercalation planes) of grains exhibit deeper Mn reduction and surface reconstruction than lateral facets, consistent with favorable oxygen vacancy formation and migration. O2 evolution matches after frontal‐facet area normalization, identifying frontal‐facet exposure as a key structural descriptor for O2 evolution in these practical LMR electrodes.

articles.title: A Multicomponent Body‐Centered Cubic Superconducting Alloy with Exceptional Mechanical Robustness at 4.2 Kelvin
articles.abstract: The ductile‐to‐brittle transition poses a persistent challenge for body‐centered cubic (BCC) structure superconducting alloys at liquid helium temperature (4.2 K), where intrinsic brittleness frequently leads to premature material failure and severely restricts their application in extreme environments. Here we present a BCC multicomponent V‐Nb‐Ti‐Mo superconducting alloy that achieves a high fracture elongation of ∼16% while maintaining pronounced strain‐hardening capacity of ∼620 MPa at 4.2 K. This exceptional ultra‐cryogenic ductility surpasses that of nearly all reported superconducting materials, and even BCC structured alloys. The rarely reported nanoscale orthorhombic martensitic transformation and the local chemical fluctuations with V‐enriched nanoclusters considerably promote the strain‐hardening capacity. Unlike traditional BCC alloys dominated by screw dislocations, a high density of non‐screw dislocations also formed to facilitate elongation. Plenty of kink bands, which are generally difficult to form at 4.2 K, delay the fracture process. This study not only offers a viable solution to the long‐standing cryogenic brittleness problem of BCC structure alloys, but also introduces a superconducting material with superior mechanical reliability for extreme‐condition applications.

articles.title: Carbon Dioxide Synergized Photo‐Reforming for Efficient Valorization of Bio‐Polyols With a Dynamic Carbon Balance
articles.abstract: Photocatalytic upgrading of biomass‐derived feedstocks into value‐added chemicals is promising for carbon neutrality but limited by low carbon utilization and CO2 emissions from over‐oxidation. Herein, we establish a “self‐feeding” photocatalytic system coupling glycerol oxidation with concurrent CO2 photoreduction to seamlessly close the carbon loop, enabling a truly dynamic and emission‐free biomass valorization strategy. This design uses defect‐engineered metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) with atomically anchored Cu sites to synergistically activate glycerol and O2 and introduce CO2 to steer the evolution of reactive oxygen species, thereby tempering hydroxyl radicals (•OH) for selective oxidative cleavage. Under illumination, CO2 coordination with in situ formed CuI sites facilitates CO2 photoreduction and dictates chemo‐selective C–C scission via decarbonylation to avoid over‐oxidation. By kinetically matching CO2 release with in situ reduction, the system channels liberated carbon exclusively into value‐added C1 products, achieving both carbon yield and selectivity approaching ∼100%. Benchmark production rates reach 2875 µmol g−1 h−1 for CO and 1185 µmol g−1 h−1 for HCOOH (corresponding to ∼3.0 carbons per glycerol molecule), culminating in a strictly zero‐CO2‐emission process. This work resolves the classic trade‐off between oxidation depth and carbon retention and reframes CO2 as a functional reaction modulator, charting a viable paradigm for carbon‐neutral chemical synthesis.

articles.title: Cascade Catalysis of Zn/Nb Single‐Atom Sites for Wide‐Temperature Li‐S Batteries
articles.abstract: Lithium‐sulfur batteries are considered promising next‐generation energy‐storage systems owing to their high theoretical energy density. However, their practical applications are severely hindered by sluggish sulfur redox kinetics and lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) shuttling, which are significantly aggravated under extreme‐temperature conditions. To address this issue, a novel cascade catalysis strategy is developed to regulate the multistep sulfur redox process through embedding the Nb‐N4 and Zn‐N4 dual single‐atom sites within N, P co‐doped carbon fibers (Zn/Nb‐NPMCFs). In conjunction with theoretical analysis, it is clarified that Nb single‐atom site preferentially adsorbs soluble LiPSs through forming an Nb‐S bond and catalyzes their conversion, whereas Zn single‐atom site facilitates subsequent Li2S‐related redox conversion. With the cascade catalysis effect enabling accelerated sulfur conversion and suppressed LiPSs shuttling, the assembled Li‐S batteries with Zn/Nb‐NPMCFs as free‐standing sulfur hosts deliver good electrochemical performance over a wide temperature range, retaining 651.8 and 401.1 mAh g−1 under 50°C and −20°C at 0.5 C, even after 500 cycles, respectively. This work provides a guideline for improving multistep sulfur redox kinetics in Li‐S batteries.

articles.title: Chiral Au@Semiconductor Yolk–Shell Nanostructures with Tailored Chiroptical Properties and Chirality‐Dependent Photocatalysis
articles.abstract: The spatial configuration of chiral metal‐semiconductor hybrid nanostructures directly determines the coupling efficiency between chiral plasmonic metals and semiconductors, which in turn affects their key physical and chemical properties and applications in diverse scenarios. However, precise spatial control of complex chiral hybrid nanostructures with increased structural and compositional diversity remains a significant challenge. Herein, we develop a general bottom‐up synthetic strategy for the construction of chiral Au@semiconductor yolk–shell nanostructures. By using chiral Au@Cu2O nanostructures with tunable geometric parameters as a chiral core, a finely controlled redox‐coupled ion exchange process is employed to realize the transition from a Cu2O shell to other semiconductors, including Cu7S4, Cu2‐xSe, CdS, and CuFeS2, to form chiral Au@semiconductor yolk–shell structures. More importantly, intriguing shell‐dependent chiroptical activities were experimentally observed and further elucidated by the theoretical simulations. The controllable integration of chiral plasmonic nanostructures with semiconductor components further allows applications in chirality‐dependent photocatalysis. The insights gained from this work provide an important knowledge framework for understanding the coupling of the semiconductor shell with the chiral plasmonic core that underpins the design of multifunctional chiral hybrid plasmonic nanomaterials toward catalysis and photonics.

articles.title: Constructing Fast Sensing‐Monitoring System via Spillover‐Free Hydrogen Reaction Path
articles.abstract: Hydrogen (H2) leakage monitoring is paramount for the safety of hydrogen fuel cells. However, traditional metal‐sensitized oxide semiconductor sensors often suffer from sluggish response caused by the limited hydrogen spillover kinetics. Herein, we explore a spillover‐free hydrogen response strategy via constructing a disordered 3LiPdPt‐sensitized interface on ZnO supports (3LiPdPt/ZnO) for ultrafast and low‐concentration H2 detection. We find the introduction of Li+ can collapse the regular PdPt interface and induce stable amorphization even at high temperature. The resultant 3LiPdPt/ZnO sensor can achieve ultrafast response (<4 s) to 3–200 ppm H2, superior hydrogen response (13–50 ppm of H2) and excellent long‐term stability. In‐situ experiments confirm that the disordered 3LiPdPt interface can bypass the hydrogen spillover limitation to realize a direct reaction between activated hydrogen and oxygen species. This path fundamentally eliminates the reliance on long‐range hydrogen diffusion and thus improves the sensing response speed reactive. Moreover, we demonstrate an autonomous monitoring system by equipping the sensors on fuel cell electric vehicle devices for dual‐mode (continuous/intermittent) H2 leakage assessment. Therefore, our proposed strategy reveals a fundamental understanding of the hydrogen sensing mechanism and may create a new path for highly effective H2 detection.

articles.title: Correction to “Controlling Nuclei Growth and Phase Transition of CsFA‐Based Perovskite During Slot‐Die Coating via Solvent Engineering for High‐Performance Solar Cells and Modules”
Correction to “M2 Macrophage‐Derived Exosomes Inhibiting Neutrophil Extracellular Traps for Ischemic Stroke Therapy”
Correction to “Revisiting Cobalt Dopability in GeTe System to Design Modulation‐Doped Thermoelectrics”
Crown‐Ether‐Based Covalent Organic Network Membranes for Hydration‐Governed Li+/Mg2+ Separation
articles.abstract: Selective Li+/Mg2+ separation remains a central challenge for sustainable lithium extraction because ion transport in confined aqueous environments is governed by coupled steric and hydration effects rather than ionic size alone. Here, we report a crown‐ether‐based covalent organic network membrane for hydration‐governed mono/divalent ion sieving. Unlike conventional crown‐ether materials that rely on cavity‐specific host‐guest recognition, the conformational flexibility and steric hindrance of dibenzo‐18‐crown‐6 induce locally ordered yet globally disordered packing, transforming the nominal ∼3 nm intrinsic cavity into sub‐nanometer transport channels with an effective aperture of ∼0.9 nm. Structural analyses reveal that the exposed ether oxygen atoms of crown‐ethers reconstruct oxygen‐rich confined hydration interfaces that regulate hydrated‐ion partitioning and migration. Thus, the membrane exhibits high mono/divalent ion discrimination, delivering a Li+/Mg2+ selectivity of ∼3900 together with high Li+ flux, and also demonstrating efficient K+/Mg2+ and Cs+/Sr2+ separation with selectivities of ∼3140 and ∼840, respectively. Spectroscopic studies, density functional theory calculations, and molecular dynamics simulations collectively reveal a dual physical‐thermodynamic blockade mechanism, where steric confinement suppresses hydrated divalent ions and hydration‐mediated thermodynamic compensation facilitates monovalent ion transport. The membrane maintains robust performance under concentrated and Mg‐rich conditions, highlighting the potential of engineered transport architectures for lithium extraction and precise ionic separations.

articles.title: Dual‐Axial Nitrogen Coordination‐Induced Mn Charge Localization at Fe‐Mn Dual‐Atom Sites for Enhanced Sulfur Redox Kinetics
articles.abstract: The optimization of coordination environments for heteronuclear dual-atom catalysts (DACs) has been a formidable challenge in lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries, arising from complex electronic coupling induced by inherent inter-metallic-site charge transfer at heteronuclear sites. Herein, an Fe-Mn dual-atom catalyst (FeMn-(Nax)2 DAC/NC) with dual-axial nitrogen coordination anchored on nitrogen-doped carbon is rationally constructed to achieve the directional electronic modulation of active sites. The axial nitrogen ligand reconfigures the electronic distribution of Fe-Mn heteronuclear sites, inducing Fe-to-Mn charge transfer and further charge localization on the Mn center. The electronic effect precisely modulates Mn d-orbital energy levels, reinforcing the d-p orbital hybridization between active sites and lithium polysulfides (LiPSs). The FeMn-(Nax)2 DAC/NC strengthens the chemical adsorption of LiPSs to suppress the shuttle effect, and further bidirectionally accelerates the rate-determining steps of sulfur redox: the solid‑to‑solid conversion from Li2S2 to Li2S and the oxidative dissociation of Li2S. Consequently, the resultant sulfur cathodes deliver a discharge capacity of 682 mAh g− 1 at 5 C and an ultralow capacity decay rate of 0.047% per cycle over 1000 cycles at 3 C. This work offers a novel strategy for optimizing the redox kinetics of sulfur cathodes in Li-S batteries.

articles.title: Dynamically Modulated Ultralong Organic Phosphorescent Materials: Achieving Wide‐Range Lifetime Tunability for Multicolor Data Storage
articles.abstract: Ultralong organic phosphorescence (UOP) materials have attracted growing research attention in the field of optical information storage, anti‐counterfeiting, and data encryption owing to their unique long‐lived emission characteristics. However, the widespread application of UOP‐based information storage is currently constrained by two main limitations: the dominant binary (on/off) encoding mode with limited information capacity, and the lack of high‐precision, facile data‐writing approaches compatible with scalable fabrication. In this work, we develop a time‐resolved information storage strategy based on widely and precisely tunable UOP lifetimes, which is realized by rationally controlling the polymerization degree of the polymer host. Combining with digital processing (DLP) 3D printing method, the photosensitive materials 3‐TBAOF@HEA:AA and 4‐TBAOF@HEA:AA are designed and developed with tunable UOP lifetimes from 4.6 to 1577.50 ms. Leveraging this tunability of broad lifetime, we demonstrate time‐dependent information storage including multicolor information display and direct photopatterning on flexible 2D thin films. The 3D‐printable UOP system with precisely controllable phosphorescence lifetimes provides a viable material platform for constructing high‐level data security storage devices.

articles.title: In Situ and Dynamic Reconfiguration of Nonlinear Optical Absorption by Carbon Nanotube Optical Fiber
articles.abstract: Nanomaterial‐based nonlinear optical absorbers, such as saturable absorbers and optical limiters, have been widely employed for laser intensity manipulation. However, their nonlinear absorption regimes are typically constrained by static nonlinear responses within specific spectral regions. Tuning the operational regime generally necessitates material functionalization or complex post‐treatments. Consequently, reconfiguring the nonlinear absorption regime in a monolithic device remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate in situ manipulation of the nonlinear interaction strength using an optical fiber‐integrated single‐walled carbon nanotube absorber, which exhibits reconfigurable nonlinear optical absorption. Our monolithic device enables dynamic onset tuning of optical limiting within a designated spectral excitation energy range, in addition to supporting saturable absorption operation. Furthermore, leveraging the tunable nonlinear optical response of a saturable absorber, we realize a passively mode‐locked fiber laser with an unprecedented tuning range of 10 GHz and a side‐mode‐suppression ratio exceeding 30 dB, surpassing other nanomaterial saturable absorber‐based GHz light sources. Our device fabrication strategy features a simple configuration and low cost compared to static nonlinear optical absorbers, and it can be readily extended to other types of nonlinear optical nanomaterial absorbers. This approach may find immediate applications in flexible light intensity control, optical signal processing, and intelligent physical systems requiring dynamic nonlinear activation functions.

articles.title: Lattice‐Level Negative Thermal Expansion Enables Thermomechanical Self‐Compensation in High‐Rate Lithium Batteries
articles.abstract: Localized Joule heating in high‐rate lithium metal batteries often induces severe thermomechanical failure of polymer separators and accelerates thermal runaway in cells with Ni‐rich NCM cathode. Here we report a multiscale separator design strategy that translates lattice‐level negative thermal expansion into macroscopic thermomechanical self‐compensation. In this design, Cu2P2O7 is coupled with the PVDF‐HFP matrix through a PDA mediated interface. Temperature‐dependent structural analysis and thermal‐response tests demonstrate the anisotropic lattice contraction of Cu2P2O7, which relieves the thermally induced deformation of PVDF‐HFP through PDA mediated interfacial interactions. The amine‐rich PDA layer further suppresses corrosive hydrofluoric acid during the cycling, improving interfacial durability. The resulting composite membrane maintains complete dimensional stability up to 200°C while preserving high ionic conductivity and a uniform Li+ flux. As a result, Li||Li symmetric cells with the self‐compensating separator operate for more than 3000 h at 1 mA cm−2. When paired with Ni‐rich NCM811 cathodes, full cells maintain 1000 stable cycles at 5 C and deliver 135 mAh g−1 at 60°C after 100 cycles. This work demonstrates a solid‐state negative thermal expansion strategy for active separator protection, providing a materials route for mitigating thermomechanical failure in high‐power lithium metal batteries.

articles.title: Localized Nicotinamide Riboside Delivery Through a Reversible Affinity Hydrogel Promotes Myocardial Restoration
articles.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI), a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, is characterized by acute ischemic injury followed by mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, redox imbalance, and adverse cardiac remodeling. NAD+‐a vital coenzyme—is rapidly perturbed after MI and represents a potential metabolic target for supporting myocardial recovery. However, existing biomaterial formulations have limited efficacy because of their insufficient loading and local delivery of NAD+ and other small hydrophilic molecules to the myocardium. Herein, we present an injectable, on‐heart adhesive hydrogel capable of efficiently loading and gradually releasing nicotinamide riboside (NR), a precursor of NAD+, to restore NAD+ levels in infarcted cardiac tissue. Phenylboronate‐modified chitosan forms reversible yet high‐affinity interactions with NR, enabling controlled delivery; while the hydrogel network is engineered from crosslinking with gallol‐modified chitosan that provides tissue adhesion and facilitates in situ gelation upon injection. In a murine MI model, hydrogel‐mediated NR delivery increased NAD+ availability and improved cardiac function and electrophysiology. Benefits included reduced injury, improved redox and metabolic function, and preserved cardiac structure. Mechanistically, NR protection converged on the SIRT1–p65 axis, limiting ferroptotic and inflammatory injury while preserving mitochondrial function. Thus, the hydrogel provides a cardiac‐adhesive platform for NR delivery, restoring NAD+ homeostasis and promoting recovery after MI.

articles.title: Meso‐Substituent Engineering Tunes Co‐OOH Binding in Cobalt Porphyrins for Selective H2O2 Electrosynthesis
articles.abstract: Cobalt porphyrins are prototypical molecular catalysts for two‐electron oxygen reduction to H2O2 because of their well‐defined CoN4 active sites and synthetically tunable ligand frameworks. However, conventional phenyl‐substituted cobalt porphyrins generally exhibit limited H2O2 selectivity due to excessively strong Co‐OOH chemisorption, which can favor O─O bond activation and the competing four‐electron oxygen reduction pathway. Herein, we establish a meso‐substituent engineering strategy to regulate Co‐OOH interaction in cobalt porphyrins without altering the primary CoN4 coordination motif. By progressively replacing meso‐phenyl groups with thienyl and bithienyl substituents, the optimized CoT2TP catalyst achieves a H2O2 Faradaic efficiency of 98.4% together with a H2O2 production rate of 74.96 mg cm−2 h−1 at 120 mA cm−2. In situ attenuated total reflection surface‐enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR‐SEIRAS) reveals a continuous blue shift of the O─O stretching vibration of adsorbed *OOH with increasing thiophene incorporation, indicating weakened Co‐OOH chemisorption and facilitated Co─OOH bond cleavage. Density functional theory calculations further show that bithienyl substitution shifts the Co d‐band center away from the Fermi level and optimizes the *OOH adsorption strength. This work establishes remote meso‐substituent regulation of Co‐OOH binding as a molecular design strategy for selective H2O2 electrosynthesis.

articles.title: Morphology‐Engineered ZIF Nanosheet Membranes With 4‐Membered‐Ring Apertures for Propylene/Propane Separation
articles.abstract: Precise hydrocarbon separations remain a major challenge for membrane technologies because molecular discrimination is often limited by poor control over pore accessibility and transport pathways in conventional mixed‐matrix membranes (MMMs). Here, we report a morphology‐engineering strategy that transforms the intrinsic pore anisotropy of ZIF nanoparticles into selectively exposed 4‐membered‐ring apertures within two‐dimensional (2D) nanosheets, which are subsequently assembled into highly oriented 2D ZIF MMMs. The pore system is reactivated through a soft chemical activation that removes residual surfactants while preserving structural integrity and solution processability. A shear‐flow‐induced pre‐alignment process directs the in‐plane orientation of 2D ZIF nanosheets within the polymer matrix, aligning the aperture channels parallel to the gas transport direction to maximize hydrocarbon molecular recognition. Multiscale characterization and simulations reveal a direct structure–transport relationship linking nanosheet orientation, aperture‐specific diffusion, and macroscopic separation behavior. The resulting 2D ZIF‐8 nanosheet MMMs exhibit enhanced mechanical robustness together with outstanding hydrocarbon separation performance, delivering a 332% increase in C3H6 permeability and a 274% improvement in selectivity relative to the pure polymer membrane. This work provides a general strategy for programming pore accessibility and orientation in 2D MOF MMMs for precise molecular separations.

articles.title: Nanoimprint‐Enhanced Organic Heterojunction Phototransistors for Bipolar Optical Encoding in Reservoir Computing
articles.abstract: Optoelectronic reservoirs require transient states with sufficient electrical contrast and diverse temporal dynamics. However, weak optical‐to‐electrical transduction reduces the resolvability of reservoir states, whereas unipolar photoresponses restrict how successive optical inputs modulate the residual device state. Here, we report a nanoimprint‐enhanced PDVT‐10/F16‐CuPc heterojunction organic phototransistor that combines amplified photocurrent output with wavelength‐dependent bipolar dynamics. Periodic nanostructures introduced into the PDVT‐10 layer enhance broadband optical absorption and photocurrent generation, enabling a minimum detectable irradiance of 0.65 µW cm−2 at 430 nm. Meanwhile, the heterojunction generates wavelength‐dependent photocurrent transients with opposite polarities and distinct relaxation behaviors, enabling bipolar optical encoding in which binary 0 and 1 inputs are represented by optical pulses at two wavelengths that drive the photocurrent state in opposite directions. Consequently, successive inputs can selectively reinforce, offset, or reverse the residual photocurrent state, yielding more distinguishable and history‐dependent reservoir trajectories. This bipolar encoding improves reservoir‐state distinguishability by expanding the accessible photocurrent range and reducing state overlap under fluctuations, increasing nine‐class human action‐recognition accuracy from 77.04% to 83.3%. Combining two bipolar reservoir groups further increases recognition accuracy to 90.0%. This work establishes a compact device paradigm that unifies weak‐light sensitivity with temporal dynamics, advancing hardware‐efficient processing of complex temporal information.

articles.title: Revealing the Intrinsic Ion Species, Diffusion Paths, Governing Factors for Charge Carriers of Cement‐Based Structural Capacitors (CSCs)
articles.abstract: Integrated structural/functional rechargeable CSCs combine the load‐bearing properties of construction with electrochemical energy storage, thereby expanding the functional capabilities of modern buildings by providing distributed and adaptive energy storage. However, many fundamental scientific issues‐including the dominant ionic species, ion diffusion pathways, and the key factors governing charge‐carrier transport—remain unclear, hindering the rational design of CSCs. In this work, we first employ a unidirectional charging method to identify Na+ and K+ as the dominant charge carriers in CSCs. Subsequently, a novel Zn‐based cement structural capacitor (Zn‐CSC) is designed, in which Zn‐containing species serve as a tracer to qualitatively reveal the direction and spatial pathways of field‐assisted ion transport through the interconnected porous network of the cement matrix. Furthermore, the fundamental factors governing charge‐carrier behavior are investigated: (1) the concentration of charge carriers in the cement pore solution is positively correlated with the energy‐storage performance of CSCs; (2) a reduction in the water content of the cement electrolyte hinders the transport of Na+ and K+ ions, leading to diminished energy‐storage capability; and (3) the solidified, percolating 3D micro‐/nanoporous network formed within the cement electrolyte serves as the critical pathway for efficient charge‐carrier transport.

articles.title: Rigid π‐Bridge Conformational Locked Crosslinker for Non‐Destructive Direct Photopatterning of Colloidal Quantum Dot
articles.abstract: Colloidal quantum dots (QDs) are promising emitters for next‐generation displays, yet direct photolithography often causes severe photophysical degradation that compromises device performance. Although molecular rigidification can alleviate photodamage, it usually reduces crosslinker solubility, limiting compatibility with octane‐dispersed QDs. Here, we propose a conformation‐locked π‐bridge design that simultaneously enhances molecular rigidity and solubility. Using fluorinated phenyl (F1) and biphenyl (F2) π‐bridge crosslinkers as model systems, we reveal how conformational regulation governs QD photopatterning. The conformation‐locked F2 suppresses molecular torsion while maintaining excellent octane solubility, enabling high‐fidelity photopatterning with a resolution of 12,700 PPI. Meanwhile, the extended π‐conjugation increases its molar extinction coefficient to 77,598 L mol−1 cm−1, reducing the required UV exposure dose to 2 mJ cm−2. As a result, patterned QDs retain over 95% of their photoluminescence quantum yield and 97% of their fluorescence lifetime. QLEDs fabricated from F2‐patterned QDs exhibit an external quantum efficiency of 24.40% and a maximum luminance of 237,692 cd m−2, with both performance metrics essentially preserved after patterning. Furthermore, the enhanced exciton binding energy significantly improves operational stability, extending the device lifetime (T95) from 421 h to 2,324 h at 1,000 cd m−2. This work provides a general strategy for low‐dose, non‐destructive, high‐resolution QD photolithography.

articles.title: Self‐Assembled Supramolecular Host–Guest Composite Enables Interfacial Regulation Toward Dendrite‐Free Aqueous Zinc Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: The instability of zinc anodes during reversible deposition and dissolution in the aqueous electrolyte constitutes a critical bottleneck limiting the lifespan of aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs). Herein, we utilize a straightforward and supramolecular self-assembly approach involving 4-sulfocalix[6]arene (SCA[6]) and N,N’-dimethyl-9,9’-biacridinium dinitrate (LCG), driven by cooperative host-guest recognition and electrostatic forces. The spontaneous interfacial assembly of these components enables the construction of a protective interphase on zinc anodes and functions as a “molecular switch” to regulate the Zn2 + solvation structure, facilitate ion transport, and accommodate volumetric fluctuations during cycling. Consequently, the LCG/SCA[6]-modified interface effectively mitigates corrosion and dendrite growth, thereby significantly enhancing the electrochemical stability and cycling performance of AZIBs. As a result, the (LCG/SCA[6])2-Zn symmetric cell can maintain stable operation for over 3800 h at 1 mA cm−2 and 1 mAh cm−2. The (LCG/SCA[6])2-Zn||I2 coin cell retains a specific capacity of 200.50 mAh g−1 with a capacity retention rate of 87.25% at 2 A g−1 even after 14 000 cycles. Considering the low cost and simplicity of LCG/SCA[6] film fabrication, this supramolecular composite presents a promising strategy for enhancing the stability of zinc anodes.

articles.title: Time‐Domain Regulation of Electrolyte Microenvironments Enables 30 mA cm−2 Stable Lithium Plating/Stripping for High‐Voltage Lithium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: The practical application of high-voltage lithium metal batteries (LMBs) is severely hindered by interfacial instability and structural degradation, fundamentally originating from “time-domain mismatch” between rapid parasitic reactions and sluggish interface passivation. Herein, we propose a time-domain responsive in situ gel polymer electrolyte (SiNCO-GPE) to dynamically regulate the electrolyte microenvironment. The (trimethylsilyl)isocyanate (SiNCO) acts as a “scavenging cage” to eliminate trace water and hydrogen fluoride, while its reaction products subsequently participate in interfacial evolution. The in situ polymerized poly(vinylene carbonate) integrated with poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) electrospun fiber skeleton creates a F-O co-coordination environment to facilitate fast Li+ transport. The electroactive isocyanate group in SiNCO, together with lithium difluoro(oxalato)borate and fluoroethylene carbonate, decomposes preferentially to rapidly construct a robust B/N/F-rich interphase layer during initial cycling on both the anode and cathode, while the Si-containing scavenging products are dynamically incorporated into the interphase layers during prolonged cycling to accommodate mechanical stress. The SiNCO-GPE enables exceptional Li plating/stripping stability for over 4000 h at 1 mA cm− 2 and withstands an ultrahigh current density of 30 mA cm− 2 over 70 h, while the Li||LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 cell delivers an outstanding capacity retention of 90.5% after 500 cycles at 4.7 V, offering new insights into the development of durable high-voltage LMBs.

articles.title: Trieffect Dense Organic‐Derived Coating Enabling Synergistic Bulk Stability and Interfacial Reactivity for Superb Zn‐Mn Batteries
articles.abstract: The practical application of aqueous Zn-MnO2 batteries is hindered by sluggish Zn2+ diffusion kinetics, severe Mn dissolution, and “dead” MnO2 accumulation in Mn2+-containg electrolytes, leading to inferior rate capability and rapid capacity decay. Herein, we designed an organic-modified MnO2 uniformly encapsulated by 1,4-dihydroxybenzene (HQ) to simultaneously regulate bulk stability and interfacial reactivity of HQ-MnO2 hybrid (denoted as H-MnO2) via a facile solvent-free ball milling method. In/ex situ characterization and theoretical calculation results reveal that the dense HQ-derived coating with Mn─O─C interfacial bonds significantly boost charge diffusion kinetics and improves the structural robustness of H-MnO2. Furthermore, the redox-catalytic HQ-derived layer with C═O/C─OH couples efficiently promotes selective H+ insertion ability as well as boosts cathodic Mn2+/MnO2 conversion to prevent irreversible ZnMn2O4 and “dead” MnO2 accumulation simultaneously. As a result, the Zn//H-MnO2 battery exhibits an outstanding capacity of 575 mAh g−1, superior rate performance, and ultra-long lifespan over 15 000 cycles. Moreover, 192.5 Wh kgH-MnO2 −1 pouch cell with practical high-mass loading maintained 100% capacity retention after 130 cycles, demonstrating the effectiveness of trieffect-integrated organic interfacial engineering for high-energy and durable Zn-MnO2 systems.

articles.title: Understanding the Multi‐Electron Conversion Mechanism and High Performance of NbCl5 Cathodes in All‐Solid‐State Lithium Batteries
articles.abstract: Conversion‐type cathodes are promising candidates for high‐energy all‐solid‐state lithium batteries due to their high capacities enabled by multi‐electron redox chemistry. However, their practical application is severely hindered by large voltage hysteresis and rapid capacity decay arising from sluggish Li‐ion transport and structural degradation during conversion reactions. Herein, we develop a high‐valent NbCl5 cathode with continuous electronic pathways, enabling highly reversible four‐electron conversion with ultralow discharge–charge overpotentials. The NbCl5 cathode delivers a reversible capacity of 281 mAh g−1 at 0.1 C and retains 70% of its initial capacity at 1.0 C after 2000 cycles. Notably, it exhibits minimal voltage hysteresis across four electrochemical plateaus (0.08, 0.03, 0.03, and 0.01 V, respectively), achieving an energy efficiency of 98.9%, which surpasses reported conversion‐type and most layered oxide intercalation cathodes. We revealed that conversion‐induced interfaces between crystalline LiCl and low‐valent niobium chloride nanodomains facilitate Li‐ion migration within the cathode bulk and across the cathode/solid electrolyte interface. Meanwhile, the internal framework remains structurally stable during prolonged conversion reactions, as evidenced by only a slight increase in porosity from 2.48% to 3.55% after 200 cycles. This chemo‐mechanical synergy accelerates Li‐ion transport and maintains intimate interfacial contact, thereby enabling ultralow voltage hysteresis and durable cycling performance.

articles.title: Unlocking Thermoelectric Performance in Cu2SnSe3 Through Controlled Structural Ordering
articles.abstract: Diamond‐like semiconductors offer a versatile platform for the design of highly efficient energy‐converting materials, owing to their tunable electronic structures and high charge carrier mobility. A thorough understanding and precise control of their structural complexity and defect chemistry are, however, essential for optimizing their transport properties. Here, we demonstrate that both the spatial arrangement of tetrahedral motifs and the polymorphic landscape of the diamond‐like semiconductor Cu2SnSe3 can be precisely controlled through post‐synthesis annealing. Electron diffraction combined with precession‐assisted electron diffraction tomography reveals that structural disorder at the sub‐µm length scale, arising from the coexistence of monoclinic and cubic structures, promotes charge carrier trapping within the induced localized states. The degree of localization plays a key role in shaping the temperature dependence of the electronic properties, which evolve from amorphous‐like hopping conduction to conventional valence‐band transport as the annealing temperature increases from 573 to 947 K. Optimum hole mobility and thermoelectric performance are achieved once a single crystallographic phase is obtained by annealing above 873 K. These findings showcase the detrimental influence of local structural disorder on charge carrier transport, providing an additional degree of freedom for tailoring functional properties in crystalline semiconductors.

articles.title: cis/trans‐Through‐Space Charge‐Transfer Isomers Enabled by Acceptor Fusion for High‐Efficiency Thermally‐Activated Delayed Fluorescence and Circularly Polarized Emission
articles.abstract: Multi-π-stacked through‑space charge‑transfer (TSCT) emitters have shown great potential for developing efficient thermally-activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) toward organic light‑emitting diodes (OLEDs) applications. New design paradigms are highly demanded for constructing multi-π-stacked TSCT-TADF emitters, especially the chiral ones with chiroptical activity.
