articles.title: Hydrogen production by thermal catalytic decomposition of ammonia in aqueous phase
articles.abstract: The results demonstrate that aqueous NH 3 can be thermocatalytically decomposed to H 2 and N 2 at these comparatively mild temperatures.

articles.title: In vivo genome-editing therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy: Preclinical studies and first-in-human trial
articles.abstract: A single-dose AAV-CRISPR therapy restores dystrophin in humanized DMD mice and achieves durable editing with manageable safety in non-human primates. In a first-in-human DMD trial, the therapy yields molecular evidence of muscle editing but reveals a fatal dose-dependent immune complication, highlighting the urgent need to expand the safety margin of systemic AAV-CRISPR treatments.

articles.title: Shared α-helix chimeraffibodies enable linker-free bispecific protein design
articles.abstract: Bispecific proteins often rely on flexible linkers that increase conformational heterogeneity. Qiu et al. present AlphaSync, a geometry-guided framework that integrates α-helical binders through helix sharing. The resulting Chimeraffibody retains HER2-albumin co-recognition while improving pharmacokinetics, tumor localization, and predicted immunogenicity liability.

articles.title: BCLAF1 and responses to RAG-induced DNA breaks enforce pre-B cell checkpoint
articles.abstract: During early B cell development, pre-B cells encounter signaling from pre-B cell receptor (pre-BCR) and DNA damage responses (DDR) triggered by RAG-induced DNA double-stranded breaks (DSBs) generated during immunoglobulin light chain (Igl) recombination. These signals drive cooperative and antagonistic programs to promote pre-B cell checkpoint. Here, we show in vivo that pre-B cells transition between distinct subpopulations predominated by either pre-BCR or RAG DSB-induced DDR signals. DDR initiates early in pre-B cells undergoing Igl recombination then drives cellular programming during terminal pre-B stages. We find that RAG DSB-induced DDR regulates coordinated pre-B cell differentiation, in part, by activation of the transcriptional repressor complex SPIC/BCLAF1. Loss of BCLAF1 disrupts pre-B cell developmental progression resulting in concomitant expression of pre-BCR and DDR programs with breakdown in segregation of clonal expansion and Igl recombination. These studies show that RAG DSB-induced DDR and BCLAF1 preserve pre-B cell checkpoint integrity in vivo during Igl recombination.

articles.title: Baseline microbial ecology encodes probiotic responsiveness through distinct metabolic and network configurations
articles.abstract: Probiotic efficacy in inflammatory bowel disease varies widely between individuals, and the sources of that variability remain poorly understood. D-lactate is a microbiota-derived metabolite that accumulates during intestinal inflammation and is associated with epithelial barrier dysfunction, which motivated our use of a consortium selected to contribute none of it. Here we show that its benefit is not an intrinsic property of the administered strains but is determined by the pre-existing ecological state of the recipient microbiome. Across three independent mouse resources, preventive administration reduced disease severity and histopathological damage only where baseline communities carried higher diversity and more complex co-occurrence architecture; in those animals the consortium preserved community structure and metabolic output, restoring disease-disrupted metabolites, and selectively raising butyrate and propionate. Sustained exogenous D-lactate did not abolish protection, placing D-lactate as a tractable readout of ecological restoration rather than its effector. Responsiveness is encoded in the baseline microbiota and predictable before intervention, establishing probiotic efficacy as a stratifiable property of the host microbiome.

articles.title: CCN1-mediated stress signaling underlies intrinsic cardiomyocyte dysfunction in spinal muscular atrophy
E2 displacement of CIP2A from TOPBP1 activates the DNA damage response during papillomavirus life cycles
articles.abstract: The papillomavirus life cycle is linked to epithelial differentiation, and the virus manipulates differentiation to facilitate viral production. One such manipulation is the activation of the DNA damage response (DDR), which promotes viral replication via homologous recombination. Here, we show that the papillomavirus transcription/replication/segregation factor E2 activates the DDR. During differentiation, E2 attenuates sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) activity, enhances the acetylation of DDR factors, and displaces cancerous inhibitor of protein phosphatase 2A (CIP2A) from DNA topoisomerase II-binding protein 1 (TOPBP1), resulting in CIP2A-mediated inhibition of protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) and ataxia-telangiectasia mutated (ATM) activation. E2 associates with TOPBP1 and ATM while reducing TOPBP1-ATR complexes and ataxia-telangiectasia and Rad3-related (ATR) activation. This ATM-high, ATR-low DDR phenotype promotes viral replication and cell proliferation. We observe this DDR activation in E2-expressing keratinocytes, human papillomavirus 16 (HPV16)-positive cells, Mus musculus papillomavirus 1 (MmuPV1)-induced lesions, HPV-positive head and neck cancer cell lines, and HPV16-positive patient-derived xenografts. ATM inhibition preferentially kills E2-expressing cells, supporting ATM signaling as a potential therapeutic target in HPV-associated disease retaining E2 expression and episomal genomes.

articles.title: Early mitophagy defects and impaired mitochondrial energy metabolism drive target organ damage progression: Lessons from the Fabry heart
Embryonic reprogramming drives anaplastic transformation in thyroid carcinoma
articles.abstract: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma (ATC) is a highly aggressive malignancy that often arises through anaplastic transformation of papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). Although genetic drivers such as BRAF and TP53 mutations are implicated, the mechanisms underlying this transition remain poorly understood. Here, we show that human ATC loses thyroid differentiation and acquires pluripotency-associated features, accompanied by MAPK pathway activation. Guided by parallels with induced pluripotent stem cell reprogramming, we develop an in vivo reprogramming mouse model. Forced expression of Oct3/4, Sox2, Klf4, and c-Myc (OSKM) induces anaplastic transformation of Braf-mutant thyroid epithelium even without Trp53 mutation, yielding an ATC-like phenotype that shares molecular and histological features with human ATC. A conventional Braf/Trp53-mutant model shows similar features. Reintroduction of NKX2-1 into human and murine ATC cells partially reverses embryonic reprogramming, suppresses proliferation and induces redifferentiation toward a PTC-like phenotype. Embryonic reprogramming is a central driver of anaplastic transformation and supports redifferentiation strategies.

articles.title: Heterogeneous contributions of APOBEC3 deaminases to substitution and indel mutagenesis in lung adenocarcinoma
Mechanisms of vesicular monoamine transporter 2 modulation by amphetamines and lobeline
articles.abstract: Amphetamine-type stimulants (ATSs) disrupt the brain monoaminergic system and strongly stimulate motivation, movement, and addiction. Vesicular monoamine transporter 2 (VMAT2) plays a vital role in monoaminergic neurotransmission by sequestering monoamines in presynaptic vesicles. How ATS binds to and regulates VMAT2 remains elusive. Here, we report the cryo-EM structures of human VMAT2 in complex with four ATSs (AMPH, METH, MDMA, and MDA) and the inhibitor lobeline, revealing the molecular mechanisms underlying ATS recognition and modulation. ATSs mimic monoamines and occupy the substrate-binding site of VMAT2, indicating that ATSs function as substrates and thus redistribute the vesicular monoamine pools to the cytosolic pools. Lobeline adopts an unexpected dual-binding mode and locks VMAT2 in a lumen-facing conformation, inhibiting monoamine and ATS uptake. Our dopamine release assay revealed that lobeline regulates AMPH-induced dopamine release by modulating both VMAT2 and DAT. This study provides important mechanistic insights into VMAT2 modulation by amphetamines and lobeline.

articles.title: RAStoERK: A reference interaction atlas for insights into signaling and disease
articles.abstract: The RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK pathway has been extensively studied for its roles in physiology and disease, yet a systems-level view of its interplay with the broader cellular context is lacking, limiting insight into paralog-specific roles, mutation-driven rewiring, and cross-pathway integration. To address this, we simultaneously mapped the interactomes of all pathway components and their activating and inactivating mutations, identifying 2,500 high-confidence interactors, 88% of which previously unreported, and generating a high-confidence, comprehensive reference map of the pathway in resting and activated states. The pathway behaves like a "molecular organism" that connects to other signaling complexes, operates from distinct subcellular sites, and integrates into networks relevant to physiology and disease. Dataset exploration uncovers paralog- and mutation-specific interaction signatures and pathway-level crosstalk, including previously unknown connections to mRNA metabolism and WNT signaling. The interactomes available at RAStoERK.univie.ac.at provide a foundational community resource for unbiased discovery, targeted mechanistic studies, and potential therapeutic exploration.

articles.title: Role of Leu and Val synthesis in sensing mitochondrial nutrient and energy availability
articles.abstract: How cells integrate nutrient availability to coordinate metabolism and growth remains poorly understood. Here, we identify branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) synthesis as a metabolic sensing system linking mitochondrial activity to translational and transcriptional control. Yeast limits Leu and Val import and instead relies on their synthesis, allowing BCAA production to reflect mitochondrial anabolic capacity. Reduced Val synthesis activates Gcn2, whereas reduced Leu synthesis inhibits TORC1, together decreasing translation efficiency and restricting growth. This response lowers levels of the transcriptional repressor Mig1, suppressing the Warburg/Crabtree effect and promoting alternative carbon source utilization. Remarkably, pharmacological inhibition of Leu/Val synthesis induces this metabolic reprogramming even in nutrient-rich medium, indicating that mitochondrial BCAA synthesis can partially override other nutrient-sensing pathways. Thus, BCAA synthesis couples mitochondrial anabolic capacity to Gcn2 and TORC1 activity and, through translational control of transcription factor abundance, shapes cellular metabolism.

articles.title: SIR2-mediated filament assembly activates the NLR-like protein Avs5 for bacterial antiviral defense
articles.abstract: Like mammalian nucleotide-binding and oligomerization domain receptors (NLRs), bacterial NLR-like proteins mediate antiviral defense. Avs5, a representative of a large family of short bacterial NLR-like proteins, contains an N-terminal SIR2 effector, a central nucleotide-binding domain (NBD), and a C-terminal sensor domain. Whereas canonical inflammasome NLRs use NBD oligomerization to nucleate effector-domain filaments, Avs5 forms SIR2-mediated filaments that couple receptor assembly to NADase activation. In the resting state, ATP-bound Avs5 is monomeric and subsequently forms a SIR2-mediated dimer that likely represents an intermediate in a stepwise activation pathway. Upon activation, ATP-dependent conformational remodeling of the NBD promotes conversion of these dimers into active filaments. Structure-guided mutagenesis, biochemical assays, and functional analyses show that filament assembly is required for efficient NAD+ hydrolysis and antiphage defense. These findings reveal an effector-driven activation mechanism and extend the principles by which NLR proteins couple higher-order assembly to immune defense across domains of life.

articles.title: Single-cell multi-omics reveals archetypal regulatory programs shared across T cell subsets
UFSP2 constitutes a targetable vulnerability via deUFMylation-dependent activation of AKT oncogenic signaling
articles.abstract: AKT hyperactivation is a hallmark of many human cancers and contributes to poor clinical outcomes, yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we show that AKT undergoes UFMylation, and loss of AKT UFMylation promotes colorectal tumor development and confers resistance to the AKT inhibitor AZD5363 (capivasertib). Furthermore, p53 activates ubiquitin-fold modifier 1 (UFM1) during the cell cycle to inhibit AKT activity. Conversely, AKT phosphorylates UFM1 to reduce its own UFMylation, establishing a feedback loop that sustains AKT activity. Moreover, we provide evidence that UFSP2 functions as a major cellular deUFMylase for AKT, and genetic ablation or inhibition of UFSP2 suppresses AKT activity to retard tumorigenesis in vivo. Together, these findings provide a mechanistic framework for UFMylation-dependent AKT regulation and support further investigation of UFSP2 inhibition as a potential strategy to modulate AKT signaling in colorectal cancer.

articles.title: Tumor digital twins uncover therapeutic strategies in triple-negative breast cancer
articles.abstract: Victori et al. present a mechanistic computational model of triple-negative breast cancer that integrates prior biological knowledge with patient data from the PARTNER clinical trial. These personalized tumor digital twins recapitulate treatment responses, identify mutational and transcriptomic response biomarkers, and recommend targeted therapies, highlighting their potential to support precision oncology.

articles.title: 5-Hydroxy-2(5 H )-furanone (HFO) – a versatile and bio-based platform chemical
articles.abstract: 5-Hydroxy-2(5 H )-furanone (HFO) emerges as a versatile bio-based platform chemical, combining renewable accessibility, rich multifunctional reactivity, asymmetric synthesis potential, and routes to high-value chemicals and sustainable materials alike.

articles.title: Transition metal-catalyzed carborane cage B–H activation and functionalization: a mechanistic view
articles.abstract: Icosahedral carboranes have extensive applications owing to their unique properties. This review summarizes advances in the mechanistic study of transition metal-catalyzed carborane cage B–H activation and functionalization.

articles.title: Alloy-Assisted Formation of Vanadium-Rich Thiophosphates with Enhanced Charge Transport and Glassy Magnetism
articles.abstract: Vanadium-based thiophosphates in the MPQ3/M2P2Q6 family provide an unusual platform for coupling mixed-metal valence, metal vacancies, and 2D magnetism, but access to phase-pure multimetal solid solutions with verified chemical homogeneity remains limited. Here, we show that multication alloying provides a route to incorporating V into layered thiophosphates while retaining the mixed-valent, vacancy-containing character of V2−xP2S6. This approach yields Fe1.25V0.6P2S6, Ni1.25V0.6P2S6, Co1.25V0.6P2S6, and high-entropy V-containing compositions. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction (scXRD) and electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) mapping confirm formation of layered single-phase alloys and chemical uniformity both across the surface and through the flake thickness. Optical measurements show semiconducting band gaps spanning ∼1.33−1.66 eV, while temperature-dependent transport reveals markedly enhanced conductivity and low activation energies (∼0.2−0.3 eV) relative to conventional divalent TM2P2S6 analogs. Oxidation-state mapping indicates robust mixed-valent V2+/V3+ character consistent with defect-assisted hopping and self-doping linked to vanadium vacancies, likely causing enhanced conductivity. Magnetic measurements further show composition-dependent behavior, consistent with magnetic frustration and glassy components in Fe1.25V0.6P2S6 and (VMnFeCoNi)2P2S6, highlighting the role of multimetal disorder in shaping exchange interactions. Together, these results establish a route to phase-pure, conductive V-containing thiophosphate alloys and expand the tunable design space for coupled transport and magnetism in layered chalcophosphates.

articles.title: Linking Thermal Expansion to Transient Porosity in a Pair of Highly Flexible Activated 3D Zn(II)-Based MOFs
articles.abstract: Two Zn(II)-based mixed-ligand metal−organic frameworks (MOFs) were synthesised using solvothermal methods and fully characterized (SCXRD, PXRD, TGA, DSC, FTIR, HSM). The MOFs are formulated as [Zn2(NDC)2(AzPy)2]n˙n(DMF)3 (ZNA150-DMF) and [Zn(NDC)(AzPy)0.5]n˙n(DMF)0.5 (ZNA90-DMF), where NDC2− = 2,6-naphthalene dicarboxylate, AzPy = 4,4′-azopyridine and DMF = N,N′-dimethylformamide, and are synthesized at 150 °C and 90 °C, respectively. Single crystal X-ray diffraction analysis confirmed that ZNA150-DMF and ZNA90-DMF are non-interpenetrated and triply interpenetrated, respectively. Both MOFs are highly flexible, displaying large changes in their unit cell parameters and void space features upon desolvation with the void space of both desolvated forms (ZNA150-act and ZNA90-act) consisting of isolated voids, thus leading to transient porosity, where these isolated pockets temporarily connect into channels to facilitate sorption. ZNA90-act carbon dioxide sorption isotherms have inflection points indicating a pressure-sustained structural change, as proven by variable-pressure single crystal and powder X-ray diffraction studies on ZNA90-act immersed in a CO2 gas environment. Variable-temperature single crystal X-ray diffraction studies on both activated MOFs, in the absence of gas, show that these are highly flexible, displaying colossal thermal expansion properties with changes in void space features. These changes tend towards what was observed for ZNA90-act under CO2 pressure, thus possibly linking flexible MOF behavior under the two sets of conditions.

articles.title: Predictive Inorganic Synthesis Based on Machine Learning Using Small Data Sets: A Case Study of Hydrodynamic Diameter-Controlled Copper Nanoparticles
articles.abstract: Copper nanoparticles (Cu NPs) have a broad applicability, yet their synthesis is sensitive to subtle changes in reaction parameters. This sensitivity, combined with the time- and resource-intensive nature of experimental optimization, poses a major challenge in achieving reproducible and size-controlled synthesis. While machine learning (ML) shows promise in materials research, its application is often limited by scarcity of large high-quality experimental data sets. This study explores ML to predict the DLS-derived hydrodynamic diameter of Cu NPs from microwave-assisted polyol synthesis using a small data set of 25 in-house performed syntheses. Latin hypercube sampling is used to efficiently cover the parameter space while creating the experimental data set. Ensemble regression models successfully predict hydrodynamic diameters with good predictive performance given the limited data set. Since quantitative regression requires a unique DLS-derived hydrodynamic diameter, the regression model is restricted to monomodal DLS distributions, while a complementary classification model identifies synthesis conditions for which quantitative prediction is applicable. Using equivalent out-of-sample validation (OOB and LOOCV), the ML and DoE models showed comparable generalization (MAE = 40.92 and 40.46 nm, respectively). The final ensemble model achieved an R2 of 0.74, an MAE of 23.81 nm, compared to an R2 of 0.60, an MAE of 33.54 nm for the DoE model, while retaining the complete synthesis parameter space, making it better suited for synthesis guidance. Additionally, classification models using both random forests and large language models (LLMs) are evaluated to distinguish between large and small particles. These classification models exhibited only modest predictive performance, indicating that this small data set is insufficient to fully exploit the capabilities of complex LLMs. Overall, this study demonstrates that carefully curated small data sets, paired with robust classical ML, can effectively support the synthesis of Cu NPs and highlights that for lab-scale studies, complex models like LLMs may offer limited benefits. The validation experiments further indicate the potential of ML guided synthesis to improve the efficiency of experimental optimization and reduce resource consumption.

articles.title: Quantitative Investigation of Spatial Inhomogeneity of Transition Metal Deposition in Commercial Automotive Cylindrical Cells under Overvoltage Conditions
articles.abstract: Transition metal (TM) dissolution from the cathode and deposition on the anode in lithium−ion batteries is a key degradation mechanism, yet its spatial distribution in commercial cylindrical automotive-grade cells remains insufficiently understood. In this study on lithium−ion cells 18650 with a NMC811/graphite technology, we reveal a pronounced radial inhomogeneity in cathode metal deposition on the anode, with significantly higher accumulation in the inner windings of the jelly roll compared to the outer regions, identifying a critical vulnerability in the cell design while operating in overvoltage conditions. Spatially resolved near-edge edge X-ray absorption fine structure measurements further highlight this geometry dependence, revealing a higher fraction of Ni4+ in the inner windings, whereas the outer regions are dominated by Ni2+. This radial gradient correlates with intrinsic geometric characteristics of cylindrical cells, where the smaller bending radius in the inner windings may plausibly contribute to elevated mechanical stress, higher compressive pressure, and reduced heat dissipation in the cell core. The findings directly link cell geometry to both the extent and chemical state of TM deposition, proving its central role in degradation processes.

articles.title: A Female-Specific Life Course Approach to the Prevention and Management of Cardiovascular Disease: A Presidential Advisory From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in women, contributes markedly to healthcare expenditures, and is projected to increase substantially by 2050 if current trends continue. There is growing recognition of the complex role of sex as a biologic variable and its influence on cardiovascular health and disease. However, cardiovascular risk remains underrecognized and underaddressed in girls and women, particularly as it relates to female-specific exposure to sex hormones (both endogenous and exogenous), which are systemic modulators of cardiovascular biology. Moreover, girls and women uniquely experience fragmented care spanning specialties, including pediatrics, adolescent medicine, primary care, obstetrics and gynecology, maternal-fetal medicine, cardiology, endocrinology, hematology, and neurology. Consequently, there is a need for a unified life course approach that addresses the female-specific interconnectedness of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health. To address these gaps, the American Heart Association, in collaboration with the American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine, established a Female Life Stage framework to optimize the prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in girls and women. Physiologic changes in sex hormones define clinically distinct life stages (ie, perimenarche, ovarian cycling, perimenopause, postmenopause), which directly inform female-specific considerations for screening, prevention, and management of cardiovascular disease. This presidential advisory details the framework and its scientific rationale, highlights opportunities for implementation across settings, and identifies priorities for research, clinician education, patient advocacy, and policy. This framework offers a transformative opportunity to equitably improve cardiovascular health for all girls and women.

articles.title: Cardiac Allograft Vasculopathy Demonstrated by Coronary Angiography and Histopathological Correlates
Care Pathways to Support People Living With Heart Failure

Comprehensive Centers of Excellence for Women’s Cardiovascular Care: A Science Advisory From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine
articles.abstract: Improving cardiovascular health in women is an urgent public health priority given the persistent and pervasive gaps in awareness, prevention, and management of cardiovascular disease in this population. Advances in scientific understanding have led to increased recognition of female-specific considerations in cardiovascular disease, which informed the development of the Female Life Stage construct by the American Heart Association in collaboration with the American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine. This construct integrates assessment of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health across life stages. However, gaps remain in operationalizing this construct and optimizing the delivery of patient-centered, interdisciplinary care among women. Over the past several decades, women’s cardiovascular centers have emerged as leaders, expanded rapidly, and elevated the recognition of cardiovascular diseases that exclusively, disproportionately, or differently affect women (eg, myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries, spontaneous coronary artery dissection, Takotsubo syndrome). In this science advisory, we describe the current landscape of women’s cardiovascular centers and propose a national infrastructure to support the expansion of dedicated Comprehensive Centers of Excellence for Women’s Cardiovascular Care. These centers are conceptualized as interdisciplinary care models comprising 4 defining pillars: interdisciplinary clinical care, education and training, research, and community engagement. By establishing integrated pathways that span clinical disciplines, these centers can reduce fragmentation, enhance earlier risk identification, and expand opportunities to increase representation of women in clinical research. In doing so, they offer a bold opportunity for a scalable and equitable model to improve cardiovascular health for all women.

articles.title: Consensus Guidance for the Female-Specific Prevention and Management of Cardiovascular Disease: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine
articles.abstract: There is growing recognition that the optimal prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in girls and women requires attention to sex-specific considerations relevant to the interconnected domains of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health across the life course. Dysregulation in these health domains tends to co-occur and is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease. However, healthcare for girls and women is uniquely fragmented across clinical specialties, including pediatrics, adolescent medicine, primary care, obstetrics, maternal-fetal medicine, gynecology, cardiology, endocrinology, hematology, and neurology. Furthermore, inconsistent alignment across society guidelines contributes to missed opportunities to optimize cardiovascular health. Therefore, the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine convened a multisociety science advisory group and developed the Female Life Stage construct. This construct defines 4 distinct and clinically meaningful stages—perimenarche (S1), ovarian cycling (S2), perimenopause (S3), and postmenopause (S4)—to enable female-specific screening, prevention, and treatment considerations. In addition, this construct incorporates pregnancy as a unique modifying life event when cardiovascular risk may emerge or be unmasked (eg, adverse pregnancy outcomes). This scientific statement crosswalks major society guidelines, synthesizes the evidence, and provides consensus-based clinical guidance for each Female Life Stage and interconnected health domain (ie, hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health). We conclude with a call to action to improve clinical workflows, enhance clinician education, and address scientific and implementation gaps to improve cardiovascular health in girls and women.

Effect of Activin Type II Receptor Signaling in Patients With HFpEF and Pulmonary Hypertension: A Critical Analysis of Biological Mechanisms and Clinical Trials
articles.abstract: The totality of evidence indicates that the mechanisms underlying the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with combined postcapillary and precapillary pulmonary hypertension (CpcPH) associated with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) differ meaningfully from those responsible for the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension. CpcPH-HFpEF is a complex disorder involving the pulmonary veins, left atrium, and pulmonary arterioles, but recent evidence has highlighted a potentially central role for pulmonary venous and left atrial (LA) dysfunction. Epicardial adipose tissue occupies anatomical proximity to both structures, allowing derivative secretory products to influence their structure and function. The most well-characterized proinflammatory adipokine released from an expanded epicardial fat mass is activin A, which causes fibrosis and cardiomyocyte stiffness and senescence in underlying tissues by signaling through activin type II receptor signal transduction. Such signaling regulates pulmonary venular responses to mechanical stretch, and circulating activin A is elevated in patients with HFpEF who have enlarged LA chambers, pulmonary venous hypertension and increased pulmonary vascular resistance. The adipokine hypothesis of HFpEF identified activin A and activin type II receptor signaling as key adipokine mediators in the pathogenesis of HFpEF. Experimentally, activin A signaling promotes the development of both atrial myopathy and HFpEF, and activin type II receptor ligand traps alleviate HFpEF and ameliorate both the pulmonary vascular and left heart abnormalities in experimental models in which CpcPH-HFpEF is induced by obesity. These collective observations led to the prospective hypothesis that adipokine modulation by sotatercept would mediate benefits on the left heart in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF. These expectations were validated when the CADENCE trial showed that sotatercept decreased both pulmonary artery wedge pressures and left atrial volume index in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF, which are effects that could not explained by a decrease in pulmonary vascular resistance. Activin A released from an expanded epicardial adipose tissue promotes both pulmonary venous and left atrial remodeling and fibrosis in vivo, which (in turn) are effects that can be attenuated by an activin A decoy. The efficacy of sotatercept to slow the progression of CpcPH-HFpEF is now being tested in a phase III outcomes trial.

Outcomes of Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome by Subtype and Presence of Ventriculocoronary Connections: A Fetal Heart Society Multicenter Retrospective Study
articles.abstract: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) is classified by anatomic subtype: mitral atresia and aortic atresia (MA/AA), mitral stenosis and aortic atresia (MS/AA), and mitral stenosis and aortic stenosis (MS/AS). The MS/AA subtype is associated with ventriculocoronary connections (VCCs). We assessed whether specific HLHS subtypes are associated with an increased risk of mortality and whether this risk is stratified by VCCs identified during fetal or postnatal echocardiography. We also assessed whether the type of neonatal intervention performed modified the risk. We performed a multicenter retrospective cohort study of fetuses and infants <2 months old with HLHS who were admitted between January 2012 and December 2016 to participating Fetal Heart Society institutions. Clinical and demographic data were collected. Fetal and transthoracic echocardiograms from a subset of patients with MS/AA and those with suspected VCCs were reviewed. Cox proportional hazards analysis was performed, controlling for cardiac center (random effect), birth weight, genetic diagnosis, extracardiac malformation, and restricted/intact atrial septum. Among 16 centers, 591 patients were born alive with intention to treat. MA/AA was the most common subtype (261, 44%), followed by MS/AA (200, 34%) and MS/AS (130, 22%). Of those with MS/AA, 115 (58%) had suspected VCCs. Median follow-up was 9.0 (interquartile range: 7.0, 10.8) years. Overall transplant-free survival (TFS) was 55.6% at 5 years and 49.4% at 10 years. When comparing MA/AA, MS/AS, and MS/AA with and without VCCs (reference group: MS/AA without VCCs), MS/AA with VCCs had the lowest TFS (hazard ratio [HR], 1.69 [1.12, 2.57]; 5-year TFS, 44.7%; 10-year TFS, 40.3%). This was followed by MA/AA (HR, 1.40 [0.95, 2.05]; 5-year TFS, 54.1%; 10-year TFS, 46.6%). Survival of MS/AA without VCCs (5-year TFS, 60.4%; 10-year TFS, 56.9%) was similar to MS/AS (HR, 0.91 [0.59, 1.41]; 5-year TFS, 65.0%; 10-year TFS, 58.3%). Among those with a prenatal diagnosis of HLHS (n=532), patients with MS/AA and VCCs suspected on fetal echocardiogram had a lower TFS compared with those with MS/AA without fetal suspicion for VCCs (HR, 1.79 [1.12, 2.85]). Fetal echocardiography was used to diagnose VCCs in 33 of 103 (32%) cases with MS/AA and VCCs suspected postnatally. Of patients with MS/AA and VCCs, type of stage I palliation was not associated with TFS ( P =0.784). In a large, multicenter cohort of HLHS patients, the MS/AA subtype with VCCs had the lowest TFS. Prenatal diagnosis of VCCs was associated with a lower TFS. This study underscores the prognostic value of assessing for VCCs in patients with HLHS both before and after birth.

ROR2 Drives Right Ventricular Heart Failure Through Disruption of Proteostasis
articles.abstract: No therapies exist to reverse right ventricular failure (RVF), and the molecular mechanisms that drive RVF remain understudied. We recently reported that the developmentally restricted noncanonical WNT receptor ROR2 (receptor tyrosine kinase-like orphan receptor 2) is upregulated in human RVF in proportion to severity of disease. Here we test the mechanistic role of ROR2 in RVF pathogenesis. ROR2 was overexpressed or knocked down in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes and then characterized using confocal microscopy, RNA sequencing, proteomics, proteostatic functional assays, and pacing to assess contractile properties. The impact of cardiac ROR2 expression was evaluated in mice by AAV9-mediated overexpression and by AAV9-mediated delivery of short hairpin RNA to knockdown ROR2 in a pulmonary artery banded pressure overload model of RVF. ROR2 -modified mice were evaluated by echocardiography, histology, and right ventricle protein synthesis and proteasome capacity. In neonatal rat ventricular myocytes, we find that ROR2 profoundly dysregulates the coordination between protein translation and folding. This imbalance leads to excess protein clearance by the ubiquitin proteasome system with dramatic impacts on sarcomere and cytoskeletal structure and function. Inhibiting the ubiquitin proteasome system or restoring chaperone expression is sufficient to partially rescue ROR2-induced structural and contractile deficits in cardiomyocytes. In mice, forced cardiac ROR2 expression is sufficient to disrupt proteostasis and drive RVF, whereas conversely Ror2 knockdown partially rescues proteostasis and right ventricle structure and function in a pressure overload model of RVF. In sum, ROR2 is a key driver of RVF pathogenesis through proteostatic disruption and thus provides a promising target to treat RVF.

A comparative legal analysis of migratory bird conservation along the African–Eurasian flyway
articles.abstract: Despite decades of international agreements aimed at biodiversity conservation, millions of migratory birds continue to be illegally killed each year along the African–Eurasian flyway, particularly in the Mediterranean, posing a persistent challenge to global conservation efforts. We compared legal frameworks in 10 countries to determine how implementation gaps have emerged between conservation legislation and enforcement. Using purposive sampling and comparative legal analysis, we examined how international conservation conventions and EU directives have been translated into national legislation and implemented in practice. Our findings revealed a fragmented conservation governance system in which enforcement consistently lags behind legal commitments, contributing to continued biodiversity loss, including the 78% decline in the European turtle dove (Streptopelia turtur) since 1980. Across diverse legal and institutional settings, cultural traditions, economic incentives associated with hunting tourism, and lobbying pressures have repeatedly weakened compliance and enforcement. Although legal penalties range from modest administrative fines to criminal sanctions, inconsistent enforcement limits their deterrent effect. By identifying common patterns across multiple jurisdictions, we identified the institutional factors that sustain implementation gaps and argue that narrowing these gaps will require stronger political commitment, greater enforcement capacity, and explicit recognition of wildlife crime as a serious conservation and environmental offense. Análisis jurídico comparativo de la conservación de aves migratorias a lo largo de la ruta afro‐euroasiática Resumen A pesar de décadas de acuerdos internacionales destinados a la conservación de la biodiversidad, cada año se siguen matando ilegalmente millones de aves migratorias a lo largo de la ruta migratoria afro‐euroasiática, especialmente en el Mediterráneo, lo que supone un desafío persistente para los esfuerzos de conservación a nivel mundial. Comparamos los marcos jurídicos de diez países para determinar cómo han surgido los vacíos de aplicación entre la legislación en materia de conservación y su cumplimiento. Usamos un muestreo intencional y un análisis jurídico comparativo para examinar cómo se han transpuesto a la legislación nacional y se han aplicado en la práctica los convenios internacionales de conservación y las directivas de la UE. Nuestros resultados revelaron un sistema de gobernanza de la conservación fragmentado, en el que la aplicación de la ley va sistemáticamente a la zaga de los compromisos legales, lo que contribuye a la pérdida continua de biodiversidad, incluida la disminución del 78% de la tórtola europea (Streptopelia turtur) desde 1980. En diversos contextos jurídicos e institucionales, las tradiciones culturales, los incentivos económicos asociados al turismo cinegético y las presiones de los grupos de interés han debilitado repetidamente el cumplimiento y la aplicación de la ley. Aunque las sanciones legales van desde modestas multas administrativas hasta sanciones penales, la aplicación inconsistente limita su efecto disuasorio. Cuando identificamos patrones comunes en múltiples jurisdicciones, logramos determinar los factores institucionales que perpetúan las deficiencias en la aplicación de la normativa y sostenemos que, para reducir dichas deficiencias, es necesario un compromiso político más firme, una mayor capacidad de aplicación de la ley y el reconocimiento explícito de los delitos contra la fauna silvestre como infracciones graves en materia de conservación y medio ambiente.

articles.title: A framework to assess trajectories of societal and biological extinction
articles.abstract: Threatened species that are societally extinct, which refers to the loss of a species’ presence in human societies, are less likely to receive conservation attention, potentially resulting in their biological extinction going unnoticed. However, little is known about the process and forms of such extinction. Thus, we aimed to quantitatively demonstrate the concept of societal extinction. We hypothesized that societal extinction leads to reduced conservation efforts for the affected species, which may, in turn, be associated with their biological extinction. We developed a framework for the trajectories between societal and biological extinction that involves four corner states and nine pathways of societal presence that can be characterized using quantitative metrics. A case study was conducted using Google Trends data for species listed on the 2020 Japanese Red List, together with information on private‐sector contributions to conservation. Notably, more than half of the species remained societally threatened, meaning they were close to societal extinction. In contrast, conservation efforts, such as tax donation schemes and nonmonetary corporate contributions, were primarily directed toward societally extant (particularly prevalent) species that were consistently searched over time. A small number of biologically extant species were nevertheless societally threatened, suggesting a potential divergence between the biological and societal status of species. Thus, species that are not only biologically but also societally threatened should be prioritized as targets for public conservation efforts, as they are less likely to receive sufficient support from the private sector. To inform future research efforts, we also summarized data on the societal presence of a selection of species from multiple perspectives beyond Google Trends. Un marco de trabajo para evaluar las trayectorias de la extinción biológica y social Resumen Las especies amenazadas que se encuentran en situación de extinción social, término que hace referencia a la pérdida de la presencia de una especie en las sociedades humanas, tienen menos probabilidades de ser objeto de medidas de conservación, lo que podría dar lugar a que su extinción biológica pase desapercibida. Sin embargo, se sabe muy poco sobre el proceso y las formas que adopta dicha extinción. Por ello, nuestro objetivo fue demostrar cuantitativamente el concepto de extinción social. Planteamos la hipótesis de que la extinción social conduce a una reducción de los esfuerzos de conservación para las especies afectadas, lo que, a su vez, podría estar asociado a su extinción biológica. Desarrollamos un marco para las trayectorias entre la extinción social y la biológica que incluye cuatro estados extremos y nueve vías de presencia social que pueden caracterizarse mediante métricas cuantitativas. Se llevó a cabo un estudio de caso utilizando datos de Google Trends sobre las especies incluidas en la Lista Roja de Japón de 2020, junto con información sobre las contribuciones del sector privado a la conservación. Cabe destacar que más de la mitad de las especies seguían amenazadas desde el punto de vista social, lo que significa que se encontraban cerca de la extinción social. Por el contrario, los esfuerzos de conservación, como los programas de donaciones fiscales y las contribuciones corporativas no monetarias, se dirigieron principalmente hacia especies socialmente existentes (especialmente prevalentes) que fueron buscadas de forma constante a lo largo del tiempo. No obstante, un pequeño número de especies biológicamente existentes se encontraban amenazadas desde el punto de vista social, lo que sugiere una posible divergencia entre el estado biológico y el social de las especies.…

articles.title: Detection of trade in products derived from threatened species using machine learning and a smartphone application
articles.abstract: Illegal and unsustainable wildlife trade remains a major conservation challenge and is increasingly shifting to online marketplaces where monitoring is difficult. To address this gap, we used real‐world images from online platforms, enforcement seizures, and market inspections to develop a deep‐learning object detection framework to identify products derived from three highly traded species: elephant, pangolin, and tiger. Our dataset of 39,941 images included both wildlife products and visually similar nonwildlife items, reflecting real enforcement complexity. We used cross‐entropy and asymmetric focal loss functions to train Faster Region‐based convolutional neural network (Faster R‐CNN) models and compared species‐specific and multispecies training strategies. The best‐performing model, trained with cross‐entropy on all species combined, achieved an overall accuracy of 84.2%, with high performance for pangolin (93.6%) and tiger (90.3%) and moderate performance for elephant (71.1%). Although asymmetric focal loss increased recall, it substantially reduced precision. We deployed the optimized model in a prototype smartphone application, potentially usable in real‐world settings for monitoring online images. With an independent test set, the application achieved 91.3% accuracy and an F‐score of 0.86. These results demonstrate the potential of object detection models to support scalable, real‐time monitoring of wildlife trade and enable the rapid triage of suspicious posts, regulatory compliance, and conservation decision‐making. Detección del comercio en productos derivados de especies amenazadas mediante aprendizaje automatizado y aplicaciones en teléfonos inteligentes Resumen El comercio ilegal e insostenible de fauna silvestre sigue siendo un importante reto para la conservación y se está desplazando cada vez más hacia los mercados en línea, donde resulta difícil llevar a cabo una vigilancia eficaz. Para enfrentar esta carencia, utilizamos imágenes reales procedentes de plataformas en línea, incautaciones realizadas por las fuerzas del orden e inspecciones de mercado para desarrollar un marco de detección de objetos basado en el aprendizaje profundo, con el fin de identificar productos derivados de tres especies muy comercializadas: el elefante, el pangolín y el tigre. Nuestro conjunto de datos, compuesto por 39, 941 imágenes, incluía tanto productos de fauna silvestre como artículos no silvestres visualmente similares, lo que refleja la complejidad real de la labor de las fuerzas del orden. Utilizamos funciones de entropía cruzada y de pérdida focal asimétrica para entrenar modelos de red neuronal convolucional basada en regiones más rápidas (faster R‐CNN) y comparamos estrategias de entrenamiento específicas para cada especie y multiespecíficas. El modelo con mejor rendimiento, entrenado con entropía cruzada sobre todas las especies combinadas, alcanzó una precisión global del 84.2%, con un alto rendimiento para el pangolín (93.6%) y el tigre (90.3%), y un rendimiento moderado para el elefante (71.1%). Si bien la pérdida focal asimétrica aumentó la recuperación, redujo sustancialmente la precisión. Implementamos el modelo optimizado en una aplicación prototipo para teléfonos inteligentes, que podría utilizarse en entornos reales para la supervisión de imágenes en línea. Con un conjunto de datos de prueba independiente, la aplicación alcanzó una precisión del 91.3% y un índice F de 0.86. Estos resultados demuestran el potencial de los modelos de detección de objetos para facilitar una vigilancia escalable y en tiempo real del comercio de fauna silvestre, así como para permitir la rápida clasificación de publicaciones sospechosas, el cumplimiento normativo y la toma de decisiones en materia de conservación.

articles.title: Diplochorous Seed Dispersal of Rafflesiaceae by Fruit‐Consuming Squirrels, Rats and Treeshrews, Then Seed‐Burying Dung Beetles
articles.abstract: Understanding seed‐dispersal of Rafflesiaceae species is essential to conserve this extraordinary family of parasitic plants. We present evidence supporting diplochorous seed dispersal, involving primary endozoochorous dispersal by small mammals, followed by secondary exozoochorous dispersal by dung beetles. Methods employed included in situ live capture of small mammals in traps, placed over developing Sapria himalayana fruits, in situ observations of dung beetles handling the small dung pellets of primary dispersers and ex situ experiments with both dispersers. Dung pellet analyses (number, weight, expulsion time and ratio of undamaged to broken seeds) indicated that the most capable primary seed dispersers were the nocturnal rat Maxomys surifer (among four species studied) and, during daytime, the squirrel Dremomys rufigenis and, to a lesser extent, the treeshrew Tupaia belangeri. Dispersal distances were likely to encompass multiple host Tetrastigma spp. (lianas). Dung beetles served as secondary dispersers. They removed all faecal pellets of primary dispersers from the soil surface within 24 h, burying them up to 7 cm deep. The beetles also released seeds from the faecal matrix by microphagy, enabling the seeds to come into intimate contact with hosts' fine roots and root hairs, through which infection likely occurs. Forty‐one beetle species (including seven new species) were involved, with Ochicanthon thai and Onthophagus lindaae being the most abundant. Further research throughout the distribution of Rafflesiaceae species, particularly in the Philippines, regarded as a centre of Rafflesia diversity, is likely to add to primary and secondary disperser diversity.

articles.title: Disentangling the Drivers of Fish Community Variation in a Highly Urbanized Estuary Based on Hierarchical Modeling of Species Communities (HMSC)
articles.abstract: Biodiversity conservation and management in highly urbanized estuaries have garnered widespread global attention. However, the environmental response mechanisms of fish communities in these estuaries remain poorly understood, hindering their ecological health and sustainable development. Here, we utilized Hierarchical Modeling of Species Communities (HMSC), a burgeoning and powerful framework, jointly investigating how the species occurrences, species traits, and spatiotemporal structure of fish communities respond to environmental variables in the Pearl River Estuary (PRE). It exhibited seasonal variation in species composition, taxonomic diversity, functional diversity, and functional‐space occupancy of fish communities, and several CWM traits showed directional seasonal shifts. Furthermore, the HMSC framework showed that environmental filtering was the primary driver of the spatiotemporal dynamics in fish community. Salinity, pH, and phosphate were identified as key environmental drivers of species distributions and trait‐mediated responses. Functional traits showed contrasting responses along the phosphate gradient, whereas habitat‐level residual species associations revealed distinct positive and negative co‐occurrence patterns that reflect shared environmental filtering rather than stochastic assembly. The study elucidates the environmental response mechanisms of fish community dynamics by integrating taxonomic and functional diversity perspectives, offering new insights into the assembly of estuarine fish communities.

articles.title: Geographic Variation in Peromyscus leucopus Population Size and Small Mammal Community Richness in Northern Pennsylvania
articles.abstract: The white‐footed mouse, Peromyscus leucopus, is a generalist species found throughout the eastern and central United States that serves as an important reservoir for many tick‐borne pathogens relevant to human health. Patterns of P. leucopus relative abundance within small mammal communities have been shown to correlate with the prevalence of Borrelia burgdorferi, the main causative agent of Lyme disease, in vector species. However, efforts to investigate patterns of P. leucopus population size and small mammal community structure often lack geographic variation. In this study, we characterized patterns of P. leucopus population size and small mammal community species richness across a broad geographic range in Pennsylvania. Population sizes and small mammal community richness values in northeastern Pennsylvania (mean N̂$$ \hat{N} $$ = 28.6; mean richness = 5.3) were greater than those in northwestern Pennsylvania (mean N̂$$ \hat{N} $$ = 19.7; mean richness = 2.8). Projected changes in climate and the expansion of human‐caused disturbance have the potential to greatly influence the prevalence of P. leucopus in small mammal communities, so regular characterizations of P. leucopus community dynamics will likely be helpful to inform projections and assessments of human exposure to tick‐borne pathogen risk.

articles.title: Multi‐Scale Habitat Drivers of Hainan Gibbon Distribution: Integrating Macro‐Environmental and Fine‐Scale Ecological Factors for Targeted Conservation of Threatened Species
articles.abstract: As habitat fragmentation intensifies due to Anthropocene impacts, ecological variation across spatial scales may cause conservation strategies to misalign with species' actual needs. Understanding how cross‐scale spatial heterogeneity in ecological variables shapes species distributions is therefore critical to optimize conservation prioritization. The Critically Endangered Hainan gibbon is restricted to highly degraded forests, yet the interplay of ecological drivers shaping its current distribution, from macro‐environmental constraints to fine‐scale habitat selection, remains poorly quantified. This study integrates two‐year monitoring data from all seven known Hainan gibbon groups (GA‐GG, representing the global population) using a multi‐scale sampling design. We employed 395 population‐level and 135 group‐level plots to evaluate 23 ecological variables spanning macro‐ (e.g., climate) to micro‐scales (e.g., food plant diversity), identifying drivers of gibbon distribution. We found that population‐scale distribution is driven by climatic and topographic factors (e.g., precipitation, elevation), whereas group‐scale distribution responded to fine‐scale habitat features (e.g., food plant diversity, terrain ruggedness, crown area). GC distribution reflects optimal foraging (preference for food plant diversity), whereas GE adopts an energy‐conserving strategy (selecting complex terrain with high food plant abundance). Habitat suitability followed a J‐shaped threshold response at the population scale, and divergent responses at the group level (rapid in GE, stable in GC). These findings underscore the need for scale‐ and habitat‐specific conservation: expanding climatically and vegetatively suitable areas at the population level, restoring food availability in GE habitats, and maintaining stability in GC habitats. Our multi‐scale mechanistic framework provides actionable conservation insights, with applications for other range‐restricted species in fragmented landscapes.

Analysis of the spatiotemporal pattern and driving mechanism of ecological restoration in the Kubuqi Desert
articles.abstract: The health of desert plant life is closely linked to the stability of the local ecological equilibrium, where both human actions and shifts in climate serve as primary influences on environmental security. This research examined the temporal and spatial variations in vegetation NDVI and climatic elements within the Kubuqi Desert between 2000 and 2023. It utilized partial correlation analysis, multiple linear regression, and the geodetector method to uncover the underlying drivers of NDVI dynamics. Additionally, the study applied an ARIMA model to forecast the NDVI trajectory for the upcoming five-year period. The findings indicated that: (1) Plant life in the Kubuqi Desert has experienced substantial enhancement, with more than 80.61% of the region demonstrating a highly notable upward trajectory in NDVI; nonetheless, the general vegetation is projected to display slight anti-persistence going forward. (2) Annual precipitation, annual average high temperature, and annual average low temperature all showed an increasing trend. (3) Land transfer mainly occurred among barren land, cultivated land, and grassland, with the conversion from barren land to grassland accounting for 15.49%. (4) Precipitation and high temperature are key factors affecting NDVI distribution, with a 2–3month lag effect on NDVI. (5) Vegetation NDVI will show an increasing trend over the next five years. This study will provide certain data support for vegetation restoration strategies in the Kubuqi Desert.

articles.abstract: Human brain cellular xenograft (HBCX) models are emerging as a system to study human brain physiology and pathology in vivo. Mancuso and colleagues discuss how HBCXs enable in vivo interrogation of human-specific brain cell biology, neuroimmunology, disease modeling, and genetic risk and their potential for functional genomics, therapeutic discovery, and preclinical assessment of cell-based therapies for central nervous system disorders.

articles.abstract: Cost-effective Li2ZrCl6 halides with regulated configurational complexity combine rapid lithium-ion conduction with ultralow electronic conductivity and superior oxidative stability. A robust zirconium oxychloride cathode-electrolyte interphase is formed during cycling, enabling 4.4 V all-solid-state LiNi0.85Co0.1Mn0.05O2 batteries to operate for up to 3,700 cycles.

articles.title: Following the rules? Different thermal and temporal life‐stage responses of biometrics across four decades in a songbird population
articles.abstract: Using biometric data collected over 33 years in a Mediterranean population of Great tits we reveal a dynamic phenotypic mosaic where long‐term trends decouple from immediate thermal effects. By integrating life‐stage sensitivities, we show how ontogenetic buffering and life‐history trade‐offs contribute to shape avian responses to a changing climate. Abstract Global warming is widely associated with changes in body size and shape, with these variations typically framed within the context of Bergmann, Allen and the Temperature‐Size rules. However, evaluating phenotypic change only against these rules can limit our understanding of how immediate plastic reactions to temperature interact with long‐term trends. Also, phenotypic responses may differ among life stages, due to their different thermal sensitivity and life‐history role. We examined body size and shape variations across life stages in a Mediterranean great tit (Parus major) population monitored over four decades, during which mean annual temperatures increased by approximately 1.7°C. Adults were the life stage most responsive to temperature and their mass declined by 0.84% for every 1°C of warming, while wing length shortened. Instead, tarsus length, a measure of structural size, increased with temperature in both nestlings and adults at a comparable magnitude, consistent with Allen's rule. Nestling mass near fledging showed no thermal response. Among reproductive traits, clutch size tended to decrease with temperature without reaching statistical significance and egg mass showed no thermal response, yet total clutch mass, an integrated measure of reproductive output, declined significantly with warmer laying temperatures. Long‐term temporal trends did not consistently mirror these thermal effects. Adult mass declined across the study period, matching the direction of its thermal response, whereas adult tarsus length shortened over time despite lengthening with temperature. Wing length and nestling mass both remained stable. Egg mass declined and clutch size increased across the study period, despite their lack of thermal response. These results demonstrate that while warming can proximately affect body size, long‐term temporal trends can be decoupled from immediate thermal effects, and that mass and structural size do not necessarily vary together. This creates an underappreciated mosaic of phenotypic responses across life stages and generations, with potential consequences for fecundity, morphology and fitness. Our findings highlight the importance of integrating ontogenetic perspectives into evolutionary ecogeographic theory and raise questions about which ‘rules’ will govern the trajectories of avian populations under climate change.

Drought legacies weaken resistance and plant‐mycorrhizal associations but not recovery
articles.abstract: Repeated drought reduced resistance under the most severe drought conditions, yet this mesic grassland recovered rapidly once drought ended. At the same time, AM fungal colonization of the dominant grass remained reduced, revealing a mismatch between above‐ground recovery and below‐ground legacies and showing that different ecosystem components can recover at different rates. Abstract Drought legacies can shape how grasslands respond to increasingly frequent climate extremes, yet their influence on future resistance and recovery remains unclear, particularly in mesic grasslands, where productivity is strongly linked to precipitation availability. Using a long‐term field experiment, we tested how zero, one or two prior experimentally imposed extreme droughts influenced grassland resistance to a subsequent 4‐year extreme drought (2018–2021) and recovery after drought in 2022. We quantified above‐ground net primary productivity and species composition, as well as plant functional traits and arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungal colonization of the dominant grasses at the site, to evaluate above‐ and below‐ground legacy effects. Differences in productivity resistance among drought‐legacy treatments were small during the first three drought years and became evident only in the final, most severe drought year, when resistance was lowest in plots exposed to two prior droughts. However, above‐ground productivity recovered to similar levels across all treatments in 2022, demonstrating substantial short‐term recovery despite contrasting drought histories. The dominant grass, Andropogon gerardii, exhibited higher specific leaf area and greater leaf production during the recovery year, indicating increased investment in rapid resource capture and regrowth. Additionally, AM fungal colonization of A. gerardii declined with repeated drought exposure and remained lowest in plots exposed to two prior droughts even after above‐ground productivity recovered. In contrast to these traits and below‐ground changes, species composition, including richness, evenness, turnover and absolute cover, remained stable across all treatments and years. Synthesis: Repeated drought reduced resistance under the most severe drought conditions, yet this mesic grassland recovered rapidly once drought ended. At the same time, AM fungal colonization of the dominant grass remained reduced, revealing a mismatch between above‐ground recovery and below‐ground legacies and showing that different ecosystem components can recover at different rates.

articles.title: Aligned Self-Assembled Nanostructure by Chemical Force Trigger, Biased Migration, and Oscillatory Hydrogel Growth
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Cells generate pico-to-nanonewton forces through metabolic circuits and diffusion for downstream processes, including stress fiber assembly and cellular growth. The inherent complexities of the system’s processing, reactivity, and adaptability make it difficult to recapitulate in a synthetic setting. Herein, we compartmentalized the urease-urea feedback-controlled reaction network (FCRN), demonstrating global vs local function adaptability by coupling with peptide self-assembly. Compartmentalized FCRN (c-FCRN) facilitates chemical energy-to-mechanical energy conversion, creating forces on the piconewton scale, allowing nanofiber alignment, akin to what a cell does. The trade-off between multiple microscale interactions in the chemo-material network implies molecular-biased migration resembling chemotactic-like directed motion in synthetic settings, which promotes spatial self-assembly remodelling. Consequently, regulating the reaction-diffusion chemistry, we demonstrate oscillatory hydrogel growth by encasing the c-FCRN with a physical membrane barrier. Furthermore, c-FCRN provides a rudimentary structure-building system to create various complex hydrogel structures, bypassing the 3D printing tools. Thus, the chemo-material network provides proof-of-concept for biomimetic material development by emulating biologically inspired technologies.

articles.title: Amorphous Halide Cathodes Enable 75C All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Power delivery in all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) is often pursued by maximizing the bulk ionic conductivity of cathode active materials (CAMs), while grain-boundary (GB) ion-transport barriers caused by lattice mismatch remain a major kinetic bottleneck. Here, we reveal that minimizing GB transport barriers, rather than simply enhancing intrinsic conductivity, unlocks ultrafast ion-transport in halide CAMs. Amorphization converts crystalline LiVCl4 into a conformal amorphous phase that preserves short-range V–Cl coordination while minimizing long-range ion-transport tortuosity. Despite lower bulk Li+ conductivity, amorphous LiVCl4 dramatically reduces GB-associated interfacial resistance and enables a catholyte-free cathode (CAM content: 90 wt %) to deliver a capacity of 74.3 mAh g–1 at 5 mA cm–2, compared with 10.2 mAh g–1 for the crystalline counterpart. Meanwhile, the ASSLB further operates across a wide temperature range from −30 to 60 °C and achieves 84.2% capacity utilization at an ultrahigh A-LiVCl4 areal loading of 53.4 mg cm–2. Coupled with amorphous LiTaOCl4, the ASSLB achieves 102.1 mAh g–1 at 20 mA cm–2 (∼75C) and retains 82.3% capacity after 16,000 cycles. These results establish amorphization-enabled conformal interfaces as a new paradigm for ultrahigh-power ASSLBs.

articles.title: Cisplatin Conjugated with Vinylsulfonamide Cross-Links Pyruvate Kinase M2 to Trigger Ferroptosis
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Cisplatin serves as a first-line chemotherapeutic agent due to its DNA binding property. However, this intrinsic electrophilicity drives off-target interactions with proteins, which compromises anticancer efficacy, and also suggests the presence of unexplored targets. To identify platinum-binding proteins, a class of platinum(II) complexes containing a covalent vinylsulfonamide group were designed to provide stronger affinity for target engagement. By using competitive chemical proteomics technology, pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) was identified as the direct target of Pt1. The intracellular binding involved the recognition of the Cys49 pocket via cis-platinum moiety, which was strengthened by the synergistic event of platinum-centered ligand exchange and vinylsulfonamide-mediated covalent anchoring. This effective multimodal interaction disrupted PKM2 oligomerization and promoted its nuclear translocation. Subsequently, Pt1 induced ferroptosis via the PKM2-HMOX1 axis, further enhanced by mitochondrial oxidative stress. In xenograft models, Pt1 exhibited antitumor efficacy comparable to that of cisplatin, along with lower hepatotoxicity. This study presents a cisplatin conjugate that induces ferroptosis through intramolecular protein cross-linking, providing a synergistic coordination-covalent strategy for nonclassical platinum-based therapeutics.

articles.title: Comparing Nuclear Reaction Coordinates Driving Photoinduced Proton-Coupled Electron and Energy Transfer
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Proton transfer is coupled to electron transfer or electronic excitation energy transfer in proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) and proton-coupled energy transfer (PCEnT) reactions, respectively. Although photoinduced PCET and PCEnT have been studied extensively in anthracene–phenol–pyridine molecular triads, the nuclear reaction coordinates for these two pathways are still unknown. Herein, we identify the nuclear reaction coordinates for PCET and PCEnT in the triads by sampling the seam space between the relevant intersecting diabatic states. The reaction coordinate has contributions mainly from anthracene and phenol for PCET but involves the entire triad, including pyridine, for PCEnT. Both reaction coordinates involve motions related to contraction of the phenol C–O bond as well as motions within the anthracene rings that differ for PCET and PCEnT due to different charge distributions. The proton acceptor motion contributes more to the PCEnT than the PCET reaction coordinate. Both PCET and PCEnT reactions are concerted in that there is no stable intermediate, but they are both most likely asynchronous. Our analysis also suggests that PCET proceeds through a conical intersection in its minimum energy pathway, whereas PCEnT moves through an avoided crossing. The quantum mechanical treatment of the transferring proton within a vibronically nonadiabatic framework suggests that the kinetic isotope effect may be greater for PCEnT than for PCET, although more extensive calculations are required for confirmation. Understanding the fundamental similarities and differences between PCET and PCEnT mechanisms will help guide the design of proton-coupled systems that favor either charge transfer or energy transfer.

articles.title: General Synthesis of Inverse Opal Covalent Organic Framework Photonic Crystals
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Constructing highly crystalline inverse opal covalent organic framework photonic crystals (IO COF PhCs) remains challenging due to the incompatibility between the spatial confinement required for inverse opal replication and the synthesis process of COFs. Inspired by the semi-solid chitin infiltration and confined solidification process in beetle photonic architectures, a solvent-free template-assisted melt pressing (STAMP) strategy is developed for the general synthesis of crystalline IO COF PhCs. The quasi-solid precursor state facilitates efficient template infiltration while remaining reactive for COF crystallization, affording ordered macroporous photonic architectures within 3 min. This strategy is broadly applicable to a library of 16 COFs spanning β-ketoenamine, hydrazone, imine, and imide linkages, yielding decimeter-scale monoliths with designable structural colors across the visible spectrum. By integrating periodic macroporosity, permanent framework porosity, and photonic functionality into one material platform, the resulting IO COF PhCs enable cross-scale programmable optical encoding and visually self-reporting adsorption. The application potential of IO COF PhCs is demonstrated for biomimetic anti-counterfeiting patterns and structural-color-indicated Au capture. This work establishes a general route toward crystalline IO COF PhCs and provides a versatile platform for coupling molecular functionality with photonic regulation in advanced smart materials.

articles.title: Harnessing Surface Wrinkling Instability for Visualizing Dynamic Chemistry in Polymer Networks
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Studying dynamic chemical behaviors is fundamental to understanding and regulating the dynamic responses and functions of polymer materials. However, real-time, intuitive, and selective visualization of these molecular processes─particularly when multiple dynamic motifs coexist─remains a major challenge. Herein, we introduce surface wrinkles as a visualization platform that directly translates dynamic chemical behaviors in polymers into observable macroscopic morphological changes. Using a dual-cross-linked polymer network (DCN) containing quadruple hydrogen bonds and mechanical bonds as a model system, we fabricate stable wrinkles via modulus mismatch in a bilayer architecture. In situ microscopy reveals that acid-triggered dissociation of quadruple hydrogen bonds causes rapid wrinkle erasure due to network disruption, whereas base-induced rotaxane sliding leads to gradual wrinkle erasure owing to network relaxation, reflecting their distinct dynamic mechanisms and time scales. Rheological analyses on single-cross-linked model networks corroborate these macroscopic observations at the molecular level. Moreover, by programming wrinkle patterns with “write–hide–read” functionality, we achieve macroscopic visualization and differentiation of microscopic dynamic processes. This work establishes surface wrinkling as a powerful and intuitive platform for real-time monitoring of dynamic chemistry and provides valuable insights for designing functional polymer materials with tunable macroscopic properties.

articles.title: Macrocycle Size-Controlled Dynamic and Static Chirality in Donor–Acceptor [2]Catenanes
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Chiral [2]catenanes, a prominent class of mechanically interlocked molecules (MIMs), can exhibit either static or dynamic mechanostereochemistry. Controlling these mechanostereochemical states without altering the covalent connectivity, however, remains challenging. Herein, we report a series of chiral [2]catenanes derived from ExBox and cycloparaphenyleneperylene (CPPP), whose dynamic behavior is altered by the size of the CPPP macrocycle. We identified a sharp, size-dependent threshold: The conformational stereogenic unit of [7]CPPP is kinetically locked, whereas those of [8]CPPP and [9]CPPP are dynamic at room temperature. This conformational stereochemistry strongly biases the co-conformational stereochemistry in the catenane, effectively resulting in a single dominant diastereomer. This effective coupling of the two stereogenic units allows the conformational stereochemistry to be biased by the ion pairing of the interlocked cationic ring with a chiral anion. This research highlights the potential of mechanically interlocked architectures for controlling the dynamic mechanostereochemistry.

articles.title: Mechanistic Insights of Electroreductive Cobalt-Catalyzed Asymmetric Radical Addition
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Transition-metal-catalyzed asymmetric electroreduction has emerged as a compelling platform for enantioselective C–C bond formation, with notable advances in electroreductive cross-coupling. Translating this success to stereocontrolled radical additions across unsaturated bonds remains a formidable challenge, particularly for the construction of fully substituted stereogenic carbon centers. Herein, we report an electroreductive, cobalt-catalyzed asymmetric radical addition of diverse organohalides to α-imino esters. This protocol delivers enantioenriched α-quaternary amino acid derivatives in up to 95% ee, completely circumventing the need for stoichiometric metal reductants. Beyond its synthetic utility, the electrochemical platform uniquely enables the direct interrogation of the operative electron-transfer events. A comprehensive mechanistic study─encompassing cyclic voltammetry, in situ electrochemical EPR spectroscopy, DFT calculations, stoichiometric experiments, and radical-trapping experiments─elucidates a highly orchestrated catalytic manifold. Crucially, we demonstrate that the α-imino ester serves a dual role, acting as both a radical acceptor and a redox-active ligand for the chiral cobalt catalyst. Subsequent cathodic reduction of the resulting cobalt–imine complex generates a key low-valent species that engages the alkyl halide via a turnover-limiting single-electron transfer (SET) to produce the requisite alkyl radical. Overall, this work establishes a robust electrochemical framework that synergizes reaction innovation with fundamental mechanistic elucidation in asymmetric radical catalysis.

articles.title: Quantum Ghost Spectroscopy Reveals Hidden Coherence in Molecular Aggregates
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Ultrafast spectroscopy of complex molecules has been achieved under light–matter coupling by the use of laser pulses and single photons. Yet, the excited-state dynamics essential to photochemistry is suffering from the convolution of multiple relaxation pathways and limited resolution in nonlinear signal, which still remain challenging. To address these, we develop time-resolved quantum ghost spectroscopy (tr-QGS) with entangled light, which enables a background-free detection of excited-state emission while offering precise control over temporal resolution. We apply this approach to perylene bisimide (PBI-1) trimers by combining a quantum description of light-molecule interaction with time-dependent density matrix renormalization group (TD-DMRG) simulations. This explicitly includes five vibrational modes and nonadiabatic coupling between electronic states. Our simulations reveal that tr-QGS captures electronic coherence oscillating at 0.6 eV for ∼50 fs, a signature of nonadiabatic coupling that was obscured in time-resolved measurements. Moreover, we observe a direct transfer from electronic to vibrational coherence at 200 fs, providing real-time visualization of vibronic relaxation pathways. Photon entanglement eliminates background noise and ground-state bleaching artifacts, which plague time-resolved measurements. These results establish tr-QGS as a transformative tool for interrogating nonadiabatic dynamics in molecular aggregates, light-harvesting complexes, and photocatalysts, offering a route to reveal quantum coherence effects in chemistry with unprecedented precision.

articles.abstract: Why does corrosion attack specific sites under some conditions but spread uniformly under others? Liang et al. combine real-time nanoscale imaging with atomistic simulations to show that corrosion reflects a competition between local structural heterogeneity and thermodynamic driving force. Near equilibrium, strained regions preferentially corrode and promote localized pitting; far from equilibrium, stronger driving forces overwhelm these local differences and produce rapid, uniform corrosion. The findings provide a framework for understanding and controlling localized material degradation.
