Here, polymer coordination with PVP enables stable, alloying-free α-FAPbI3 thick films by controlling crystallization and lattice strain. The resulting detectors combine high sensitivity, low-dose operation, and fast response, enabling high-resolution, real-time X-ray imaging.

articles.title: An AI‐based and coding‐free integration for forest Leaf Area Index calculation
articles.abstract: Seasonal and spatial variations in Leaf Area Index (LAI, or plant area index, PAI) are challenging to delineate in tropical forests because the changes are often too subtle to be reliably detected. Many existing DHP software tools offer one‐click processing of all images using auto‐threshold segmentation (e.g. HemispheR, HemiPy and Hemisfer), but they produce results with large discrepancies. Some software (e.g. CAN‐EYE) requires manual tuning of each image, making large‐scale analysis impractical. We analysed 19,044 images from four tropical forest subtypes and found that using coding‐free AI software to process hemispherical images can significantly improve the consistency of canopy‐sky segmentation, thereby improving the detection of temporal and spatial variation of PAI. The results show that replacing the auto‐threshold segmentation with AI substantially reduced inter‐software disagreement, with the mean inter‐software range for PAI decreasing from 4.31 to 1.19, and delineating correct seasonal and spatial patterns. CAN‐EYE could identify the correct seasonal patterns but produced less accurate results than the CAN‐EYE‐AI integrated approach due to subjective bias. The high consistency achieved after AI integration enables reliable cross‐site and temporal comparisons. As users can combine the AI segmentation with other DHP software, our integrated, affordable and coding‐free method offers wide applicability and high consistency of PAI measurements, facilitating the advancement of tropical forest monitoring and research.

articles.title: Every scientist a modeller? The promise and peril of AI‐assisted mechanistic models
articles.abstract: Mechanistic models, expressed as simulations that can be run and visualised, are a powerful way to understand biological and other systems. Building them, however, requires formulating mathematical or rule‐based descriptions and translating them into working code, skills that many ecologists and other disciplinary researchers do not have. Generative AI can now perform much of this translation, making mechanistic modelling accessible to researchers, educators and students previously excluded by its technical demands. But delegating this translation to AI also carries real risks: modelling assumptions can become hidden, plausible but incorrect code can pass unnoticed, and the skills and critical habits that model building once developed may never form. We examine the benefits and risks of using generative AI as a modelling companion at each stage of model development (conceptual specification, formalisation, implementation and exploration), drawing on recent experimental evidence on AI‐assisted learning and on a worked predator–prey example built with AI, with a rule‐based epidemic model as a parallel case. At each stage we identify where consequential decisions are silently delegated to the AI and set out practical mitigations that keep human judgement engaged without requiring the technical skills AI has made optional: specifying the conceptual model explicitly before engaging AI, having the AI translate its formalisation back into plain language, testing the implementation against outcomes known from domain knowledge and designing the interface to support interrogation. This new opportunity is substantial: researchers, educators and students who understand their systems but have never been able to build models of them are now able to explore these systems mechanistically, testing how components interact and how the system responds to conditions it has not yet experienced, questions that correlative approaches alone cannot answer. Used carelessly, AI risks eroding modelling skill for little lasting benefit, but used deliberately, in the ways set out here, it opens a new pathway to mechanistic understanding without removing the critical thinking the old technical barrier once enforced.

Complementary Metal-Oxide Semiconductor-Compatible Phototransistor Platform for Neuromorphic Broadband Vision
articles.abstract: Photodetection and neuromorphic computing promises sensing at the edge, yet most optoelectronic synapses lack spectral breadth or scalable silicon integration. Here we report a dual-gate synaptic transistor integrating colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) with a silicon-on-insulator (SOI) channel in a complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS)-compatible platform. This architecture synergistically combines the SOI channel for efficient charge transport and signal amplification with the CQD layer serving a dual role as a broadband absorber (300–1700 nm) and a charge-trap medium. The device exhibits a responsivity of 639 A W–1 and specific detectivity exceeding 3 × 1012 Jones at 1550 nm, parallelly emulating short- and long-term plasticity, multilevel conductance tuning, and highly programmable synaptic dynamics. The top gate enables reversible potentiation and depression, and self-powered operation supports low-power sensing and light-driven learning. We demonstrate system-level utility in a synaptic array that achieves pattern recognition with peak accuracy exceeding 96%, establishing a pathway to silicon-integrated, energy-efficient neuromorphic vision.

Giant Resistance Switching Ratio Exceeding 106 through a Reversible 2D–3D Structural Phase Transition in Nonequilibrium (Pb1– x Sn x )Se Thin Films
articles.abstract: Control and switching of electrical resistance in semiconductors are important for high-performance electronic devices. Here, we realize giant resistance switching in nonequilibrium (Pb1–xSnx)Se films through a reversible structural transition between three-dimensional (3D) rock-salt (RS)-type and two-dimensional (2D) GeS-type phases. The solid-solution films were fabricated by reactive solid-phase epitaxy of SnSe/PbSe bilayers followed by rapid thermal quenching. Se-flux annealing of the PbSe template suppressed Pb precipitation, enabling chemically homogeneous, single-phase nonequilibrium RS-type films up to x = 0.58. Increasing the Sn content from x = 0.43 to 0.58 systematically increased the 2D–3D structural transition temperature and enhanced the resistance switching ratio to 4.9 × 106, far exceeding those of representative transition-metal oxide thin films (∼102–104). The giant resistance switching originates from the nearly complete transformation (∼98%) of the conductive 3D phase into the high-resistance 2D phase. These results establish crystal-dimensionality switching as a promising new mechanism for high-performance electronic switching devices.

articles.title: Long-Range Single-Molecule Transport and Assembly at Liquid Nitrogen Temperatures
articles.abstract: The bottom-up construction of functional matter from individually positioned atoms and molecules requires deterministic control over capture, transport, and assembly on surfaces. Although atomic manipulation is well established, extending comparable control to molecules remains challenging due to their complex internal degrees of freedom and surface interactions. Here, we demonstrate controlled single-molecule transport and assembly at liquid nitrogen temperatures using a scanning tunneling microscope. We designed a molecule with an intrinsic electric dipole moment, enabling efficient noncontact manipulation via electrostatic coupling to the tip. This strategy allows stable long-range translation and the programmable formation of defined dimers and larger assemblies. Systematic mapping of the operational parameter space, supported by first-principles calculations, identifies an electrostatic driving mechanism governing motion. Our approach shifts molecular nanomachine research from demonstrations under extreme cryogenic conditions to positional control under experimentally more accessible temperatures, establishing a practical platform for programmable molecular-scale engineering.

articles.title: Programming-Current-Induced Mechanism Crossover Enables Reconfigurable Memory Window in In2Te3 Selector-Only Memory
articles.abstract: Selector-only memory (SOM), which integrates threshold switching and data storage within a chalcogenide layer, is a promising high-density memory technology, yet the regulation of memory characteristics and underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here we demonstrate that programming current (Ip) regulates the competition between composition-driven and trap-associated switching processes in amorphous In2Te3 devices. Decreasing Ip from 10–2 to 10–4 A reversibly changes the positive-read threshold voltage (Vth) ordering from Vth, SET > Vth, RESET, yielding an inverted memory window of up to 1.53 V, to Vth, SET < Vth, RESET, with a conventional memory window of ∼0.5 V. Cross-sectional energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy reveals state-dependent In/Te redistribution at high Ip, consistent with composition-mediated modulation of conductive pathways. At low Ip, atomic redistribution is suppressed and trap-associated transport modulation is enhanced, with extracted trap depths of 0.51 eV (SET) and 0.63 eV (RESET), establishing Ip as a means of modifying SOM memory characteristics without complex engineering.

articles.title: Spontaneous Nanoscale Wiggling in Cleaved WTe2
articles.abstract: Structural deformation of crystal lattices has emerged as a powerful pathway to engineer and boost electronic properties through lattice geometry. However, realizing ultrafine structural modulations remains challenging without external strain imposed by substrates, prestrain, or artificial patterning. Here, using scanning tunneling microscopy, we show that the cleaving process spontaneously induces nanoscale wiggling in 1T′-WTe2 without such external strain sources. Furthermore, scanning tunneling spectroscopy reveals pronounced electronic reconstruction and spatially resolved spectral modulations between the top and valley regions of the wiggling. Combined with first-principles calculations, our results show that this wiggling substantially modifies the local electronic structure relative to the unstrained flat region, suggesting electronic structure reconstruction driven by spontaneous lattice deformation. These findings establish spontaneous nanoscale wiggling as a self-formed structural modulation for local electronic-structure engineering in strain-sensitive low-symmetry layered materials.

articles.title: Stacking-Order-Dependent Electronic Properties of MoTe2/WSe2 Moiré Bilayers
articles.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) moiré bilayers have realized a wide range of strongly correlated and topological phenomena. The physics in these materials is often sensitive to the interlayer stacking order. Polarization-resolved optical second harmonic generation (SHG) is the most used technique for stacking order characterization but unverified for most heterobilayers. Here we calibrate the optical SHG for angle-aligned MoTe2/WSe2 bilayers by the scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM). We directly compare the transport and magnetic properties and the electronic phase diagram for two distinct stacking orders. With the calibrated stacking order assignment, we clarify the interpretation of earlier results, including the nature of the Chern insulator, mechanism of an electric-field-tuned metal–insulator transition at half band filling, and the Kondo lattice physics. Our work provides a consistent picture of the relation between the stacking order and the electronic properties of MoTe2/WSe2 moiré bilayers.

articles.abstract: Understanding the triggers of autoimmunity might lead to better therapies, with hair loss among the conditions for which underpinning factors have come to light.

articles.title: The Selfish Gene, 50 years on — it’s time for an update
articles.abstract: A focus on the gene alone has become outdated. Books that capture the complexity of life deserve centre stage.

articles.title: Women might have invented language — but not alone
articles.abstract: An eloquent analysis of the origins of human speech suggests that social cohesion, not conflict, drove our use of words.

articles.title: A double debris disc around a white dwarf sculpted by two planetary bodies
articles.abstract: Scientists discovered a white dwarf star circled by two nested rings of gas that were probably shaped by two hidden planetary bodies, one asteroid-sized and one Pluto-sized. The star’s unusual four-peaked light signature reveals a striking new kind of planetary debris system.

articles.title: Retention of primordial atmospheres through giant impacts
articles.abstract: Giant impacts help rocky planets retain hydrogen-rich atmospheres because accreted mass increases atmospheric gravitational binding more than collisional heating drives atmospheric loss. This may explain the bimodal radius distribution of exoplanets.

Enzymatic oxidative esterification with an unconventional regioselective control
articles.abstract: Regioselective esterification remains challenging, particularly when multiple alcohol groups with similar reactivity are present. Now it has been shown that aldehyde dehydrogenases can be engineered into oxidative ester synthases with programmable alcohol selectivity, enabling controlled ester bond formation through active-site remodelling.

articles.title: Building materials and emissions from rebuilding under increasing climate-driven flood hazards
articles.abstract: This study shows that expected annual replacement material demand and rebuilding emissions from floods across Europe could rise more than tenfold by 2080, highlighting the need for flood adaptation and climate mitigation.

articles.title: Declining spring production in the Barents Sea ice zone under climate forcing
articles.abstract: Barents Sea spring primary production has markedly declined over recent decades, driven by reduced nutrient and light availability, with potential implications for the stability of Arctic food webs and biodiversity.

articles.title: Engineered d-p orbital hybridization unlocks dilute CO2 electrolysis to byproduct-free CH4-rich syngas
articles.abstract: Electrochemical conversion of CO2 from dilute flue gas into methane remains limited by complex byproducts. Here, the authors integrate a tin-nickel catalyst into flow cells to convert captured CO2 directly into methane-rich syngas with near-zero multicarbon byproducts.

articles.title: Plasmonic vortex cavities toward the ultra-compact limit
articles.abstract: Optical vortices enable optical orbital angular momentum science and technology, but their spot size limits nanoscale integration and interactions with matter. This study uses a plasmonic cavity to compress their radii toward the ultra-compact limit.

articles.title: Trace H2O2-triggered Fenton-like reaction by secondary coordination sphere in iron-based metal-organic frameworks
articles.abstract: Fenton-like water treatment is limited by inefficient hydrogen peroxide activation and short-lived reactive radicals. Adding nearby nitrogen sites to iron metal-organic frameworks boosts peroxide use and traps radicals, enabling rapid pollutant removal.

articles.title: A CD4-lineage erythro–myeloid progenitor within the adult bone marrow defines an alternative pathway for macrophage generation
articles.abstract: Tissue-resident macrophages originate from distinct developmental sources, but their adult replenishment is thought to depend exclusively on circulating monocytes. Here Tikoo and colleagues identify a CD4-lineage erythro–myeloid progenitor (EMPROR) in the adult bone marrow that provides an alternative pathway for macrophage generation.

articles.title: The EMPROR’s new groove
articles.abstract: Two studies shed new light on macrophage origins. Perivascular macrophages derive from extraembryonic erythromyeloid progenitors arising at a newly discovered hematopoietic site at the maternal–fetal interface and a related population of adult bone marrow progenitors.

articles.title: The maternal–fetal interface is an early hematopoietic niche enriched in distinct erythro-myeloid progenitors
articles.abstract: Jain et al. identify a unique extraembryonic hematopoietic niche at the maternal–fetal interface that is distinct from the yolk sac and is capable of producing CD4+CSF1R− erythro-myeloid progenitors.

articles.abstract: As presented at the ESMO Congress 2026: In the global phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE trial, neoadjuvant durvalumab plus chemotherapy in patients with resectable and borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer, followed by multidisciplinary reassessment, enabled surgery in most patients, leading to encouraging pathological complete response rates, and no additional safety concerns were reported when patients with unresectable tumors continued with chemoradiotherapy and consolidative durvalumab.

articles.abstract: Acute myelin injury responses are well defined, but microglia adaptations to chronic damage remain unclear. Mouse models reveal a chronic demyelination-associated microglial state marked by inflammation, lysosomal dysfunction and myelin-damaging activity.

articles.title: Microglial NUS1 deficiency drives dopaminergic neurodegeneration through intercellular iron dysregulation in Parkinson’s disease models
articles.abstract: Using cellular and mouse models, this study reports that deficiency of the Parkinson’s disease risk gene NUS1 in microglia disrupts intercellular iron homeostasis, leading to neuronal iron overload and dopaminergic neurodegeneration.

articles.title: A simple twist to altermagnetism
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional altermagnets hold promise for next-generation spintronics but remain difficult to synthesize. Now, altermagnetism has been observed in an orthogonally twisted van der Waals homostructure, opening possibilities for ultrathin devices.

articles.title: Curvature and cell mechanics control tissue organization
articles.abstract: Tissue geometry mechanically regulates cell behaviour across scales. Now, it can be predicted when cells switch from full adhesion to rapid partial detachment on curved surfaces.

articles.title: Three-dimensional cell morphology is mediated by curvature sensing and interfacial stress
articles.abstract: Cells adhering to micro-curved surfaces can exhibit either complete adhesion or partial interior detachment. This is now found to be determined by the balance between the cell contractile stress and the cell–substrate adhesion stress.

articles.title: Single-cell tumour phylogenetics
articles.abstract: Single-cell sequencing has transformed the study of tumour evolution by enabling high-resolution reconstruction of cancer phylogenies. This Review discusses the models, assumptions and computational approaches underlying single-cell tumour phylogeny inference, and it highlights emerging applications in cancer biology, patient stratification and evolutionary forecasting.

articles.title: Reconstructing Cenozoic grasslands in North America and western Eurasia: evidence for cold‐season grasses from 3D phytolith morphology
articles.abstract: Pie charts illustrate the composition of fossil grass silica short‐cell phytolith (GSSCP) assemblages at investigated fossil sites in the United States and Türkiye and representative 3D meshes of classified phytoliths. Summary Pooideae, the largest grass subfamily, radiated in the Northern Hemisphere from the Paleocene onward and today dominates cold‐season and high‐altitude grasslands. Fossil phytolith assemblages suggest pooid‐rich ecosystems during the Oligocene–Miocene, but the lack of quantitative phytolith identification has limited reconstruction of early grassland composition and ecology. We combined 3D geometric morphometrics of grass silica short‐cell phytoliths (GSSCPs) with machine‐learning classification and phylogenetically informed climate modelling. A dataset of modern GSSCPs was used to classify Eocene–Miocene phytoliths from Türkiye and the US Great Plains and reconstruct paleoclimate. 3D GSSCP morphology distinguished modern grass subfamilies and tribes. Fossil assemblages contained mainly phytoliths assigned to Bambusoideae and Pooideae (including Poeae I and II). In modern grasses, Crenate and Polylobate phytolith dimensions correlated with temperature and precipitation. Fossil Crenates and Polylobates yielded climate estimates warmer and wetter than today. Ancestral state reconstructions indicated milder winter conditions at early Pooideae nodes, with cold tolerance arising early. Major temperate grass lineages (Poeae I and II) were established earlier than previously recognized, and Pooideae‐rich grasslands were present by the Oligo‐Miocene under warmer, wetter climates than today. These findings demonstrate the value of 3D phytolith morphometrics for interpreting early grassland evolution.

articles.title: Clinical training exposure and perceived stress among nursing students: Examining the moderating role of social support
articles.abstract: by Majed M. Aljabri, Bandar S. Alharbi, Endale Alemayehu Ali Background Psychological stress is highly prevalent among nursing students. The clinical exposure is a major factor contributing to psychological stress, but there is a lack of consistent evidence, particularly in the context of Middle Eastern countries. The aim of this study was to quantify the association between clinical exposure and perceived stress among nursing students, and to assess whether perceived social support moderates this relationship. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study among nursing students from King Saud University. The Perceived Stress Scale was used to measure psychological stress, and the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support was employed to measure perceived social support. The clinical exposure was quantified as the average number of hours spent per week. We employed multivariable linear regression to determine the association. The regression analysis was adjusted for age, gender, living arrangements, and employment status. Results Higher perceived social support was significantly associated with lower perceived stress (β = −0.05, 95% CI −0.09 to −0.01). Clinical exposure was not significantly associated with perceived stress. Students living alone had significantly lower levels of perceived stress (β = −0.37, 95% CI −0.63 to −0.11), as did students working part-time (β = −0.34, 95% CI −0.54 to −0.13). The interaction model revealed that perceived social support was inversely associated with perceived stress levels (β = −0.14, 95% CI −0.23 to −0.04). A statistically significant interaction was observed among students with less than 10 hours of clinical exposure per week. This exploratory finding suggests that the association between perceived social support and stress may differ among students with limited clinical exposure. However, the finding was based on a single statistically significant interaction and should be considered preliminary and hypothesis-generating. Conclusions Higher perceived social support was associated with lower levels of perceived stress among nursing students. Interventions aimed at enhancing the social support system may be beneficial in reducing stress, especially during the early clinical exposure period.

articles.title: Comparative longitudinal evaluation of DIMS, progressive addition and single-vision lenses on myopia progression, binocular and visual performance in Spanish children
articles.abstract: An 18-month prospective, non-randomized comparative observational study evaluated the effects of different optical corrections on myopia progression, binocular vision, and visual performance in Spanish children. Forty-five myopic participants aged 9–14 years were allocated to single-vision lenses (SV), low-addition progressive addition lenses (PALs), or defocus-incorporated multiple segments lenses (DIMS). Assessments included spherical equivalent (SE) and axial length (AL), comprehensive accommodative function evaluated by measuring amplitude of accommodation, positive and negative relative accommodation, accommodative facility, and accommodative response, and binocular function evaluated by measuring phorias, fusional vergences, and stereopsis. In addition, contrast sensitivity (CS), visual disturbance index (VDI), and subjective visual quality were assessed at baseline and at 6, 12, and 18 months. After 18 months, SE progression was −0.59 D for SV, −0.51 D for PALs, and −0.30 D for DIMS, corresponding to a 49% reduction with DIMS compared to SV. AL increased by 0.24, 0.27, and 0.23 millimeters, respectively, although inter-group differences were not significant for AL. Accommodative and binocular functions, visual acuity, CS, and VDI remained stable, while distance stereopsis improved in the DIMS group. These findings suggest an association between DIMS lens wear and reduced myopia progression compared with SV lenses in this cohort, without clinically relevant differences in accommodative or binocular function, visual acuity, or subjective visual quality.

articles.title: Continued post-weaning social isolation is associated with persistent, sex-specific changes in sociability and social interaction dynamics in mice
articles.abstract: Early social experience is critical for the maturation of social behavior, and its disruption during juvenile development may confer long-term psychiatric vulnerability. Juvenile social isolation (j-SI) after weaning is widely used as a model of early social deprivation; however, its developmental and sex-specific effects on spontaneous social interaction remain unclear. We examined the behavioral consequences of post-weaning social isolation in male and female C57BL/6J mice (Mus musculus). Mice were individually housed from postnatal day (P)21, and spontaneous social interaction was assessed longitudinally at P35, P49, and P63 during prolonged cage-based sessions using an augmented reality-based behavioral monitoring system. Locomotor activity, inter-mouse distance, mean contact duration per initiated encounter, and interaction dynamics were quantified during the light and dark phases. Juvenile social isolation was associated with greater inter-mouse distance across most developmental stages and sex-phase combinations, whereas reductions in mean contact duration per initiated encounter varied by sex, developmental stage, and light/dark phase. Locomotor activity varied by developmental stage and sex, with late-emerging increases particularly evident during the dark phase in isolated mice. In contrast, lower interaction-partner switching in isolated males was detected only at the earliest stage (P35) during the light phase. An important design feature is that isolated mice were reunited at testing with cage mates from which they had been separated for more than two weeks and were therefore effectively unfamiliar, whereas group-housed mice were tested with continuously familiar cage mates; the reported effects therefore reflect social isolation together with its intrinsic reduction in social familiarity. These findings indicate that continued post-weaning social isolation is associated with persistent, sex-specific alterations in sociability and social interaction dynamics. Our results further suggest that juvenile social experience may shape the developmental maturation and temporal organization of social interaction across adolescence and early adulthood.

articles.title: Defining clinically meaningful pain reduction after spinal injections using an 11-point numerical rating scale and patient-reported relative reduction of pain
articles.abstract: Background We aimed to establish thresholds for assessing clinically meaningful pain improvement after spinal injections using numerical rating scale (NRS) and patient-reported relative reduction (PRR) of pain. Methods This single-center retrospective study included 1,828 patients who received spinal injections at our spinal intervention center and completed a 2-week follow-up telephone interview in 2017. NRS absolute and relative reductions were calculated using the NRS scores before injection and at follow-up. The PRR and 5-point global perceived effect (GPE; 1, completely recovered; 2, much improved; 3, slightly improved; 4, no change; and 5, worsened) were recorded. The mean ± standard deviation (SD) of NRS absolute reduction, NRS relative reduction, and PRR in the GPE 2 and 3 subgroups were calculated. Receiver-operating-characteristic curve analysis was used to determine the cutoffs for NRS absolute and relative reduction and PRR in predicting the substantial clinically important difference (SCID, GPE 1–2) and minimal clinically important difference (MCID, GPE 1–3). Results The mean ± SD of NRS absolute and relative reduction, and PRR in the GPE 2 and GPE 3 were 4.5 ± 1.8, 65.4% ± 21.1%, and 67.7% ± 14.8% and 2.4 ± 1.4, 36.8% ± 22.5%, and 35.7% ± 16.1%, respectively. The cutoffs for predicting SCID and MCID were NRS absolute reduction of ≥3 and ≥1, NRS relative reduction of ≥50% and ≥10%, and PRR of ≥50% and ≥20%, respectively. Conclusions The NRS absolute and relative reduction and PRR thresholds were established to differentiate SCID and MCID in terms of pain improvement after spinal injections.

articles.title: Dissociation between muscle activation, spinal joint load, and subjective perception in passive back support exoskeleton use
articles.abstract: One important purpose of back support exoskeletons (BSEs) is to reduce the stress to the lumbar spine and alleviate the low back pain. However, most previous studies introducing BSEs have argued for their effectiveness based only on easily measurable physiological outcomes such as muscle activation. Motivated by this gap, we examined whether the muscle activation of the back muscle during load handling with a passive BSE can faithfully reflect the estimated L5–S1 joint reaction forces and subjective perceptions. Experiments involving 12 healthy young adults revealed that the BSE significantly reduced average thoracic erector spinae muscle activation during both lifting and lowering the load, and lumbar erector spinae muscle activation during lowering. The BSE also reduced integrated thoracic erector spinae muscle activation during lowering. L5–S1 joint reaction forces were also significantly reduced by the BSE (p < 0.001). Participants reported a lower rate of perceived exertion (p < 0.05). However, the lack of associations among all metrics suggests that inferring one measure from another remains limited when evaluating the efficacy of a BSE.

articles.title: Does low confidence drive reliance on AI, or does reliance erode confidence? A four-wave RI-CLPM study of chinese language and literature undergraduates
articles.abstract: Generative AI tools are now routinely used by Chinese Language and Literature majors for tasks once considered the province of individual literary craft: drafting verse, shaping narrative prose, revising fiction. Two competing accounts describe what this means for students’ confidence in their own creative writing. A cognitive-offloading account holds that repeated reliance on AI displaces the mastery experiences through which writing self-efficacy is built, so reliance erodes confidence over time. A compensatory-use account holds the reverse: students whose confidence is already low turn to AI to avoid the discomfort of unassisted composition, so low confidence drives reliance. Cross-sectional and standard cross-lagged designs cannot separate these accounts because they confound stable between-person differences with genuine within-person change. We addressed this using a random-intercept cross-lagged panel model (RI-CLPM) across four waves spanning one academic year among Chinese Language and Literature undergraduates (N = 390 recruited; N = 387 analyzed under full-information maximum likelihood, of whom 298 supplied complete four-wave data). Generative AI writing reliance (GAWR) and literary creative writing self-efficacy (LCWSE) were assessed at each wave. The trait-level association between the two constructs was negative and could not be distinguished from zero (r = −.342, Δχ²(1) = 2.26, p = .133). At the within-person level, declines in self-efficacy predicted subsequent increases in reliance (β = −.276, p p = .072). We state explicitly that this second result is not interpretable as evidence against erosion: a Monte Carlo power analysis put this design's power to detect an effect of that magnitude at 53.2%, close to a coin flip, so the erosion pathway is undetermined in these data and this null supplies no basis for concluding that erosion does not operate. A direct comparison of the two cross-lagged paths favored compensation (Δχ²(1) = 8.83, p = .003; bootstrap 95% CI for the difference [.020, .218] across 5,000 resamples), with the qualification that this comparison sets an adequately powered estimate against an underpowered one and therefore describes what this design was able to detect. Compensation is the pathway this study establishes; whether reliance also erodes confidence over a longer horizon is an open question. We discuss implications for writing pedagogy in Chinese Language and Literature programs and for how underpowered null results should be interpreted in AI-in-education panel research.

articles.title: Epidemiological characterization of avian influenza virus circulation in pigeons and quail across different production systems in Chattogram, Bangladesh
articles.abstract: Pigeons and quail contribute to poultry production, nutrition, and livelihoods in Bangladesh; however, their role in avian influenza virus (AIV) circulation remains poorly understood. These poultry species are widely reared and traded alongside chickens and ducks in household farms, commercial systems, and live bird markets, where inadequate biosecurity may create an overlooked ecological niche for AIV circulation, reassortment, and potential zoonotic spillover. Between November 2021 and April 2022, we conducted a cross-sectional study in Chattogram, Bangladesh, to estimate the prevalence and subtype-specific distribution of AIV and to identify factors associated with AIV positivity in pigeons and quail. A total of 300 birds (108 pigeons and 192 quail) were sampled from households, commercial farms, and live bird markets. Oropharyngeal and cloacal swabs were collected from each bird and tested for the AIV matrix gene using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction, followed by subtype-specific detection of H5, H7, and H9. Data collected from bird owners and traders included bird demographic characteristics, bird source, and health status using a structured questionnaire. The overall prevalence of AIV was 14.3% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 10.6–18.8). Quail had a higher prevalence (18.2%, 95% CI: 13.0–24.4) than pigeons (7.4%, 95% CI: 3.3–14.1). Among detected subtypes, H9 was most prevalent (11.3%, 95% CI: 7.9–15.4), followed by hemagglutinin (HA)-untyped (2.7%, 95% CI: 1.2–5.1) and H5 (0.3%, 95% CI: 0.001–1.8), while H7 was not detected. Quail had higher odds of AIV positivity than pigeons (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 4.1, 95% CI: 1.8–10.6); clinically sick birds (aOR = 2.9, 95% CI: 1.4–6.2) and birds sampled from household farms (aOR = 2.8, 95% CI: 1.2–6.5) also had higher odds of AIV positivity. These findings indicate that pigeons and quails, which are understudied poultry species, may contribute to the maintenance and transmission of AIV within mixed poultry production and marketing systems in Bangladesh. Integrating these species into routine AIV surveillance is therefore necessary to strengthen early detection, inform control strategies, and reduce the risk of zoonotic spillover.

articles.title: Exploratory baseline mucosal transcriptomics and vedolizumab response in ulcerative colitis
articles.abstract: Currently, there are still no reliable pre-treatment biomarkers for vedolizumab in ulcerative colitis. To investigate baseline mucosal signals, we reconstructed the discovery cohort from GSE73661 and evaluated the derived panel in the blood samples from GSE191328 and the independent mucosal RNA-seq cohorts from E-MTAB-7845. The reconstructed cohort comprised 24 baseline samples, including 14 composite responders and 10 non-responders. Through repeated LASSO variable selection, the study identified an exploratory gene set consisting of ZNF689, TPRXL, ZC3H10, and MRPL55. The selection procedure yielded a mean held-out AUC of 0.611 across 18 complete nested-validation repetitions; this does not independently validate the final gene set. When the fixed gene set was projected exploratorily, the AUC for 17 blood samples was 0.458 (95% CI 0.162–0.755), and the AUC for 27 independent UC mucosal samples was 0.534 (95% CI 0.293–0.775). The apparent AUC of this gene set on the discovery set was 1.000, and 500 full-process bootstrap analyses indicated that gene selection was unstable. Among the three targeted inflammatory panels, interferon-γ showed a directional difference that was not statistically significant (mean GSVA score difference −0.425; nominal P = 0.066; adjusted P = 0.197). Expression scales and clinical endpoints differed across cohorts. The above results describe post-selection separation within the discovery cohort and do not establish reproducible predictive performance, tissue specificity, or a definitive four-gene signature.

articles.title: Expression of Concern: Spatial and temporal differences and convergence analysis of multidimensional relative poverty in ethnic areas
From sounds to sentences: A longitudinal study of phonological and emergent literacy predictors of early writing in Turkish children
articles.abstract: This longitudinal study examines how preschool children’s phonological awareness and emergent literacy skills relate to their early writing performance in first grade. Conducted within the context of a transparent Turkish orthography, the study aims to identify early cognitive-linguistic correlates of subsequent writing development. A total of 97 children (aged 66–77 months) from preschools in a socioeconomically diverse Turkish district were followed over two academic years. In the first year, participants were assessed using the LAP-3 Early Literacy Subtest and the Phonological Awareness Test to measure their emergent literacy and phonological skills. One year later, their writing performance was evaluated using a validated sentence construction assessment. Non-parametric statistical tests and correlation analyses were conducted to examine developmental variations and relationships among the variables. Results revealed statistically significant correlations between early writing performance and both phonological awareness (r = .46, p < .01) and emergent literacy (r = .32, p < .01). Specific sub-skills such as syllable segmentation, rhyming awareness, and letter-sound correspondence showed the strongest associations with writing performance. These skills did not differ significantly by age or gender. The findings highlight the foundational role of preschool phonological and emergent literacy skills in early writing development. This study contributes empirical data from a transparent orthography. Given the correlational design, these findings should be interpreted as evidence consistent with developmental literacy theories rather than as confirmation of causal or predictive mechanisms; they emphasize the importance of early identification and instructional support in preschool settings to promote future writing success.

articles.title: Gene density homogeneity is disrupted by repetitive DNA Expansion
articles.abstract: The democratization of sequencing has led to a wealth of high-quality genome assemblies from across the Tree of Life. One pattern that has emerged is that chromosomes within a genome can vary drastically in their gene density (e.g., human chromosomes 13 and 19, with gene densities of 17.5 and 60.5 genes per megabase, respectively). To our knowledge, the cause of this variation in gene density has not been explored. In this study, we leveraged genome assemblies of 262 vertebrate species to examine the range of within-genome variation in gene density. We combined gene density data with repeat landscape analyses in each species. We predicted that genomes with more recently expanded repeat families should show greater variation in gene density, because repetitive elements accumulate unevenly across the genome, while chromosomal rearrangements such as fusions, fissions, insertions, deletions, and inversions homogenize gene density over time. Our empirical analysis reveals a significant yet variable effect of repeat expansions, with additional processes likely contributing to variation in gene density.

articles.title: Grb2 phosphorylation antagonizes EGFR-driven ras activation by interfering with condensate assembly
articles.abstract: by Henry T. Phan, Chun-Wei Lin, Brittany L. Stinger, Joseph B. DeGrandchamp, L. J. Nugent Lew, Serena J. Huang, Jay T. Groves Upon ligand binding, the kinase domain of EGFR phosphorylates multiple tyrosine residues on the receptor cytoplasmic tail through a trans-autophosphorylation process. Phosphotyrosine sites on activated receptors recruit Grb2, which further recruits SOS to initiate downstream signaling by activating Ras. Multivalent binding between SOS and Grb2, as well as direct Grb2:Grb2 interactions, contribute to formation of a protein condensate of activated EGFR. The condensed state of EGFR facilitates autoinhibition release in SOS and exerts regulatory control over signal propagation from activated EGFR to Ras. While kinase activity of EGFR is an essential driver of this signaling process, phosphorylation at residue Y160 on Grb2 blocks Grb2:Grb2 binding and can interfere with EGFR condensation. Here, using a reconstituted system, we examine how titrating kinase activity in the EGFR system can both promote and inhibit signal output to Ras. The results reveal how effects of tyrosine kinase inhibition can, under some circumstances, promote Ras activation by inhibiting negative feedback through Grb2 phosphorylation and disruption of a Grb2 SH2/SH3 dimer interface.

articles.title: Hydraulic performance of 14-G hemodialysis catheters versus an 8-Fr arterial cannula in a mock 3-kg small-dog cardiopulmonary bypass circuit
articles.abstract: Arterial cannulation for cardiopulmonary bypass in small dogs is challenging because small vessel diameters may preclude use of appropriately sized pediatric arterial cannulas. Although off-label use of 14-gauge hemodialysis catheters has been reported, their pressure–flow characteristics under small-dog cardiopulmonary bypass conditions remain unclear. This in vitro study evaluated one 8-French pediatric arterial cannula and six 14-gauge hemodialysis catheter specimens—separate side-hole and sealed specimens at effective lengths of 25, 32, and 38 mm—in a closed-loop mock circuit for a 3-kg small dog. A 34% (w/w) glycerol–water solution (viscosity 2.8 cP at 28°C) served as an approximate Newtonian blood analogue. The Stockert S5 pump flow-rate setting was increased from 50 to 350 mL/min; 50–300 mL/min was prespecified as the primary analysis range and 350 mL/min as exploratory. The reported outlet pressure was recorded 1,000 mm upstream of the test device, while inlet pressure was monitored 300 mm downstream and regulated to 60 mmHg; six technical runs per condition were conducted using the same physical device and circuit setup. Within the primary analysis range, outlet pressure was approximately 136–137 mmHg at 300 mL/min; mean differences for the 14-G specimens versus the 8-French cannula were +0.33 to +0.67 mmHg, with 95% confidence intervals from −1.33 to +2.15 mmHg. At 350 mL/min, outlet pressures were higher for all three side-hole 14-gauge specimens than for the 8-French cannula. At 300 mL/min, outlet pressure was approximately 2–3 mmHg lower for the side-hole specimens than for the sealed specimens across all catheter lengths. Together, these findings indicate small observed circuit-level differences in outlet pressure among tested devices within this standardized mock small-dog cardiopulmonary bypass circuit, but do not establish formal equivalence, device-to-device interchangeability, or clinical validity.

articles.title: Intersectional stereotypes: How age and race shape perceptions of women in the United States
articles.abstract: This study examined the influence of older age and race (White/Black/Arab) on stereotypes of women. To evaluate whether age and race shape stereotype content for an intersectional group relative to its superordinate racial or superordinate older age identities, 525 Amazon Mechanical Turk participants were asked to list up to five words or short phrases that most people associated with these target groups. Overall, the study found stronger support for a distinctiveness hypothesis, whereby the most distinct identity of an individual’s intersectional identity influenced their associated characteristics. For example, because being White is common in the United States, old White women had more stereotypes in common with their old superordinate identity than their White identity. This suggests that the nation’s population characteristics may be predictive of the stereotypes associated with different intersectional groups. Overall, this research reveals the complex interplay between stereotypes of age and race for women, underscoring the need to acknowledge intersectional identities and cultural norms. Such insights can enhance our pursuit of inclusive and accurate societal perceptions.

articles.title: MIF inhibitor ISO-1 attenuates ischemia-reperfusion injury in a rat model of donation after circulatory death liver transplantation
articles.abstract: Macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) is an early mediator of ischemia–reperfusion injury (IRI), however, the evidence on its role in orthotopic liver transplantation (OLT), particularly with donation after circulatory death (DCD) grafts is limited. Given its key regulatory function, this study investigated the effects of IRI on graft injury and assessed whether the use of ISO-1, a small-molecule MIF-inhibitor, affect IRI in a rat DCD-OLT model. 196 male Lewis rats were randomized into DBD control, DCD-30 min, DCD-60 min, DCD-30 + ISO-1, and DCD-30 + vehicle groups (n = 7/group/time-point). ISO-1 was administered before controlled cardiac arrest (0–60 min) and 3 h cold preservation before arterialized OLT. Animals were sacrificed at 1, 3, 24, and 168 h post-reperfusion. DCD grafts showed marked injury, with the DCD-60 group exhibiting lethal IRI. ISO-1 significantly reduced early hepatocellular injury compared with vehicle (AST:294 ± 63 vs 867 ± 211 IU/L, p = 0.017) and resulted in values comparable to DBD controls. Serum HMGB-1 (11 ± 2.8 vs 26 ± 6.2 pg/mL, p = 0.045) and MIF (45 ± 5.3 vs 144 ± 27.5 ng/mL, p = 0.034) levels were similarly decreased following ISO-1 application. ISO-1 improved graft microcirculation at 24 h, attenuated histological injury, and was associated with an altered time course of CD163 + macrophage infiltration. ISO-1 pre-treatment attenuated hepatocellular injury and was associated with improved graft microcirculation and reduced DAMP release, supporting further mechanistic and translational evaluation in DCD liver transplantation.

articles.title: Multi-scale feature fusion network optimization and edge intelligent detection for transmission line insulator
articles.abstract: In response to the accuracy loss caused by lightweight networks on edge devices and the difficulty in accurately detecting small defect targets, this paper studies the lightweight You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8) transmission line insulator defect detection algorithm based on Three-Branch Attention Mechanism (TBAM) and Enhanced Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Network (EMSFFN), which can perform high-precision detection on edge intelligent devices of unmanned aerial vehicles. Aiming at the problem of significant differences in the number of image categories in the current aerial insulator defect dataset, the dataset was expanded through image data augmentation to generate more minority class samples, balance the number of samples in each category. Experiments show that compared with YOLOv7, YOLOv8, YOLOv9, Detection Transformer (DETR) and Faster Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (Faster R-CNN), the model parameters and computational complexity of TBAM-YOLOv8-EMSFFN are relatively low. Its AP reaches 99.2% and the mAP reaches 98.7%. Therefore, the TBAM-YOLOv8-EMSFFN model is suitable for unmanned aerial vehicles carrying edge intelligent devices to achieve power inspection.

articles.title: Perceived consequences of extreme risk protection orders: A qualitative study of respondents from California
articles.abstract: by Veronica A. Pear, Christopher E. Knoepke, Lisa B. Geller, Amy Barnhorst, Ari Davis, Rose Kim, Garen J. Wintemute Background Extreme risk protection orders (ERPOs) temporarily prohibit the purchase and possession of firearms by people at high risk of harming themselves or others. This study drew on the experiences of ERPO respondents to learn about the perceived short- and long-term consequences of the law. Methods For this qualitative descriptive study, we conducted 24 semi-structured interviews between March and November 2024 with respondents to ERPOs issued in California between 2016 and 2020. We purposively sampled 250 respondents for whom we had previously abstracted ERPO court case data to ensure adequate representation across domains of interest (e.g., demographics, location) and invited respondents to participate in the study by mail. All interviews were recorded, double coded, and thematically analyzed. Results Our diverse participants described heterogeneous consequences across 4 domains: violence risk, legal/economic outcomes, opinions/attitudes, and social/emotional wellbeing. Two participants believed their ERPOs prevented violence and 1 was unsure; the rest believed that they would not have committed violence irrespective of the ERPO. Some perceived the ERPO to have had negligible effects on their lives, while others described both positive consequences, including self-reflection and behavior change, and negative consequences, including employment or housing difficulties, stigmatization, damaged relationships, loss of trust in legal institutions, and perceived exacerbation of violence risk. Participants reported that they were not connected to mental health care or other supportive services through the ERPO process. Conclusions Participants perceived ERPOs to have varied and mixed consequences. These accounts identify outcomes that warrant consideration in ERPO research, policy, and implementation. Future research should assess the prevalence and distribution of these consequences and evaluate whether policy refinements can reduce adverse experiences without compromising the public health benefits of these laws.

articles.title: Performance evolution in Olympic swimming over the last 100 years: A retrospective stroke-based analysis
articles.abstract: This retrospective study examined the historical progression of Olympic swimming performance across 24 Olympic Games from Paris 1924 to Paris 2024. Finalist race data for 1553 women and 1641 men were extracted from the official World Aquatics database, including final times, reaction times, and calculated swimming speeds across all strokes (freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, butterfly) and Olympic distances (50–1500 m). Across all strokes and distances, final times demonstrated substantial reductions over the century, with the most pronounced improvements observed in freestyle and long-distance events. The largest percentage improvements in performance were observed during specific Olympic cycles, including 1956, 1972, and 2008, which coincided with major developments in pool engineering, competition regulations, training methodologies, and swimsuit technology. Swimming speeds increased consistently in all events, while reaction-time analyses revealed significant improvements across Olympic Games during the period in which reaction-time data were recorded. Overall, these findings demonstrate substantial long-term improvements in Olympic swimming performance and provide a comprehensive historical overview of performance changes across strokes, distances, and sexes. The periods associated with the largest performance improvements coincided with major technological, biomechanical, and regulatory developments in the sport. The results may serve as valuable benchmarks for coaches, athletes, and sports scientists to evaluate long-term performance trends and prepare for future international competitions.

Viscosity variation in fluid flows across scales
articles.abstract: Although most treatments of fluid mechanics consider the fluid viscosity to be constant or uniform, many systems have a viscosity that varies in time or space. Examples arise in microbial habitats, in the ocean, and in Earth’s mantle. In this review, the authors explain how viscosity gradients occur in real systems, examine how these gradients lead to new phenomena at both low and high Reynolds number, and highlight open research questions.

articles.title: Advances in the management of renal cell carcinoma
articles.abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is the most common form of kidney cancer, with 435 000 patients newly diagnosed worldwide each year. In addition to morphology and histology, molecular subtyping has advanced the diagnostic classification of RCC. Contemporary diagnosis relies on cross sectional imaging in the form of computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging and selective biopsy. For localised disease, nephrectomy remains the standard of care, with partial nephrectomy being an option for smaller tumours. Ablation or stereotactic radiation is appropriate for selected patients. Adjuvant pembrolizumab provides improved disease-free and overall survival in high risk clear cell RCC. In metastatic disease, the introduction of immune checkpoint inhibitor based combinations has extended overall survival, providing a durable response in some patients. Despite these advances, primary and secondary resistance, along with the lack of predictive and prognostic biomarkers, remain a challenge.

articles.abstract: Iza-bren showed a significant improvement in progression-free survival versus chemotherapy in patients with HR+/HER2– breast cancer previously treated with endocrine therapy, CDK4/6 inhibitors, and one or two lines of chemotherapy (including taxanes). The overall survival data were immature, and an overall survival benefit has not been established. These results suggest that iza-bren could be a new treatment option for this population in China; however, further evaluation of iza-bren in global populations and in earlier lines of therapy for HER2-negative breast cancer is warranted.

articles.abstract: In participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR TKIs, iza-bren significantly prolonged progression-free survival, although treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse were more frequent than with chemotherapy. To our knowledge, these findings provide the first phase 3 evidence for a bispecific antibody–drug conjugate and support iza-bren as a potential treatment option in this population.

These findings support sac-TMT as a new standard of care for patients with endometrial cancer who have received chemotherapy and immunotherapy and have few effective treatment options.

articles.title: [Comment] Multiple standards of care in non-small-cell lung cancer after EGFR-TKI therapy: progress, fragmentation, or inevitability?
articles.abstract: The treatment landscape of EGFR-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer harbouring exon 19 deletion or L858R mutations has advanced remarkably over the past two decades. Although acquired resistance to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) is inevitable in most patients, novel compounds such as bispecific antibodies and antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) have expanded the armamentarium of options after EGFR-TKI therapy. Following the global MARIPOSA-2 trial that showed superior progression-free survival (PFS) of amivantamab plus platinum–pemetrexed chemotherapy over platinum–pemetrexed chemotherapy alone in patients who have progressed on osimertinib,1 this is the second-line option preferred by major guidelines including the National Comprehensive Cancer Network and the European Society for Medical Oncology.

articles.title: Alison Berner: Connecting oncology and gender medicine
Assessment of comprehensiveness of national cancer control plans using a multiagent artificial intelligence model: a global analysis
articles.abstract: BackgroundNational cancer control plans (NCCPs) vary in scope and comprehensiveness, yet expert-led review is resource intensive and limits cross-country comparability. We aimed to assess NCCP comprehensiveness across 50 countries using the policy reasoning integrated sequential model (PRISM), a validated multiagent artificial intelligence (AI) system.MethodsWe identified the most recent national NCCP for each country from the International Cancer Control Partnership repository, the WHO Noncommunicable Disease Document Repository, and government websites; sub-national plans, broader non-communicable disease or health-sector strategies, drafts, and superseded versions were excluded. We developed an analytical framework of 12 elements and 76 sub-elements, aligned with WHO, International Cancer Control Partnership, and Union for International Cancer Control guidance and validated it through a modified two-stage Delphi process (online survey of 67 experts; triangulation workshop with 31 participants). PRISM comprised document ingestion (Qwen2.5-VL-72B), policy analysis with retrieval-augmented generation (Llama 4 Scout, 109B), and semantic quality assurance. PRISM was validated against masked dual-expert ratings for six purposely selected NCCPs, then applied to all NCCPs. Scores were normalised to 0-5 and medians compared across World Bank income group and WHO region.FindingsWe identified 50 NCCPs that met the inclusion criteria. Median overall comprehensiveness was 2·78 (IQR 2·25-3·09), with high comprehensiveness classified as 4·0-5·0, moderate as 2·0-3·9, and low as 0-1·9. Europe (2·96; 2·78-3·35) and lower-middle-income countries (2·97; 2·48-3·15) had the highest medians; the western Pacific (2·21; 1·78-2·87) and low-income countries (2·05; 1·94-2·22) had the lowest. Element-level medians were highest for implementation (4·17; 3·54-4·38), health services (3·89; 2·63-4·19), and governance and organisation (3·67; 3·35-3·98), and lowest for financing (1·88; 1·00-2·69), outcomes (1·83; 1·33-2·33), and threats (2·19; 1·72-2·34). Financing showed the largest gaps-only five of eleven financing sub-elements had median scores of 1·0 or less.InterpretationOur analysis suggests that NCCP comprehensiveness varies substantially between countries with consistent weaknesses in financing, outcome measurement, and contextual analysis. A shared health systems framework and scalable AI appraisal tools, such as PRISM, could support more complete, comparable, and actionable plans to strengthen cancer control globally by providing the possibility for rapid analysis of comprehensiveness of NCCPs and generation of timely, achievable, and evidence-informed, context-specific plans that use the latest data.FundingHarvard University.

Curative-intent management of de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma: an evidence-based consensus guideline from the International Collaborating Oncology Organisations
articles.abstract: Patients with de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma were historically deemed incurable and treated with palliative intent. Emergence of potent systemic therapy in combination with local treatment for both locoregional and metastatic diseases has enabled long-term survival in some patients. This international guideline was developed through consensus-building by 54 experts from 46 centres across 18 countries or regions and endorsed by 17 oncology organisations. 32 recommendations across seven clinical domains were formulated, including 29 strong (≥80% agreement [consensus] or high quality of evidence) and three conditional recommendations (67-79% agreement). We recommend that curative-intent treatment should be offered to medically fit patients with no more than three metastatic lesions in two or fewer organs at baseline or following response to systemic therapy; multimodality treatment (comprising immunochemotherapy, locoregional radiotherapy, metastasis-directed therapy, and maintenance therapy) is recommended. This guideline provides a practical framework for standardisation of clinical management of de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma and identification of key evidence gaps for future research.

articles.title: Development of the Children's Oncology Group long-term follow-up guideline for cancer genetics evaluation in childhood cancer survivors
articles.abstract: Up to 12% of childhood cancer survivors have an underlying cancer predisposition syndrome (CPS). As a result, these childhood cancer survivors are at increased risk for developing and succumbing to subsequent malignant neoplasms. Identifying childhood cancer survivors with CPS is essential to improving overall outcomes by informing tailored approaches to cancer screening, treatment, and, for some, risk-reducing interventions. Despite these potential benefits, it is often unclear which childhood cancer survivors warrant referral for genetic counselling and germline genetic testing. Using an evidence-based approach, a standardised guideline for referral for cancer genetics evaluation of childhood cancer survivors at high risk of having a CPS was developed and incorporated into the Children's Oncology Group Long-Term Follow-Up Guidelines for Survivors of Childhood, Adolescent, and Young Adult Cancers. This Policy Review details the importance, development, and anticipated impact of this new guideline. Raising awareness of this guideline is crucial to enhancing the integration of genetics into survivorship care and improving health outcomes for childhood cancer survivors with CPS.

Zamtocabtagene autoleucel, a tandem CD20–CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy, for second line treatment of large B-cell lymphoma in patients ineligible for transplantation (DALY 2-EU): primary analysis of an open-label, multicentre, randomised phase 2 study
articles.abstract: BackgroundAnti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy is the standard second-line treatment for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma. However, there is no evidence from randomised controlled trials in patients ineligible for transplantation. To address this gap, we compared zamtocabtagene autoleucel (zamto-cel), a CAR T-cell therapy directed at CD20 and CD19, with rituximab-gemcitabine-oxaliplatin (R-GemOx) chemoimmunotherapy in patients ineligible for transplantation with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma.MethodsDALY 2-EU is an open-label, multicentre, randomised, phase 2 trial conducted at 45 centres across 12 countries in Europe. Eligible patients were adults (aged ≥18 years) with second-line relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma confirmed histologically who were ineligible for transplantation and had received first-line chemoimmunotherapy containing a combination of an anthracycline-based regimen and an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody, with Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status score of 2 or less. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to zamto-cel (single intravenous infusion of 2·5 × 106 fresh (ie, non-cryopreserved) CAR T-cells per kg, capped at 100 kg, produced in a closed automated system) or R-GemOx (rituximab [375 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1], gemcitabine [1000 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1 or 2], and oxaliplatin [100 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1 or 2] administered for up to eight 14-day cycles). Randomisation was done with an interactive web response system and stratified by age, gender, lactate dehydrogenase, International Prognostic Index, histology, time to relapse after the start of first-line therapy, and country. The primary endpoint was event-free survival assessed by a masked independent review committee and compared all patients randomly assigned to the zamto-cel and R-GemOx groups using a one-sided log-rank test. Safety was assessed in all patients who received study treatment. This ongoing trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04844866).FindingsBetween Oct 14, 2021, and Jul 16, 2024, 219 patients were screened and 160 were randomly assigned to zamto-cel (n=82) and R-GemOx (n=78). The median age was 74·0 years (IQR 70·5-77·0). Patients were predominantly male (100 [63%] of 160 were men and 60 [38%] women) and White (91 [57%]), with race not reported for 64 (40%). Median vein-to-vein time for zamto-cel was 15 days (IQR 15-16). With a median follow-up of 17·0 months (IQR 9·0-22·8), event-free survival was longer in the zamto-cel group than in the R-GemOx group (6·21 months [95% CI 3·84-13·77] vs 2·53 months [1·97-3·35]; HR 0·39 [95% CI 0·27-0·58]; pInterpretationThe risk-benefit ratio observed in the DALY 2-EU study supports consideration of zamto-cel as a second-line standard treatment option for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma who are ineligible for transplantation.FundingMiltenyi Biomedicine.

articles.title: A Unified Arena for LLM Agents across Diverse Eurogame
articles.abstract: Interactive environments offer a practical way to evaluate large language model (LLM) agents, and competitive games extend this evaluation to decisions shaped by competing goals and other agents' choices. Yet existing evaluations confined to individual games or execution frameworks leave unclear which competitive advantages persist across settings. We introduce DECE (Diverse Eurogame Competitive Environments), a unified arena spanning ten Eurogames with shared interfaces and evaluation protocols. These games combine lasting strategic commitments, competition over shared resources, and multiple routes to victory. Our primary study evaluates 12 model-harness configurations, spanning nine models and four execution harnesses, in 480 three-player matches across ten games. The main and supplementary studies comprise 1,032 completed matches in total. These comparisons reveal broad cross-game ranking agreement alongside game-specific strengths. Matched studies show that the same model can perform differently across execution harnesses, adding another source of variation to these profiles. These performance advantages do not consistently translate into better token or cost efficiency, making resource use an additional consideration when comparing configurations. Together, the findings support evaluating complete agent configurations by both their competitive performance across games and the resources needed to achieve it.

articles.title: A theory of noisy linear recurrent neural network learning dynamics
articles.abstract: Biological neural networks are noisy: their dynamics involve difficult-to-predict fluctuations which are likely due not just to chaos, but also to a variety of low-level biophysical processes. Despite the omnipresence of intrinsic noise, its theoretical consequences are incompletely understood, especially in the context of learning. For example, does noise meaningfully shape representation learning, or is it better viewed as a nuisance factor whose presence or absence changes little about what solution is found and when? Here, we argue that intrinsic noise can significantly modulate representation learning in recurrent neural networks (RNNs), since it can strongly break solution-space degeneracies and in some cases control whether a non-degenerate solution exists at all. We show that this is true for an analytically tractable model of noisy RNN learning with a linear activation function and white noise inputs. We find that, in the so-called rich regime (where weights are initialized with small values), noise strongly modulates the directions in which the read-in, readout, and recurrent weights align. Moreover, we find that noise produces a kind of phase transition: for sufficiently high noise, a non-degenerate solution is not even optimal if parameter scales are limited (e.g., via regularization). These results extend recent analytic work on RNN representation learning and show that noise can act as a fundamental determinant of representations.

articles.title: Atomic Security Concerns: Towards a Foundational Language for Security Knowledge Representation
articles.abstract: Cybersecurity governance, risk management, compliance, and security architecture rely on numerous concepts, including security properties, domains, controls, risks, implementation measures, capabilities, and compliance requirements. Although these concepts are widely used, they are often represented through heterogeneous abstractions and vocabularies, making relationships among them difficult to express consistently and leaving much of the associated reasoning dependent on expert knowledge. This paper introduces the concepts of Security Concerns and Atomic Security Concerns (ASCs) and explores the hypothesis that cybersecurity knowledge may be represented through a finite set of foundational concerns. Inspired by the role of atoms in chemistry, the proposed approach views cybersecurity concepts as compositions of more fundamental concerns rather than as independent abstractions. Hence, Atomic Security Concerns could be viewed as a common abstraction layer for the representation of cybersecurity concepts, independently of their domain, nature, or level of granularity. Building upon this perspective, the paper explores how Atomic Security Concerns may provide the vocabulary of a cybersecurity language and how cybersecurity concepts may be represented as concern sets supporting explicit relationships among concepts. The contribution of this work is intentionally conceptual: it introduces a framework and research hypothesis for investigating the foundations of a common language for cybersecurity knowledge representation, reasoning, and future formalization.

articles.title: Audit Where Hacks Pay: Budgeted Strong-Verifier Audits Against Reward Hacking in GRPO
articles.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards trains on cheap checks, such as unit tests, that a policy can learn to game, while a stronger check is too expensive to run on every rollout. We study how to spend a limited strong-verifier budget in GRPO, separating which weakly passing rollouts to audit from what reward a caught hack receives. At a fixed policy state with centered advantages, the expected update depends on a design only through each rollout's marginal audit probability and correction; reflecting a caught hack's reward about the failure reward negates the advantages of an all-hack group; and auditing whole groups with the fewest weak passes first (low-pass budgeted audits, LB) minimizes the advantage mass left on hacks among pass-count designs with a fixed correction when a label's value falls with the pass count. We tested this analysis in actual LLM training: from each run's starting state, the sign of this mass on a frozen panel predicted whether hacking would be suppressed in 33 of 39 runs, including 13 of 16 preregistered ones. In LeetCode (Wong et al., 2026) and Countdown-Code (Khalifa et al., 2026), LB drives hacking to near zero, while random audits with the same penalty and budget do not and use more labels. We also find that the randomness of the update affects training: in Countdown-Code, two unbiased corrections, per-item reward-level IPW and a group-level advantage correction, bring hacking down too but end 6.1-11.8 and 8.0-11.5 points lower in held-out accuracy than LB at the same budget. A full audit, which the group-level correction reproduces in expectation, stays within about two points of LB in three seeds, while LB uses 28% of its labels, and allocating the same correction by pass count recovers most of the loss (one seed). Training outcomes thus depend not only on the expected update but also on the randomness of its estimate.

articles.title: Auto-Research Arena: Benchmarking and Advancing Auto-Research in Language Modeling
articles.abstract: As autonomous research systems become more capable, benchmarks must both evaluate their performance and support meaningful research progress. We introduce Auto-Research Arena, a multi-target benchmark for evaluating autonomous research systems and discovering ideas in language modeling. Arena supports diverse research objectives within a shared experimental environment by separating admissibility from improvement: model quality and resource constraints determine whether a result qualifies, while the selected target measures progress among admissible results. We instantiate Arena in language model pretraining with nine targets spanning model, data, training, and inference efficiency, and evaluate seven research harnesses using two foundation models. Arena clearly differentiates existing harnesses across research objectives, with several sophisticated methods outperformed by our simple sequential search baseline, indicating substantial headroom in current auto-research systems. Beyond evaluation, Arena reveals a substantially broader frontier of model and system ideas aligned with active research directions. Reusing these discoveries in a new quality-driven search yields lower training loss under matched data and FLOPs and lower held-out BPB at the same model size. Together, Arena provides a common framework for benchmarking autonomous research and expanding its scope in language modeling. The code is available at https://github.com/Auto-Research-Arena/auto-research-arena

articles.title: Beyond Physical Illness: Can Clinical Narratives Reveal Emerging Mental Health Risks in Chronically Ill Patients?
articles.abstract: Mental-health risks such as depression, dementia, and suicidal ideation can emerge during hospitalization among chronically ill patients and may worsen without timely recognition and intervention. However, most existing mental health studies focus on patients with established psychiatric conditions rather than patients hospitalized primarily for physical illness. In this work, we investigate whether latent mental-health risk in chronically ill patients can be inferred from longitudinal clinical narratives. We construct a weakly supervised cohort around 4,000 patients from MIMIC-III using mental-health evidence extracted from discharge summaries. A hierarchical state-space framework derives mental-health representations from day-wise clinical narratives and models their temporal evolution for risk estimation throughout hospitalization. Preliminary results demonstrate improved binary risk prediction using the proposed representations and show distinct model derived risk trajectories between risk and no-risk cohorts, providing a foundation for studying emerging mental-health risks in chronically ill patients.

articles.title: CLOSURE: Cross-Channel Closure for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection
articles.abstract: Multivariate time series produced by industrial installations and server clusters are under continuous monitoring, and anomaly detection is the first line of defense before a local fault escalates into a system-wide failure. In the absence of labels, the dominant paradigm trains a reconstruction model on normal data and scores the residual to reach a verdict. Recent work has steadily enriched the expressiveness of the recovery map through Transformers, diffusion models, and cross-scale associations. A residual, however, only certifies that an observation can be recovered; it does not certify that the variables still explain one another as they do under normal operation. A coordinated yet unfamiliar operating transition inflates the residual without breaking any relationship, whereas a sensor drifting away from its peers may leave the residual silent. Methods that fold inter-variable dependencies into the reconstruction objective inherit this ambiguity, because their relational evidence is ultimately supervised by the same recovery loss. We therefore propose CLOSURE, which evaluates recoverability and cross-channel consistency as two normal-data prediction tasks learned in separation. The recoverability task is solved by a diffusion reconstructor conditioned on a discrete memory of normal temporal bases. The consistency task is solved by a relation-closure operator that predicts every channel exclusively from the others, where the target's own trajectory is withheld and sparse signed gates decide which peers are actually used. The two scores are reconciled only through calibration on normal data. Extensive experiments show that CLOSURE consistently outperforms recent reconstruction-, frequency-, and topology-based detectors on public benchmark streams, confirming the value of examining consistency alongside recoverability.

articles.title: Can JEV Support Clinical Trial Criteria Assessment?
articles.abstract: Clinical trial prescreening requires distinguishing unmet conditions from insufficient evidence in patient records. Given patient records, criterion questions, and predefined answer options, we retrospectively compared JEV, a non-generative decision model returning native option probabilities, with schema-constrained Qwen Flash across 2,048 test patient-condition pairs from TrialGPT and question-answer datasets derived from MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV, all evaluated under strict Zero Data Retention (ZDR) policies to ensure clinical data privacy. Both models assessed conditions individually or in batches sharing the same patient context, with performance measured against reference labels. In batch mode, JEV and Qwen achieved similar macro-F1 scores on TrialGPT (0.652 vs. 0.660) and MIMIC-IV (0.807 vs. 0.814), whereas JEV substantially outperformed Qwen on MIMIC-III (0.768 vs. 0.534; $Δ$ = +0.234, 95% CI: 0.187-0.281). This advantage largely reflected higher recall for conditions labeled as having insufficient information (56.3% vs. 9.9%). Across all three datasets, JEV also had lower observed median job latency (1.18-1.40 vs. 2.80-8.90 s) and 53%-74% lower estimated cost per condition. These findings position JEV as an initial assessment component that provides criterion-level judgments and flags potential information gaps for review. JEV's observed errors in interpreting clinical evidence underscore the need to verify its outputs against patient records before they inform eligibility decisions.

articles.title: Center-of-Mass Interpretation of Evolution Strategies
articles.abstract: Evolution strategies (ES) update a model by sampling a population of perturbed copies, scoring each one, and moving in the reward-weighted direction of the perturbations. This update is usually presented as an estimate of a smoothed gradient. We present a geometrical interpretation of this update instead. Treat each perturbed model as a particle and its reward as the particle's mass. Before scoring, every particle has the same mass and the population balances at its centroid. Once rewards are assigned, it balances at its reward-weighted center of mass instead.
