These results establish SiC and thermal substrate engineering as a route to thick-ferromagnet spintronic oscillators for coherent microwave generation in nanoscale devices.

articles.title: Higher-harmonic spin-wave excitation by a superconducting antenna with vortices
articles.abstract: The interaction between superconductivity and magnetism provides new routes for controlling nonlinear excitations in hybrid systems. While dc-driven Abrikosov vortices (fluxons) are known to interact with spin waves, the ability of confined, nearly harmonic vortex oscillations to generate higher-frequency spin-wave modes remains unexplored. Here, by combining time-dependent Ginzburg--Landau modeling with spectral analysis of the microwave near field, we demonstrate higher-harmonic spin-wave excitation driven by a superconducting microstrip antenna in the Shubnikov phase. Unlike conventional harmonic-generation mechanisms associated with nonlinear magnetization dynamics, the magnetic layer remains a linear receiver, whereas the superconducting antenna generates the nonlinear microwave field. We show that nearly sinusoidal vortex motion and the accompanying redistribution of superconducting screening currents produce higher harmonics that couple to spin-wave modes. This response arises from spatial-to-temporal transduction, whereby harmonic vortex motion and the associated redistribution of screening currents convert a spatially nonuniform magnetic-field profile into higher temporal harmonics. Magnetic flux quanta thus act as active nonlinear elements for frequency conversion, extending the accessible spin-wave frequency range in superconducting--magnonic hybrids.

articles.title: Information-theoretic entropy imaging of quantum matter
articles.abstract: Phase transitions can generate intricate spatial organization invisible to spatially averaged probes, yet quantitative measures of this organization remain limited. Here we develop "entropy imaging," an information-theoretic technique that harnesses lossless compression to quantify spatial complexity, predictability, and order in quantum materials. Using this approach, emergent spatial textures can be imaged and converted into an experimentally-accessible observable: the computable information density (CID), a compression-based measure of information complexity that approaches the Shannon entropy rate in the large-system limit. Applied to millikelvin microwave impedance microscopy of graphene, the method reveals a pronounced maximum in the CID near quantum Hall transitions, a quantitative measure of the information-rich spatial organization of the critical landscape. A disordered Hofstadter model reproduces this behavior and shows that the CID can identify the quantum critical point from a sequence of images, without ensemble averaging over disorder realizations. The same framework tracks fractional quantum Hall transitions and resolves isolated fractional puddles that coexist with a disordered background. By contrast, the trivial band-edge crossover in a MoSe2/WS2 moiré heterobilayer exhibits qualitatively different behavior, suggesting that the pronounced CID enhancement observed at the quantum Hall critical point is not simply a generic feature of a conductive-insulating crossover. We further show that the geometric information encoded in CID is not reducible to a correlation length, and it can even distinguish spatial textures with identical multifractal statistics. Together, these results establish lossless compression as a framework for quantifying emergent spatial organization in quantum materials, with portability across imaging modalities and physical systems.

articles.title: Information-thermodynamic principles unveil the response of complex networks to perturbations
articles.abstract: Understanding how complex networks respond to perturbations is key to uncovering their functional organization. We show that, for a maximum-entropy perturbation prior, standard diffusion cannot increase response entropy, a measure of the diversity of the system's response. To overcome this limitation, we develop a density-matrix-based information thermodynamics of perturbation responses along arbitrary dynamical trajectories. We show that this framework is grounded in an information-theoretic principle of least dissipation and introduces a generalized free energy that quantifies deviations from an instantaneous diffusive reference. We then illustrate the formalism using nonlinear complex networks, revealing regimes of enhanced response diversity that cannot be captured by standard diffusive descriptions.

articles.title: Interaction dependence of the critical correlation length amplitude ratio in anisotropic scalar lattice $φ^4$ theory
articles.abstract: We investigate critical correlations in the weakly anisotropic two-dimensional scalar lattice $φ^4$ theory and demonstrate that a previously reported independence of the correlation length amplitude ratio from the local interaction strength does not hold. Monte Carlo simulations instead reveal a pronounced dependence of this ratio on the interaction strength. As the coupling is increased, the amplitude ratio interpolates between the continuum and Ising limits, highlighting a nontrivial interplay between lattice effects and local interactions. These findings call for a revised theoretical description of anisotropy effects at finite coupling in this prototypical lattice field theory.

articles.title: Interfacial bacteria-driven rotation of free-floating active droplets
articles.abstract: Active droplets provide a platform for converting microscopic propulsion into macroscopic flow. Previous realizations of bacteria-driven droplet rotation typically rely on nearby solid boundaries, external fields, or dense active nematics. Here, we report autonomous rotation of droplets in a three-dimensional aqueous two-phase system driven by interfacial population of \textit{Pseudomonas aeruginosa}. Combining confocal microscopy with fluid particle dynamics simulations, we show that amphiphilic bacteria accumulate at the dextran--polyethylene glycol interface and preferentially move and orient along the local tangent. Interfacial localization partitions the force-free swimming dipole between the two liquid phases, allowing either phase to experience a finite active torque while the combined system remains torque balanced. The simulated interfacial population is more spatially heterogeneous than in the experiments, emphasizing that both the bacterial distribution and its signed orientational organization can influence the instantaneous torque. Over the accessible size range, the macroscopic angular velocity exhibits an inverse-radius ($R^{-1}$) dependence. We also formulate a theoretical model to rationalize this scaling law, revealing how the macroscopic rotation is governed by collective interfacial swimming and surface coverage. These results identify a fluid-interface-mediated route for converting swimmer activity into macroscopic rotational flow and establish a strategy for harnessing interfacial active matter to regulate droplet dynamics.

articles.title: Inverse origami inspired by insect morphogenesis: geometric design of wrinkle structures for curved surface formation
articles.abstract: Insect exoskeletons abruptly acquire complex three-dimensional forms during metamorphosis from larva to pupa. This transformation occurs through the unfolding of preformed wrinkle structures inside the larval body under internal pressure. Inspired by this process, we investigate an inverse-origami strategy for fabricating curved surfaces. Whereas conventional origami produces three-dimensional objects by folding a flat sheet, this strategy produces curved surfaces by unfolding preformed wrinkle structures. The central design problem is to derive a wrinkle structure from a prescribed target surface. Our key idea is to regard a wrinkle structure as a unidirectional stretching field, which specifies at each point the stretch produced when the structure unfolds. We first derive such a field from the target surface geometry and then translate it into spatially varying wrinkle directions and spacing, so that the wrinkle structure unfolds into the target. The resulting numerical designs approximate the intrinsic metric of the target surface. We demonstrate the method on multiple target surfaces through numerical construction, mechanical unfolding simulations, and 3D-printed prototypes. This work provides a biologically inspired geometric design principle for encoding prescribed surface shapes in wrinkle structures, as well as a framework for designing and fabricating deployable curved surfaces.

articles.title: Investigation of the Microstructural and Magnetic Properties of Ni on GeSn Layers
articles.abstract: Thermal processing of nickel (Ni) layers on germanium-tin (GeSn) can strongly modify the Ni film and the Ni/GeSn interface within a restricted thermal budget; however, the influence of GeSn crystalline quality on Ni-Ge-Sn interfacial evolution and the magnetic response of the Ni layer remains incompletely understood. Here, Ni (15~nm)/Ge$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$/Ge/Gd$_2$O$_3$/Si(111) heterostructures ($x = 0.08$ and $0.10$) were investigated following rapid thermal annealing at 573 and 973~K for 10~s using X-ray diffraction, pole-figure analysis, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy depth profiling, and temperature- and field-dependent magnetization measurements. Annealing at 573~K preserves the crystallographic texture of Ge$_{0.92}$Sn$_{0.08}$, whereas Ge$_{0.90}$Sn$_{0.10}$ exhibits microtwin formation and reduced structural integrity. Annealing at 973~K, employed as a severe upper-bound thermal reference, causes extensive structural degradation in both heterostructures, with substantially greater deterioration in the higher-Sn sample. XPS depth profiling reveals progressive Ni-Ge-Sn intermixing accompanied by pronounced Sn surface segregation with increasing annealing temperature. Magnetization measurements show coexisting ferromagnetic and superparamagnetic contributions in the as-deposited and 573~K samples, whereas annealing at 973~K strongly suppresses the ferromagnetic response, producing highly unsaturated $M(H)$ loops together with reduced saturation magnetization and coercivity. These magnetic changes are consistent with extensive interfacial alloying and dilution of the metallic Ni layer. This study establishes a direct correlation between GeSn crystalline quality, interfacial diffusion, and magnetic behavior.

articles.title: Learning by Confusion Locates a Parametrization-Dependent Fisher Information Maximum
articles.abstract: Learning by confusion (LBC) is a machine-learning method for locating phase transitions without assuming a known order parameter. Its characteristic accuracy curve contains a central maximum that is interpreted as the transition point, but what determines the location and finite-size scaling of this maximum has remained unclear. We derive an exact balance condition for the Bayes-optimal confusion peak and show that, for equilibrium systems with a single swept parameter, the peak closely follows the maximum of the corresponding Fisher information. This immediately gives its finite-size scaling and reveals an unexpected dependence on how the data are sampled: the same configurations arranged on grids uniform in $T$, $\ln T$, or $β=1/T$ can yield different finite-size pseudocritical trajectories. Tests on the Ising, Blume-Capel, Potts, and Baxter-Wu models confirm the prediction across continuous, tricritical, and first-order transitions. Our results identify the statistical quantity measured by LBC and show that finite-size machine-learning estimates can depend on the parametrization of the training data as well as on the underlying physics.

articles.title: Local Broadband Gigahertz Spectroscopy via SQUID-on-Tip DC Readout
articles.abstract: Superconducting microwave circuits are shaped by their local electromagnetic environment, yet standard microwave measurements do not resolve the local fields and device features that govern their behavior. Here, we combine microwave spectroscopy, nanoscale magnetic sensing, and topographic imaging in a single tapping-mode SQUID-on-tip microscope. The nonlinear Josephson response converts local GHz excitations into Shapiro steps, enabling quantitative measurements of microwave frequency signals and their excitation strength using only DC readout. Applied to a superconducting coplanar waveguide resonator, local spectroscopy reproduces the power-dependent resonance and nonlinear bifurcation observed in microwave transmission measurements. Spatially resolved measurements map the microwave response while simultaneously recording topography and static magnetic features, including vortices and Meissner screening currents. Electromagnetic simulations reveal how coupling through the superconducting probe leads limits spatial resolution and guides localized detector designs. Together, these capabilities establish a platform for correlating microwave circuit dynamics with the local structural and magnetic environment of superconducting devices.

articles.title: Local Koopman modes of saddle-point diffusions: exact singular functions and a data-driven estimator
articles.abstract: Coherent sets-regions of phase space that resist mixing-organize transport in stochastic dynamical systems and are encoded in the leading singular functions of the stochastic Koopman operator. These are typically computed numerically and globally; a local, analytic theory near a fixed point has been missing, although fixed points and the transitions between them organize the flow. We supply the local theory for a saddle, the transition state through which probability flows between basins. Naively the construction fails-probability escapes along unstable directions, the invariant measure is non-normalizable, the singular functions leave $L^2$, and singular values exceed one. We show that conditioning on non-escape (a Doob's $h$-transform) repairs this; that the required $h$ is the unique stabilizing solution of an algebraic Riccati equation; and that the resulting slow modes decay at the escape rate along the unstable manifold. We obtain these modes in closed form-products of Hermite polynomials in canonical coordinates times the $h$-function-and use their unitary structure to derive a data-driven estimator: canonical correlation analysis on conditioned trajectories. When a single unstable direction dominates, the leading mode is the reaction coordinate, locally recovering the stable manifold and committor of transition-path theory. The construction connects coherent sets to transition-path theory, to the stabilizing Riccati solution of linear control, and to the time-reversed dynamics of generative diffusion models.

articles.title: Magnetic susceptibility and superfluid density of inhomogeneous superconducting films: the Tc-mosaic model
articles.abstract: Whole-sample and mutual-inductance part-sample measurements of the linear magnetic susceptibility, $χ$, of superconducting films are routinely used to obtain the London penetration depth, $λ(T)$, assuming uniform superconductivity. However, spatially resolved probes show that many films of current interest are inhomogeneous on micrometer scales. Here we ask whether a distribution of local transition temperatures in a fully gapped film can produce an apparent line-nodal, $T$-linear $λ(T)$. The film is modeled as a random Voronoi mosaic of domains with $T_c$ distributed between $T_{c,\min}$ and $T_{c,\max}$ with s-wave (also d-wave, for comparison) London response inside each domain. We show that detectable screening appears only below the percolation temperature, $T_p$, and the transition broadens with the spread of $T_c$. For s-wave domains, $λ(T)$ remains activated for any $T_{c,\min}>0$. Only for $T_{c,\min}=0$ does it become a power law, $Δλ\propto T^n$ with $n\approx1.7$, but then the onset of screening drops to $T_p=T_{c,\max}/2$. Weighting the $T_{c}$ distribution towards $T_c\to0$ (more low-$T_{c}$ domains) can bring $n$ closer to 1 ($n\approx1.2$), but simultaneously pushes the apparent transition, $T_p$, more than an order of magnitude below $T_{c,\max}$. For d-wave domains, the linear term survives, and its relative slope is enhanced almost fourfold for $T_{c,\min}=0$. Hence, a $T$-linear $λ(T)$ measured in a film with screening onset within a factor of a few of $T_{c,\max}$ by whole-sample or mutual-inductance part-sample measurements cannot originate from $T_c$ mosaicity in a fully gapped superconductor.

articles.title: Maximization of nuclear fusion reactivity via optimal energy distributions
articles.abstract: We investigate the optimization of nuclear fusion reactivity relative to the choice of energy probability distribution. A single Maxwell-Boltzmann (MB) distribution is found to be optimal in the region where reactivity is a concave function of the average available kinetic energy, specifically near the reactivity peak. Conversely, in regions where the reactivity curve is convex, optimization is achieved through a bimodal MB distribution. We then discuss our results in the context of three classes of generalized energy distributions (superstatistics), which are modeled as a continuum of MB distributions. As expected, in all cases examined, the reactivity gains provided by superstatistics are bounded by the proposed optimal distribution. Finally, we apply these findings to deuterium-deuterium and deuterium-tritium fusion processes using empirical parametrizations of their respective cross sections. For both reactions, employing optimal bimodal MB distributions at low average energies-of particular interest for magnetically confined plasmas-yields a reactivity enhancement of approximately a factor of 2.

articles.title: Microscopic Derivation of Stochastic Thin-Film Equation and Extensions to Two-Layer and Evaporating Films
articles.abstract: While classical thin-film hydrodynamics models widely govern macroscopic fluid layers, they fail to capture the molecular-level thermal fluctuations that dictate nanoscale interfacial dynamics. Standard stochastic extensions rely on the long-wave approximation of the continuum fluctuating Navier-Stokes equations; however, this top-down paradigm lacks a formal connection to microscopic particle trajectories and cannot readily accommodate complex, non-equilibrium boundary mechanisms. We resolve this limitation by deriving the stochastic thin-film equation directly from the exact underlying N-particle Hamiltonian dynamics. This is achieved via a systematic, bottom-up coarse-graining framework based on a generalized fluctuating dynamic density-functional theory. Crucially, this first principles formulation offers unparalleled flexibility, enabling the seamless integration of multi-layered interfaces and non-conserved dynamics such as evaporation. For these complex configurations, our framework rigorously yields entirely novel stochastic thin-film equations featuring emergent noise terms that encapsulate microscopic fluctuations missing from classical top-down models.

articles.title: Modeling the CNOT gate in Germanium double quantum dots
articles.abstract: We model a controlled-NOT (CNOT) gate mediated by exchange interactions in a realistic Ge/GeSi hole spin-qubit device. We use for that purpose a computationally efficient framework based on a compact dressed basis of many-body singlet and triplet states, which enables fast time-dependent simulations that would be prohibitive within a conventional configuration-interaction approach. We discuss the dominant sources of infidelity in ideal (noise-free) devices. On the one hand, the nonadiabaticity of the tunnel barrier ramps, enhanced by the transverse component of the exchange interaction, imposes limits on the speed of the CNOT gate. On the other hand, the AC Stark shift of the conditional resonance and the off-resonant driving of the complementary transition can significantly degrade the gate fidelity and call for a careful optimization of the driving conditions. Finally, we investigate the impact of quasi-static charge noise on the fidelity of the CNOT gate. We find that the capture of charges near the qubits can strongly disrupt the conditional operation, while the nanometer-scale motion of charges results in a loss of fidelity that sensitively depends on the position and strength of the corresponding dipole. Our results quantify the requirements on barrier control, microwave driving, and charge-noise stability for high-fidelity two-qubit operations in Ge/GeSi hole-spin qubits.

articles.title: Momentum-resolved thermodynamics and barrier-free order-parameter collapse in spin-orbit-coupled superconductors under a Zeeman field
articles.abstract: Spin-orbit coupling (SOC) can enhance the critical Zeeman field of clean superconductors beyond the Pauli limit. We develop a momentum decomposition of the zero-temperature free energy to investigate spin-singlet $s$-wave superconductors with general time-reversal-symmetric SOC. The SOC component perpendicular to the Zeeman field enhances the critical field and suppresses first-order features, whereas the parallel component favors Pauli-limited thermodynamic behavior. Applying this framework to Rashba superconductors and Ising superconductors with weak Rashba SOC, we identify the origin of the abrupt collapse of the superconducting order parameter at the critical field. Competing angular contributions produce a nearly flat free-energy landscape, allowing a barrier-free order-parameter collapse distinct from the conventional Pauli-limited first-order transition.

articles.title: Multipartite dynamics beyond bipartite entanglement equilibration
articles.abstract: Entanglement equilibration need not mark the end of quantum-information dynamics in quantum thermalization. We show that the complete Schmidt spectra of a fixed tripartition can become stationary while its multipartite correlation structure, distinguished by local-unitary invariants, continues to evolve. This separation occurs exactly within a finite window in self-dual kicked-Ising dynamics and asymptotically in Haar-random circuits. We further demonstrate an independently tunable timescale for multipartite dynamics using quantum-error-correcting codes. When coupled to a locally scrambling bath, ordinary entanglement approaches equilibrium through rapid local scrambling, while weak logical--bath coupling drives a slower reorganization of multipartite correlations. These results reveal a deeper distinction than the ordering of equilibration times: bipartite entanglement and multipartite correlation structure can probe distinct physical channels of quantum-information dynamics, rather than merely different stages of the same relaxation process.

articles.title: Nanoscale mapping of native defects in Td-MoTe2 and their impact on graphene-based van der Waals heterostructures
articles.abstract: We investigate native defects and their impact on the electronic structure of Td-MoTe2 and graphene/Td-MoTe2 van der Waals heterostructures using scanning tunnelling microscopy and spectroscopy. STM reveals a high density of circular, hollow surface defects that we attribute to Te vacancies. STS on pristine MoTe2 shows semimetallic, V-shaped dI/dV spectra with subtle low-energy states. The vacancies suppress the tunnelling conductance below the Fermi level without introducing new sharp defect-related resonances, consistent with a vacancy-induced redistribution of Mo-Te spectral weight rather than the appearance of new electronic states. In the heterostructure, graphene preserves these MoTe2 fingerprints with no noticeable graphene doping or charge transfer. Our results demonstrate that isolated native Te vacancies act as spectroscopically weak perturbations to the low-energy electronic structure of graphene. The graphene overlayer further screens their impact on the electronic structure, making graphene/Td-MoTe2 heterostructures intrinsically tolerant to such interface defects.

articles.title: Optimised growth of epitaxial D019 Mn3Ge(0001) thin films via single target sputtering
articles.abstract: Materials with chemical identity Mn3X, where X is Sn, Ga, or Ge, are Heusler alloys with intriguing properties that are fundamentally and technologically interesting. They have topological properties with a non-trivial band structure that identify them as Weyl semimetals in the bulk. Their magnetic properties, which give rise to the topological band structure through spin-orbit coupling, are determined by their Kagome lattice structure, making them chiral non-collinear antiferromagnets. Among these materials, Mn3Ge is particularly interesting because it has a larger Berry curvature, leading to a large anomalous Hall conductivity and motivating potential spintronic applications. The desirable properties are only obtained when Mn3Ge has the D019 crystal structure, so producing an easily reproducible growth recipe is the main objective of this paper. Here we show that ultra-high-quality thin films of Mn3Ge with D019 symmetry can be grown from a Mn5Ge target on an Al2O3(0001) substrate with a Ru(0001) seed layer. The expected non-collinear antiferromagnetic order was confirmed by the finding of weak zero-field magnetisation (0.0086 +/- 0.0002) mu_B/Mn that does not saturate at high magnetic fields and has a Neel temperature of (291 +/- 2) K.

articles.title: Orbital-selective correlations in kagome flat bands of Co$_3$Sn$_2$S$_2$
articles.abstract: Geometrical flat bands provide an ideal platform for studying electronic correlations and quantum-geometric effects. Although the ferromagnetic Weyl semimetal \CoSnS is generally considered a moderately correlated system, recent spectroscopy experiments have revealed a flat-band feature near the Fermi level ($\EF$) that is absent in conventional density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Using DFT plus dynamical mean-field theory and a minimal kagome model, we show that this feature arises not from heavy-fermion-like dynamical band renormalization, but from the shifting of a $d_{x^2-y^2}$ dominated geometrical kagome flat band toward $\EF$ driven by orbital- and spin-dependent self-energies. The relocated flat band enhances the local Berry curvature near $\EF$, resulting in a strongly energy-dependent anomalous Hall conductivity and a giant anomalous Nernst effect. Our findings establish an orbital-selective correlation mechanism for positioning geometrical flat bands at $\EF$, and propose anomalous thermoelectric transport as a sensitive probe of flat band induced topology.

articles.title: Parametrically Enhanced Ergotropy and Charging Power in a Three-Mode Bosonic Quantum Battery
articles.abstract: Quantum batteries are quantum systems that potentially serve as fuel for other quantum devices by receiving and supplying energy. In this work, we propose a theoretical scheme to enhance ergotropy and charging power of quantum Battery in the system under consideration through squeezed light. Moreover, The system comprises a coherently driven charger cavity, a strongly dissipative auxiliary cavity acting as a mediator, and an energy--storage battery cavity. Quantum nonreciprocity and directional energy flow are established via destructive quantum interference between the direct coupling path and the loss--engineered indirect path. A degenerate optical parametric amplifier integrated into the charger cavity acts as an active, phase--sensitive energy source that injects two--photon quantum excitations and anomalous correlations. Using a strictly open--quantum--system framework derived directly from the Lindblad master equation, we obtain the full expectation--value dynamics and stationary states. We show that active parametric driving drastically increases the stored energy and peak charging power while maintaining nonreciprocal energy trapping in the battery. We achieve a multi-order-of-magnitude boost in the battery's stored energy, charging power, and ergotropy. We also analyze the effects of pure dephasing on the charging power, ergotropy, and extractable work quality.. Although two--photon pumping introduces photon--number fluctuations that slightly lower the fractional ergotropy ratio ${\cal W}_{\rm B}/{\cal E}_{\rm B}$, the absolute extractable work remains substantially elevated compared to unassisted configurations.

articles.title: Phonon-assisted shift-current from first-principles: application to AlN monolayer
articles.abstract: In this work, we present a first-principles approach to investigate phonon-assisted shift current in extended systems. Our method combines the special displacement technique with real-time simulations based on the dynamical Berry phase. Merging these two frameworks enables direct access to non-linear optical responses at finite temperatures, while naturally incorporating phonon scattering and phonon-assisted electronic transitions into the time-dependent dynamics. This allows us to capture temperature-dependent features and lattice fluctuations that are essential for a realistic description of non-linear photocurrent generation. As a representative example, we apply our approach to the shift-current response of a monolayer of hexagonal AlN (h-AlN). This system provides an ideal testing ground because it features an indirect band gap and lacks inversion symmetry. Moreover, h-AlN layers of different thicknesses have been fabricated and characterized in a variety of experimental settings, opening the concrete possibility of testing our predictions. Our results demonstrate the relevance of phonon-mediated processes and the importance of temperature in determining the magnitude and spectral features of the shift current in layered materials.

articles.title: Quantum state revivals, time quasicrystals, and entanglement steering in a Fibonacci-driven central-spin model
articles.abstract: Motivated by the search for non-equilibrium phases of matter beyond the Floquet paradigm, we propose a route to realize perfect revivals and time quasicrystals (TQCs) in a Fibonacci-driven central-spin model with Ising interactions between the central and satellite spins in the absence of disorder. We analytically demonstrate that when the interaction strength, $λ$ is tuned to $2 m π$, no entanglement is generated between the central and satellite spins at stroboscopic times, independent of the strength of the transverse driving field and the drive sequence. This leads to indefinitely long-lived quasiperiodic oscillations in satellite spin magnetization. Furthermore, for initial states with a definite bath magnetization, no entanglement is generated when the transverse driving field, $θ$ is tuned to $π$ for any value of $ λ$, and the satellite spin magnetization oscillations exhibit period-3 revivals at Fibonacci times. Examining the robustness of these oscillations away from this fine-tuned limit, we identify a parameter regime where the quasiperiodic response does not decay over the timescales probed, giving rise to a long-lived $π$-pulse-proximate TQC regime. We further show that at special Clifford points, the system exhibits perfect quasiperiodic oscillations of the satellite spin magnetization, with a parity-dependent Fourier response. This response persists over the timescales probed, even away from the Clifford points for an even number of satellite spins, leading to the formation of a Clifford-proximate TQC. Finally, we demonstrate that at this Clifford points, the system is steered along an entangled trajectory, leading to the dynamical generation of Bell-cat and spin-cat states. These states exhibit magnetization of collective spin fluctuates quadratically with the number of satellite spins, thereby enabling Heisenberg-limited metrology.

articles.title: Reference-state dependence and interface scaling of superfluid response in a two-dimensional crystal
articles.abstract: Grain boundaries modify both transport paths and the surrounding crystal, making their contribution to superfluid stiffness difficult to isolate. We quantify these contributions in stationary two-dimensional soft-core Gross--Pitaevskii (GP) crystals using tensor response, independently prepared bicrystals, and measured interface lengths. A one-percent change of lattice spacing alters the bulk stiffness by approximately 5--9\%, comparable to the boundary contribution. For the same defective state, two bulk references give relative excesses of 0.027\% and 4.15\%. Matching the comparator to grain strain and chemical potential yields positive diagonal excesses in paired preparations at three interaction strengths. Within a twelve-state family with comparable grain interiors, the excess is robust to 288 bulk substitutions and follows an approximate length-per-area relation. Independent fixed-area pairs yield a line-response coefficient 3.1\% higher than the three-size estimate. Size and directional dependence restrict this relation to the specified crystal conditions. Reduced link networks relate the directional response to the organization of boundary connections but do not accurately resolve every small bulk-subtracted excess. The results distinguish boundary enhancement from changes in the surrounding crystal and establish a quantitative comparison protocol for superfluid transport in defective crystals.

articles.title: Rigid Band Shift in Electron-Doped Kagome Metal
articles.abstract: We study the effects of Sn-site doping on the electronic structure of nonmagnetic kagome metal YV$_6$Sn$_{6-x}$Sb$_x$ by infrared spectroscopy and density-functional theory. The results for samples with $x$ = 0 and 1.4 demonstrate that partial substitution of Sn by Sb acts as a rigid shift of the Fermi level while leaving the band dispersion largely intact. Our findings establish Sn-site substitution in YV$_6$Sn$_6$ as a route to systematically investigate band-filling-dependent electronic properties of nonmagnetic kagome metals.

articles.title: Rigid Particle-Induced Anomalous Softening in Elastomer Composites
articles.abstract: Particle-filled soft composites generally stiffen as particle loading increases, imposing a trade-off between functionality and compliance. Here, we show that this trade-off can be overcome by designing particles to actively direct gelation rather than act as passive fillers. In a sol-rich elastomer matrix, sol-phase kinetics redirect network formation towards particle-mediated assembly, yielding anomalous softening despite increasing particle content. This response is governed by topological reconfiguration of the load-bearing network during gelation rather than by filler loading alone. A structure-based model captures the composition-dependent onset of this behaviour, and the same response is reproduced across distinct particle systems. The resulting materials combine functionality with softness, energy dissipation, and recoverability under large deformation. These findings establish topology-guided gelation as a general strategy for engineering compliant functional composites for soft robotic actuation, conformal interfaces, and other systems that require both deformability and embedded material functionality.

articles.title: Simplified Parisi Ansatz III: Constructive Cavity Method and Ultrametricity
articles.abstract: We present a physical explaination of the Constructive Cavity Method (CCM) for the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model, which identifies the decomposition of the cavity variables into layers with the random overlap structure of Aizenman--Sims--Starr. We describe the low-temperature excitations through a dilute gas of defects relative to the ground state. The sharing of these defects among the descendants and the renewal of the fluctuations along new branches produce the GREM structure and the ultrametricity of the overlaps. This mechanism is developed first with a finite number of defects and then extended to exponential populations of states. At fixed kernel, the Gaussian covariances of the fresh fields connect the complete cavity variables, including their common components, to the same hierarchy that determines the Gibbs masses. We also correct some ambiguities of earlier formulations.

articles.title: Synchronization-controlled transport near an absorbing transition: Effective Enskog kinetic theory of a driven granular monolayer
articles.abstract: Synchronization with vibrating boundaries can qualitatively alter the dynamics of confined granular fluids and control the collision-induced transfer of energy to horizontal motion. We develop an Enskog kinetic theory for the active phase of a driven granular monolayer within the framework of the $Δ$-model, which accounts for the transfer of energy from the vertical to the horizontal degrees of freedom of grains. Synchronization effects are incorporated through a state-dependent effective collision rule governed by the interplay between the local collision frequency and a characteristic synchronization time. A viscous drag force is also included to account for energy dissipation arising from interactions with the confining plates. Within this framework, we characterize the homogeneous active state and use it as the reference state for a Chapman--Enskog expansion. The solution of the Enskog equation to Navier--Stokes order then yields explicit expressions for the shear and bulk viscosities, the thermal conductivity, the diffusive heat coefficient, and the first-order contribution to the cooling rate, consistently accounting for inelasticity, damping, finite-density effects, and synchronization. Event-driven molecular-dynamics simulations show that the theory accurately describes the steady temperature and shear and bulk viscosities over a broad region of the active phase. Close to the discontinuous synchronization-controlled absorbing transition, deviations are mainly attributed to the mean-field coarse-graining of the microscopic synchronization dynamics: fluctuations of the collision-dependent injection amplitude and correlations between synchronization and pre-collisional velocities become increasingly important. These results provide a kinetic description of synchronization-controlled transport and delineate its range of validity near the absorbing transition.

articles.title: The fate of $s_{\pm}$ superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$
articles.abstract: Motivated by the recent measurement of high-temperature superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate system La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ in the bulk as well as thin film samples, we seek to understand the role of the interlayer coupling in this system in dictating the pairing symmetry. Many proposals posit the existence of an $s_\pm$ superconducting phase in close competition with the mroe conventional cuprate-like $d$-wave state in both weak- and strong-coupling theories. However, at least in the latter, the effects of Coulomb repulsion and the double occupancy constraint have been largely neglected. In this manuscript, we propose a mean-field fractionalization treatment that captures the full $SU(2)$ particle-hole symmetry of the t-J model at half-filling, and show how a systematic treatment of this new symmetry leads to an added Coulomb pseudopotential constraint - one that is absent in the usual $U(1)$ treatment. We then apply this new fractionalization scheme to a simplified bilayer t-J model of La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$, showing how the Coulomb pseudopotential suppresses the existence of $s_\pm$ symmetry in favor of $d$-wave pairing.

articles.title: The mathematical journey of spatial reciprocity
articles.abstract: Over the past three decades, evolutionary game theory in structured populations has witnessed explosive progress. Counterintuitive cooperative phenomena discovered in simulations have stimulated the development of rigorous mathematical theories to describe the underlying dynamics. In this paper, we review these theoretical advancements, including pair approximation and coalescent theory, which offer analytical solutions to evolutionary games on networks. We summarize the key results obtained by these theories, while also discussing their limitations, such as high computational complexity and constrained flexibility when applied to complex models. We therefore suggest that mathematical approaches provide a complementary tool for understanding cooperation in structured populations alongside simulations.

articles.title: Theoretical description of high-harmonic spectroscopy for uniaxial nematic and isotropic liquid crystals
articles.abstract: Enabled by their controllable optical anisotropy, liquid crystals form a cornerstone of linear optical and display technologies. Bringing the versatile platform into the nonlinear regime, we explore its nonlinear optical anisotropy by high-order harmonic generation spectroscopy. Through a comprehensive study targeting gas, liquid, nematic, and crystalline phases, we present a semi-empirical tight-binding approach that provides insight into the intermolecular character of ultrafast light-driven electron dynamics across soft-matter mesophases. We demonstrate how intermolecular electron hybridization enables spectroscopic access to structural properties, such as the nematic director and order parameter. Outlining such foundational mechanisms opens avenues towards nonlinear liquid crystal devices and ultrafast soft-matter spectroscopies.

articles.title: Trajectory Functionals in the Thermodynamics of Radiation-Induced Damage in Structural Materials
articles.abstract: This paper delivers a novel self-consistent non-local kinetic framework based on dose-dependent semi-Markov renewal transport and the generalized Doob's h-transform to evaluate the structural degradation of WWER-1000/1200 fuel claddings. By leveraging the Feynman-Kac formalism, we map the continuous microscopic defect path trajectories generated by the Liouville operator directly onto the evolution of the macroscopically integrated damage potential. The framework accounts for long-range memory effects in the degradation kinetics via a non-vanishing structural commutator of the path Liouville operator and Zwanzig-Mori projection operators, which mathematically links the spatial restrictions of microscopic sinks to energetic path penalties. Spatial profiling of the cladding's mean lifetime, demonstrates a distinct sigmoidal, S-shaped degradation trajectory encompassing distinct incubation, linear growth, and avalanche breakdown stages. The numerical results reveal an abrupt, localized reduction in the operational lifespan near the cladding boundaries. This marginal vulnerability is shown to be a direct physical consequence of boundary stress field singularities at the fuel cladding interface and localized embrittlement. The developed path integral architecture provides a strict thermodynamic link between non-equilibrium fluctuations and the global Griffiths macro-barrier, offering a robust predictive tool for high-burnup nuclear fuel safety assessments.

articles.title: Twist-controlled imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems
articles.abstract: We construct a controllable imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems using spatially modulated local rotations without changing initial bipartite entanglement spectra and correlation magnitudes. This feature unambiguously isolates the redistribution of spectral weights as the sole driver of the anomalous relaxation. Using the compact-boson description, we reveal that these twists act as precise mode selectors: higher-harmonic twists exclusively populate high-energy standing waves, structurally bypassing slow-decaying infrared modes to accelerate convergence. We derive exact analytical crossing times for these reversals and demonstrate that intentionally reintroducing the slow-mode population systematically delays the ITME. This exact mechanism is validated beyond the fixed-point theory via calculations on interacting XXZ chains and ladders. Furthermore, a twelve-qubit simulation of variational quantum imaginary-time evolution reproduces the reversals and their controlled delay, providing a concrete route to realize this protocol in realistic quantum circuits. Ultimately, these results provide a strictly controllable and exact starting point for realizing and investigating the imaginary-time Mpemba effect, establishing a foundational paradigm to harness anomalous non-equilibrium relaxation in quantum ground-state preparations.

articles.title: Wrinkling dynamics of thin crystalline sheets and its dependency on topological defects
articles.abstract: We investigate the wrinkling dynamics of thin crystalline sheets under uniaxial compression using a Surface Phase-Field-Crystal-Helfrich (SPFCH) model, which captures the coupling between crystalline order, out-of-plane deformations, and topological defects. In particular, the model allows us to track and characterize two distinct classes of defects, namely those forming in the underlying hexagonal crystal lattice, such as dislocations and grain boundaries, and defects in the wrinkling patterns, known as wrinklons. By resolving the evolution and interactions of these defects, we investigate how the interplay between in-plane and out-of-plane relaxation mechanisms influences wrinkling onset and the coarsening regime. Our results indicate that crystalline defects do not affect coarsening scaling, but they quantitatively affect the onset of wrinkling and the emerging wrinkling wavelength, promote more irregular wrinkle patterns with a higher density of wrinklons, and modify long-timescale morphological evolution.

articles.title: A Density-Matrix Formulation of Vibrational Circular Dichroism Spectra for Møller-Plesset and Configuration Interaction Methods
articles.abstract: We reformulate the overlap of wave-function derivatives that defines the atomic axial tensors (AATs) and velocity-gauge atomic polar tensors (VG-APTs) used to compute vibrational circular dichroism (VCD) rotatory strengths. In place of our earlier determinant-level derivatives, the new approach expresses these tensors as contractions involving molecular-orbital derivative integrals, perturbed and unperturbed one- and two-electron density matrices, and dot products of the perturbed correlated wave-function amplitudes. Following the elegant treatment of the diagonal Born-Oppenheimer correction by Gauss and co-workers, the formulation holds for any real, normalized CI-like wave function. The two-electron density contribution vanishes exactly, because one perturbation is real (nuclear) and the other imaginary (magnetic field or momentum); this removes multiple terms from our earlier AAT and VG-APT expressions for second-order Møller-Plesset perturbation theory (MP2) and configuration interaction singles and doubles (CISD). We also present a simplified form of the origin-independent length-gauge [LG(OI)] rotatory strength that avoids the singular-value decomposition of the outer product of the length-gauge APT and VG-APT vectors for each mode, and that clarifies how the LG(OI) and velocity-gauge rotatory strengths are related. Applying the density-based AATs and VG-APTs to ($P$)-hydrogen peroxide, (\textit{S})-methyloxirane, and (\textit{S})-3-chloro-1-butyne, we find that discrepancies among the gauges arise chiefly from basis-set incompleteness in the VG-APT. The charge-sum rule serves as a useful measure of that incompleteness, independent of the correlation method.

articles.title: An Ab Initio Quantum-Chemistry-Based Three-Temperature Approach for Non-Equilibrium Hypersonic Flows: Application to Homogeneous 0-D Chemical Systems
articles.abstract: This work presents an ab initio quantum-chemistry-based one-bin, three-temperature (1-bin 3T) model for non-equilibrium thermochemistry of homogeneous chemical systems in their electronic ground state, derived using the multi-group maximum-entropy principle. The proposed framework captures both vibrational and rotational non-equilibrium effects, thereby enabling an accurate representation of thermochemical behavior in high-temperature gases. To account for departures from equilibrium dissociation, a non-equilibrium correction factor derived from ro-vibrational State-to-State (StS) analysis is incorporated into the population distribution. Because this correction is constructed from the quasi-steady-state (QSS) distribution, the resulting model is valid only for systems and conditions under which the QSS assumption holds. The proposed 1-bin 3T model is validated across a broad range of zero-dimensional test cases through comparisons with high-fidelity StS simulations and Direct Molecular Simulations (DMS). The results demonstrate excellent agreement between the reduced-order model and high-fidelity approaches for both dissociating and recombining environments. Overall, the 1-bin 3T model shows strong potential as an efficient and accurate framework for modeling non-equilibrium thermochemical behavior, while keeping computational costs orders of magnitude lower than the high fidelity ro-vibrational StS simulations.

articles.title: Lanthanide Crystal Field Theory in the J-Mixing Regime: $f^n$ Configurations
articles.abstract: The low-energy sector of the lanthanide $f^n$ shell is to first approximation governed by the interplay of three interactions: Coulomb repulsion, spin-same-orbit coupling and the ligand crystal field potential. To rationalize the energy landscape in different chemical environments, it is desirable to extract the phenomenological crystal field parameters from experimental data; however, in practice, high-dimensional fitting procedures complicate their routine determination. Here, we present a computational extraction procedure based on real tensorial sets and the $U(7)$ canonical chain that, unlike existing operator equivalent methods, takes all $J$ multiplets of the lowest-energy $LS$ term into account, ensuring meaningful results even in the presence of considerable $J$-mixing. Two series of lanthanide compounds, [Ln(III)(C$_8$H$_8$)$_2$]$^-$} and doped Ln(III):Y$_2$O$_3$} (Ln $\in$ {Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm, Eu}) serve as examples for high- ($D_{8h}$) and low-symmetry ($C_2$) scenarios. Consequences for the generalisation toward actinides are briefly discussed.

articles.title: Preparing State-Selected Molecular Beams with high Efficiency using Quantum Cascade Lasers
articles.abstract: We demonstrate the ro-vibrational state-selective preparation of CO molecules ($v$ = 0, J = 0 $\rightarrow$ $v$ = 1, J = 1) in an internally cold molecular beam using a continuous-wave, narrow-linewidth distributed feedback type quantum cascade laser, with an output wavelength of 4.65 $μ$m. Using a modulation-free wavelength stabilization scheme, we show that population transfer to near saturation levels can be obtained with sufficient long term stability, as needed for state-resolved scattering experiments. We show preliminary results of CO molecules prepared in the $v$ = 1 state, scattering from a clean Cu(100) surface. This study showcases the promise of QCL based excitation for state-selected molecular beam based scattering experiments, especially involving transitions in the mid-infrared domain ($λ$ > 4.5 $μ$m) which are otherwise difficult to access using conventional sources.

articles.title: State-specific perturbation theory for configuration interaction singles: Theoretical analysis, benchmarks, and improvement with size-intensive level shifts
articles.abstract: We recently proposed a state-specific second-order perturbation theory based on the configuration interaction singles (CIS) state, termed CIS(2). Here, we clarify its theoretical connections, assess the accuracy of its excitation energies in greater detail, and develop size-intensive level shifts to improve both accuracy and convergence of its amplitude equations. We first derive the MP2 structure of its working equations and show that our previously introduced Hybrid partition recovers CIS(D) when the ground-state Fock operator is used and the residual Fock action on the CIS reference is neglected. For this partition, an expanded benchmark shows that using the CIS-state Fock operator improves Rydberg and especially charge-transfer accuracy relative to CIS(D), while slightly worsening valence accuracy. We analyze how the hole and particle densities contribute to these changes in excitation energy, which differ among the classes. We then introduce size-intensive level shifts that preserve the ground-state correlation contribution of noninteracting fragments while leaving the ground-state MP2 energy unchanged. With appropriately calibrated parameters, these shifts improve overall accuracy and substantially accelerate convergence without increasing the formal scaling of the amplitude solve. Different optimal parameters for valence and Rydberg states reveal the limitations of a common parameter. The analysis further shows that shifting the contracted-triples block contributes markedly to the excitation-energy correction in addition to accelerating convergence.

articles.title: Why Emission Spectral Profile of Diverse Fluoro-phores Look Alike with Thick Polymer Overlayers?
articles.abstract: Fluorescence from fluorophore-polymer overlayers reflects an interplay between molecular photo-physics and thickness dependent optical propagation. Combining spectrally resolved single mole-cule measurements, transition dipole moment orientation analysis and ensemble fluorescence, we show that structurally and photophysically distinct fluorophores can exhibit similar red shifted emission profiles under thick polymer overlayers even without additional reflecting surface. This similarity indicates a common optical transfer function imposed by the overlayer rather than a pure-ly fluorophore specific molecular response. Although local molecular interactions, excited state dy-namics and vibronic coupling govern intrinsic emission, the overlayer modifies detected spectra through refractive index contrast, dielectric boundary reflections, cavity effects and collection ge-ometry. Vibronic energy spacing distributions remain largely preserved as thickness changes, whereas spectral positions and relative intensities vary systematically. Thus, polymer thickness pri-marily reshapes detected spectrum through optical propagation and outcoupling while retaining vi-brational modes. Time dependent density functional theory identifies candidate Franck-Condon and Herzberg-Teller active dye modes contributing to spectral fluctuations and dipole reorientation.

articles.title: A van der Waals Floating-Gate Platform for Broadband Optoelectronic Neuromorphic Computing
articles.abstract: Artificial synapses that integrate nonvolatile memory with broadband optoelectronic learning are essential for next-generation neuromorphic computing. However, their realization remains challenging because conventional floating-gate memories exhibit limited optical functionality and poor scalability. Here, we report a van der Waals ReS2/hBN/InSe floating-gate synaptic transistor that combines efficient charge storage with broadband optoelectronic learning in a single device architecture. The heterostructure incorporates InSe as a floating-gate layer for stable charge storage, hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) as a tunneling dielectric, and ReS2 as a photoresponsive channel, enabling carrier tunneling under electrical and optical stimulation. Through the combined operation of these layers, the device achieves a large memory window, an on/off current ratio exceeding 10^6, stable multilevel conductance states, and reliable retention over 10^4 s. Broadband visible-to-near-infrared optical excitation enables controllable synaptic weight modulation and the emulation of essential synaptic functions, including short- and long-term plasticity, paired-pulse facilitation, and pulse-amplitude- and pulse-duration-dependent plasticity. Optical potentiation and electrical depression further enable bidirectional modulation of synaptic weights. Beyond these synaptic functions, the device demonstrates higher-order learning through associative and discrimination conditioning inspired by the Pavlovian learning paradigm, as well as reconfigurable Boolean logic driven by electro-optical inputs. These results establish a multifunctional van der Waals floating-gate platform that integrates nonvolatile memory, broadband optoelectronic learning, and adaptive information processing within a single transistor, providing a promising strategy for compact, energy-efficient neuromorphic hardware.

articles.title: Control of the Electronic and Atomic Structure of the Altermagnetic α-MnTe Surface via Substrate-Induced Surfactants
articles.abstract: Altermagnets are a novel class of materials with unique momentum dependent spin-polarization of the electronic band structure, which opens up new avenues for spintronic devices. Altermagnetic α-MnTe is particularly interesting for such applications due to its giant spin splitting and the persistence of altermagnetic order up to room temperature. Growth of thin films is, however, challenging and governed by interactions with the substrate. As a result, the surface of α-MnTe thin films exhibits very different atomic structures in dependence of the substrate material. Whereas on SrF2(111) an atomically clean, perfectly (2x2) reconstructed surface forms, on InP(111)A the MnTe surface is always InTe terminated due to super-segregation of In from the substrate to the surface. Most strikingly, the InTe surfactant layer displays a quasi-periodic dislocation network to accommodate the InTe/MnTe lattice mismatch. This leads to the emergence of distinct surface states in dependence of surface termination that strongly affect the electronic band structure at the surface as shown by angle resolved photoemission and tunneling spectroscopy. Thus, control and characterization of the atomic structure of the surface is fundamentally important for understanding the properties of altermagnets and provides room for engineering and tailoring of spin-polarized states in actual devices.

articles.title: High-efficiency solid-state electrochemical thermal switching through phonon engineering of 2D materials
articles.abstract: Reversible solid-state thermal switches with large thermal contrasts remain rare, yet are essential for advanced thermal management. Using universal machine-learned interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) and density functional theory (DFT), we screen 57 transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), spanning the 1T and 2H phases with Li and Mg intercalation. Among the candidates, Li$_a$ZrS$_2$ combines exceptional thermal conductivity switching with low heat capacity. Lithiation to Li$_{0.125}$ZrS$_2$ reduces the cross-plane thermal conductivity from approximately 3.7 to 0.05 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$. The switching behaviour exceeds that of previously reported solid-state electrochemical thermal switches. Device-level modelling further demonstrates the potential for waste-heat recovery, with a pulsed system capturing 86\% of the energy recovered by an ideal switch. We attribute the switching behaviour to substantial softening of the Zr--Zr framework, with the mean force constant decreasing from approximately 4.2 to 1.2 eV $\mathrm{\mathring{A}}^{-2}$, alongside enhanced scattering of heat-carrying acoustic phonons. These findings establish electrochemical intercalation as a promising route to engineering thermal transport in layered materials.

articles.title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
articles.abstract: Long-term stability remains a critical challenge limiting the photovoltaic and optoelectronic applications of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites. In these materials, the choice of the organic spacer plays a key role not only in enhancing environmental stability, but also in determining their structural characteristics and carrier dynamics. Here, we present an environmental photo- and thermal-stability analysis of BA2PbI4 and PEA2PbI4 two-dimensional lead halide perovskites by means of confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy techniques. We have investigated two different organic spacers, n-butylammonium (BA) and 2-phenylethylammonium (PEA), which provide comparable room-temperature luminescence in freshly exfoliated perovskite nanoflakes and degrade similarly through the removal of organic components and fast crystal phase decomposition into PbI2 and Pb0. However, we observed that the PEA organic cation significantly improves crystal morphology and suppresses lattice defects, resulting in slower degradation and enhanced resistance to light and thermal stress under ambient conditions. Our findings indicate that structural and chemical engineering, along with surface passivation and encapsulation strategies, are essential for achieving long-term stability in two-dimensional halide perovskite devices. Nevertheless, optimizing the balance between stability and device performance remains a critical consideration.

articles.title: Magnetoelectric Exchange Spring for Spin-Wave Logic with Ultralow Energy Consumption
articles.abstract: Spin waves (magnons) are intrinsically free of Joule heating during their propagation in magnets. Exploring, understanding, and manipulating such quasiparticles not only helps reveal the exotic magnonic phenomena in condensed matter physics but also underpins the development of information devices with low energy consumption. However, achieving low-power and scalable control of spin-wave propagation remains a critical challenge. Herein, a magnetoelectric exchange spring has been artificially designed and constructed across an interface between ferroelectric BaTiO3 and ferromagnetic (La,Sr)MnO3 with low magnetic damping, in which polarization-modulated orbital reconstruction tailors local magnetic anisotropy and enables reversible control of spin-wave propagation. By successfully deviating from the Janovec-Kay-Dunn law, reversal polarization of engineered BaTiO3 (Ps~1.2 uC cm^-2, Vc~0.4 V) is sufficient to switch the coherent magnon transport in the (La,Sr)MnO3, indicating the magnetoelectric heterointerface may serve as a promising candidate for atto-joule control of spin-wave propagation (normalized to a 10*10 nm^2 device). Furthermore, taking advantage of amplitude, phase, and frequency to encode spin waves, all 16 compact Boolean logics with ultralow energy consumption have been designed. The artificial magnetoelectric exchange spring can be broadly applicable to various material choices, offering a versatile platform for developing energy-efficient and integrated magnonic devices.

articles.title: Multi-objective Bayesian optimization reveals HiPIMS deposition rates exceeding direct current sputtering
articles.abstract: Pulsed sputter processes are essential for a wide range of applications from hard coatings to microelectronics. High power impulse magnetron sputtering (HiPIMS) offers unique possibilities for process design due to its high ionized flux fraction. Because of the high peak-current densities involved, correspondingly high plasma densities generate many ions. This enables tuning of kinetic energies by applying accelerating bias potentials. However, some HiPIMS processes have low deposition rates due to the back-attraction these ions experience with the negatively charged sputter target. Recent work in HiPIMS has targeted this problem, exploring complex pulsing schemes such as bipolar, multi-pulse, or chopped HiPIMS. These pulsing schemes introduce another problem: process complexity. As such, the process space, even with coarse intervals quickly blows up to 1E5-1E20 possible process combinations. This calls for efficient and intelligent sampling, which can be enabled by machine-learning algorithms such as Bayesian optimization. In this work we use multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) to efficiently sample the process space of pulse-packets, targeting high ionization flux fractions and deposition rates. Over 2,000 distinct processes were sampled during this exploration. Surprisingly, we found that many HiPIMS processes, including single pulse, can achieve deposition rates higher than DC references. In fact, at a working pressure of 1.0 Pa and moderate ionization rates of 5-20% we found that ms-scale pulses were ideal. We hypothesize these processes maximize gas rarefaction, creating a low-collision channel between the target and the substrate. These results showcase previously unreported behavior of pulsed sputter processes and challenge a long-held trade-off between film quality and speed in thin-film manufacturing.

articles.title: Nonlocal Einstein Relation in Confined Phonon Hydrodynamics
articles.abstract: Einstein relations connect carrier mobility to macroscopic transport coefficients and constitute a fundamental link between microscopic dynamics and transport. In phonon hydrodynamics, this connection is conventionally local: the drift-induced thermal conductivity is proportional to the local drift mobility. Here we show that this relation becomes intrinsically nonlocal under spatial confinement. We derive a nonlocal Einstein relation, $κ_H(y) = \int P(y-y')μ(y'),dy'$, in which hydrodynamic thermal conductivity $κ_H(y)$ at one position depends on collective drift mobility $μ(y')$ across the entire cross-section of the channel. In the small-Knudsen-number limit, our nonlocal theory recovers the viscous heat equation and the local Einstein relation. At finite Knudsen number, nonlocality produces intrinsic boundary slip and distinct size-scaling behavior of the drift mobility $μ$ and hydrodynamic thermal conductivity $κ_H(y)$. First-principles calculations for graphite show that nonlocality broadens the channel-size window over which thermal conductivity exhibits superlinear size dependence. Temperature-dependent simulations further show that the nonlocal theory captures the emergence of a hydrodynamic peak in thermal conductivity normalized by ballistic conductance, whereas the local theory fails to accurately predict its magnitude. Our results establish a microscopic connection between collective phonon mobility and heat conduction beyond local hydrodynamics.

articles.title: Optical Thermometry in Monolayer WS2: Raman and Photoluminescence Spectroscopy from 5 K to 1273 K
articles.abstract: Reliable temperature measurement is essential for characterizing and engineering two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor devices, yet optical thermometry of 2D materials has so far been demonstrated only over narrow temperature windows spanning a few hundred kelvin. Here, we establish a comprehensive optical thermometry framework for monolayer WS2 from 5~K to 1273~K. We show that: (i) the out-of-plane A1g Raman mode shifts linearly with temperature above 100~K, with a slope of -0.0138 cm^{-1}/K in non-encapsulated WS2 (fitted over 298-1223~K) and a measurably smaller slope of -0.0121 cm^{-1}/K in an hBN-encapsulated sample (fitted over 100-1273~K); (ii) photoluminescence spectra measured over the same 5--1273~K range provide an independent optical indicator of the temperature: the neutral-exciton emission redshifts continuously with temperature and is well described by the semi-empirical Pässler model. The two indicators probe distinct physical mechanisms, lattice anharmonicity and bandgap renormalization, and together provide contact-free thermometry for monolayer WS2 from 5~K to 1273~K, an approach applicable to 2D semiconductors more broadly.

articles.title: Precursor Ratio-Controlled Chloride Vacancies in Lead-Free KCuCl3-x Memristors for Forming-Free Gradual Resistive Switching and Neuromorphic Learning
articles.abstract: Defect engineering of memristive materials offers a powerful strategy for regulating ionic transport and analog resistive switching required for neuromorphic computing. Here, we report a wet chemical synthesis route for chloride-vacancy (VCl) engineering in lead-free all-inorganic KCuCl3-x thin films and establish a direct correlation between defect concentration, electronic structure, transport dynamics, and neuromorphic performance. Controlled precursor-ratio variation systematically tunes the VCl concentration in KCuCl3-x thin films, driving preferential vacancy formation at the terminal chloride sites, band-gap narrowing, and enhanced electronic disorder. W/KCuCl3-x/FTO memristors exhibit stable bipolar VCM-type resistive switching, with increasing VCl concentration promoting forming-free operation. An optimal VCl concentration (~ 1.3*10^21 cm^-3) provides a balance between ionic mobility and defect controllability, resulting in highly linear potentiation/depression characteristics and superior pulse endurance (>104 cycles). When the experimentally measured conductance characteristics of the optimized memristor are implemented as synaptic weights in artificial neural network simulations, recognition accuracies of 98.96% and 91.82% are achieved on the MNIST and Fashion-MNIST datasets, respectively. These findings establish precursor ratio-controlled VCl engineering as an effective strategy for simultaneously optimizing ionic transport, analog switching, and neuromorphic learning in lead-free halide perovskite memristors, providing a general materials design principle for energy-efficient neuromorphic electronics.

articles.title: Pulsed Laser Deposition of Ferroelectric SrTiO3 Shells Enables Polarization-Controlled Charge Separation in TiO2 Photoanode
articles.abstract: Ferroelectric polarization offers a powerful route to govern the interfacial charge separation in photoelectrodes; however, chemically converted ferroelectric shells lack sub-nanometer thickness control, coherent strain retention, and chemically clean interfaces. Here, we use pulsed laser deposition to fabricate stoichiometric SrTiO3 shells on hydrothermally grown TiO2 nanorod arrays, achieving atomically defined core-shell architectures while preserving the one-dimensional transport geometry. The photocurrent density followed a volcano-shaped dependence on shell thickness and reached 1.9 mA cm-2 at 1.23 V versus RHE under AM 1.5G illumination for the optimized 15-mins sample, exceeding the established hydrothermal benchmark. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy revealed a tetragonally distorted, oxygen-stoichiometric shell, identifying coherent interfacial strain rather than defect dipoles as the origin of the ferroelectric order. Kelvin probe force microscopy directly imaged a polarization-induced built-in electric field whose magnitude scaled with charge-transfer efficiency and photocurrent density. Together, these complementary structural, chemical, electrostatic, and device-level measurements established a quantitative strain-polarization-built-in field-charge separation relationship. This work transforms ferroelectric photoanode engineering from empirical optimization into an atomically controllable and predictive materials strategy for high-efficiency solar water-splitting devices. This approach is readily extendable to visible-light absorbers and complex ferroelectric heterostructures.

articles.title: Retention-constrained fine-tuning of a pre-trained aluminium MACE potential for non-equilibrium defect dynamics and plasticity
articles.abstract: Adapting a pre-trained machine-learning interatomic potential for non-equilibrium defect dynamics and plasticity requires improving defect accuracy without degrading the near-equilibrium elastic and vibrational response. Here we achieve this balance for the aluminium MACE potential QP17 by integrating conditional readout uncertainty, iterative full-parameter updates and protocol-compatible relative-energy anchoring. Sensitivities over 144 linear readout weights guide acquisition, with within-batch covariance updates and evolving neural representations. After four active-learning rounds (32 acquired configurations and 400 gradient updates), force-uncertainty acquisition reduces mean development force error from 22.43 to 21.52 meV/Angstrom, outperforming random sampling (22.70), geometry-diversity selection (22.46) and uniform training across all 104 candidate labels (22.71) under the same update budget. All three force-uncertainty runs satisfy bulk-mechanical retention criteria: historical relative-energy error decreases from 0.375 to 0.207 meV/atom, while harmonic phonon root-mean-square drift remains below 0.05 THz. Matched objective ablations reveal that relative-energy anchoring suppresses harmonic drift. Out-of-sample evaluations across planar faults, twin boundaries and grain boundaries demonstrate transferable gains in defect energies and deviatoric stresses, even though virial stresses are never fitted. A closed-loop molecular dynamics and density functional theory (MD-DFT) pilot confirms that automated acceptance gating intercepts updates that violate historical elastic-group energy or vibrational tolerances. Together, these components establish a retention-constrained fine-tuning protocol for improving plastic-deformation observables while preserving the tested bulk mechanical response.

articles.title: Temperature-dependent magnetic properties of the antiferromagnet Mn$_2$Au
articles.abstract: Mn$_2$Au is one of the most promising materials for antiferromagnetic spintronics due to its high Néel temperature, moderate anisotropy, layered spin structure allowing current induced spin-orbit-torques, and ultrafast spin dynamics. Further understanding and control of the magnetic order in Mn$_2$Au for ultrafast spintronics applications via ultrashort electric/optical means requires accurate understanding of how its magnetic properties depend on temperature. Here we present atomistic spin dynamics simulations of the temperature-dependent macroscopic magnetic properties of Mn$_2$Au single crystals. We introduce a spin Hamiltonian based on previous ab initio calculations which produces temperature-dependent scaling of the anisotropy constants with magnetisation consistent with Zener-Akulov-Callen-Callen power laws. The calculated temperature dependence of exchange stiffness follows a scaling law with magnetisation of $m^{1.83}_e$ , and predicts a temperature-dependent domain wall width that agrees very well with direct simulation. Our model provides an understanding of temperature-dependent magnetic properties of Mn$_2$Au that enables large-scale simulation of the working conditions of spintronic devices.

articles.title: Third harmonic generation in the transition metal trichalcogenides
articles.abstract: The transition metal trichalcogenides (TMTs) are an interesting class of layered 2D materials that have strong anisotropic electrical and optical properties. We report on the polarization-dependent nonlinear optical response of exfoliated crystals at the third harmonic using non-resonant excitation with a 1560 nm femtosecond laser. All members of the TMT crystal family explored (ZrS3, HfS3, TiS3, and NbS3) display large anisotropy in their polarized third harmonic generation signal, with anisotropy ratios as large as chi_11/chi_22 ~ 6.5. From the expected nonlinear dependence of these monoclinic and triclinic crystals we extract the relative nonlinear susceptibility coefficients. We find that the anisotropy ratio is largest for ZrS3 and decreases across the family, a trend we associate with the proximity of the third harmonic energy to the strongly b-polarized absorption edge of each material. NbS3, the only triclinic crystal, displays a pronounced anisotropy in thick flakes that is strongly reduced in the thinnest flakes, which we attribute to a partial relaxation of the Peierls-type Nb-Nb dimerization that underlies the triclinic distortion. The large anisotropic nonlinear response in this crystal family sets it apart from other 2D materials and makes it particularly attractive for further investigation.

articles.title: Zeeman-field-induced three-spin interactions and relativistic coupling to the scalar spin chirality
articles.abstract: Magnetic fields are commonly incorporated in atomistic spin models through the Zeeman energy of individual magnetic moments. Starting from a microscopic electronic Hamiltonian, we show that the Zeeman coupling of conduction electrons also generates field-linear three-spin interactions, the lowest-order corrections allowed by time-reversal symmetry. Using a Green-function expansion of the grand potential, we identify two classes of interactions. Isotropic terms of the form $(\mathbf S_i\cdot\mathbf S_j)(\mathbf S_k\cdot\mathbf B)$ exist without spin-orbit coupling, and their total strength obeys a sum rule involving the three-site electronic loop at the Fermi energy. Relativistic terms require spin-orbit coupling and include $\mathbf K_{ijk}\cdot\mathbf B,χ_{ijk}$, where $χ_{ijk}=\mathbf S_i\cdot(\mathbf S_j\times\mathbf S_k)$ is the scalar spin chirality. We show that this coupling is forbidden in the spin channel without spin-orbit coupling, whereas the orbital channel recovers the orbital-flux mechanism of Mott insulators. Exact diagonalization of the Hubbard trimer confirms the independence and additivity of both channels. For magnetic trimers in Rashba electron gases, we derive analytical expressions showing that $\mathbf K_{ijk}$ lies in-plane at first order in spin-orbit coupling but vanishes for $C_{3v}$-symmetric trimers, where an out-of-plane component emerges at second order. These interactions can shift magnetization-step fields and modify field-induced noncoplanarity. In the continuum limit, the chirality coupling splits skyrmions from antiskyrmions, while the relativistic terms generate a field-dependent Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction.

articles.title: $κ$-Parametrized Boltzmann Distribution Sampling on Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
articles.abstract: Generative models use training data to produce new samples that resemble the original, with applications in classification and recommendation systems. Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs) are at the core of generative models but suffer from the computational intractability of training, which relies on sampling an unknown Boltzmann Distribution (BD). The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) can assist RBM training, potentially providing benefits over strictly classical strategies. One particular problem is determining the quantum circuit depth for an arbitrary problem size that yields the expected sampling results. In this study, we evaluate QAOA-assisted sampling of BDs using Qiskit's Aer Simulator by analysing the inverse effective temperature of the distribution, $κ$, for tractable problem sizes. The results provide numerical evidence, based on Qiskit Aer simulations, that parameterized annealing-scheduled QAOA (PAQ-QAOA) can approximate RBM Boltzmann sampling for the tractable instances considered, while hardware performance and scaling remain open questions.

articles.title: A Control Line Multiplexing Framework for Scalable Quantum Computing
articles.abstract: Universal fault-tolerant superconducting quantum computers are expected to require millions of physical qubits; yet extending the prevailing dedicated-control-line paradigm to this scale would exceed the wiring density and cooling-power budget of dilution refrigerators. Microwave frequency-division multiplexing (FDM) revolutionized classical communications by enabling many independent channels to share common transmission infrastructure. Translating this principle to superconducting quantum control, however, requires an all-microwave architecture and experimental validation of frequency-multiplexed gate control.
