articles.title: A license to disperse: climatic niche lability and geographic expansion shape the diversification of Oleaceae
articles.abstract: SEM for seven variables (rPC1, rPC2, rPC3, rFRic, FRic, dispersal, and speciation) in Oleaceae and that in Jasmineae and Oleeae, respectively. Summary Patterns of species diversity reflect interactions among ecological, biogeographic, and lineage‐specific evolutionary processes. Oleaceae provides a useful comparative system because its five tribes differ markedly in species richness, geographic extent, dispersal history, and genomic background. Using distribution data for 476 species and a time‐calibrated phylogeny of 283 Oleaceae species spanning all five tribes, we integrated ecological niche modelling, ancestral‐range and climatic‐niche reconstruction, diversification‐rate analyses, and phylogenetic comparative methods while accounting for uneven tribal sampling. Climatic niche position and breadth evolved heterogeneously across Oleaceae, while major range expansions beyond the reconstructed ancestral Asian region were concentrated in Jasmineae and Oleeae. Climatic niche evolution and speciation rates were not consistently coupled; rather, their relationships with dispersal and diversification were lineage‐ and climatic‐axis‐specific. Oleeae showed more coordinated associations among niche evolution, dispersal, and speciation, whereas Jasmineae exhibited a more restricted, axis‐specific pattern. The ancient whole‐genome duplication (WGD) in Oleeae may have contributed to its distinctive evolutionary trajectory. Overall, our results support a conditional ‘license to disperse’ framework in which climatic niche lability facilitates geographic expansion, thereby indirectly increasing opportunities for diversification.

articles.title: A single‐nucleus multiome profiling reveals the regulatory programs driving plant nematode–induced syncytium
articles.abstract: Single‐nucleus transcriptome profiles of Heterodera schachtii–induced syncytium on Arabidopsis roots. Summary Plant‐parasitic cyst nematodes induce the formation of specialized feeding structures, known as syncytia, within host roots by orchestrating extensive transcriptional and epigenetic reprogramming. Here, we generated parallel single‐nucleus RNA‐seq and ATAC‐seq libraries from fully developed Heterodera schachtii–induced syncytia on Arabidopsis roots. We analyzed high‐quality transcriptome and chromatin profiles independently and in an integrated framework. We identified multiple transcriptomic cell states, several of which were highly syncytium‐enriched and spanned vascular and cortical identities. Differential expression analysis identified hundreds of syncytium‐enriched genes, and pseudotime trajectory inference points to potential compartmentalization or functional heterogeneity of syncytium nuclei, consistent with the possibility of distinct transcriptional programs within or between mature syncytia. Joint clustering of snATAC‐seq with snRNA‐seq delineated syncytium‐unique chromatin accessibility landscapes, with several cell states exhibiting extensive open chromatin linked to upregulated genes. Motif enrichment across these accessible regions highlighted cis‐regulatory elements mainly for AP2, bZIP, bHLH, MYB, and TCP transcription factors and identified functionally validated members of these families as candidate regulators of syncytium identity. Our study establishes a multiome atlas of syncytial cells and uncovers the regulatory programs driving nematode feeding site maintenance, as well as transcriptionally distinct nuclear states that may reflect functional specialization within or between the syncytia.

articles.title: Frenemies forever: when parasitic fungi become an insect's secret weapon
articles.abstract: Insect symbiotic yeast and fungi shape host–plant interactions. Summary Plant‐feeding insects pose a major threat to global food production, and finding sustainable pest control strategies is challenging. Insect‐associated symbiotic microorganisms fulfill important beneficial functions for their host insects, enabling them to adapt and thrive in a changing environment. Understanding how these interactions evolve and what they mean for insect–plant interactions is key to the development of novel targets and potential tools for pest control. Since yeast and fungal insect symbionts are understudied in comparison to bacterial symbionts, this Tansley Insight explores their role in insect–plant interactions.

articles.title: High‐light adaptation via ferredoxin‐mediated tuning of the photosynthesis–photoprotection trade‐off
articles.abstract: Proposed model of the alternative regulation of the photosynthesis in Fd1‐OE Nicotiana tabacum plants. Summary Plants continuously adjust photosynthesis to balance growth and photoprotection under changing environmental conditions. Environmental fluctuations frequently impose a mismatch between energy production and CO2 assimilation. How photochemical reactions are regulated to maintain performance under these conditions remains a central question in plant biology. We previously developed transplastomic tobacco (Fd1‐OE plants) overexpressing ferredoxin displaying enhanced photoprotection and growth penalties with a variegated leaf phenotype under glasshouse conditions. Here, we investigate how these plants respond to different growth irradiances using physiological, ultrastructural, and photosynthetic analyses, including Pulse‐Amplitude Modulation (PAM), gas exchange, and P700 absorbance measurements, and dynamic‐light assays. Fd1‐OE plants progressively recovered growth, leaf phenotype, and photosynthetic performance as growth irradiance increased, reaching near wild‐type performance at 1400 μmol m−2 s−1. This enhanced adaptation to ‘high‐light’ was associated with a larger fraction of open Photosystem II reaction centers and enhanced nonphotochemical quenching. Dynamic‐light analyses further revealed faster plastoquinone (PQ) turnover, a more oxidized (PQ) pool and enhanced electron withdrawal downstream of Photosystem I. Our results indicate that ferredoxin overexpression redefines the balance between photochemistry and photoprotection. This adjustment shifts adaptation toward higher irradiance and enhances photosynthetic performance under changing light environments. Electron partitioning downstream of Photosystem I emerges as a promising target to improve photosynthetic resilience. Resumen Las plantas regulan continuamente la fotosíntesis para equilibrar el crecimiento y la fotoprotección frente a condiciones ambientales cambiantes. Las fluctuaciones ambientales imponen con frecuencia un desajuste entre la producción de energía y la asimilación de CO2. La forma en que se regulan las reacciones fotoquímicas para mantener el rendimiento bajo estas condiciones continúa siendo una cuestión central en la biología vegetal. Previamente desarrollamos plantas de tabaco transplastómicas (Fd1‐OE) que sobreexpresan ferredoxina y presentan una fotoprotección mejorada, junto con penalizaciones en el crecimiento y un fenotipo foliar variegado bajo condiciones de invernadero. En este trabajo, investigamos cómo estas plantas responden a diferentes irradiancias de crecimiento mediante análisis fisiológicos, ultraestructurales y fotosintéticos, incluyendo mediciones con PAM, intercambio gaseoso y absorbancia de P700, así como ensayos bajo luz dinámica. Las plantas Fd1‐OE recuperaron progresivamente el crecimiento, el fenotipo foliar y el rendimiento fotosintético a medida que aumentó la irradiancia de crecimiento, alcanzando un rendimiento cercano al del tipo silvestre a 1400 μmol m−2 s−1. Esta mayor adaptación a condiciones de ‘alta luz’ se asocia con una mayor fracción de centros de reacción del fotosistema II abiertos y un mayor NPQ. Los análisis bajo luz dinámica revelaron además una mayor velocidad de recambio de las plastoquinonas, un pool de plastoquinonas más oxidado y una mayor extracción de electrones cadena abajo del fotosistema I. Nuestros resultados indican que la sobreexpresión de ferredoxina redefine el equilibrio entre la fotoquímica y la fotoprotección. Este ajuste desplaza la adaptación hacia irradiancias más altas y mejora el rendimiento fotosintético frente a entornos lumínicos cambiantes. La partición de electrones cadena abajo del fotosistema I emerge como un blanco prometedor para mejorar la resiliencia fotosintética.

articles.title: Pathogen nutrient acquisition strategy mediates the strength of diversity–disease relationships in natural grasslands
articles.abstract: Overview of the study sites. Summary The relationship between biodiversity and disease risk is a cornerstone of disease ecology, yet predicting its direction and strength remains challenging. Pathogen nutrient acquisition strategies may be key to resolving this context dependency, but their roles in mediating diversity–disease relationships are poorly understood. Here, we combine a large‐scale survey spanning 2000 km in natural grasslands with advanced statistical modeling to demonstrate that pathogen nutrient acquisition strategy is a critical mediator. We show that diseases caused by biotrophic pathogens (e.g. rusts and powdery mildews), which depend on living host tissues, exhibit a significantly negative diversity–disease relationship, whereas diseases caused by necrotrophic pathogens (e.g. leaf spots and blights) show no significant relationship. Furthermore, the strength of this negative relationship for biotrophic pathogens is amplified in regions with higher disease severity. Bayesian structural equation modeling reveals that plant species richness directly reduces biotrophic disease severity, while for necrotrophic pathogens, precipitation is the primary driver of severity, with no direct effect of richness. Our findings provide a trait‐based framework linking climatic drivers, pathogen nutrient acquisition strategies, and the strength of diversity–disease relationships. These results enhance our ability to predict disease dynamics under biodiversity loss and inform biodiversity‐based disease management strategies.

articles.title: Phosphatidylcholine acyl turnover facilitates thylakoid lipid remodeling and promotes plant survival under heat stress
articles.abstract: Coordinated galactolipid–TAG conversion during heat stress–induced thylakoid lipid remodeling. Summary Heat stress destabilizes chloroplast membranes, requiring rapid lipid remodeling to maintain photosynthetic function. Although thylakoid lipid remodeling and triacylglycerol (TAG) accumulation are established heat responses, the role of phosphatidylcholine (PC) acyl turnover remains unclear. We investigated lysophosphatidylcholine acyltransferase 1 and 2 (LPCAT1/2), REDUCED OLEATE DESATURATION1 (ROD1), phospholipid:diacylglycerol acyltransferase 1 (PDAT1), and lipins in heat‐induced lipid remodeling and thermotolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana. Using genetic, lipidomic, physiological, and photosynthetic analyses, we examined mutants defective in PC acyl editing, PC–diacylglycerol (DAG) interconversion, TAG synthesis, and phosphatidic acid dephosphorylation during heat stress. Loss of LPCAT1/2 severely impaired basal and acquired thermotolerance, caused irreversible photosystem II damage, and disrupted thylakoid lipid remodeling. rod1 showed minor defects, whereas rod1 lpcat1/2 exhibited enhanced thermosensitivity. In mature vegetative plants, pdat1‐2 showed thermotolerance and photosystem II defects comparable to lpcat1/2. Lipin‐mediated phosphatidic acid dephosphorylation provided the major DAG source for heat‐induced TAG synthesis. Defective PC acyl turnover also increased free fatty acids and lipid peroxidation. These findings establish LPCAT1/2‐mediated PC acyl turnover as a central regulator of heat‐induced membrane remodeling and thermotolerance and link lipin‐dependent DAG production and TAG synthesis with chloroplast membrane homeostasis.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and chemotherapy versus standard of care for locally advanced rectal cancer (UNION): a prespecified interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial
articles.abstract: BackgroundTo our knowledge, UNION is the first phase 3 trial to assess a neoadjuvant strategy incorporating radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and chemotherapy compared with standard care in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, which reported positive results for the primary endpoint (blinded independent review committee [BIRC]-assessed pathological complete response rate; 39·8% vs 15·3%). Here, we present a prespecified interim analysis of event-free survival.MethodsThis open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial was conducted at nine hospitals in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years with untreated cT3-4 or N+ rectal adenocarcinoma (≤10 cm distance from the anal verge) and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1; stratified by clinical T stage and N stage), using permuted blocks, to receive neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy (25 Gy in five fractions) followed by two cycles of intravenous camrelizumab (200 mg on day 1) plus CAPOX (oral capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1-14 and intravenous oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 on day 1; experimental group) or long-course chemoradiotherapy (50·4 Gy in 28 fractions with concurrent oral capecitabine 825 mg/m2 twice daily) followed by two cycles of CAPOX (standard-of-care group). After surgery, both groups received six cycles of adjuvant CAPOX, and the experimental group additionally received adjuvant camrelizumab for up to 15 cycles. The primary endpoint was BIRC-assessed pathological complete response rate in the intention-to-treat population, which has been previously reported. Here, we performed a prespecified interim analysis of investigator-assessed event-free survival (one of the key secondary endpoints, defined as time from randomisation to radiographic progression precluding surgery, local recurrence or distant metastasis, or death) in the intention-to-treat population (all randomly assigned patients) with a boundary of a two-sided p values less than 0·0102. Safety was evaluated in all patients who received at least one dose of the study treatment according to the assigned regimen. The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04928807, and is active, but no longer recruiting.FindingsBetween July 23, 2021, and March 1, 2023, 231 patients (153 [66%] males and 78 [34%] females; 227 [98%] were Han Chinese, and four [2%] were other ethnicity Chinese) were randomly assigned to the experimental group (n=113) and standard-of-care group (n=118). As of Oct 1, 2025, the median follow-up duration was 36·7 months (IQR 32·6-39·9) in the experimental group and 34·7 months (31·1-39·1) in the standard-of-care group. The 3-year investigator-assessed event-free survival rate was 91·3% (95% CI 83·9-95·4) in the experimental group versus 77·4% (67·9-84·4) in the standard-of-care group (stratified hazard ratio 0·33 [0·15-0·71]; two-sided log-rank p=0·0029). During the entire treatment period, the most common grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were decreased lymphocyte count (23 [20%] of 115 in the experimental group vs 31 [28%] of 112 in the standard-of-care group), decreased white blood cell count (13 [11%] vs 16 [14%]), decreased neutrophil count (13 [11%] vs 13 [12%]), and decreased platelet count (seven [6%] vs 15 [13%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 22 (19%) versus 15 (13%) patients, with the most common being decreased platelet count (one [1%] vs six [5%]), and radiation gastroenteritis (two [2%] vs four [4%]). Treatment-related deaths occurred in one patient in the experimental group (septic shock related to chemotherapy, but unrelated to camrelizumab) and none in the standard-of-care group.InterpretationIn this interim analysis, short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and CAPOX significantly improved 3-year event-free survival in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, with a safety profile similar to long-course chemoradiotherapy followed by CAPOX.…

articles.title: Extremal and global-time statistics of sluggish random walks with stochastic resetting
articles.abstract: We study the extremal and global-time statistics of a one-dimensional sluggish random walk, whose diffusivity decays as a power law of the distance from the origin, under Poissonian resetting to the origin. A change of variable maps the process onto a signed Bessel process, so that renewal theory applies. We obtain the exact Laplace transform of the distribution of the maximum over a finite window. At long times the centered maximum of the transformed process follows the Gumbel law, and in physical space the typical maximum grows as a power of the logarithm of the window length. The far-tail rate function does not depend on $α$ in the Bessel variable, so the second-order dynamical transition known for Brownian resetting, between maxima produced by a single anomalously long inter-reset interval and maxima produced by an interval occupying essentially the whole window, holds for every $α$. The time of the maximum is uniformly distributed in the bulk of the window, with boundary layers that shift its mean above the midpoint logarithmically in the window length. The last-passage time through the origin has an exact density, and the time elapsed since it converges to a Gamma law. Reflection symmetry makes the occupation time of the positive half-line and the last-passage time uncorrelated. The results reduce to the Brownian case and agree with simulations.

articles.title: Non-magnetic impurities as a quantum microscope of finite size effects in spin chains
articles.abstract: Finite-size effects are ubiquitous in quantum matter, yet typically invisible in the thermodynamic limit; when system size is restricted, boundaries and confinement reveal modified spectra, correlations, and emergent phenomena. With growing access to well-controlled few-spin systems, these effects are now directly observable and offer a route to probing universal physics and enabling quantum information applications. Here, we study finite-size physics in the quasi-one-dimensional Ising-like quantum antiferromagnet Ba(Co$_{1-x}$Mg$_x$)$_2$V$_2$O$_8$ with $x = 2\%$ and $x = 5\%$, where non-magnetic Mg$^{2+}$ ions fragment the Co$^{2+}$ spin chains into finite segments. Combining inelastic neutron scattering and numerical calculations, we identify distinct regimes with fundamentally different low-energy quantum excitations: spinons confined to chain boundaries, and a cluster mode in shorter chains corresponding to a collective reversal of the Néel-ordered segment without classical analogue. Our results demonstrate how chemical substitution acts as a quantum microscope providing direct access to boundary-shaped excitations in strongly correlated spin systems.

articles.title: Spontaneous magnetic diode effect in Co$_{1/3}$TaS$_2$
articles.abstract: When electrons move through non-trivial spin textures in magnetic metals, conduction electrons couple to magnetic order through both their charge and their spin, acquiring non-trivial equations of motion and a dynamic spin polarization providing the foundation of spintronics. These mechanisms are, however, almost invariably reciprocal and the resistance a current encounters does not depend on its flow direction. Here we show that a chiral crystal lattice and an independently reversible chiral magnetic order together produce a diode whose forward direction is set by the magnetism rather than by the structure. In the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet Co$_{1/3}$TaS$_2$, whose chiral lattice hosts a chiral magnetic order of its own, independent handedness, we observe a pronounced nonreciprocal resistance. Unlike conventional electrical magnetochiral anisotropy, which is driven by an external magnetic field, our spontaneous magnetic diode effect arises from an internal noncoplanar spin texture with vanishing net magnetization. Symmetry analysis and model calculations show that the effect originates from the interplay of noncoplanar spin order and spin-orbit coupling, which generates a chiral, time-reversal-symmetry-breaking electronic response. Crucially, reversing the magnetic handedness reverses the sign of the nonreciprocal resistance, demonstrating magnetic control of the diode polarity.

articles.title: Synthetic staggered fields switch Neel vectors probed by magnetic resonance
articles.abstract: Electrical detection of antiferromagnetic order is a critical challenge for antiferromagnetic spintronics owing to their vanishing macroscopic magnetisation. While magnetic resonance has demonstrated sub-terahertz antiferromagnetic spin pumping and nonlinear magnon dynamics, its application to electrically contacted on-chip devices has room for further exploration. Here we show that magnetic resonance enables direct electrical detection of Néel vector states. A $180^\circ$ reversal in synthetic antiferromagnets is realised by current-driven effective fields with opposite polarisation acting on each magnetic sublayer, which we term synthetic staggered fields. The switching induces a $π$ phase shift of precessional motion in time, producing hysteretic rectified voltages in our phase-sensitive detection scheme. Angular-dependent resonance analysis offers further insight into the Néel vector directions, pointing to a model beyond the macrospin formalism. We address this by defect-incorporated micromagnetic simulations that reveal fragmented domain states after current excitation. An extracted current density of $7.4\times10^{9}$ A/m$^2$ is, to our knowledge, the lowest reported value for the room-temperature Néel vector switching and we show that it scales with the in-plane uniaxial anisotropy both experimentally and numerically. Synthetic staggered fields and the resonance-based methodology provide a research platform for nanoscale characterisation of electrically driven antiferromagnetic textures, guiding the development of high-frequency on-chip spintronic architectures.

articles.title: Second order N-Electron Valence state Perturbation Theory for polaritonic systems
articles.abstract: Molecules strongly coupled to optical cavities often show multi-configurational character, which the cavity can enhance by mixing electronic states. Describing them accurately requires a complete treatment of correlation between all the involved quantum particles. The available QED ab-initio methods do not treat it in its completeness except for QED-FCI. We extend second-order N-electron valence state perturbation theory (NEVPT2) to polaritonic chemistry, in its state-specific (QED-NEVPT2) and quasi degenerate (QED-QD-NEVPT2) forms. Here, the correlation due to the interaction of more degenerate configurations comes from a QED-CASSCF reference, while that associated with instantaneous interactions between the particles is added by second-order perturbation theory. Application of the methods to ammonia, ethylene and formaldimine revealed that this approach represents the perfect alternative to the well established QED-Coupled Cluster approach when the molecular system is described by more degenerate configurations. The approaches developed in this work have the potential to become state-of-the-art methodologies for the description of reactivity and photochemistry in polaritonic systems.

articles.title: A thermodynamic correction layer for machine learning interatomic potentials
articles.abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials enable atomistic simulations with near \textit{ab initio} accuracy over large length and time scales. Foundation models extend this capability across the periodic table but inherit the thermodynamic description of the electronic structure methods used to generate their training data. Small errors in relative phase stability can therefore produce large errors in transformation temperatures. We introduce an additive thermodynamic correction layer that shifts phase free energies towards an assessed reference without retraining or modifying the base potential. A first order thermodynamic construction converts the required phase free energy shifts directly into configuration energy targets, which are fitted using a linear atomic cluster expansion and refined iteratively from measured free energies. We apply the method to melting and solid to solid transformations across elements with different crystal structures using a foundation GRACE model. After the correction, all transformation temperatures lie within the prescribed tolerance of the assessed values, including Ca, Ti, and Zr, where a solid to solid transition and melting are corrected together. Static energy curves, bulk moduli, and liquid structure remain close to those of the base model. Vacancy formation energies, thermal expansion, and liquid density depend on the corrected phase balance and change where the correction is large. The method requires neither retraining, differentiable dynamics, nor access to the parameters of the base potential. It provides a modular route for combining transferable atomistic models with assessed phase thermodynamics.

articles.title: Axion Quasibound States in the Continuum and Their Enhanced Axion Nonlinearity
articles.abstract: Dynamical axion quasiparticles (DAQs) in condensed-matter systmes have emerged as a fascinating platform for exploring axion physics and nonlinear optical phenomena. However, the amplitude of the coherent oscillating $θ$ field is even smaller than that of the static counterpart, making the experimental observation of DAQs particularly challenging. Here, we introduce symmetry-sensitive bound states in the continuum (BICs) physics to enable the all-optical detection of DAQs and enhance DAQ-mediated second-harmonic generation (SHG). Specifically, we uncover that DAQs induce optical shear that breaks the $C_{2z}$ symmetry of metagratings without geometric engineering, thereby converting symmetry-protected BICs into axion quasi-BICs (qBICs). In this context, the evolution of the quality factor and topological charge in momentum space, together with the appearance of optical resonances in far field associated with axion qBICs, offers achiral optical signatures for DAQ detection beyond the widely used Kerr and Faraday effects. Furthermore, by exploiting axion qBICs in the critical coupling regime to enhance fundamental optical field, we show that the SHG efficiency can be enhanced more than $10^5$-fold compared to bulk axion materials, achieving a conversion efficiency exceeding $10^{-6}~W^{-1}$. The SHG is governed by the magnetoelectric coupling, which differs from that in conventional SHG materials. Our findings establish a new approach for probing DAQs via achiral optical effects, while providing a versatile route for reconfigurable photonics and terahertz nonlinear optics.

articles.title: Computational screening of amorphous lithium trivalent-metal chloride solid-state electrolytes
articles.abstract: Amorphous solid-state electrolytes (SSEs) are attractive candidates for safe, high-energy-density all-solid-state batteries. The recent discovery that amorphous LiTaCl$_6$ and LiNbCl$_6$ reach room-temperature ionic conductivities above 10 mS cm$^{-1}$ with activation energies below 0.2 eV has spurred a broad search for new amorphous halide Li conductors. Here we report a computational screening of amorphous lithium trivalent-metal chlorides (Li-M(III)-Cl) using molecular dynamics driven by a universal machine-learning force field. For the sixteen Li-M(III)-Cl compositions spanning fifteen rare-earth elements and indium, all phases exhibit fast room-temperature Li$^+$ diffusion, with diffusivities of roughly $2$-$5 \times 10^{-7}$ cm$^2$ s$^{-1}$. After scaling the conductivity versus diffusivity relation to an experimental LiTaCl$_6$ reference, the estimated room-temperature conductivities range from 7.7 mS cm$^{-1}$ for amorphous Li$_3$InCl$_6$ to 14 mS cm$^{-1}$ for amorphous Li$_3$ScCl$_6$. With a low activation energy of 0.18 eV, amorphous Li$_3$ScCl$_6$ is predicted to be among the most conductive amorphous halide electrolytes. To rationalize the composition-dependent transport, we identify two descriptors: the Li$^+$ vibrational density of states (VDOS) center, which correlates inversely with diffusivity, and the average number of correlated bodies in string-like Li$^+$ motion. Compositions in which Li$^+$ has a lower VDOS center and migrates more by individual hopping rather than by concerted motion exhibit higher Li-ion diffusivities. These results suggest rich Li-ion transport characteristics in amorphous halide SSEs.

articles.title: Controllable charge-spin conversion in sliding multiferroic metal Fe3GaTe2
articles.abstract: Controlling charge--spin conversion within a single magnetic material is important for compact spintronic devices. Using first-principles calculations, symmetry analysis, and Wannier-based linear response, we study the Edelstein and spin Hall responses of sliding-ferroelectric bilayer \ce{Fe3GaTe2}. Two degenerate ground states with opposite interlayer sliding vectors and out-of-plane dipole moments are separated by a calculated switching barrier of about $16.3$~meV per unit cell. Magnetization orientation determines the allowed current-induced spin components, while ferroelectric switching induces component-selective sign reversals governed by $M_z\mathcal T$ for in-plane magnetization and by $M_z$ for out-of-plane magnetization. The Edelstein response is strongly energy dependent, with spin accumulation approaching $2~\hbar$ for $\mathbf m\parallel+y$ under a reference field of $1$~V/Å. Momentum-resolved analysis links the TR-even and TR-odd Edelstein responses to $Γ$-centered constant-energy contours and localized interband features, respectively. Spin-conductivity contributions show the opposite momentum-space character, with broad sign-competing spin Berry curvature for TR-even and narrow Fermi-surface contours for TR-odd. The transverse spin Hall conductivity reaches $\sim10^{3}\,(\hbar/e)(\mathrm{S/cm})$ and depends strongly on ferroelectric state and magnetization direction. Magnetization rotations in the $xy$ and $xz$ planes reveal symmetry-allowed higher angular harmonics in both spin accumulation and spin-current responses. These results establish sliding-ferroelectric bilayer \ce{Fe3GaTe2} as a tunable platform for reconfigurable spin accumulation and spin-current generation.

articles.title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Interfacial nonradiative recombination limits tin-lead perovskite photovoltaics. Here we show that neutral ethylenediamine chelates undercoordinated metals at tin-rich surfaces, weakens metal-iodide bonds, and removes excess tin, reconstructing the surface towards a stoichiometric tin-to-lead ratio. In contrast, protonated ethylenediammonium iodide initially passivates undercoordinated metal sites before undergoing defect-assisted deprotonation. Atomistic simulations reveal that subsurface iodide vacancies promote iodide migration and lower the energetic cost of deprotonation. Ethylenediamine-induced reconstruction produces stronger n-type surface character, facilitates electron extraction into C60, and suppresses interfacial nonradiative recombination, enabling methylammonium-free solar cells with a power conversion efficiency of 25.86%. Together, these distinct surface reaction pathways and the defect-assisted evolution of the passivating species underscore the importance of understanding perovskite surface chemistry for the rational design of molecular passivation strategies.

articles.title: Crystal-surface polarity enables nonreciprocal transport in a centrosymmetric kagome magnet
articles.abstract: Every crystal surface breaks inversion symmetry even when the bulk is centrosymmetric, creating an intrinsic boundary polarity ($\mathbf{\mathit{P}}$). Here we show that this polarity enables zero-field nonreciprocal transport in the centrosymmetric kagome magnets TbMn$_6$Sn$_{6-x}$In$_x$. In symmetric TbMn$_6$Sn$_{4.4}$In$_{1.6}$ microdevices, opposing side surfaces exhibit second-harmonic longitudinal resistances of comparable magnitude and opposite sign. Reversing the spontaneous magnetization ($\mathbf{\mathit{M}}$) reverses both signals, whereas rotating $\mathbf{\mathit{M}}$ so that the toroidal moment $\mathbf{\mathit{P}} \times \mathbf{\mathit{M}}$ has no component along the current suppresses the response. In pristine TbMn$_6$Sn$_6$, the signal switches off across the spin-reorientation transition, providing a chemically ordered control of the same symmetry relation. Spatial potential mapping indicates that the nonlinear boundary contribution is distinct from the bulk linear conduction. Spin-orbit-coupled surface states associated with topological bands may enhance the effect. Crystal-surface polarity therefore offers a broadly applicable route to zero-field rectification in centrosymmetric magnetic conductors around room temperature.

articles.title: Designing sustainability under Earth-system rate constraints
articles.abstract: Sustainability debates are monopolized by quantities: total energy use, material stocks, or recycling volumes. These metrics are informative, but they obscure a more fundamental constraint. On a materially closed but energetically open Earth, long-term viability is governed by rates: power density, areal power density, and the rate at which dispersed materials can be repurified under dif- fuse solar fluxes. We develop a physical framework that links technological metabolism, material dilution, and recycling limits through these rate con- straints. This perspective clarifies why many contemporary technologies remain viable only through stock drawdown and high-power buffering, and why green growth strategies often shift rather than resolve the underlying mismatch between industrial activity and Earth-system dynamics. We argue that long-term sustain- ability requires both quantitative reduction in aggregate industrial throughput toward rate-bounded regimes and the development of technologies qualitatively compatible with biospheric operating conditions.

articles.title: Edelstein Effect in Ferromagnetic Monolayers Fe3GaTe2 and Fe3GeTe2
articles.abstract: The Edelstein effect enables intrinsic current-induced spin polarization in noncentrosymmetric van der Waals magnets. Here, we compare the Edelstein responses of monolayer \ce{Fe3GaTe2} and \ce{Fe3GeTe2} using first-principles Wannier-based linear-response calculations. Despite sharing the same noncentrosymmetric $D_{3h}$ symmetry and selection rules, the two materials show markedly different time-reversal-even and -odd spin accumulations in magnitude, sign, and energy dependence. Strong responses occur mainly near $-0.4$~eV in \ce{Fe3GaTe2} and $+0.4$~eV in \ce{Fe3GeTe2}. At the intrinsic Fermi level, atom-resolved analysis shows that Ga-to-Ge substitution reverses the even contribution of the inequivalent Fe3 site for both in-plane magnetization directions and enhances its negative odd contribution, reorganizing the cancellation among atomic sites. Momentum-resolved calculations link the hole-side response of \ce{Fe3GaTe2} to a few large $Γ$-centered Fermi contours, whereas the electron-side response of \ce{Fe3GeTe2} involves dense Fe-$3d$ bands with strong interband contributions. The even response arises from incomplete cancellation of opposite-sign intraband Fermi-surface contributions, while the odd response originates from interband coherence between closely spaced states. Magnetization rotation reveals symmetry-constrained angular dependences with higher-order harmonics, especially in the $xz$ plane, while biaxial strain causes substantial amplitude changes and sign reversals. These results show how crystal symmetry, electronic structure, magnetization orientation, and lattice deformation govern the intrinsic Edelstein effect in \ce{Fe3$X$Te2} ($X=\mathrm{Ga},\mathrm{Ge}$).

articles.title: Field misalignment effect on the in-plane magnetoresistance in the high-temperature superconductor FeSe/SrTiO3
articles.abstract: The azimuthal angular dependence of the in-plane magnetoresistance provides a powerful probe for detecting rotational symmetry breaking in superconductors, which has significant implications for understanding the superconducting pairing symmetry and the intertwined orders. However, in two-dimensional or layered superconductors with strong anisotropy between in-plane and out-of-plane critical fields, measuring the in-plane magnetoresistance is particularly challenging as it is extremely sensitive to the field misalignment. Here we perform systematic electrical transport measurements on ultrathin FeSe films grown on SrTiO3 substrates. By remounting the same FeSe film to change the field misalignment, two qualitatively different angular dependences of the in-plane magnetoresistance are observed in the superconducting transition region, indicating the extreme sensitivity of the measurement to field misalignment. The observed anisotropic in-plane magnetoresistance can be well captured by our geometric model considering the field misalignment effect. Our work provides a practical framework for disentangling the misalignment effect and investigating the in-plane rotational symmetry breaking in two-dimensional or layered superconductors.

articles.title: From Autonomous Knowledge Generation to Generalizable Property Prediction: A Precision-First Pipeline for Electro-Optic Materials Discovery
articles.abstract: Electro-optic materials, whose refractive index changes linearly with an applied electric field (the Pockels effect), set the speed and energy of optical modulators and microwave-to-optical links for quantum computing. Designing better materials requires optimizing composition alongside temperature, strain, and bias field. However, general repositories lack electro-optic tensor data. We present a pipeline that builds such a database from literature following the rule: "no value is better than a wrong value." The pipeline has five stages: physics-aware acquisition, layout-aware extraction via LLM and deterministic table parsers, a three-tier verification gate, cross-paper consensus using median and median absolute deviation, and a noise-robust surrogate model audited by leave-one-material-out (LOMO) testing. Physics enters directly: notation is mapped, point-group symmetry-forbidden Pockels components are rejected, equivalent labels are merged, and values carry provenance tags. In a run over 49 publications, the gate processed 816 candidates into 414 accepted, 215 held for review, and 187 rejected. Against a hand-certified gold standard of 303 values from 16 papers, the run achieved a precision of 0.51 and recall of 0.48 for exact record matches. Across four database snapshots, held-out materials where the surrogate model beat a predict-the-mean baseline grew from 1 of 4 to 9 of 13 as the database expanded from 10 to 22 materials. While not a controlled comparison, this trend supports the premise that a precision-oriented, physics-checked database can power forward models beyond its training set and clarifies requirements for inverse material design.

articles.title: Interfacial Orbital Rashba Edelstein Effect Identified in CoO/Cu/Pt Trilayers
articles.abstract: We investigate the generation of orbital angular momentum currents at engineered Cu-oxide interfaces using CoO/Cu/Pt thin-film trilayers. Angular-dependent magnetoresistance measurements on samples with varying Cu interlayer thickness reveal systematic changes in both longitudinal and transverse resistance components, including a sign inversion of the signal. By systematically varying the Cu interlayer thicknesses, we disentangle the spin and orbital contributions to the magnetoresistive response. Our results show that large orbital currents originate from the interfacial orbital Rashba-Edelstein effect due to the presence of the Cu-O bonds at the CoO/Cu interface. Unlike previously studied CoO/Cu bilayers that rely on uncontrolled natural oxidation, our trilayer geometry enables reproducible and stable orbital-current generation at ambient conditions. Our results identify Cu-oxide interfaces as efficient sources of orbital angular momentum and clarify the microscopic mechanism underlying orbital current generation. Consequently, this work establishes a well-defined materials platform for all-orbitronic devices that does not require relativistic spin-orbit coupling or orbital-spin interconversion processes.

articles.title: MatOS: An Agent Operating System for Materials Research
articles.abstract: Materials research relies on scattered and growing data, knowledge, and simulation tools, and a single study often spans multi-day workflows across literature analysis, computation, and experiment. Large language model agents can now retrieve materials data, operate simulation codes, and close design-synthesis-characterization loops with autonomous laboratories. However, extending these agents with new capabilities, keeping long-running tasks on track, and letting them learn from past tasks and user feedback remain difficult. Here we present MatOS, an agent operating system for materials research with three core components: (1) a layered scientific asset graph that organizes data, knowledge, tools, skills, roles, and workflows as reusable assets; (2) a stateful adaptive workflow that runs tasks as explicit execution graphs with scientific checks, so that they can be resumed and traced; and (3) evidence-driven asset evolution, which revises these assets from execution records and user feedback. On ResearchClawBench, MatOS improves on the previously best-performing agent by 11.15% with the same base model and extends the cost-score Pareto frontier. With a common base model, it outperforms Codex CLI and Claude Code, exceeding Codex CLI by 2.13% on MatTools and 4.17% on SciAgentGym. In eight research cases, MatOS narrowed more than 30 million candidate structures to 97 solid-electrolyte candidates, identified 89 halide variants with higher computed conductivity than their parent structures, linked the force errors of 11 pretrained interatomic potentials to local atomic environments, and supported two new methods that reduce errors by 3.1% and 13.6% relative to their baselines. These results show that organizing research capabilities as reusable, evolving assets enables agents to carry out long, multistage materials studies. Code is available at https://github.com/DingyangLyu/MatOS.

articles.title: Methyl radicals dynamics on (100)--(2x1):H diamond surfaces based on refined variational transition state calculations of gas-surface reaction rate coefficients
articles.abstract: Theoretical modelling of diamond growth should ideally provide estimates of the growth rate depending on experimental conditions. To that end, a description of all possible reactions related to the competing adsorption, desorption and migration mechanisms is required. Here, we provide precise calculations of the reaction rate coefficient of methyl-related reactions on hydrogen-terminated (100) diamond surface, as $\mathrm{CH_3}$ is known to be the main growth precursor in chemical vapor deposition (CVD) growth of diamond. To achieve this goal, we successfully combined Density Functional Theory (DFT) and variational transition state theory (VTST), allowing to extend our analysis to barrierless reaction. Our rigorous treatment of the quasi-free rotation of $\mathrm{CH_3}$ adsorbates on the surface allows us to overcome numerical errors for the finite difference calculations of the vibrational spectra for evaluating the partition functions of the system. Our results suggest that the mechanism that deplete the $\mathrm{CH_3}$ concentration the most is the absorption on a surface radical site. We also evidence the anisotropy of $\mathrm{CH_3}$ migration along the dimer of the (100)-(2x1):H surface. In a more general perspective, the calculated reaction rates coefficient for methyl reactions and migration presented in this work, together with the data for hydrogen reaction and other main gas surface reactions, bridge the gap between the atomic-scale description and the large-scale modelling of diamond growth.

articles.title: No Value Is Better Than a Wrong Value: Finding and Handling Erroneous Data in Literature-Mined Datasets for AI
articles.abstract: Machine learning across materials science, chemistry, energy, and medicine increasingly relies on literature-extracted datasets due to a lack of curated databases. However, automated extraction introduces errors: text recognition misreads digits, units and notations are confused, values are misattributed, and LLMs hallucinate numbers. Drawing on our work building an electro-optic property database, we present a taxonomy of errors organized by their origin and signatures, alongside a layered framework for error detection. The framework combines schema and provenance checks, physical admissibility (bounds, symmetry, and governing equations), cross-source statistical consensus, model auditing, and suspicion-ranked review. In a production run, our verification gate halted 402 of 816 candidate values with typed reasons. Yet, an audit against curated references showed that 30 of 112 accepted values were defective; standard symmetry rules alone caught 21 of these. On measured BaTiO3 and KNbO3 tensors, constitutive identities caught 8 of 10 single-value errors and isolated the corrupted entries. In a controlled benchmark, the combined framework caught 81% of errors at 85% precision, including errors in single-report materials, bringing model accuracy on held-out data to within 3% of a model trained on clean data. Uncleaned data severely impairs discovery: 89% of the twenty largest values were errors, causing AI searches to prioritize false positives. Once bad numbers are controlled, missing measurement conditions emerge as the main limit, as distinct records become indistinguishable without full context. We outline directions for the field, including shared physics rule libraries and self-reporting databases.

articles.title: Phase field dislocation dynamics prediction of stacking fault widths in Cu-Al Alloys using generalised stacking fault energy from DFT and interatomic potentials
articles.abstract: The equilibrium width of intrinsic stacking faults is an important material parameter affecting key deformation phenomena. Here, we perform a comparative assessment of $γ$-surfaces generated using MD -- with a classical embedded-atom potential (ZW) and a machine-learned Gaussian Approximation Potential (GAP) -- and density functional theory (DFT), for Cu-Al alloys of varying Al content, and incorporate them as an energy term in PFDD simulations to obtain the equilibrium SFW. All three methods reproduce the lattice parameter and elastic moduli of Cu and Cu-Al alloys in reasonable agreement with each other and with experimental measurements from literature, but the MD-derived $γ$-surfaces, for both ZW and GAP, deviate substantially from DFT at the seven characteristic points, with the largest discrepancies at $T$ and $T_1$. When incorporated into PFDD, the DFT-derived $γ$-surfaces successfully predict an equilibrium SFW that increases with Al content and agrees well with standalone MD measurements and experimental values for pure Cu, whereas the MD-derived $γ$-surfaces do not yield an accurate SFW within PFDD, as the altered generalized stacking fault energy landscape causes the dissociating partials to become pinned soon after separation. These results show that DFT-derived $γ$-surfaces remain the more reliable route to alloy SFW prediction, and interatomic potentials must capture the shear path accurately to enable robust, efficient MD-PFDD modelling of stacking faults in alloys.

articles.title: Phase fluctuations dominated superconductivity in a thick Granular Boron-Doped Diamond film
articles.abstract: We investigate the superconducting properties of a 1.2-μm-thick granular boron-doped diamond film, where tightly packed grains form a disordered network of Josephson junctions. The film exhibits a sharp superconducting transition at a critical temperature, T_c ~ 3 K. Its transport properties are well described by the Ambegaokar-Halperin theory of phase fluctuations. Direct measurements of the penetration depth using a two-coil mutual inductance technique reveal classic phase-fluctuation-dominated behavior: below T_c, the superfluid density (n_s) varies linearly over a wide temperature range - a hallmark of thermal phase fluctuations - before crossing over to a T^2 dependence at ultra-low temperatures. Both the large low-temperature penetration depth, λ(0) ~ 8.8 μm, and the slope of the linear ns variation in the thermal regime reveal a remarkably low superfluid stiffness in the range of 0.5-0.8 K. These results establish granular boron-doped diamond films as an excellent model system for investigating the role of long-wavelength phase fluctuations in three-dimensional superconductors.

articles.title: Photoinduced charging and spatially selective photochemistry on ferroelectric surfaces
articles.abstract: Ferroelectric surfaces exhibit polarization-dependent photoreactivity and provide a route to program chemical patterns through local electrical control of polarization. Observations accumulated over several decades show reaction products in domain interiors, at domain boundaries, and in other selected regions, indicating that the mechanisms extend beyond a single polarization-induced band-bending picture. Here we analyze light-induced charging and interfacial reactions on uniformly polarized ferroelectrics and domain patterns, for dry surfaces and surfaces in contact with an electrochemically active solution. A common semiconductor transport and charge-conservation framework distinguishes five cases: an isolated dry ferroelectric, a dry ferroelectric connected to a carrier reservoir, a blocking ferroelectric-electrolyte junction, a reactive interface with an external carrier return, and two opposite domains coupled through the solid and electrolyte. Analytical solutions and numerical evaluations connect stationary potentials versus illumination to differential optical spectra and finite light-step responses. We further examine the doping effects on static potentials in all five cases and dynamic photovoltage in the isolated film and a fixed-polarization, bare-surface contacted-film variant. For reactive interfaces, the same framework determines reduction and oxidation rates, their spatial distributions, and accumulated reaction amount. The analysis covers surface charging and photochemical conversion beyond deposition, while retaining the electrical and chemical boundaries that distinguish finite charging from sustained turnover, and explains the observed range of photodeposition morphologies. Finally, this framework builds the theoretical foundation for the modulated photovoltage imaging methods that can readily be realized in SPM under illumination.

articles.title: Real-Time Correlation of Relaxation, Dephasing, and Two-level System Dynamics in Transmon Qubits
articles.abstract: Materials improvements in transmon qubits have yielded remarkable advances in qubit lifetimes (T1)and coherence times (T2). However, state-of-the-art superconducting qubits experience temporal fluctuations in their performance, which limit gate fidelities and quantum processor performance. We observe correlated increases in qubit relaxation and dephasing rates that last for minutes to hours, which we call T1 and T2 excursions. Using interleaved lifetime and coherence time measurements, noise spectroscopy, and two-level-system (TLS) spectroscopy, we find that these excursions are caused by single or few strongly-coupled TLS defects that spectrally diffuse into resonance with the qubit frequency. Our measurement protocol provides a powerful tool for understanding the noise sources that cause temporal fluctuations in superconducting qubit performance.

articles.title: Role of site-specific coordination for the structural and electronic properties of a Co-HATCN network on silver
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional metal-organic porous networks (2DMOPNs) on metal surfaces provide a versatile platform for exploring emergent electronic and magnetic phenomena in designed surface nanostructures. While the porous architecture is governed by coordination between molecular building blocks and metal centers, most 2DMOPNs utilize only one type of coordination site, leaving the impact of multiple coordination sites largely unexplored. We address this question by investigating the structural formation of a Co-coordinated 2DMOPN on Ag(111) with the linker molecule hexaazatriphenylene-hexacarbonitrile (HATCN), which has two chemically distinct nitrogen coordination sites at the peripheral nitrile groups and pyrazine-type core nitrogen atoms. Scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) reveals the transformation from a simple honeycomb HATCN structure to a Co-coordinated porous network with three structurally and electronically inequivalent molecules in a 6:3:1 ratio. The existence of two distinct coordination sites leads to selective Co coordination geometries for all three molecules, accompanied by site-specific charge transfer from Co into the former lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO), as revealed by momentum-resolved photoemission and density functional theory. Our results demonstrate that site-selective Co coordination not only controls the overall architecture of the porous network structure but also strongly influences the local electronic properties through site-specific metal-molecule interaction, providing a route to tailor the site-specific electronic structure of 2DMOPNs at the molecular level.

articles.title: Spin and Charge Photocurrents from Electric-Magnetic Dipole Interference in Centrosymmetric Crystals
articles.abstract: A common view regarding even-order nonlinear optical (NLO) effects, such as second-harmonic generation and the bulk photovoltaic effect, is that the breaking of inversion symmetry is necessary. However, this view relies on the assumption that light interacts with materials solely through its electric field. Here, we demonstrate that interference between the electric and magnetic components of the same light field can induce even-order NLO effects even in centrosymmetric materials. Using charge and spin photocurrents as prototypical examples, we present a unified microscopic theory showing how such electric-magnetic dipole interference (EMDI) drives NLO responses in inversion-symmetric crystals. Bilinear in both electric and magnetic fields, these responses scale linearly with light intensity. Combining symmetry analysis with first-principles calculations, we decompose the EMDI-induced photocurrents into shift-like and injection-like contributions and classify their dependence on crystal symmetry, time-reversal symmetry, and light polarization. Notably, we reveal that these EMDI-induced responses in centrosymmetric materials are weaker than conventional responses in non-centrosymmetric materials roughly by a factor of fine structure constant $α\approx [10^{-3}\text{--}10^{-2}] $. Nevertheless, they remain well within experimental reach. Our work thus unlocks NLO functionalities in centrosymmetric materials for e.g., materials characterization, photonics and optoelectronics. This is vital given that many functionally importantly materials, such as cubic Si and cubic $\mathrm{SrTiO_3}$, possess inversion symmetry.

articles.title: TCSP3.0: Template-Based Crystal Structure Prediction with Coefficient-Preserving Element Substitution and Structural Diversity
articles.abstract: Template-based crystal structure prediction (CSP) transfers a known crystal structure to a new composition by element substitution, so its accuracy depends on retrieving suitable templates, mapping elements and ranking the resulting candidates correctly. Auditing the original TCSP2.0 implementation on the T180 benchmark, we found that 469 of its 2,347 selected structures (20%) have the wrong composition, caused by element mappings that ignore stoichiometric coefficients and by sequential text substitution that cascades or corrupts element symbols. We propose TCSP3.0, which enforces coefficient-preserving mappings, substitutes species simultaneously on parsed structures and validates every candidate's composition and cell. It further adds periodic-number retrieval, soft oxidation-state evidence, radius-compatibility scoring, structural deduplication, and ORB-v3 machine-learning-potential relaxation and energy ranking of its candidates, as used by deep generative CSP baselines. TCSP3.0 achieves Top-1 and Top-20 match rates of 72.2% and 90.6% on T180, compared with 28.3% and 45.6% for TCSP2.0, and a Top-20 match rate of 74.0% on a new 800-target benchmark (T800). On T180 it also outperforms PNcsp+ and deep generative models CrystalFlow and MaskGXT (Top-1 72.2% versus at most 63.9%). Even without relaxation, TCSP3.0 reaches 67.8% at Top-1 and 90.6% at Top-20 in a median of 28 s per target on two CPU cores, about ten times faster than CrystalFlow. Paired ten-arm ablations on T180 and T800 show that most of the improvement comes from the correctness fixes; structural deduplication significantly improves the Top-5 match rate, embedding-based retrieval is required for coverage, and the remaining scoring features have small or null effects.

articles.title: Transition Metal-Anchored Newly Synthesized Aza-Triphenylene Monolayer for Efficient Hydrogen Evolution Reaction: Insights from DFT
articles.abstract: First-principles calculations were employed to explore the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity in two-dimensional aza-triphenylene monolayers functionalized with transition metals. Among the various metals studied, Co, Ru, and Y demonstrate outstanding catalytic efficacy, lowering the hydrogen adsorption free energy from -0.78 eV for pure aza-triphenylene to 0.05, 0.20, and 0.06 eV, respectively. Volcano plot analysis corroborates their enhanced HER activity. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations confirm thermal stability, while the electronic structure and charge transfer analysis reveal the strong catalyst-surface interaction. Metal decoration also improves the carrier mobility, particularly for Ru-functionalized aza-triphenylene. The climbing-image nudged elastic band calculations for Co-functionalized aza-triphenylene exhibit activation barriers of 1.61, 2.29, and 5.88 eV for the Volmer, Heyrovsky, and Tafel reactions, respectively, highlighting a preferred Volmer-Heyrovsky route with the Heyrovsky being the rate-determining step. These findings highlight the potential of transition-metal-functionalized aza-triphenylene as a promising platform for developing efficient HER electrocatalysts.

articles.title: Disrupting Interfacial Hydrogen-Bonding Networks via Dynamic Reconstruction Strategy for Enhanced CO2-to-C2+ Electrocatalysis
articles.abstract: The morphology and microenvironment of ion-conducting polymers (ionomers) on the catalyst electrode surface critically govern the CO2 electrocatalytic performance. Herein, we report a dual-reconstruction strategy that synergistically tailors the surface structure of the Nafion ionomer using positively charged molecules and solvent effect. By combining a low-dielectric-constant solvent (isopropanol) with arginine cations, the optimized electrode achieves an 83.6% Faradaic efficiency for multicarbon (C2+) products at a high current density of –500 mA cm–2 in 1 M KOH. Based on experimental characterization and MD simulations, we propose a structural model in which the Nafion side chains are oriented away from both the catalyst surface and the electrolyte phase. In situ spectroscopic analyses, theoretical calculation, and experimental evidence suggest that this structural reorganization disrupts the interfacial hydrogen-bonding network, suppresses the competing hydrogen evolution reaction, improves effective gaseous CO2 accessibility, and facilitates C–C coupling along an energetically favorable *OC–COH pathway. This work provides valuable insights into microenvironment engineering of ionomer–catalyst interfaces for efficient CO2 electrolysis.

articles.title: Gallium-Containing ZSM-5 Zeolites Improve Hydrocracking Selectivity to Propane
articles.abstract: Polyolefin hydrocracking over Brønsted acidic ZSM-5 produces light hydrocarbons with narrow product distributions, but further increases in propane and butane selectivity are required to improve process economics and sustainability. Here, we examined the effect of various metal and metal oxide dopants, namely Pt, Pt-Sn, SnOx, ZnOx, and GaOx, on ZSM-5-mediated polyolefin hydrocracking and identified GaOx as a selective promoter for light gas formation. Incorporation of gallium oxide (3 wt % Ga) was shown to increase propane selectivity from 40 c-wt %, achieved over ZSM-5, to near 60 c-wt %, reaching a combined propane and butane selectivity of 85 c-wt %, while maintaining solids conversion. To elucidate the role of gallium oxide, we used ex situ and operando characterization techniques to probe acidity, local coordination environment, and the spatial distribution of GaOx species. Extra-framework gallium oxide introduced via incipient wetness impregnation reduced the measured acid site density from 1275 to 911 μmol g–1, decreased the Brønsted/Lewis acid site ratio, and formed a high-coverage GaOx layer on the external surface of the zeolite. Operando experiments show that Ga is present in both Ga3+ and Ga1+ under reaction conditions. Attempts to disperse gallium oxide through reductive pretreatments led to an increase in the Lewis acid site concentration and a 10 c-wt % decrease in propane selectivity, highlighting the importance of the specific location, structural, and acidic configurations. Systematic variation of impregnation methods to control location and dispersion revealed a synergistic interaction between gallium oxide and zeolite acid sites, with propane selectivity strongly influenced by spatial proximity of GaOx to acid sites. Furthermore, vapor-phase flow reactions with a model compound demonstrated a decrease in intermediate product formation compared to the zeolite alone. The optimized catalyst was validated across diverse polyolefin substrates and resulted in similar increases to propane selectivity, yielding >80 c-wt % combined C3–C4 selectivity across the range of polyolefin substrates.

articles.title: Stabilizing Cobalt Sites with d10-Configured p-Block Cations for Iridium-Free Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
articles.abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) requires anode catalysts that sustain acidic oxygen evolution in practical stacks with minimal noble-metal content. Cobalt spinel oxides are cost-attractive but dissolve rapidly in acid as cobalt sites over-oxidize under anodic bias. Here we show that incorporation of d10-configured p-block cations (Sb, Ge, In, and Ga) into Co3O4 stabilizes cobalt sites by promoting robust heterometallic Co–O–M interactions. Density functional theory predicts dopant-driven charge redistribution that suppresses over-oxidation of octahedral Co while maintaining favorable binding of oxygen intermediates. Operando Co K-edge X-ray absorption and time-resolved dissolution measurements confirm reduced oxidation-state dynamics and cobalt loss, whereas a d-block d10 control (Zn) shows no such stabilization. In a PEMWE single cell at 80 °C, Sb/Co3O4 reaches >3500 mA cm–2 at 2.0 V and operates for >1000 h at 250 mA cm–2. This work establishes p-block d10 incorporation as a general route to iridium-free PEMWE anodes.

articles.title: Robust Full-Spectrum-Responsive Multi-junction Tandem Solar Cells via Enhanced Near-Infrared Photon Harvesting
articles.abstract: Developing robust multi-junction tandem photovoltaics remains constrained by the instability of mixed-halide perovskite subcells, given their dominating contribution to overall power output. Integrating near-infrared (NIR) PbS quantum dots (QDs) with FAPbBr3 and crystalline silicon (c-Si) broadens spectrum utilization while improving overall operational stability by reducing the perovskite power contribution. However, enlarged (100) facets and the trade-off between film thickness and quality limit efficient NIR photon harvesting. Herein, a Lewis-basic dihydrazide molecule achieves universal passivation across diverse PbS QD facets via synergistic lead chelation and hydrogen-bonding interactions. Consequently, 0.8 eV PbS QD solar cells with a 685 nm-thick active layer achieve a short-circuit current density of 41.31 mA cm–2 and a 1100-nm-filtered efficiency of 1.80%. The resulting FAPbBr3/c-Si/PbS triple-junction tandems achieve a promising efficiency of 31.04%, with the perovskite subcell contributing 30.4% of the total power output, demonstrating a well-matched operational lifetime. This work offers a strategic framework for efficient multi-junction tandem photovoltaics.

articles.title: Think Simple, Communicate Better
All-in-One Mitochondria-Targeted Iron-Based MOF “Nanomissiles” for Synergistically Potentiated Tumor Ferroptosis, Dual Phototherapy, and Chemotherapy
articles.abstract: Pronounced heterogeneity and adaptability of tumors inherently curtail monotherapeutic efficacy, necessitating rationally integrated multimodal regimens that enable precise intervention, overcome resistance, and eradicate heterogeneous cell populations within the complex tumor microenvironment (TME). All-in-one mitochondria-targeted “nanomissiles” were created by emodin (Em)-Fe3+-gated, doxorubicin (DOX)-loaded PCN-600(FeIII) (denoted as DOX@ME) nanoparticles for synergistic multimodal tumor therapy integrating ferroptosis, photodynamic therapy (PDT), mild photothermal therapy (MPTT), and chemotherapy. DOX@ME achieved on-demand release of DOX in response to the TME [such as low pH, glutathione (GSH), hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), and adenosine-5′-triphosphate (ATP)] and near-infrared laser, via the disassembly of the Em-Fe3+ gating films and/or the degradation of the PCN-600(FeIII) nanocarriers. Under both 660 and 808 nm laser irradiation, DOX@ME effectively triggered apoptosis via chemotherapy, PDT, and MPTT while robustly accelerating reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, GSH depletion, glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) downregulation, and lipid peroxide (LPO) accumulation to enhance ferroptosis. Moreover, DOX@ME could alleviate thermotolerance by depleting intracellular ATP and downregulating protective heat shock protein 70 to boost the curative efficacy of MPTT. DOX@ME exhibited excellent antitumor efficacy and good biocompatibility and biosafety in A549 tumor-bearing nude mice. Collectively, DOX@ME demonstrates robust clinical translational potential for precision cancer therapy.

articles.title: Disulfidptosis-Driven Immune-Activated Multimodal Therapy for Glioblastoma with Systemic Safety Control
articles.abstract: Effective glioblastoma therapy requires simultaneous solutions to poor blood–brain barrier (BBB) penetration, insufficient tumor-selective killing, and treatment-related systemic toxicity. We hypothesized that a BBB-penetrating nanoplatform capable of generating distinct H2S exposures in tumor and normal tissues could enhance antitumor efficacy while mitigating doxorubicin (DOX)-induced cardiotoxicity. Here, DOX-loaded metastable molybdenum disulfide nanoflowers functionalized with an I6P8 peptide (DOX@MSI) were developed. After BBB transport and tumor accumulation, the acidic, H2O2-rich, and GSH-rich microenvironment accelerates nanoplatform degradation, promoting GSH depletion and enhanced H2S/DOX release. High local H2S upregulates xCT, while H2S/DOX-mediated mitochondrial inhibition suppresses NADPH regeneration, synergistically triggering disulfidptosis. Meanwhile, H2S suppresses the JAK2/STAT3/IDO axis, alleviating DOX-induced immunosuppression and enhancing immunogenic cell death and T-cell-mediated antitumor immunity. In contrast, slower degradation under physiological conditions enables sustained low-level H2S release, reducing the level of oxidative stress and ERK-associated apoptosis in cardiomyocytes. Together with NIR-enhanced photothermal therapy, DOX@MSI suppresses orthotopic glioblastoma while reducing cardiac injury, thereby integrating tumor-selective multimodal therapy with active organ protection.

articles.title: Kinetic Access to Focal Conic Domains in Photonic Cellulose Nanocrystal Films
articles.abstract: Cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) self-assemble into cholesteric structures that enable sustainable photonic films, but controlling their pitch, domain morphology, and angular color response remains challenging. Here, we investigate how salt concentration and sonication dose jointly regulate the evaporation-induced self-assembly of CNC suspensions. Across 24 dish-cast films, polarized optical microscopy, time-lapse imaging, rheology, electron microscopy, and angle-resolved spectroscopy reveal that these processing parameters affect not only the cholesteric pitch but also tactoid nucleation, transport, coalescence, and the onset of kinetic arrest. Increasing NaCl concentration generally blue-shifts the photonic response, whereas sonication red-shifts it by fragmenting CNC bundles, with the magnitude of this effect decreasing as ionic content increases. At intermediate ionic content, low sonication doses produce extended cholesteric domains with comparatively narrow spectral responses, while the abundance of focal conic domains (FCDs) increases with sonication dose, culminating in FCD-rich films at moderate sonication. Refined parameter scans show that FCDs form within a finite processing window. Time-lapse imaging shows that FCDs appear abruptly after tactoid growth and coalescence, as macroscopic motion becomes strongly restricted during late-stage evaporation. Concentration- and residence-time-dependent rheology further demonstrates that the material response evolves throughout the assembly pathway. The FCD-rich film retains a narrow local reflection band while exhibiting the smallest angular displacement of the reflection maximum among the films examined. These findings show that salt and sonication regulate the kinetic accessibility of elastically driven focal conic structures, providing a route to tune domain morphology, spectral bandwidth, and iridescence in CNC photonic films.

articles.title: Mechanics-Guided Conformal Probes Enable Crystallographically Resolved Anisotropic Interlayer Friction Measurements in Low-Symmetry 2D Materials
articles.abstract: Interlayer sliding in two-dimensional (2D) materials is generally assumed to be weakly anisotropic, even as low-symmetry layered crystals with strongly direction-dependent properties continue to emerge. Here we adopt a mechanics-guided conformal probe design that enables quantitative measurement of crystallographically resolved interlayer friction between anisotropic 2D materials. Using Ta2NiSe5 as a model system, we demonstrate pronounced interlayer friction anisotropy approaching 2 orders of magnitude, substantially larger than its moderate in-plane friction anisotropy and the values reported for high-symmetry layered materials. Atomic-resolution lateral force mapping reveals a hierarchical friction landscape composed of atomic lattice corrugation and twist-induced moiré modulation, with the moiré wavelength evolving systematically with relative misorientation. These results show that interlayer friction in low-symmetry 2D materials is governed by a multiscale, orientation-dependent potential energy landscape and constitutes an independent mechanical degree of freedom. The conformal probe platform provides a general route to probe and engineer direction-selective interlayer mechanics in van der Waals systems.

articles.title: Nanoscale Immune Activator for Enhancing CD8+ T Cell Infiltration in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
articles.abstract: The infiltration of CD8+ T cells into the hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) microenvironment is a well-established determinant of immunotherapy efficacy and patient prognosis. However, the regulatory mechanisms governing this process and the therapeutic strategies capable of modulating it remain largely unexplored. Here, we identify HCC-IN-247 as a candidate compound that enhances IFNβ-driven CD8+ T cell infiltration both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the long noncoding RNA LINC02084 directly interacts with the transcription factor GLIS1 and facilitates its recruitment to the IFNβ promoter. HCC-IN-247 was identified through screening to target the LINC02084-GLIS1 binding interface, thereby stabilizing this RNA–protein complex. Stabilization of the complex significantly enhances IFNβ transcription, which in turn upregulates CXCL10 and CXCL11 expression and promotes CD8+ T cell infiltration. Furthermore, this study engineered a nanoparticle-based delivery system, designated Lip@RA@BSA-PD-L1/IN-247, for the codelivery of HCC-IN-247 and the anti-PD-L1 antibody atezolizumab in HCC treatment. These nanoparticles exhibited robust tumor-specific accumulation and elicited potent synergistic antitumor activity against HCC in mice. Collectively, our findings establish HCC-IN-247 as an activator of the tumor immune microenvironment and provide a preclinical basis for a combined immunotherapeutic approach to HCC.

articles.title: Selective Electronic Pre-Activation of OH Bonds in Extremely Confined Water
articles.abstract: Water under molecular-scale confinement is not simply a geometrically restricted form of bulk water, but can acquire distinct electronic, structural, and collective properties. However, how such an extremely confined state reshapes water’s intrinsic chemistry remains poorly understood. Here, using ab initio calculations and enhanced-sampling machine-learning potential molecular dynamics, we show that extreme two-dimensional confinement activates water for proton generation. Monolayer-confined water exhibits a substantially lower free-energy barrier for forming separated H3O+ and OH– ions than bulk water, and this tendency is further enhanced by lateral compression and nuclear quantum fluctuations. This enhanced reactivity does not arise from a uniform weakening of all water molecules. Instead, confinement makes OH bonds breaking selectively. The water molecule contains electronically distinct OH bonds, with weak in-plane bonds preferentially activated for proton release, while stronger dangling bonds remain relatively inactive. The surrounding hydrogen-bond network then provides disordered pathways for proton relocation, and the enhanced in-plane polarization stabilizes the charged products. Our results suggest that two-dimensional confined water can act as an active and superdielectric medium as indicated by recent experiments. Our findings reveal extreme confinement as a route to tune water-mediated chemistry, with implications for nanofluidics, geochemical pores, biological environments, and catalytic interfaces.

articles.title: Subshell-Confined Symmetry Lowering and Prolonged Excited-State Dynamics in Large Silver Nanoclusters
articles.abstract: Symmetry breaking has the potential to counteract the shortening of excited-state lifetimes with increasing nuclearity and metallicity but is difficult to accomplish in large nanoclusters, whose multishell frameworks are strongly coupled. Here, we report a four-shell silver nanocluster, Ag104, in which the principal reconstruction is concentrated in an Ag52S22 subsurface shell, and whose inner core and outer ligand-protected motifs retain closely similar topologies relative to its highly symmetric Ag100 analogue – a structurally related pair that enables the correlations accompanying localized symmetry distortion to be examined. The two clusters also differ in composition and thiolate substitution pattern, so the comparison probes coupled structural and electronic changes. Electronic-structure calculations and real-space charge analyses showed that subshell-confined symmetry breaking lifts electronic degeneracies, redistributes oscillator strength, and induces pronounced spatial charge separation, thereby reducing electron–hole overlap. Ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy further revealed an unexpected order-of-magnitude increase in carrier lifetime from ∼500 ps in Ag100 to ∼5 ns in Ag104 and distinctly activated phonon-assisted relaxation in Ag100 compared to Ag104. This establishes a strategy for engineering large atomically precise nanoclusters with long-lived excited states.

articles.title: Watching Electrochemical Interfaces in Motion with High-Speed Atomic Force Microscopy
articles.abstract: Electrochemical processes involve transient phenomena, including nucleation and growth, phase transformations, dissolution, ion transport, and interfacial restructuring, which are difficult to capture simultaneously at nanoscale and in real time under electrochemical controls. High-speed atomic force microscopy (HS-AFM), originally developed for dynamic biological imaging, combines nanometer-scale spatial resolution with frame times of approximately 0.1–5 s/frame, extending into the subsecond regime, enabling direct visualization of electrochemical interfaces under operando conditions. This perspective highlights emerging applications of HS-AFM in electrochemistry, including electrodeposition, nanoparticle dissolution, corrosion, lithiation-induced morphological evolution, protein adsorption, and nanobubble dynamics. HS-AFM reveals that mechanistic insight often resides in transient, nonequilibrium pathways rather than equilibrium structures alone. Advances will enable real-time nanoscale correlation of interfacial structure, kinetics, and electrochemical function.

articles.title: Basal stacking faults provide partial dislocations that mediate pyramidal slip in magnesium alloys
Damage incubation and evolution in tungsten under BR2 neutron irradiation: Insights into the role of rhenium
Effects of Irradiation on the Hydrothermal Corrosion and Microstructural Evolution of Ti3SiC2
Understanding early stages of low-temperature hydrogen-driven direct co-reduction of Fe-Ni mixed oxide thin films at the near atomic scale
Mineral Particle Suspensions in Carbonate Electrolyte Enable LiF‐Rich Interphases for Durable Lithium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: The solid electrolyte interphase in lithium metal batteries determines cycling stability but often suffers from the incomplete decomposition of fluorinated components. Herein, we demonstrate that suspending LiF and Li2O particles in a carbonate‐based electrolyte promotes the defluorination of fluoroethylene carbonate and lithium hexafluorophosphate. These particles preferentially adsorb fluorinated electrolyte species and induce electronic polarization, thereby modulating their redox reactivity and facilitating interfacial decomposition toward LiF. The generated LiF, together with the trace dissolution and interfacial reprecipitation of suspended LiF particles, continuously enriches the electrode surface with LiF‐rich inorganic species. This process results in the formation of a bilayer interphase on both the lithium metal anode and LiNi0.6Co0.2Mn0.2O2 cathode, featuring a flexible inner layer and a dense LiF‐rich outer layer.
