Integrating and completing the databases of known crystals therefore moves the limits of both routes: it widens what screening can reach and sets the reference against which generated crystals are judged new.

articles.title: Rationalizing charge transfer: a single-molecule case study across three distinct surfaces
articles.abstract: Organic molecules are versatile building blocks for the formation of complex low-dimensional nanostructures on surfaces. Recently, interest has grown in translating on-surface synthetic protocols from noble metal surfaces to insulating surfaces, which offer technological relevance, and to magnetic or superconducting surfaces, which offer new routes to correlated phases. It is important, therefore, to understand how these alternative surfaces may alter the properties of adsorbates through processes like charge transfer and screening. Evidence for charge transfer is often obtained experimentally via scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and spectroscopy (STS), and theoretically via density functional theory (DFT). In this work, we systematically compare the properties of isolated macrocyclic emeraldine (Me$_6$) molecules on three different surfaces: metallic Au(111), a semiconducting ferromagnetic monolayer of FeCl$_2$, and a cleaved superconducting surface of bulk 2H-NbSe$_2$. We show that STS and DFT alone are insufficient to quantify charge transfer for these cases. Instead, we complement these methods with Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) measurements and model Hamiltonian calculations to demonstrate that on Au(111) and FeCl$_2$, Me$_6$ molecules donate a single electron to the substrate, whereas on NbSe$_2$ two electrons are transferred from molecule to substrate. Our work provides insight into the interplay of charge transfer, screening, and molecule-substrate coupling, and develops experimental and theoretical methods for comparing the properties of adsorbates across different surfaces for future studies.

articles.title: Side-Chain Engineering Controls Molecular Packing and Vertical Electron Transport in Discrete n-Type NDI-T2 Oligomers
articles.abstract: High-efficiency vertical charge transport in multilayer organic optoelectronic devices highly depends on molecular structure and arrangement. Using two T2-(NDI-T2)2 conjugated oligomers with ethylhexyl (EH) and octyldodecyl (OD) side chains as a model system, their effects on electron transport are investigated using, among other techniques, atomic force microscopy (AFM), conductive atomic force microscopy (C-AFM), grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS), steady-state optical spectroscopy, and time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) calculations. The oligomers of both materials exhibit relatively disordered structures in the as-cast state, whereas annealing enhances structural order and leads to side-chain-dependent changes in molecular stacking. EH-based films show a smaller annealing-induced photoluminescence shift than OD-based films, suggesting less pronounced stacking and conformational rearrangements, consistent with TDDFT-supported exciton analysis. The current-voltage characteristics are analyzed using the space-charge-limited current (SCLC) model. After annealing, both materials exhibit improved vertical electron mobility. The EH-based films reach a maximum mobility of 1.2 x 10^-4 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1. The combined results suggest that the shorter EH side chains modify the out-of-plane packing environment and facilitate vertical electron transport. These results establish a structure-property relationship between side-chain structure, molecular order, exciton coupling and vertical mobility, providing a molecular design basis for optimising organic semiconductors through side-chain engineering.

articles.title: A Compact Single-Beam Optically Pumped Magnetometer Based on Absorption Detection
articles.abstract: We demonstrate a compact single-beam optically pumped magnetometer (OPM) employing a pure 87Rb microfabricated vapor cell with 500 Torr buffer gas. The residual magnetic field is actively minimized to below 400 pT through a combination of mu-metal magnetic shielding and internal compensation coils. We systematically characterize the OPM response as a function of laser detuning and optical intensity, and derive the magnetic-field sensitivity from the signal slope and noise amplitude spectral density. A best sensitivity of 11 fT/Hz^1/2 is achieved near the resonance transition at an optimal optical intensity, using a small cell volume of only 0.027 cm^3. Furthermore, a miniaturized OPM prototype was developed using a folded flexible printed circuit board (FPCB) to integrate the vapor cell, a compact heater, and magnetic-field coils into a cubic sensing head. Two coil configurations patterned directly on the FPCB were investigated. Under optimized operating conditions, the OPM prototype achieved a sensitivity of 66 fT/Hz^1/2. These results demonstrate that high-buffer-pressure single-beam OPMs can achieve excellent sensitivity, establishing a pathway toward compact and scalable arrays.

articles.title: A note on the monotonicity of observational ergotropic advantage
articles.abstract: Very recently, Mahanti et al. (arXiv:2609.18735) introduced the observational ergotropic advantage, which gives the maximum value of extra work that a measurement can obtain with respect to all incoherent measurements. However, the above quantity does not show monotonic behaviour under the resource theory of measurement coherence. So, the search for a resource theory in which it is a monotone was open. We derive the monotonicity of this quantity using energy-preserving channels and passive resets as free operations and energy-incoherent measurements as free objects. We show the monotonicity property of the measure as a necessary criterion of measurement transformation, but it turns out not to be a sufficient condition. It is further established that the measure is not convex. A short analysis of bounds and tightness of the measure using a degenerate Hamiltonian is also given.

articles.title: An Invitation to Algebraic Methods in Quantum Theory
articles.abstract: In this paper, we present various well-studied examples of quantum systems, and discuss how they might be analysed algebraically. We analyse the harmonic oscillator, hydrogenic atom, optical components, and particle spin using multiple algebraic methods, and highlight the central importance of algebraic relationships between operators in determining the physical character of the system. In particular, we show: the ubiquity of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{so}(2,1)\cong\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$ as the ``spectrum generating algebra''; the role of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$ in determining the action of optical components; that an elementary algebraic approach to particle spin offers novel insights into its nature versus the usual approaches; and how understanding the full (often hidden) symmetry of a problem enables it to be solved immediately without the need to solve differential equations. We hope this work will serve as a gentle introduction to algebraic methods in quantum mechanics for the interested reader --- we therefore signpost active areas of research within the community.

articles.title: Bounding single-copy information causality violations
articles.abstract: Information causality is a physical principle that constrains bipartite post-quantum nonlocal correlations from information-theoretic assumptions. A direct characterization of the correlations satisfying it, however, remains difficult because the defining entropic condition must hold for all admissible protocols in the corresponding task. Here, we formulate the single-copy information causality problem as an optimization over all protocol parameters and simplify it by proving a deterministic reduction. We then show that generic adaptive multi-copy protocols can be represented as single-copy protocols applied to an effective behavior obtained by local wirings. As a consequence, for families of correlations closed under wirings, excluding single-copy violations suffices to exclude all finite-copy adaptive-protocol violations. We formulate the resulting membership and set-inclusion problems as optimization problems and discuss possible semidefinite programming relaxations. As an application, we study expansions of the information causality functional around zero-capacity channels, generalizing a method recently employed by Gachechiladze and Miklin to derive the Tsirelson--Landau--Masanes boundary from information causality. For expansions centered on channels whose output distribution has full support, imposing the second-order constraints for all single-copy protocols characterizes exactly the set of macroscopic locality in the CHSH scenario. Expanding instead around appropriate constant-output channels with perturbations that change the channel support, we show that every single-copy IC violation can be witnessed already at first order with a channel of arbitrarily small capacity.

articles.title: Certain Quantum States Already Require Quantum Time Evolution
articles.abstract: Model-independent tests of quantum theory, such as Bell inequality violations, focus on static properties of the theory and do not rely on its dynamical aspects. Hence, this core part of quantum theory remains largely untested in a model-independent way. We show that the structure of quantum time evolution can be examined by testing the consistency between the state space and the dynamical laws. Considering a class of generalized phase-space theories, we find that certain quantum states can only be part of a theory if the time evolution is quantum: their evolution in anharmonic potentials would otherwise result in unphysical, negative marginal distributions. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the existence of the first excited state of a quantum harmonic oscillator is already sufficient to single out the Moyal bracket (quantum dynamics) to leading order in $\hbar^2$. We outline how theory-independent Wigner tomography of this state can be used to empirically exclude nonquantum dynamical theories.

articles.title: Classical Pre-Training of Large Shallow Parametrized Quantum Circuits through Pauli Propagation and deployment on Quantum Hardware
articles.abstract: Scaling parametrized quantum circuits to a larger number of qubits is a central challenge in Quantum Machine Learning: gradient estimation via the parameter-shift rule quickly becomes prohibitively expensive, while gradient-free optimizers offer limited convergence guarantees. We apply the Pauli propagation framework to a broad class of Quantum Machine Learning problems in which the loss is expressed as a function of expectation values of the circuit's observables, while keeping the relevant quantity of interest, such as the quantum state or its samples, classically intractable to compute. By propagating the observables backward through the circuit, we obtain an explicit parametric expression for the loss that can be minimized entirely on classical hardware. We also present complementary strategies to make propagation tractable at large scale, including weight-based and degree-based truncations and pruning heuristics. We demonstrate the approach on two benchmarks run on 64-qubit circuits: Variational Quantum Eigensolver on a two-dimensional Ising model, and training of a discrete-type generative model for binary images. In both cases, the classically pre-trained parameters are deployed on the IBM quantum processor ibm_berlin. For generative learning, we additionally show that the circuits considered here require substantially fewer parametrized gates than IQP-style ansätze, reducing transpilation overhead and making deployment on current quantum hardware feasible.

articles.title: Compression of turbulent flow data through an extended space-time correlation: certification against the modal energy budget
articles.abstract: The fidelity of direct numerical simulation now outpaces the storage and data-movement capacity available for the resulting fields. We present an open, distributed, GPU-accelerated low-rank compression framework for large turbulent flow databases. We assess it using two direct numerical simulations of a controlled diffusion compressor cascade under laminar and turbulent inflow conditions. Compression is formulated using a correlation operator over space and time, which is two orders of magnitude larger than that of snapshot POD. Its dominant range is extracted with a randomized range finder based on communication-avoiding hierarchical QR. The compressed databases are evaluated through a hierarchy of increasingly strict diagnostics, from instantaneous reconstruction and second-order statistics to the modal turbulent kinetic energy budget and its nonlinear interscale transfer. The budget terms are far more sensitive to compression than fieldwise or one-point errors. They remain accurate at conservative compression and degrade sharply once the retained energy is relaxed. The near-wall dissipation and the interscale transfer degrade the most and set the admissible compression level. An aggressive reduction preserves every one-point statistic to within a few per cent while corrupting both by an order of magnitude more. The dissipation error is confined to the viscous sublayer and grows with the development of the boundary layer. It is carried by the high-order modes. For both inflows, the linear budget terms scale with the discarded energy to the power $0.8$ and the triadic transfer to a power above one.

articles.title: An IL-21R STAT hypomorph circumvents functional redundancy in germinal centre responses
articles.abstract: Interleukin-21 receptor engagement initiates a Janus kinase–signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) signalling cascade that activates several STAT proteins that drive the germinal centre (GC) response. However, the relative effects of IL-21 on individual STAT proteins during the differentiation of T follicular helper (Tfh) cells and GC B cells has been difficult to distinguish. Here, we characterize a novel mutation in the interleukin-21 receptor (IL-21REINS) that creates a dominant defect in the activation of STAT1. Our findings provide evidence that IL-21-mediated activation of STAT1 has a non-redundant role in the differentiation of Tfh cells following T-dependent immunization. IL-21REINS Tfh cells were even more impaired than Tfh cells genetically deficient in IL-21R, questioning our current understanding of the role of IL-21 derived from protein knockout mice. The observation that functional compensation fails in the presence of the IL-21R hypomorph provides insight into how underlying compensation can impact our interpretation of a complex biological system.

articles.title: Correction: Targeted degradation of aberrant tau in frontotemporal dementia patient-derived neuronal cell models
Large language models poorly capture how word order shapes representations of sentence meaning in the human brain
articles.abstract: Large language models based on the transformer architecture are now capable of producing human-like language. But do they encode and process linguistic meaning in a human-like way? Here, we address this question by analysing 7T fMRI data from 30 participants reading 108 sentences each. These sentences are carefully designed to disentangle sentence structure from word meaning, thereby testing whether transformer representations of sentence meaning resemble those formed by the brain. Using representational similarity analysis, we compared representations from eight transformers and eleven other semantic models to brain activity in language regions of interest. We found that while transformer models match brain representations better than models that completely ignore word order, all transformers poorly match human brain representations of sentences that require sensitivity to structural relations such as semantic roles (who did what to whom). Further, transformers were significantly inferior to models explicitly designed to encode the structural relations between words. Our results provide insight into the nature of sentence representation in the brain, highlighting the critical role of sentence structure. They also cast doubt on the claim that transformers represent sentence meaning similarly to the human brain.

articles.title: Mapping the topographic organization of the human zona incerta using diffusion MRI
articles.abstract: The zona incerta (ZI) is a deep brain region originally described by Auguste Forel as an ‘immensely confusing area about which nothing can be said’. Despite the elusive nature of this structure, mounting evidence supports the role of the ZI and surrounding regions across a diverse range of brain functions and as a candidate target for neuromodulatory therapies. Using in vivo diffusion magnetic resonance imaging and data-driven connectivity, we identify a topographic organization between the ZI and neocortex. Specifically, our methods identify a rostral–caudal gradient predominantly connecting the frontopolar and ventral prefrontal cortices with the rostral ZI, and the primary sensorimotor cortices with the caudal ZI. Moreover, we demonstrate how clustering and gradient approaches build complementary evidence including facilitating the mapping of a central region of the ZI, connected with the dorsal prefrontal cortex. These results were shown to be replicable across multiple datasets and at the individual subject level, building evidence for the important role of the ZI in mediating frontal lobe-associated tasks, ranging from motor to cognitive to emotional control. Finally, we consider the impact of this topographic organization on the refinement of neuromodulatory targets. These results pave the way for an increasingly detailed understanding of ZI substructures, and considerations for in vivo targeting of the ZI for neuromodulation.

articles.title: Modulation of human dorsal root ganglion neuron excitability by Nav1.7 inhibition
articles.abstract: Nav1.7 voltage-gated sodium channels are strongly expressed in human primary pain-sensing neurons (nociceptors), and selective Nav1.7 inhibitors have been developed as possible therapeutic agents for treating pain, so far with disappointing clinical results. In contrast, a selective Nav1.8 channel inhibitor (suzetrigine) has had successful clinical trials. Because nociceptors express both Nav1.7 and Nav1.8 channels, it is of interest to compare effects of Nav1.7 and Nav1.8 inhibitors on the excitability of human nociceptors. To compare with previous results with suzetrigine, we characterized the effects of a selective Nav1.7 inhibitor, AM-2099, on action potential generation and repetitive firing of dissociated human dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons, studied at 37°C. Inhibition of Nav1.7 channels by 600 nM AM-2099 generally produced a substantial depolarizing shift of action potential threshold, an increase in rheobase, a decrease in action potential upstroke velocity, decrease in action potential peak, and prolongation of the refractory period. Compared to inhibition of Nav1.8 channels, inhibition of Nav1.7 channels had larger effects on threshold and maximal upstroke velocity, while action potential peak was reduced similarly by both. Nav1.8 inhibition produced much more dramatic reduction of repetitive firing than Nav1.7 inhibition. The results show that although the excitability of human DRG neurons is affected by inhibition of Nav1.7 channels, most notably by an increase in threshold and increase in refractory period, repetitive firing of the neurons in response to strong stimuli is little affected.

articles.title: Morphology and ultrastructure of pharyngeal sense organs of Drosophila larvae
articles.abstract: This study provides a comprehensive ultrastructural analysis of the pharyngeal sensory system in Drosophila melanogaster larvae, focusing on the four major pharyngeal sense organs: the ventral pharyngeal sensilla (VPS), dorsal pharyngeal sensilla (DPS), dorsal pharyngeal organ (DPO), and posterior pharyngeal sensilla (PPS). Our analysis revealed 15 sensilla across these organs, comprising four mechanosensory, nine chemosensory, and two dual-function sensilla. We identified 35 Type I neurons (6 mechanosensory and 29 chemosensory) and 6 Type II neurons with putative chemosensory functions. Additional sensory structures, including papilla sensilla and chordotonal organs in the cephalopharyngeal region, were characterized. This detailed mapping and classification of pharyngeal sensory structures completes their structural characterization and provides a foundation for future anatomical and functional studies of sensory perception in insects. This work represents a significant step toward a complete analysis of the larval sensory system, providing new opportunities for investigating how an organism processes sensory information to navigate and interact with its environment.

articles.title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis suppresses protective Th17 responses during infection
articles.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) causes more deaths annually than any other pathogen, yet an effective vaccine remains elusive. IFN-γ-producing Th1 CD4+ T cells are necessary but insufficient for protection against infection. In humans, the development of IL-17A-producing Th17 T cells correlates with protection; however, not all individuals develop a Th17 response. In mice, experimental vaccines can elicit protective Th17 cells, yet Th17s are rare in primary infection. Why Mtb fails to consistently elicit Th17s is unknown. Here, we identify factors suppressing Th17 responses during primary infection. We demonstrate that the lack of Th17 induction is independent of route and duration. Next, using Tbx21-deficient mice, we show that Mtb drives a Th1 response that is only partially protective and limits Th17 cell production in an IFN-γ-independent manner. We further reveal that the ESX-1 type VII secretion system and lipid phthiocerol dimycocerosate (PDIM) suppress Th17 responses. Infection with ESX-1 or PDIM mutants results in significantly increased Th17 T cells and IL-17A cytokine in the lungs, and infection of IL-17A-deficient animals partially restores virulence of ESX-1 and PDIM mutants. Although the ESX-1 secretion system and lipid PDIM elicit type I IFN, which can suppress Th17 differentiation, we find that suppression of Th17 is independent of type I IFN. Instead, ESX-1 and PDIM suppress production of IL-23, a cytokine that promotes Th17 differentiation, in dendritic cells found in mediastinal lymph nodes during Mtb infection. These findings define a new function of the ESX-1 secretion system and PDIM in Mtb virulence, a long-standing question in tuberculosis research.

articles.title: The new paradox of women’s health research
articles.abstract: Women have long been underrepresented in biomedical research, prompting efforts to make research more sex inclusive. These advances are essential, but they can create an unintended tension when rigorous inclusion is interpreted as requiring extensive hormonal or reproductive characterization, even when such detail is unnecessary for the question being asked. We examine this paradox, in which standards intended to strengthen research on women may inadvertently make some studies involving females harder to pursue. We argue that characterization should match the claim a study is designed to support, and that funders, institutions and journals must provide the resources needed to make such rigor feasible. Methodological progress should ultimately broaden, not narrow, the evidence base needed to improve women’s health.

articles.title: Dual Reaction Pathways on Ga2O3-ZnO/Cu for Efficient CO2-to-Methanol Conversion
articles.abstract: The design of metal–support interfaces is critical for overcoming the persistent trade-off between CO2 conversion and methanol selectivity in CO2 hydrogenation. Though an inverse catalyst with an oxide-on-metal configuration provides a platform for tuning interfacial properties, the distinct roles of multi-interfaces with different electronic properties and how they collectively govern reaction pathways remain largely unexplored. Herein, we constructed an inverse Ga2O3-ZnO/Cu catalyst to engineer dual pathways for efficient CO2-to-methanol conversion. Comprehensive characterization reveals that Ga2O3 induces charge redistribution in the catalyst for more oxygen vacancies, which enhance CO2 adsorption. The Cu-ZnO interface facilitates the formation of key intermediates along the formate pathway. Meanwhile, Ga also introduces a RWGS + CO* hydrogenation pathway to preferentially convert CO2 to methanol. In addition, Ga2O3 loading-enabled smaller Cu nanoparticles further enhanced H2 dissociation and spillover on the surface. Consequently, the optimized Ga2O3-ZnO/Cu catalyst achieves a high space time yield of methanol (728.73 gCH3OH kgcat–1 h–1) with a high methanol selectivity of 82.37% at 220 °C and 3 MPa. This work provides insights into engineering reaction pathways for methanol synthesis via the rational design of synergistic active sites.

articles.title: Dynamic Change in Oxygen Storage and Release Mechanisms of Pd/CeO2–ZrO2 Catalyst by Isotope Imaging
articles.abstract: Oxygen storage and release on oxygen storage materials such as CeO2–ZrO2 solid solution (CZ) are key phenomena for high-performance automotive three-way catalyst (TWC). In order to clarify the microscopic oxygen dynamics on TWC, oxygen storage distribution in a model catalyst comprising dense CZ substrate with Pd is visualized by combining oxygen isotope labeling and reaction quenching. The effects of temperature, oxygen storage duration, and hydrogen reduction (oxygen release) duration on 18O concentration distribution in the bulk and surface of the model catalysts are systematically investigated. In the temperature range of ≤400 °C, oxygen release and storage originated primarily from the Pd-CZ-gas triple phase boundary (TPB) and Pd surface, while the contribution from the bare CZ surface is limited. Oxygen incorporated from around the TPB diffuses in three directions: toward the CZ depth, CZ surface, and Pd surface. Furthermore, during the oxygen release process, the disappearance of the oxide layer (PdO) on the Pd and the subsequent exposure of metallic Pd accelerate oxygen release from the TPB, expanding the oxygen vacancy region deeper into the CZ directly beneath the Pd. Conversely, in the temperature range of ≥500 °C, in addition to the TPB-mediated process, the oxygen exchange on the entire CZ surface and bulk diffusion are activated, significantly expanding the storage and release regions. This study demonstrates that the OSC (oxygen storage capacity) mechanism in Pd/CZ catalyst is not static; rather, the dominant oxygen release/storage sites and transport pathways dynamically change depending on the temperature and the presence of a PdO layer.

articles.title: Gold-Catalyzed Chemoselective Dearomative Ring-Opening Modes of Indoles
articles.abstract: A gold-catalyzed dearomative cyclization of indoles with ynone-nitriles assisted by a Lewis or a Brønsted acid has been developed, which provides an efficient route to 4-azafluorenones via an unexpected indole ring-opening process. The key strategy involves the attack of an iminyl intermediate to the indoleninium species at its highly electrophilic C2 position, with both intermediates being generated spontaneously during the dearomatization process. By varying the gold catalyst and acid additives, the 1+1 and 2+1 component reactions can be achieved selectively.

articles.title: Local Electric Fields at Organic-Inorganic Hybrid Interfaces Drive Electrocatalysis
articles.abstract: The local electric field generated at organic-inorganic hybrid interfaces can profoundly influence electrocatalytic reactions, yet how molecular interfaces regulate local field distributions and reaction pathways remains poorly understood. Here, we combine grand-canonical density functional theory with in situ surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy to investigate CO2 reduction at cobalt phthalocyanine-copper (CoPc-Cu) interfaces. Density functional theory calculations show that CoPc creates a confined interfacial microenvironment and modifies the charge distribution at the Cu surface, producing non-uniform local electric fields that are experimentally probed using the vibrational Stark effect of adsorbed CO. Theory and experiment reveal that this field heterogeneity modifies CO adsorption across neighboring Cu sites and increases the adsorption-energy difference between adjacent CO intermediates, thereby lowering the barrier for C–C coupling. Consistent with this mechanism, CoPc-Cu exhibits an enhanced C2+/C1 product ratio, particularly at modest cathodic potentials where the confined hybrid interface is preserved. This work provides direct in situ evidence that organic-inorganic hybrid interfaces can regulate electrocatalytic selectivity through local electric-field engineering, offering design principles for field-enhanced CO2 electroreduction.

articles.title: Metal-Free Oxidized Carbon Nitride/ l -Proline Synergistic Catalysis: Highly Enantioselective Direct Synthesis of C2-Quaternary Indolinones via Dearomative Oxyalkylation Cascades
articles.abstract: Herein, we report a metal-free, cooperative oxidized graphitic carbon nitride/l-proline catalysis for enantioselective dearomative oxyalkylation of 2-arylindoles. The developed method leverages the band structure of g-C3N4 to efficiently generate singlet oxygen (1O2) under visible light and aerobic conditions, driving an oxidative dearomatization cascade. The resulting intermediates are intercepted via an l-proline-mediated Mannich addition, providing direct access to C2-quaternary indolin-3-ones in high yields (up to 88%) and with enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee). By integrating heterogeneous carbon nitride photocatalysis with asymmetric organocatalysis, this protocol offers a robust, recyclable alternative to traditional noble-metal catalysis for enantioselective synthesis of C2-quaternary indolin-3-ones.

articles.title: Redox Control of S -Sulfocysteine Formation in Adenosine Phosphosulfate Reductase
articles.abstract: Sulfur assimilation fuels bacterial growth by supplying the reduced sulfur required for the biosynthesis of sulfur-containing biomolecules. Adenosine 5′-phosphosulfate reductase (APSR) catalyzes the reductive step of this pathway, converting adenosine 5′-phosphosulfate (APS) to adenosine monophosphate. This reaction proceeds through nucleophilic attack by catalytic C256, located in the flexible C-terminal tail, on the sulfur atom of APS, forming a thiosulfonate enzyme intermediate. Here, we investigate this reaction in APSR from Pseudomonas aeruginosa, an opportunistic pathogen associated with severe infections, particularly in patients with cystic fibrosis. APSR contains an iron–sulfur [4Fe–4S] cluster, which participates in redox steps of the reaction. Here, we show that the redox state of the iron–sulfur cluster also controls the catalytic step. Multiscale molecular simulations investigate how oxidized and reduced cluster states affect APS binding, active site organization, and the nucleophilic attack step. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations show that the oxidized [4Fe–4S]2+ cluster stabilizes substrate interactions and the conformation of the C-terminus, facilitating a catalytically productive orientation of C256. The activation barrier of 17.7 ± 1.7 kcal mol–1 from quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) umbrella sampling MD simulations at the B3LYP-D3(BJ)/6-31G(d) level is consistent with kinetics experiments performed on an ortholog enzyme. The redox state of the iron–sulfur cluster shows its role in modulating the conformation of conserved K144, which is important for transition state stabilization in the nucleophilic attack. These findings illuminate the mechanism of this P. aeruginosa target and provide broader insight into the roles of iron–sulfur clusters in controlling enzyme reactivity.

articles.title: Disentangling Static and Dynamic Contributions to the Urbach Energy in Mixed Sn–Pb Perovskites
articles.abstract: Sn–Pb perovskites are promising low-bandgap absorbers for photovoltaics, but their efficiency is limited by the low open-circuit voltage, VOC. The VOC deficit, WOC, is related to energetic disorder, characterized by the Urbach energy, EU, comprising static and dynamic contributions. For Cs0.25FA0.75SnxPb1–xI3, these contributions were determined using time-resolved microwave conductivity (TRMC) and photoluminescence (PL) measurements between 180–350 K. For Pb-based films, both techniques provided similar EU values. However, for Sn-containing compositions (x = 0.2 and 0.5), TRMC-derived EU were twice higher than those found by PL. These differences arise from compositional heterogeneity: TRMC integrates absorption over the entire thickness while the PL-derived absorption originates from low-bandgap domains, likely from the Sn-rich top surface as revealed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). The PL-derived EU trend corresponds to the bandgap-normalized WOC, which is smallest for x = 0.5 (∼9.2 meV), attributed to the low dynamic contribution originating from the lower mass of Sn.

articles.title: Electrostatic Contributions of the Extended Environment and Local Catalytic Effects in Bipolar Membranes
articles.abstract: Catalyst layers are widely used to accelerate water dissociation in bipolar membranes (BPMs), yet their role in defining junction electrostatics and reversible reaction kinetics remains unclear. Here, we probe the electrochemical response of catalyst-containing BPM junctions using open-circuit voltage measurements, polarization analysis, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. We show that catalyst nanoparticles influence both the recovery of the membrane potential and the voltage losses associated with water dissociation and formation at the catalyst layer. These changes reflect coupled effects of catalyst surface chemistry, junction electrostatics, and proton-transfer kinetics. Notably, catalysts that recover the membrane potential do not necessarily reduce overvoltage under applied bias, highlighting that membrane-potential recovery alone is insufficient to predict BPM performance. By combining improvements in membrane-potential recovery and reaction kinetics, catalyst–ionomer interface engineering reduces water-formation losses by up to 65% and increases peak power density for energy storage by more than an order of magnitude.

articles.title: Insoluble π –d -Conjugated Small Molecules Featuring p -Type Ligands Enable All-Organic Dual-Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Organic electrodes for secondary batteries are hindered by molecular dissolution and low operating voltages. Herein, we report a coordination-driven strategy to construct insoluble π–d conjugated small molecules (BTD-M, M = Cu, Ni, or Zn) featuring high-voltage p-type triphenylamine-derived ligands (N4′,N4′-diphenyl-[1,1′-biphenyl]-3,4,4′-triamine, BTD). By precisely tuning metal–ligand coordination, we thermodynamically lock discrete molecules against electrolyte dissolution while preserving unhindered access to active sites. The optimal BTD-Cu exhibits a narrow bandgap of 0.7 eV, enabling extensive electron delocalization for electronic conductivity. This electrode delivers a near-theoretical capacity of 134 mAh g–1 at 1C and still delivers 83 mAh g–1 at 10C. Leveraging bipolar redox chemistry of p-type ligands and metal centers, the symmetric all-organic dual-ion battery achieves an average voltage of 2.4 V and a cycle life exceeding 1000 cycles. This work establishes insoluble π–d conjugated small molecules as an accessible platform for organic battery design.

articles.title: Low-Cost Iron/Manganese-Based Polyanionic Cathodes for Sustainable Na-Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Sustainable Na-ion batteries (NIBs) have attracted widespread attention in transportation vehicles and large-scale energy storage systems due to abundant sodium sources, high safety records, and favorable all-climate performance. However, their overall performance and cost are largely governed by cathode materials, which determine practical application and commercial market prospects. Iron- and/or manganese-based polyanionic cathodes not only reduce cost but also provide high working voltage and desirable cycling stability, benefiting from strong inductive effects and robust structural covalency of polyanionic groups, making them attractive for sustainable batteries. This review summarizes material design concepts, research progress, technological bottlenecks, and development directions for various types of phosphate, pyrophosphate, and sulfate cathodes. Besides, we focus on clarifying the structure–function relationships by comprehensively comparing synthesis methods, crystal structures, electrochemical behavior, and reaction mechanisms of Fe/Mn-based polyanionic cathodes for NIBs. This review provides critical guidance for the future advancement of practical NIBs.

articles.title: Three-Dimensionally Fibrillated Inorganic Composite Anion Exchange Membranes for Ampere-Scale Hydrogen Production
articles.abstract: Hydroxide-induced degradation and swelling of organic anion exchange membranes (AEMs) fundamentally limit the advancement and industrialization of alkaline hydrogen production. Here, we present a free-standing inorganic AEM comprising 90 wt % layered double hydroxides within a three-dimensionally fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene scaffold. The membrane achieves zero swelling, suppressed hydrogen crossover, and a low area-specific resistance of 0.089 Ω cm2 while remaining stable for 1344 h in 1 M and 30 wt % KOH at 80 °C, under which commercial polymeric membranes fail rapidly. The confined hydrogen-bond network within layer double hydroxide galleries promotes Grotthuss-dominated OH– transport as supported by ab initio molecular dynamics. The membrane sustains 1 A cm–2 operation for 550 h in AEM water electrolyzers and 425 h in alkaline water electrolyzers, establishing a durable inorganic AEM platform for alkaline hydrogen production and related electrochemical energy technologies.

articles.title: A Chronologically Programmed Core–Shell Microneedle Patch for Staged Therapy of Spinal Cord Injury
articles.abstract: Secondary injury following spinal cord injury (SCI) is not a unidimensional pathological process; rather, it involves a spatiotemporally organized cascade that rapidly evolves from an acute inflammatory storm and tissue breakdown to stalled repair and impaired regeneration in the subacute phase. However, most current therapeutic strategies depend on single-dose administration or isolated targets and thus fail to keep pace with the dynamic progression of SCI. Here, we developed a core–shell microneedle platform that aligns drug delivery with SCI progression by temporally decoupling the release kinetics of distinct therapeutics. The shell enabled rapid methylprednisolone (MP) release to suppress inflammatory cascades and restrict the expansion of secondary injury during the acute phase, while the core achieved sustained release of miR124-enriched M2 macrophage-derived exosomes (M2-miR124-Exo), promoting neuroprotection and microenvironmental remodeling during the subacute phase. This “suppression-then-repair” strategy synchronized treatment timing with stage-specific pathological demands, overcoming the limitations of conventional single-window delivery systems. Mechanistically, the platform promoted neuronal survival and axonal regeneration partly through modulation of key signaling pathways, including MAPK. In vivo, the platform markedly improved locomotor recovery in SCI rats, reduced lesion size, and exhibited no detectable systemic toxicity. These findings establish a programmable, pathology-guided delivery paradigm that addresses the spatiotemporal mismatch in SCI therapy and offers a promising strategy for precision intervention in complex CNS injuries.

articles.title: Displacement-Field-Induced Ionization of Defect States in High-Quality hBN
articles.abstract: Encapsulation of two-dimensional (2D) materials with hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is widely used to fabricate ultraclean van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures for optoelectronic and quantum transport studies. These devices are often operated under strong out-of-plane displacement fields that tune the electronic properties of the active 2D material, while the surrounding hBN is typically assumed to remain electronically inert. This assumption, however, neglects defect states that are present even in high-quality hBN crystals. Here, we probe their response to the applied displacement field using monolayer graphene encapsulated between hBN crystals as a sensitive charge sensor. Increasing the displacement field induces notable charge transfer between graphene and hBN, producing additional electron doping of ≈10–20 × 109 cm–2 even at the moderate displacement field (∼0.5 V nm–1), while simultaneously increasing carrier-density inhomogeneity of the graphene layer. Both effects are consistent with ionization of defect states within the hBN bandgap, with the bulk density ∼1–7 × 10–5 nm–3 varying across different hBN crystals. Our results show that displacement-field-induced defect ionization in hBN can modify the electronic response of vdW heterostructures, with direct implications for device design and interpretation of experiments.

articles.title: Flexible Nanofibrous Membrane with Valley-Cell Array of Rapid Thermal Response and Stability for Efficient Water Harvesting Performance
articles.abstract: We demonstrate a flexible nanofibrous membrane featuring a valley-cell array (NMVA). Inspired by honeycombs and spider silk, the NMVA is rationally designed using poly(vinyl alcohol), carbon black, and MOF-303 as its main components. The synergistic effect of the flexible honeycomb network, abundant hydrophilic sites of MOF-decorated nanofibers, rapid photothermal response, and multidimensional structural stability favors highly efficient adsorption and desorption dynamics during water harvesting. The valleys of the honeycomb cell arrays enhance light capture for photothermal conversion and water release, while the abundant hydrophilic sites facilitate water molecule capture and uptake. As a result, NMVA achieves a high water uptake capacity of ∼0.41 g g–1 at 25 °C and 30% RH, and can release 92% of the absorbed water within 30 min under 1 sun irradiation. For an integrated NMVA in outdoor conditions under sunlight of ∼0.76 kW m–2 on average, water harvesting capacities reach 3.85–5.0 L kg–1 day–1 at 42–68% RH through continuous all-day water uptake–release over seven cycles. This study provides insights into the design of novel materials that can be extended into the realms of water engineering for energy systems and portable devices.

articles.title: Nanoedge-Regulated Impedance Sensing for Sensitive Cardiomyocyte Mechanophysiological Investigation and Functional Drug Assessment
articles.abstract: Cardiomyocyte contraction drives the pumping action of the heart and is fundamental to cardiac mechanophysiology research. Conventional optical and force-based approaches for cardiomyocyte contraction detection are limited by phototoxicity or potential alterations in cell morphology and physiology. Electrical impedance sensing is a label-free approach for noninvasive contraction recording, but current sensor optimization still mainly relies on substantial adjustments to electrode size or pattern. Herein, we present a nanoedge-regulated impedance sensing (NERIS) approach. Electrode structures with different pit depths are designed to regulate the cell-electrode interface to precisely optimize impedance properties. Increasing pit depth shifts the peak impedance response to lower frequencies, potentially reducing detection system bandwidth demands. At the optimized frequencies, long-term recordings support quantitative analysis of cardiomyocyte mechanophysiology. Furthermore, functional cardiac drug assessment is performed by characterizing contractile responses to norepinephrine and isradipine. This NERIS approach is expected to be widely applied in cardiomyocyte mechanophysiology and cardiac drug assessment.

articles.title: Poly(acrylamido) PEG-Alternative Lipids Rescue mRNA Efficacy during Repeated Dosing and Enhance Immune Cell Delivery
articles.abstract: Following the successes of the messenger RNA (mRNA) lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vaccines against COVID-19, mRNA-LNPs are being explored for varied multidose applications including cancer immunotherapies and protein replacement therapies. LNPs rely on poly(ethylene glycol)-lipid (PEG-lipid) coatings for stability, but increasing anti-PEG antibody prevalence threatens repeat-dose efficacy and increases pseudoallergic risk, creating an urgent need for alternatives. Here, we introduce poly(acrylamido) lipids (PAM-lipids), a family of polymer lipids that effectively replace PEG-lipids in mRNA-LNP formulations. Systematic variation of monomer chemistry, molar mass, and end group reveals critical structure–activity relationships determining LNP size, polydispersity, and transfection efficiency. Varying PAM monomer chemistry allows minimization of antipolymer antibody cross-reactivity, with multiple PAM-lipids demonstrating no anti-PEG antibody binding. Several PAM-LNPs exhibit superior mRNA transfection efficacy to PEGylated clinical benchmarks in vitro and in vivo across multiple cell types, organs, routes of administration, and mRNA cargos. In particular, lead PAM-LNPs enhance mRNA delivery to dendritic cells (up to 120-fold in vitro and 3-fold in vivo) and macrophages (4-fold in vivo), with 2.5-fold superior lymph node expression, driven in part by increased cellular association and lymphoid targeting. Crucially, PAM-LNPs evade circulating anti-PEG antibodies to rescue lost mRNA efficacy after repeated dosing, resulting in 300% mRNA expression relative to that of PEG-LNPs. These findings demonstrate PAM-lipids as a chemically varied, immunologically compatible family of PEG alternatives for mRNA-LNP therapeutics.

articles.title: Riveting Rubidium in Alkali-Metal Layers: High-Performance P2-Type Layered Oxide Cathodes for Potassium-Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Layered manganese-based oxides for potassium-ion batteries (PIBs) suffer from severe structural degradation, primarily due to irreversible phase transitions, Jahn–Teller distortion, and sluggish K+ diffusion kinetics. Here, we propose an alkali-metal site riveting strategy by selectively incorporating oversized Rb+ ions into the prismatic sites of P2-type K0.55Mn0.8Ni0.1T0.1O2. The introduced Rb+ acts as a rigid pillar, expanding the interlayer spacing and reinforcing adjacent transition-metal–oxygen (TM–O) bonds. This synergistic modulation not only widens the two-dimensional diffusion channels for rapid K+ transport but also effectively suppresses the detrimental P2–P′2 phase transition and mitigates Jahn–Teller distortion of Mn3+. Consequently, the optimized K0.55Rb0.025Mn0.8Ni0.1Ti0.1O2 cathode delivers a high reversible capacity of 105.3 mAh g–1 at a current density of 20 mA g–1, outstanding rate capability (56.1 mAh g–1 at 500 mA g–1), and long-term cycling stability with 82.1% capacity retention after 500 cycles. Furthermore, a pouch cell paired with a soft carbon anode achieves 81.3% capacity retention over 300 cycles. This work demonstrates that anchoring oversized cations in alkali-metal layers provides a universal and effective strategy toward near-zero-strain layered oxide cathodes for advanced PIBs.

articles.title: Influence of coherent elastic strain on phase separation in BCC Nb–V alloys
Influence of intrinsic oxygen vacancies on interface atomic structure and functionality in fluorite and bixbyite heterostructures
A Tailored Multifunctional Lithium Organosilicate Salt Constructing Robust Interphases for High Voltage Lithium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) have attracted extensive attention due to their high energy density. However, when lithium (Li) metal is paired with high‐voltage cathode materials, its practical application is limited by issues such as continuous oxidative decomposition of electrolytes and the incompatibility between electrolytes and aggressive electrodes. Herein, we synthesize a fluorinated lithium organosilicate salt (i.e., lithium fluorobis(fluoropinacolatoborato)silicate, LiPBS) to address the aforementioned challenges. The results show that the LiPBS can form a protective and rigid‐flexible cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) on the cathode surface. Simultaneously, PBS− readily forms a coordination ion pair (CIP) with Li+, constructing an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the Li anode. Furthermore, Si─O groups in the LiPBS can effectively scavenge HF and H2O from the electrolyte. These advantageous properties enable LiCoO2 (LCO, 1.89 mAh cm−2)/Li (50 µm) coin and pouch cells to exhibit excellent cycling performance at high voltages and elevated rates‒for example, retaining 82% capacity after 250 cycles at 1 C and 4.5 V, compared to 80% retention after only 67 cycles for the LiPF6‐based counterpart. This performance is maintained even at an elevated temperature of 50°C. This work highlights the crucial role of lithium organosilicate salt in determining the electrochemical performance of LMBs.

articles.title: Axial Cl‐Coordinated Porous FeCoZn Trimetallic Single‐Atom Catalysts: Breaking the Linear Scaling Relation for Superior Oxygen Reduction Reaction and Ultrastable Zinc‐Air Batteries
articles.abstract: Single‐atom catalysts (SACs) have emerged as a research frontier in electrocatalysis. However, conventional SACs possess single metal active sites, which hardly break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of M–N4. To address this limitation, porous trimetallic single‐atom catalysts (TACs) is fabricated via ZIF‐8‐derived ion exchange and gas‐phase etching methods. The catalyst features Fe, Co, and Zn single atoms with a special M–N4 configuration where the three metal atoms share one N ligand. And axial coordination structure exists between Zn and Cl atoms. It exhibits outstanding oxygen reduction activity and stability under acidic/alkaline conditions, with a half‐wave potential of 0.81 V/0.96 V and loss of 4 mV/8 mV after 30 000 cycles. Only 6.5% performance decay is observed after 2163 h of charge‐discharge cycling in zinc‐air batteries (ZABs). Physicochemical characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the trimetallic configuration breaks the geometric and electronic structural symmetry, optimizing the adsorption of intermediates during the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Axial coordination of Cl on Zn facilitates the bridge‐type adsorption of O2 and breaks the linear scaling relationship. This work offers a novel strategy to break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of SACs and regulate reaction pathways.

articles.title: In Situ Defect Engineering of Atomically Dispersed Iridium on Mesoporous Mixed Oxide Frameworks for Robust PEM Water Electrolysis
articles.abstract: Reconciling exceptional catalytic activity with operational durability at ultralow noble‐metal loadings remains a central challenge for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis. Herein, an in situ acid‐etching‐assisted defect engineering strategy is reported for constructing an ultrahigh‐loading electrocatalyst (Ir@CM4) that predominantly features atomically dispersed iridium anchored on hierarchical mesoporous CeMn oxides. Directional Mn dissolution generates a dense oxygen vacancy network that traps Ir species, inducing a profound strong metal‐support interaction to establish a highly electron‐deficient, rigid Ir‐O‐Ce covalent framework. Consequently, Ir@CM4 delivers an exceptional mass activity of 948.15 A g−1 at 1.53 V versus RHE (31‐fold higher than commercial Ir Black). In a PEMWE full cell with an ultralow loading of 0.28 mgIr cm−2, it sustains robust operation for 6350 h at an industrial‐relevant 1 A cm−2. Multimodal in situ tracking confirms that this covalent rigidity thermodynamically locks lattice oxygen, bypassing degradation‐prone pathways to strictly enforce the highly stable adsorbate evolution mechanism. Density functional theory uncovers the quantum‐mechanical origin: strong metal‐support interaction‐induced charge transfer downshifts the Ir d‐band center to ‐3.93 eV, which circumvents traditional scaling relations by weakening antibonding orbital filling. This multiscale structural and electronic synergy effectively decouples the activity‐stability trade‐off, providing a translatable paradigm for industrial‐grade acidic water electrolysis.

articles.title: Oxyhalide‐Derived Nb‐O‐Cl Interfacial Frameworks for Mitigating Oxygen‐Related Degradation and Facilitating Li+ Transport in High‐Voltage Ni‐Rich Cathodes
articles.abstract: High‐voltage Ni‐rich cathodes coupled with sulfide solid electrolytes suffer from coupled instability of highly oxidized Ni‐O configurations and Li+ transport discontinuity under deep delithiation. Conventional oxide coatings mainly act as passive barrier layers that separate reactive contacts but remain structurally isolated from layered cathodes without simultaneously regulating interfacial chemistry and Li+ transport. Here, we report an oxyhalide‐enabled interfacial chemistry strategy based on a reconstructive Nb‐O‐Cl framework on LiNi0.83Co0.07Mn0.10O2 cathodes (denoted as C‐NCM). Derived from a mixed‐anion LiNbOCl4 (LNOC) precursor, the Nb‐O‐Cl framework undergoes mechanochemically assisted interfacial reconstruction, forming an amorphous oxyhalide interphase coupled with a Nb‐containing near‐surface region. Unlike passive oxide barriers, this chemically integrated architecture simultaneously reshapes the local Ni‐O electronic environment and mediates interface‐crossing Li+ transport. Nb‐O/Nb‐O‐Cl coordination redistributes local charge and is associated with improved retention of highly oxidized Ni‐O configurations and mitigated oxygen‐related irreversible evolution, while the Cl‐containing oxyhalide framework provides an ionically conductive transition region that facilitates Li+ migration across the cathode/electrolyte interface. Accordingly, C‐NCM exhibits reduced sulfide‐derived interphase formation and slower resistance growth, together with 88.17% capacity retention after 500 cycles at 4.5 V under high cathode loading. This work shifts cathode/sulfide‐electrolyte interface design from passive oxide‐barrier protection toward reconstructive mixed‐anion interfacial chemistry.

articles.title: Tracing and Healing Multiscale Defects for Cost‐Effective Lithium Carbonate‐Derived Layered Oxide Cathodes
articles.abstract: Lithium carbonate (LC) is markedly cheaper than lithium hydroxide (LH) but remains underused for layered oxide cathodes because LC‐derived materials perform poorly. Here, using a mid‐Ni cathode, LiNi0.65Co0.05Mn0.30O2 (N65), we trace this performance gap to LC‐induced defects that span length scales, from atomic‐scale disorder to nanoscale and microscale porosity. These defects originate from three features of the carbonate pathway that act across the solid, liquid, and gas phases, namely decoupled dehydration and lithiation, late melting of the carbonate, and a locally oxygen‐deficient atmosphere from evolving CO2. Guided by this picture, we heal the defects with a single secondary heat treatment (SH) that adds an optimized amount of LH, simultaneously replenishing lithium, restoring an oxidizing atmosphere, and densifying the structure. The resulting N65‐LC SH achieves discharge capacity, rate capability, and cycling stability comparable to those of the LH counterpart, while cutting the lithium precursor cost by 9% to 16% relative to conventional all‐LH synthesis. More broadly, the gap between LH and LC is not an intrinsic property of the carbonate but a consequence of a precursor‐specific pathway that, once traced, can be engineered around to unlock low‐cost, high‐performance Ni‐based layered oxide cathodes.

articles.title: 2D Abrupt Nano‐Junctions Blending sp–sp2 Bonds on Atomically Precise Heterostructures
articles.abstract: Two‐dimensional heterostructures combining sp–sp2$^2$ hybridization—blending graphene with graphyne‐based allotropes—offer substantial potential for enhancing the tunability of electronic and transport properties while providing significant structural flexibility, which are desirable characteristics for next‐generation nanoscale electronics. Despite such potential, their experimental realization remains elusive, as synthesized carbon heterostructures are limited to doped, graphene‐based systems exhibiting exclusively sp2$^2$ hybridization. Here, the on‐surface synthesis of covalently bonded sp–sp2$^2$ lateral heterostructures between graphene nanoribbons and graphdiyne networks on Au(111) is demonstrated. Atomic‐resolution scanning tunneling microscopy, combined with density functional theory, reveals the formation mechanism of the covalent interfacial bonds between nanoribbons and graphdiynes, also highlighting the key role of surface chemistry. Bromine atoms, deriving from the molecules dehalogenation and chemisorbed along the nanoribbon, inhibit junction formation, but bonding efficiency can be boosted up to 66% by controlled removal of these byproducts. Electronic structure and transport calculations show that the 2D heterostructure by itself is characterized by disentangled properties for the two subsystems, forming an atomically narrow junction, enabling voltage‐tunable spatial current separation in two dimensions. These results define a viable strategy for engineering graphene‐based sp–sp2$^2$ heterostructures, paving the way for the design and synthesis of all‐carbon nanoscale electronic architectures.

articles.title: A Multifunctional Ionograsper Enabling Ion‐Redistribution Proximity Sensing and Structural‐Reconfiguration‐Driven Bidirectional Actuation
articles.abstract: Autonomous soft actuators are essential for untethered intelligent robotic systems. However, achieving energy‐efficient operation and long‐term shape retention in solid‐state platforms remains a significant challenge, as most conventional systems rely on continuous power input or complex fluidic architectures. Here, we report an environmentally adaptive ionic actuator inspired by the Venus flytrap, capable of self‐sensing and bidirectional deformation without sustained external energy. By incorporating azobenzene moieties into an ionogel network, we trigger a unique nanopore‐mediated Janus actuation. A single, low‐power UV pulse (35.3 mW cm−2) induces rapid photoisomerization and localized dehydration, forming surface nanopores that facilitate asymmetric moisture uptake. This structural reconfiguration drives directional bending that is passively maintained for over 10 min, which is an exceptionally long retention time compared to conventional soft actuators. Furthermore, electrification‐induced voltage signals enable zero‐bias proximity sensing. By integrating these synergistic characteristics, we demonstrate a biomimetic ionograsper that combines ion‐redistribution‐induced sensing with energy‐efficient light‐triggered actuation for sophisticated object manipulation. Overall, this work provides a robust strategy for developing multifunctional and power‐efficient soft robots capable of intelligent environmental interaction.

articles.title: A Multifunctional Ionograsper Enabling Ion‐Redistribution Proximity Sensing and Structural‐Reconfiguration‐Driven Bidirectional Actuation (Adv. Mater. 59/2026)
articles.abstract: Bioinspired Ionic Soft Actuators In their Research Article (DOI: 10.1002/adma.74981), Hong Chul Moon, Yong Min Kim, and co‐workers propose a multifunctional ionic soft actuator that integrates ion‐redistribution‐based proximity sensing with structural‐reconfiguration‐driven bidirectional actuation. UV‐induced photoisomerization and dehydration generate a nanoporous surface that promotes asymmetric rehydration, enabling long‐lasting deformation after a single low‐power stimulus, while mobile‐ion redistribution provides self‐powered non‐contact sensing for energy‐efficient soft robotic manipulation.

articles.title: A Receptor‐Mediated Endolysosomal Recycling Chimera Enables Catalytic TNF‐α Degradation for Sustained Treatment of Mucosal Inflammation
articles.abstract: Mucosal inflammatory disorders such as dry eye disease (DED) and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), driven by TNF‐α‐mediated immune‐epithelial crosstalk, remain therapeutically challenging. Conventional inhibitors often suffer from poor mucosal permeability and transient efficacy with 1:1 binding. Although extracellular protein degradation (eTPD) technologies can eliminate pathogenic proteins, most of them operate stoichiometrically, limiting dosage efficiency and durability. Here, we report a receptor‐mediated endolysosomal recycling chimera (RECYC) platform that enables catalytic, recyclable degradation of TNF‐α with multiple turnovers, achieving sustained suppression of mucosal inflammation. RECYC integrates a pH‐responsive peptide that binds TNF‐α at physiological pH and releases it in acidic endosomes, with a CI‐M6PR‐targeting aptamer that remains pH‐stable to drive continuous recycling. The anti‐TNF‐α RECYC achieved efficient uptake and recyclable clearance of extracellular TNF‐α across conjunctival and colonic epithelial cells and macrophages, achieving superstoichiometric TNF‐α clearance with up to 7.5 catalytic turnovers. The ∼30 kDa RECYC exhibited superior tissue penetration in murine cornea and colon compared to inhibitory antibodies. In murine DED and IBD models, RECYC restored ocular surface homeostasis and reduced colon inflammation with low‐dose, infrequent administration. Human corneal limbus organoids further confirmed prolonged anti‐inflammatory activity. Together, RECYC establishes a modular, recyclable eTPD platform for sustained treatment of TNF‐α‐driven mucosal inflammation.

articles.title: A Transparent, High Refractive Index and Abbe Number Polymer for Visible Metalens by High Fidelity Nanoimprinting
articles.abstract: Simultaneously achieving high visible transparency, high refractive index (n), and a large Abbe number (υ D) in organic polymers remains a fundamental challenge. Here, a facile and efficient dual sulfur-mediated Michael addition strategy is reported to synthesize transparent high refractive index polymers (HRIPs) with large υ D. By combining main backbone de-conjugation to preserve visible transparency with rational side-chain engineering for n-tuning, the optimal polymer (H4) achieves an ultrahigh n of 1.86 at 589 nm alongside a large υ D of 34.93 and robust stability. Moreover, polymer H4 exhibits remarkable performance in nanoimprint lithography, replicating features down to 75 nm with aspect ratios up to 8.5 and a low volumetric shrinkage of only 3.23%. Notably, a nanoimprinted metalens prototype fabricated from H4 delivers a relative focusing efficiency of 49.8% at 550 nm (NA = 0.5), approaching the theoretical design value (52.94%). Therefore, the high refractive index polymer H4 bridges molecular design and manufacturable meta-optics, showing tremendous potential in scalable, flexible, next-generation photonic platforms by translating side-chain polarizability engineering into practical wavefront control.

articles.title: A Voltage‐Stabilizing MXene Additive Electrolyte Mitigates Interference From External Force on the Charge‐Discharge Process for Multifunctional Hybrid Structural Supercapacitors
articles.abstract: In structural energy storage devices (SESDs) that simultaneously store electrochemical energy and bear mechanical loading, the external force will normally affect the electrochemical performance of SESDs. One example is that, under cyclic bending stress, voltage ripples emerge in charge‐discharge curves, which cause voltage instability. In this study, we demonstrate that these voltage ripples originate from spatially heterogeneous electric field distribution within the mechanically deformed region. By using polarized electric fields formed through hydrogen bonding networks in MXene additive electrolyte, we can effectively homogenize the distribution of the electric field, thereby attenuating voltage ripples and smoothing the voltage curves. Moreover, the uniform electric field distribution promotes uniform Zn deposition and extends the device lifespan. As a result, the fabricated Zn‐ion‐based structural hybrid supercapacitor (CSHS) with MXene additive electrolyte exhibits a capacity retention of 93.6% after 10 000 three‐point bending cycles at a strain of 0.5%, much higher than that of CSHS without the addition of MXene (80.4%). The investigation into the suppression of voltage ripples of SESDs paves a viable way to design high‐performance structural power sources capable of exhibiting stable voltage under mechanical loading.

articles.title: Advances in Aerogel Materials for Energy and Environmental Sustainability
articles.abstract: Aerogels have emerged as a unique class of ultralight porous materials that combine exceptional thermal insulation with low density, high porosity, and remarkable structural versatility, enabling broad opportunities across aerospace, energy, electronics, environmental remediation, and wearable technologies. However, their widespread adoption has been constrained by the high cost, limited scalability, and energy‐intensive nature of conventional manufacturing processes, particularly supercritical CO2 drying. This review highlights recent advances in scalable and cost‐effective aerogel fabrication, including ambient‐pressure drying, templating strategies, top‐down manufacturing, chemical vapor deposition, and solution spinning, which collectively enable enhanced performance while significantly reducing production complexity and cost. We further present a unified perspective on the thermal transport physics of porous materials by systematically discussing the mechanisms of solid conduction, gas conduction, convection, and thermal radiation, and comparing aerogels with other porous architectures such as cellular foams. These fundamental insights establish rational design principles for engineering next‐generation aerogels with tailored thermal functionalities. Finally, we showcase emerging applications that extend well beyond thermal insulation, including moisture‐ and water‐driven energy harvesting, oil–water separation, high‐temperature acoustic insulation, and thermoregulating smart textiles. By bridging scalable manufacturing, fundamental thermal science, and emerging multifunctional applications, this work provides a comprehensive framework for the rational design and commercialization of next‐generation aerogels, paving the way toward their widespread adoption in advanced materials and engineering systems.

articles.title: Air‐Processed Perovskite/Silicon Tandem Solar Cells via Iodide Oxidation Suppression
articles.abstract: Efficient wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskite top cells are essential for high‐performance perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (TSCs), yet their fabrication in humid ambient air remains difficult because moisture‐ and oxygen‐induced reactions deteriorate film quality and stability. Here, 4‐[[4,6‐bis(octylthio)‐1,3,5‐triazin‐2‐yl]amino]‐2,6‐bis(1,1‐dimethylethyl)‐phenol (BTDP) is introduced into the perovskite precursor to enable WBG perovskite formation under high‐humid ambient air conditions. BTDP scavenges superoxide radical anions, inhibits I− oxidation to I2, absorbs ultraviolet light, coordinates with Pb2+ to regulate crystallization and forms a hydrophobic barrier at surfaces and grain boundaries. With this strategy, blade‐coated WBG perovskite solar cells (PSCs) fabricated at 60% relative humidity deliver a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 23.45%, which represents the highest PCE reported for air‐processed WBG PSCs with bandgap ≥1.68 eV. Mini‐modules with an aperture area of 14.81 cm2 reach 20.12% efficiency. Moreover, the method enables ambient‐air fabrication of two‐terminal perovskite/tunnel oxide passivated contact (TOPCon) TSCs with a certified efficiency of 32.59%, among the highest PCEs reported for two‐terminal perovskite/TOPCon TSCs. This study provides a scalable route to efficient, stable single‐junction and tandem perovskite photovoltaics.

articles.title: Aluminum Scandium Nitride (AlScN) for Advanced Devices: Physical Mechanisms and Emerging Applications
articles.abstract: AlScN is an emerging semiconductor material that exhibits pronounced ferroelectric switching and enhanced piezoelectric responses through the incorporation of scandium (Sc) into aluminum nitride (AlN). These properties make AlScN a promising candidate for next‐generation ferroelectric in‐memory computing architecture and radio‐frequency circuits. However, challenges arise when preparing high‐quality epitaxial films with high Sc content, including insufficient ferroelectric endurance, interface instability, and leakage current, which collectively compromise device performance and reliability. This review provides a systematic overview of the ferroelectric and piezoelectric properties of AlScN with underlying physical mechanisms, highlights the challenges in material growth and device integration, and summarizes recent advances of emerging applications in piezoelectric devices, optoelectronic devices, ferroelectric memories, and high‐electron‐mobility transistors (HEMTs). Finally, perspectives are presented on future research directions, focusing on overcoming key barriers to device implementation. With ongoing advances in material optimization and system‐level integration, AlScN presents broad prospects for energy‐efficient computing and sensing hardware, accelerating the development of artificial intelligence (AI).

articles.title: An Acid‐Neutralizing Nanoreactor Counteracts Senescence‐Driven Cartilage Degeneration in Osteoarthritis
articles.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a multifactorial degenerative joint disease characterized by irreversible cartilage deterioration associated with chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, tissue acidosis, and abnormal mechanical loading. During OA progression, inflammation‐associated metabolic reprogramming and hypoxia‐enhanced glycolysis promote lactate accumulation and local acidosis. OA‐associated acidosis may function as an exacerbating factor within this pathological microenvironment by engaging acid‐sensing pathways and contributing to chondrocyte senescence, apoptosis, and SASP‐associated inflammatory amplification, thereby exacerbating cartilage degeneration. Accordingly, therapeutic strategies that actively neutralize pathological acidity while concurrently modulating inflammatory and oxidative stress cascades may provide a more robust, disease‐modifying approach for OA intervention. Herein, we designed a nanoreactor termed OLDH‐DP@POM by integrating mildly alkaline layered double hydroxide (LDH) nanosheets with active acid‐neutralizing capability and anchoring polyoxometalates (POM) with antioxidant activity, thereby enabling coordinated regulation of pathological acidosis and oxidative stress. Meanwhile, lubrication‐enhancing zwitterionic poly(2‐methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine) (PMPC) polymer brushes were grafted, endowing the nanoreactor with superior joint lubrication and chondroprotective capability. Both in vitro and in vivo results demonstrated that OLDH‐DP@POM effectively neutralized local acidosis at osteoarthritic lesions, substantially ameliorated synovial inflammation, suppressed Piezo‐mediated mechanotransduction, delayed chondrocyte senescence, and ultimately attenuated cartilage degeneration. Overall, this work provides a promising nanotherapeutic platform for disease‐modifying treatment of OA.

articles.title: Atomically Precise Ag11 and Ag12 Nanocluster‐Assembled 2D Materials for Memristive and Neuromorphic Functionality
articles.abstract: Designing two-dimensional (2D) materials from atomically precise nanocluster building blocks is a challenging task, yet crucial for next-generation electronic devices. By tuning cluster nuclearity and ligand environment, well-defined assemblies can be designed, enabling control over optoelectronic properties at the atomic level. Herein, we report the bottom-up synthesis of two structurally distinct 2D nanocluster-assembled materials constructed from Ag12 (2D Ag12-CAM) and Ag11 (2D Ag11-CAM) nanocluster building blocks. The change in cluster nuclearity arises solely from ligand tuning; benzenethiol yields the Ag12-based framework, whereas 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)benzenethiol (BTFMBT) directs formation of the Ag11 analogue. Lateral memristive devices fabricated from these materials (D-1: 2D Ag12-CAM; D-2: 2D Ag11-CAM) exhibit coexistence of negative differential resistance (NDR) and robust resistive switching with endurance stable over 4000 switching cycles. Device D-2, based on 2D Ag11-CAM, shows a markedly enhanced on-off (I on/I off) ratio (∼ 642) compared to device D-1 (∼ 200), and more pronounced NDR. Furthermore, the 2D Ag11-CAM (D-2)-based device was evaluated for neuromorphic functionality, mimicking the adaptive behavior of biological synapses. It exhibits analogue potentiation and depression under pulse stimulation, while experimentally extracted synaptic weight updates enable an artificial neural network to achieve a test accuracy of 84.2%, approaching that of a machine learning (ML)-trained network (93.2%).

articles.title: Bifunctional Catalysis Drives Efficient and Ethanol‐Producing Aqueous Zn‐CO2 Batteries
articles.abstract: Bifunctional electrocatalysts that simultaneously drive CO2 reduction (CO2RR) and oxygen evolution (OER) in neutral electrolytes are essential for aqueous Zn‐CO2 batteries (AZCBs), but conventional designs prioritize CO2RR and are often incompatible with OER, resulting in low energy efficiency, poor reversibility, and rapid degradation of batteries. Here, we introduce a unified catalyst architecture integrating Cu and Ni single atoms with boron‐, nitrogen‐co‐doped carbon (CuNi@BNC‐T). Heteroatom co‐doping stabilizes high single‐atom loadings, enhances metal‐support interactions, and suppresses carbon corrosion, while N‐coordinated Cu+ and Ni3+ sites cooperatively boost CO2RR‐OER, enabling ethanol formation and low‐overpotential OER. This strategy achieves a 0.7 V voltage gap at 5 mA cm−2, 522 h cycling at 20 mA cm−2, and first ethanol production via AZCBs with energy efficiency of 88% (flow‐cell). By elucidating previously unresolved degradation pathways, this work also correlates catalyst dynamics with battery failure, establishing design principles for durable bifunctional catalysts in aqueous Zn‐CO2 systems.

articles.title: Bioinspired Hemostatic Dressings for Rapid and Safe Bleeding Control Via Nanofiber Bridging of Kaolin and Cotton
articles.abstract: Emergency hemostasis during prehospital care significantly reduces trauma‐related mortality. Nanoclay exhibits potent procoagulant properties, but its detachment from the substrate leads to non‐negligible adverse reactions and diminished hemostatic efficiency, hindering its clinical application. Despite improved immobilization via polymer incorporation, irreversible surface encapsulation undermines the procoagulant efficacy of nanoclays. Here, inspired by the anchoring mechanism of fish scales to skin via collagen fibers, we introduce a nanofiber‐bridged design that enables robust immobilization of nanoclay and maximized loading density, while also achieving its full exposure for optimal hemostatic performance. The microfiber‐derived nanofiber network expands the interfacial contact area and anchors nanosheet inner surfaces via synergistic covalent and non‐covalent interactions, effectively redistributing stress to resist dynamic shear forces. The resulting kaolin‐cotton hemostatic dressing demonstrates superior physical stability (no detectable kaolin leakage) and enhanced hemostatic efficacy in rat (62%), rabbit (58%), and pig (35%–43%) hemorrhage models compared with conventional hemostatic agents. Importantly, no leakage‐induced chronic inflammation was observed. Moreover, laboratory‐scale preparation and processing of 5 kg products demonstrate the feasibility of industrial‐scale production, making them further processable into various cotton‐based materials. This bioinspired dressing offers improved efficacy and safety, along with affordability, underscoring its potential for clinical translation.

articles.title: Cathode Depolarization Enables 1300‐Cycle Ah‐Level Anode‐Free Sodium Batteries
articles.abstract: Nonuniform sodium deposition limits the cyclability of anode-free sodium batteries (AFSBs), and current research mainly focuses on anode-targeted strategies. However, the influence of the cathode kinetics on sodium deposition behavior has been overlooked. Here, we firstly reveal the critical role of cathode polarization on sodium deposition uniformity via electric field coupling. Accordingly, cathode-specific charging (CSC) protocols are established for AFSBs to depolarize the cathode, where the charging current is dynamically regulated based on the state of charge (SOC)-dependent direct current inner resistance (DCIR). As expected, the CSC protocols effectively depolarize the cathodes and thus homogenize sodium deposition on the anode. Impressively, a 1.6 Ah Al/C||NFPP pouch cell reaches a record-high cyclability of 1370 cycles at 2 C, and a 3.6 Ah pouch cell reaches a high energy density of 180 Wh kg− 1 with stable cycling for 890 cycles at 0.5 C. More importantly, the cathode depolarization strategy shows application universality for diverse anode-free full cells based on Na4Fe3(PO4)2 (NFPP), Na3V2(PO4)3 (NVP), and NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2 (NFM) cathodes. This work opens an avenue for fabricating durable practical AFSBs.

articles.title: Chemical Bonding and Crystal Structure Design for Low Thermal Conductivity in Inorganic Solids
articles.abstract: Thermal conductivity is one of the fundamental manifestations of how the underlying atomic arrangement in materials facilitates heat flow. The critical role of thermal conductivity in influencing the performance of materials in the energy and quantum technologies arena makes engineering it to match functionality a crucial challenge to address. Here, we focus on intrinsically tuning thermal transport in inorganic crystalline solids through the strategic design of crystal structures. As structure is determined by the underlying chemical bonding, light is also shed on the influence of chemical bonding on thermal transport, including the concept of multicentered bonding and the role of antibonding states. In this review, we distill global research efforts into key design features rooted in chemical bonding and structural principles that enable an intrinsic property‐based descriptor‐framework for the purposeful manipulation of thermal conductivity in inorganic solids. We survey examples in which lattice thermal conductivity of crystalline solids has been pushed to extremes, specifically toward the diffusion limit or even rendered glassy. The broad and significant applicability of these principles across functional materials such as thermoelectrics, superionic conductors, ferroelectrics and halide perovskites is thus demonstrated.
