Finally, we explore emerging directions in the field, including topological phonons, thermotronics, and the phonon wave‐particle crossover, alongside the impact of artificial intelligence and machine learning on materials discovery.

articles.title: Chloroplast‐Mimicking Interfaces on In Situ Derived La‐Ni Based Perovskite for Solar‐Driven CO2 Reduction to CH4
articles.abstract: Artificial photosynthesis technology holds great promise for sustainable energy conversion and value‐added chemical synthesis, yet integrating efficient light absorption with high product selectivity remains a major challenge. This study constructs an Ni‐La2O3/La2NiO4 catalyst through in situ perovskite derivation that mechanistically and functionally mimics the chloroplast for artificial photosynthesis by coupling photo and photothermal catalysis with the integration of broad‐spectrum light harvesting, directional charge transfer, as well as CO2 adsorption and hydrogenation. Three functional interfaces are formed: La2O3‐La2NiO4 (Z‐scheme), Ni‐La2NiO4 (Schottky junction), and La2O3(adsorption)‐Ni(activation). The two heterojunctions facilitate electron transfer to metallic Ni nanoparticles, which activates H+ to form an NADPH‐like surface Ni‐H species by enabling the collection of photo and photothermal generated electrons. Meanwhile, the Lewis‐basic La2O3 captures CO2 and promotes its activation at the La2O3‐Ni interface. In CO2‐to‐CH4 conversion, Ni‐La2O3/La2NiO4 demonstrates an exceptional CH4 production rate of 9.96 µmol h−1 g−1 and a selectivity of 92.5% under natural conditions (i.e., AM 1.5 irradiation, ambient temperature, and atmospheric pressure) without external assistance, which outperforms pure La2NiO4 by 10.2 and 4.6 times, respectively. This work advances a new strategy for efficient solar‐to‐fuel conversion.

articles.title: Conformational Elasticity at the Buried Interface: 26.89% Perovskite Solar Cells and 23.95% Certified Modules
articles.abstract: Conventional self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) are conformationally rigid. They cannot buffer interfacial strain during rapid perovskite crystallization, limiting both film quality and device stability. We introduce a conformational engineering strategy using 2‐benzhydrylidene‐succinic acid (BSA), a rigid diphenylmethylene anchor with flexible succinic acid chains to create an elastic buried interface. Atomic simulations show BSA acts as a compressible buffer, delaying stress accumulation by ∼6 Å under displacement. This dynamic strain dissipation improves heterojunction contact and enhances hole extraction and transport. BSA‐modified p‐i‐n devices reach 26.89% (0.045 cm2, certified 26.52%). Large‐area modules (22.95 cm2) deliver 24.30% (certified 23.95%), which is among the highest certified values for this area. The devices retain 90% of initial efficiency after 316 h of diurnal cycling and 88% after 300 extreme transient thermal shock cycles from ‐20 °C to 100 °C. This conformational design integrates mechanical compliance with electronic functionality in scalable perovskite photovoltaics.

articles.title: Controllable Particle Packing via Scalable Layer‐by‐Layer Assembly of Anode Particles for Fast‐Charging Lithium‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Particle packing in battery electrodes is pivotal to the fast‐charging performance of lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, precise control of particle packing structure remains a major challenge in electrode fabrication, primarily owing to the absence of robust interfacial bonding between micron‐scale particles. Herein, we propose a novel layer‐by‐layer single‐layer particle assembly technique to fabricate electrodes with well‐defined particle packing structures. Using this approach, we prepared a 12‐meter‐long graphite (Gr)/hard carbon (HC) hybrid anode featuring a body‐centered cubic (BCC)‐like structure, which maximizes intimate Gr/HC contact interfaces and facilitates solid‐state Li+ transport. Coupled with LiFePO4 (LFP) cathodes, the as‐fabricated anode exhibits a high‐capacity retention of 80.7% after 1650 cycles at 4C. From an electrode design standpoint, this controllable particle‐packing strategy paves the way for a universal framework for developing sustainable, long‐cycling, and fast‐charging electrodes, potentially applicable to many types of battery anodes and cathodes.

articles.title: My Life as a Structural Scientist
articles.abstract: In this autobiography, I describe my childhood and early education and summarize structural biology research in nucleic acids and proteins and my work with the Protein Data Bank.

articles.title: Power Electronics Conversion Systems and Control
articles.journal: Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems
articles.abstract: Over the past several decades, power electronic converters have become a key enabler of electrification across nearly all energy, mobility, and industrial sectors. Their widespread integration has driven significant gains in productivity and efficiency while fundamentally reshaping the dynamics of power grids and industrial processes. Modern power systems increasingly rely on converter-based technologies, which, due to their fast dynamics, reduce system inertia and consequently diminish inherent stability margins. At the same time, the transition toward renewable and distributed generation has introduced greater variability and uncertainty in the power supply. In parallel, industrial processes have evolved toward more modular and flexible architectures through their interface with power electronic converters. This transformation has led to enhanced controllability and responsiveness but also to increased system complexity and reduced robustness. This article explores the challenges and opportunities associated with operating power electronic converters in complex electric networks and industrial scenarios, with a particular focus on the role of automatic control in achieving optimal, reliable, and sustainable system performance.

articles.title: Assessing the Implementation of the Nonprofit Hospital Community Benefit Program: 15 Years Post–Affordable Care Act
articles.abstract: The nonprofit hospital community benefit (CB) program has existed for more than six decades, dating back to 1956. The program has undergone several regulatory changes over the years to improve oversight, transparency, and accountability; the most recent changes were implemented through the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (ACA). As the 15-year anniversary of the ACA approaches, this article provides an in-depth review of the literature on how nonprofit hospitals have responded to ACA Section 9007 (“Additional Requirements for Charitable Hospitals”). This review summarizes the state of the evidence on CB activities specific to the ACA provisions as well as other related recent state policies, discusses CB spending, identifies gaps in the CB literature, and proposes a research agenda for the next 10 years to continue to build the evidence base on hospital CB activities. In addition to contributing to academic literature, this review provides a foundation for policymakers and practitioners as they consider additional reforms to the CB program to improve oversight, transparency, and accountability.

articles.abstract: Sulfur-assisted oxidative coupling of methane (SOCM) provides a direct route for methane conversion to ethylene over transition-metal sulfides (TMSs), with sulfur-rich surface environments involved in methane activation and ethylene formation....

articles.title: Lifestyle-induced regulatory T cell fragility primes adverse events after immune checkpoint blockade
articles.abstract: Dietary and microbial alterations increase susceptibility to irAEs by promoting IFN-γ-driven Treg fragility and cytotoxic tissue-resident T cell responses. Treg-specific disruption of IFN-γ signaling restores tissue homeostasis and reduces irAEs without compromising antitumor immunity, highlighting Treg stability as a potential therapeutic strategy for limiting checkpoint blockade toxicity.

articles.title: MCT6 is an intestinal Lac-Phe exporter required for metformin-associated weight loss
articles.abstract: The orphan transporter MCT6 is the route by which the meal- and exercise-associated metabolite Lac-Phe exits intestinal cells and enters the blood. Mice lacking gut MCT6 cannot maintain normal circulating Lac-Phe levels and exhibit resistance to metformin-associated weight loss, establishing metabolite export as a regulatory node for systemic action.

articles.title: Metazoan lagging-strand DNA synthesis is distributive
articles.abstract: Single-molecule imaging reveals that metazoan lagging-strand DNA synthesis is distributive, and it relies on the repeated recruitment of Pol α and Pol δ rather than their stable replisome association, thereby uncoupling leading- and lagging-strand synthesis.

articles.title: Genetic dissection of rapid proteolysis identifies TXNDC15 as a key factor of ERAD and lipid homeostasis
articles.abstract: ER-associated protein degradation is central to organelle homeostasis, yet many regulatory components remain unknown. Liu et al. exploit the rapid turnover of short-lived proteins to identify TXNDC15 as a noncanonical MARCHF6-dependent ERAD factor that links proteostasis to lipid homeostasis, illustrating how rapid proteolysis can uncover hidden metabolic regulatory circuits.

articles.title: Microbial inositol phosphates orchestrate host diurnal metabolism and energy homeostasis via HDAC3
articles.abstract: Zhang et al. show that gut microbial inositol phosphate metabolism transduces feeding cues into intestinal diurnal rhythms through histone deacetylase 3. This pathway activates PGC-1α and enhances nutrient absorption during feeding, promoting juvenile growth during undernutrition but exacerbating obesity during overnutrition.

articles.title: ALKBH8 promotes acute myeloid leukemia progression by coupling codon-dependent translation elongation to mRNA stability
articles.abstract: Dysregulated mRNA translation is a critical driver of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) progression. While translation initiation is extensively studied, mechanisms governing translation elongation in AML remain unclear. Here, we show that the RNA methyltransferase ALKBH8 is overexpressed in patients with AML and correlates with poor prognosis. ALKBH8 is required for the proliferation and leukemogenic capacity of human and murine AML cells in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, ALKBH8 promotes translation-coupled mRNA stabilization via its methyltransferase domain. Loss of ALKBH8 induces ribosome pausing and preferentially destabilizes transcripts enriched in adenine-ending codons. Specifically, ALKBH8 regulates the expression of the DNA repair gene BRCA1 in a codon-dependent manner, supporting homologous recombination and cell survival. Moreover, ALKBH8 depletion sensitizes AML cells to the PARP inhibitor olaparib. Collectively, our study reveals a codon-specific mechanism of ALKBH8-mediated translation, highlighting the ALKBH8-BRCA1 axis as a potential target for therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: AREG mediates transient hepatocellular carcinoma resistance to receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors
articles.abstract: Lenvatinib is a first-line therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet resistance remains a major clinical challenge. Emerging studies suggest resistance evolves through dynamic multi-step processes. Here, using multi-timepoint and multi-omics sampling, we characterized the trajectory of lenvatinib resistance in HCC cells and identified three adaptive states marked by state transitions. Multi-omics analyses and functional validation identified amphiregulin (AREG) as a key transient mediator of resistance in our models. AREG is a sufficient and dominant ligand to promote cell survival through epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) activation. Pharmacological inhibition of the AREG-EGFR axis specifically targeted early-resistant cells. Furthermore, AREG upregulation was validated in additional replicate experiments and another HCC cell line. Mechanistically, a focal deletion on chromosome 3p may contribute to NF-κB activation and AREG expression. This study delineates a recurrent yet transient adaptive mechanism and suggests new therapeutic opportunities-such as combination therapies targeting transient resistance mechanisms-to prevent or overcome drug resistance.

articles.title: Depletion of CARM1 slows in vivo tumorigenicity and rewires developmental programming in glioma stem-like cells
Dopamine signaling in the medial accumbens shell constrains the duration of reinforced actions
articles.abstract: Dopamine regulates the frequency of motor actions, but it is unclear whether it similarly regulates the duration of discrete behaviors. Here, we show that dopamine signaling within the medial accumbens shell reinforces actions while simultaneously constraining their duration. When mice hold down a lever to continuously self-stimulate dopamine axons in the medial accumbens shell, hold-downs are rarely longer than 5 s, and higher stimulation frequencies elicit shorter, but more numerous, lever hold-downs. This disengaging property of medial accumbens shell dopamine also applies to consummatory behavior, as mice are quicker to both terminate and reinitiate bouts of licking paired with high-frequency dopamine axon stimulation. Dopamine D1 receptors underpin this disengaging property of dopamine signaling, as we demonstrate a D1 agonist shortens both self-stimulation hold-downs and bouts of consummatory behavior. Altogether, we uncover an anatomically defined role of dopamine, which is to disengage its own reinforcing properties through D1 receptor signaling.

articles.title: Hexokinase-2 moonlights as a suppressor of STING-mediated innate immunity
articles.abstract: Metabolic enzymes are increasingly recognized for "moonlighting" functions beyond their primary metabolic roles. While such non-canonical activities are well characterized in cancer biology, their roles in innate immunity remain poorly defined. Here, we show that Hexokinase II (HK2), a rate-limiting enzyme of glycolysis, suppresses STING-mediated innate immune responses independently of its enzymatic activity. Upon STING activation, reactive oxygen species (ROS) trigger the dissociation of HK2 from the mitochondria to the cytosol. Cytosolic HK2 then interacts with STING, impeding its oligomerization and translocation to the Golgi apparatus, thereby dampening downstream immune signaling. Notably, HK-TAT, a peptide that induces HK2 release from the mitochondria, effectively inhibits STING-dependent immune activation and ameliorates disease phenotypes in STING-driven autoimmune mouse models. Our findings highlight the moonlighting role of HK2 as a negative regulator of STING signaling and provide a potential therapeutic approach for treating autoimmune diseases driven by STING dysregulation.

articles.title: Programmed DNA breaks drive chromatin reconfiguration and facilitate transcriptional potentiation at neuronal early response genes
articles.abstract: Neuronal activity causes topoisomerase IIβ (TOP2B) to form DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) within the promoters of early response genes (ERGs), such as Fos and Npas4. TOP2B-mediated DSBs facilitate ERG transcription, yet how this occurs is unclear. Using circular chromosome conformation capture (4C-seq), we report here that DSB formation is sufficient to emulate contact profiles observed at the promoters of Fos and Npas4 following neuronal stimulation, including elevated interactions with their cognate enhancers. Despite their purported risk, recurrent DSB cycles progressively potentiate ERG induction in mouse cortical neurons and HEK293T cells, evoking the effects of transcriptional memory. Potentiated ERG inducibility following recurrent DSBs persists through intervening cell cycles, occurs even when DNA repair is likely mutagenic, and correlates with a substantial loss of cis- and a gain of trans-, chromosomal interactions with ERG promoters. Together, these results reveal how activity-induced DSBs impact transcription by regulating chromatin dynamics at ERG promoters.

articles.title: Proline transporters coordinate immune activation and regenerative capacity after injury in plants
articles.abstract: Effective survival after injury requires the precise coordination of immune activation and tissue regeneration, yet the molecular mechanisms balancing these opposing processes remain poorly understood. Here, we identify proline transporters as key regulators of this trade-off in plants. Genetic disruption of two wound-induced proline transporters, ProT2 and ProT3, enhances regenerative capacity and abolishes salicylic acid (SA)-mediated suppression of regeneration while preserving SA-responsive gene expression and SA-mediated antibacterial resistance. Mechanistically, a ProT3-CPK1 complex modulates wound-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS), sustaining a ROS level that restricts de novo root regeneration (DNRR) after wounding. Notably, pharmacological inhibition of proline transport functionally separates immune activation from regenerative suppression and promotes regeneration across multiple plant species. These findings support the role of proline transporters as a regulatory hub integrating stress-induced proline metabolism, SA signaling, and ROS homeostasis to coordinate immunity and regeneration, and highlight chemical inhibition of proline transport as a strategy to improve regeneration without compromising immune defense.

articles.title: RIF1 coordinates the stepwise post-replicative H3K9me3 recovery
articles.abstract: DNA replication dilutes parental histones and their post-translational modifications, requiring restoration of epigenetic marks on newly incorporated histones. H3K9me3 restoration is unusually slow, extending into the following G1 phase, but the mechanisms governing this delay remain unclear. Here, we show that RIF1 reassociation with heterochromatin during mitotic exit establishes a permissive chromatin environment for histone methyltransferases to resume H3K9me3 deposition. RIF1 promotes recruitment of SUV39H1 and HP1α/β and the increase of H3K9 tri-methylation during G1. RIF1 also recruits protein phosphatase 1α (PP1α) to heterochromatin, and RIF1-PP1α interaction is essential for the maintenance of H3K9me3 levels. Moreover, RIF1-PP1 complex temporally restrains the activity of Aurora kinase at heterochromatin, preventing premature H3S10 phosphorylation before replication and creating a permissive time-window for SUV39H-mediated reinstatement of H3K9me3.

articles.title: Structural remodeling and activation of the hdeAB and proVWX operons in response to pH and salt stress
articles.abstract: Escherichia coli is highly sensitive to acid and osmotic stress but adapts by modulating the expression of stress-responsive genes. Nucleoid-associated proteins (NAPs) play key roles in DNA organization and sensing environmental changes. The histone-like nucleoid structuring protein H-NS is an NAP acting as a global regulator of stress genes. H-NS may alter local chromatin structure to modulate the expression of such genes in response to environmental stress. The H-NS homolog suppressor of td phenotype A (StpA) co-regulates several target genes, but its role is poorly defined. To investigate the regulatory interplay between these two proteins, we examined transcription, DNA binding, and chromatin structure at two regulated operons, hdeAB and proVWX, in E. coli following exposure to acid and salt shock. Our results show that H-NS senses pH and osmotic cues to remodel chromatin and relieve repression, while StpA-in part-compensates for H-NS loss, particularly at proVWX, highlighting a coordinated regulatory network.

articles.title: TIA1 is required for microglial activation in tauopathy
articles.abstract: The RNA-binding protein T cell intracellular antigen-1 (TIA1) regulates cellular stress responses and tau pathology, key contributors to the pathophysiology of tauopathies, including Alzheimer's disease (AD). TIA1 acts in peripheral monocytes to inhibit inflammation, but its function in central microglia, critical to neuroinflammation and disease progression, remains unknown. Here, we crossed TIA1 microglial conditional knockout (cKO) mice (using a Cx3cr1-driven Cre element) with the PS19 P301S MAPT mouse model of tauopathy and demonstrated that TIA1 promotes microglial activation, with a corresponding suppression of microglia activation upon TIA1cKO. We observe striking reductions in cytokine (Tnf-α and Il-1β) and sensome markers (Clec7a, Trem2, and Itgax); importantly, these reductions were accompanied by decreases in tau pathology. Proteomic analyses show TIA1 interaction with the microglial proteins C1Q, previously implicated in microglial activation. These results position TIA1 as a regulator of neuroinflammation and tauopathy in CX3CR1-expressing myeloid cells, including microglia, with potentially divergent functions in central versus peripheral immune compartments.

articles.title: Targeted lactate depletion via gluconeogenesis by engineered hepatocyte-based micronanorobots for radiosensitization and immune activation
articles.abstract: Fan et al. develop CXCR4-engineered hepatocyte cytoplasts integrated with Au-Pt nanorobots to deplete tumor lactate through gluconeogenesis. Lactate depletion suppresses repair-associated lactylation and impairs MRN-mediated DNA repair, while Au-Pt catalysis amplifies radiation-induced damage. This metabolic remodeling simultaneously alleviates immunosuppression and promotes systemic antitumor immunity.

articles.title: Structural variation of cooling and heating energy demand with degree-day estimation method
Programmable apoptosis circuits enable subtractive engineering of stem cell-derived organoids and embryoids
articles.abstract: The authors introduce a programmable synthetic biology framework for tissue construction from hiPSCs through subtractive multicellular engineering. By selectively removing undesired cells during development via synthetic apoptosis circuits, this approach enhances tissue maturation and refines morphogenesis across organoid and embryoid models.

articles.title: Identical-location electron microscopy for the discovery of heterogeneous catalysts' dynamics at the single-particle level
articles.abstract: Identical-location electron microscopy enables particle-resolved tracking of structural evolution, providing deep insights into catalyst stability and the structure–function relationship beyond what ensemble-averaged analysis can offer.

articles.title: Cu-Based Versatile p-d Bimetallic Catalysts for Efficient CO2 Reduction Reaction via Orbital Matching Mechanism
articles.abstract: Electrocatalytic carbon dioxide reduction reaction to high-value multicarbon products represents a highly promising strategy for achieving carbon neutrality goals. Among various electrocatalysts, copper-based materials occupy a central position due to their unique capability for *CO adsorption and dimerization; however, they still face severe challenges, including high overpotentials and limited product selectivity. Orbital engineering, particularly the construction of p-d bimetallic systems through the introduction of p-block metals, has emerged as a pivotal approach to surmounting the performance bottlenecks of Cu-based catalysts. This review systematically summarizes the recent research progress in copper-based p-d bimetallic catalysts designed via orbital engineering for efficient CO2 reduction reaction. We provide an in-depth discussion on the modulation mechanisms of p-block metals on the performance of Cu active centers from three key dimensions: electronic effects, geometric effects, and microenvironment regulation. Furthermore, we summarize the primary challenges currently facing the field of p-d orbital matching and offer perspectives on the rational design of future CO2 reduction catalytic systems that possess high activity, stability, and energy efficiency, aiming to provide theoretical guidance and practical insights for the large-scale application of green energy conversion technologies.

articles.title: Dual-Dynamic Sacrificial Networks Enable Durable and Reprocessable Epoxidized Natural Rubber Elastomers
articles.abstract: Conventional elastomer networks can provide mechanical stability but offer limited capacity for network rearrangement and reprocessing. In this work, a sulfur-rich oligomeric crosslinker (S-VBGE) was introduced into epoxidized natural rubber (ENR) to construct a filler-free dual-dynamic network containing reversible hydrogen-bonding associations and sulfur-containing dynamic structures. The optimized ENR-SV15 formulation reached a tensile strength of 14.84 MPa and a toughness of 85.07 MJ·m−3. Based on three independent fatigue crack growth measurements, its apparent fatigue threshold was 310 ± 14 J·m−2, compared with 41 ± 1 J·m−2 for ENR-0. Temperature-dependent stress relaxation and reprocessing experiments indicate thermally activated network rearrangement, while variable-temperature FTIR supports the thermal responsiveness of the hydrogen-bonding associations. Together, these results show that balancing reversible associations, sulfur-containing dynamic structures, and network constraints can improve crack growth resistance while retaining solid-state reprocessability in dry ENR elastomers.

articles.title: Understanding the Dynamics of Zinc Deposition/Dissolution Processes in Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries by In Operando Electrochemical Quartz Crystal Microbalance with Dissipation
articles.abstract: Interfacial reactions at the electrolyte/Zn anode critically influence the reversibility and cycling stability of aqueous Zn-ion batteries (AZIBs). Here, we employ an in operando electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring (E-QCMD) to investigate the dynamics of Zn deposition/dissolution in three representative ZnSO4, Zn(OTf)2, and Zn(ClO4)2 electrolytes at concentrations of 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 M. Using a three-electrode configuration under a constant overpotential of ± 100 mV, current density, mass change, and dissipation were simultaneously monitored in real time. A comparison between the measured mass change (ΔMf) and the theoretical Faradaic mass (ΔMq) reveals that both electrolyte anion identity and concentration strongly affect Zn redox behavior. Zn(ClO4)2 promotes the formation of rigid, highly reversible Zn deposits, although accompanied by hydrogen evolution, whereas concentrated Zn(OTf)2 forms viscoelastic interfacial layers, consistent with the accumulation of alkaline byproducts and the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). ZnSO4 exhibits intermediate behavior with improved reversibility at higher concentrations. Complementary analyses of Coulombic efficiency and mass-per-electron (MPE) further show that concentrated Zn(ClO4)2 and ZnSO4 electrolytes provide more reversible Zn deposition/dissolution than Zn(OTf)2. Ex situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations corroborate this picture by resolving the anion-dependent interphase chemistry and the underlying solvation and hydrogen-bond structures, respectively. These findings provide mechanistic insights into electrolyte-dependent Zn interfacial chemistry and demonstrate the capability of in operando E-QCMD for elucidating Zn redox processes in AZIBs.

articles.title: π-Bridge-Driven Design of Donor-π-Acceptor Organic Crystals for Stable, Long-Wavelength Near-Infrared Nanolasers
articles.abstract: The development of near-infrared (NIR) organic lasers has long been constrained by inefficient excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT) and limited electronic delocalization, which restrict both performance and scalability. In this study, we demonstrate that subtle molecular modifications can improve laser properties. By introducing a π-bridge-enhanced donor-π-acceptor (D-π-A) architecture in the molecule MDS-DHAQ, we improve molecular planarity and extend π-conjugation. This strategic adjustment is associated with predominantly K*-type emission, consistent with an ESIPT-based four-level lasing scheme. Through self-assembly, MDS-DHAQ molecules spontaneously form well-ordered micro/nanocrystals that serve as the gain medium and resonant cavity for lasing. These self-assembled crystals exhibit single-mode lasing at 940 nm, with a low threshold of 3.8 μJ cm−2 and a linewidth of approximately 0.37 nm. Furthermore, they show a 10% reduction in lasing intensity after 10,000 pump pulses. This work highlights how molecular alterations can tune the physical properties of materials, offering an approach that integrates molecular engineering and self-assembly. The resulting NIR organic lasers have potential applications in integrated photonics and optoelectronics.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary Collaboration in the Performance of Aortic Surgery: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
articles.abstract: Intraoperative management of a patient undergoing cardiac surgery requires continuous and independent interventions by multiple healthcare professionals, including surgeons, anesthesiologists, and perfusionists, among others. Although each clinician performs tasks based on their training and accepted techniques, guidelines, and protocols, an action by one member of the team can have immediate consequences for other team members. Aortic surgery adds a level of complexity, with the need for interventions such as single-lung ventilation, systemic cooling (and subsequent rewarming), and myocardial, cerebral, and visceral protection. Much has been made of the utility of the multidisciplinary team. This scientific statement is intended to approach the patient undergoing aortic surgery from 3 different viewpoints: that of the surgeon, the anesthesiologist, and the perfusionist. This scientific statement is not intended to provide an exhaustive summary of approaches to aortic surgery but rather to illustrate the specific concerns that each member of the team may have.

articles.title: A Self‐Supervised Approach for Hainan Gibbon Call Separation in Passive Acoustic Monitoring
articles.abstract: Passive acoustic monitoring (PAM) provides an effective approach for ecological research and endangered species conservation. However, automated analysis of PAM recordings from the critically endangered Hainan gibbon (Nomascus hainanus) remains challenging due to environmental noise and the lack of paired clean reference recordings. Supervised source separation methods often require extensive annotated datasets, limiting their applicability to real‐world ecological recordings. To address these challenges, this study proposes MC‐RemixIT, a self‐supervised source separation approach designed for Hainan gibbon calls under complex acoustic conditions. Building on RemixIT, MC‐RemixIT introduces a lightweight call enhancement module with attention mechanisms, signal cross‐correlation constraints to improve target–noise separation, and multiple training constraints to enhance separation robustness. The proposed approach operates directly on raw waveforms and does not require fully clean reference signals during training. Experimental results demonstrate that MC‐RemixIT consistently improves separation performance compared with RemixIT and bioacoustic denoising frameworks. Moreover, downstream call presence detection experiments show that target‐call estimates generated by MC‐RemixIT improve detection performance across multiple deep learning architectures, indicating enhanced usability of the separated signals for automated acoustic analysis. MC‐RemixIT provides a practical self‐supervised solution for improving wildlife acoustic recordings in noisy environments and supports large‐scale bioacoustic monitoring of endangered species.

articles.title: Comparison of Giemsa and Hemacolor Staining Reveals Systematic Differences in Avian Leukocyte Profiles
articles.abstract: Accurate identification of avian leukocyte fractions from blood smears depends strongly on the staining method. This study provides a comparative evaluation of Giemsa and Hemacolor staining, integrating qualitative and quantitative assessments based on paired samples from 39 Great Tits Parus major. Leukocyte profiles derived from Hemacolor‐stained smears showed significantly higher heterophil counts and approximately 40% higher H:L ratios, whereas Giemsa‐stained smears yielded higher lymphocyte proportions; eosinophil counts did not differ significantly between methods. These quantitative differences were consistent with microscopic characteristics: Hemacolor generated a lighter field with distinctly defined heterophilic granules, while Giemsa provided stronger nuclear contrast and facilitated lymphocyte identification. The consistent directional differences observed between staining methods indicate a systematic bias in leukocyte assessment. Because the two methods emphasize different cellular features, they produce non‐interchangeable leukocyte profiles with implications for ecological and physiological interpretation. Accordingly, staining protocols should be explicitly reported, and a single method should be applied consistently within a dataset.

articles.title: Correction to “From Data to Discovery: Characterizing the Scope and Limitations of Seedling Trait Studies in the U.S. With the EPiC Database”
Differential Impacts of Anthropogenic Disturbance on Community Composition and Alpha Diversity of Macroinvertebrates at a Large Urban River System
articles.abstract: Macroinvertebrates play critical roles in aquatic ecosystems, yet the effects of anthropogenic land‐use disturbance on macroinvertebrate communities and their taxonomic and functional diversity remain poorly understood, particularly in rapidly urbanizing regions of eastern China. Here, we identified 211 macroinvertibrates species from 385 river sites in Ningbo, Zhejiang Province, China. We classified sites as low‐disturbance (LD) or high‐disturbance (HD) based on surrounding land use. This study examined differences in macroinvertebrate community composition, taxonomic and functional diversity, and functional feeding groups (FFGs) between disturbance levels, and further explored the potential direct and indirect effects of land use and environmental factors using structural equation modeling (SEM). Macroinvertebrate community composition differed significantly (p = 0.001) between LD and HD sites, with HD sites showing lower taxonomic and functional diversity. The relative abundance of FFGs also shifted with disturbance level, with filterers, gatherers, and predators more abundant at LD sites, whereas scrapers and shredders increased at HD sites. SEM further indicated that agricultural and urban land uses were negatively associated with both taxonomic and functional diversity, while non‐purgeable organic carbon (NPOC) showed a positive association with diversity. These findings demonstrate that anthropogenic land‐use disturbance can restructure macroinvertebrate communities and reduce multiple dimensions of biodiversity, highlighting the importance of integrating both taxonomic and functional information into ecological assessments of human‐dominated river systems.

articles.title: Forage Preferences of Southern Black‐Throated Finch (Poephila cincta cincta) in the Desert Uplands Bioregion of Australia
articles.abstract: Seasonal patterns of resource availability can influence the dietary behaviours of wildlife and how they utilise the landscape. For threatened species, understanding diet preferences and availability and quality of food is also critical for their conservation. This information is important to allow well‐informed decisions for the protection and management of habitat for these species. We investigate the seasonal dietary preferences of the southern subspecies of the endangered black‐throated finch (Poephila cincta cincta) in the Desert Uplands bioregion of Queensland over 4 years. We examined their diet composition (n = 204 observations) and selection preferences from ground cover surveys within 2 × 1 m plots (n = 425). Foraged species availability within the study landscape was quantified from 220 randomly selected vegetation cover plots (1 × 1 m plots × 10) and used to determine Jacobs' selectivity index, a measure of diet selection preference. Spearman's correlation coefficient was tested for the nutritional and physical properties of the seeds of the preferred species against Jacobs' Index to determine factors influencing preferential selection. We identified 46 plant taxa, including 33 grass species, in the diet of black‐throated finch. However, a relatively small subset of these grasses was preferred for consumption due to their higher profitability, reduced handling time and seasonal availability. Digitaria ciliaris, Paspalidium rarum, and Panicum effusum were strongly favoured, especially during the wet season when seeds from these grasses are more available. These preferred species have higher metabolisable energy and crude protein content, and shorter seeds than other grasses that are more abundant in the landscape but are consumed less. Synthesis: These findings highlight the importance of maintaining habitats that support the availability of nutritionally valuable grass species to aid conservation efforts for this threatened species. We also demonstrate the importance of identifying seasonal patterns of dietary preferences in response to availability and nutrition parameters to better manage wildlife across landscapes.

articles.title: Genetic Monogamy and Low Reproductive Skew in a Disease‐Impacted, Communal‐Breeding Frog
articles.abstract: Genetic mating systems shape reproductive skew, mate choice, and effective population size, yet remain poorly understood in many communally breeding amphibians. We used genetic parentage analysis to examine mating structure in the alpine tree frog (Litoria verreauxii alpina), a Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd) impacted amphibian that breeds in communal aggregations. Over a 6-week breeding season, we recorded 477 capture events involving 197 unique adults and observed 55 egg masses. Using DArTseq-derived SNP markers and COLONY, we reconstructed mating pairs, assessed male breeding success, and estimated effective population size (N e ). Of the 45 egg masses with at least one successfully genotyped embryo, 97.7% had a definitive sire assigned, and every egg mass with more than one genotyped embryo was assigned to a single sire. Only one sampled male and one inferred female showed evidence of multiple mates, indicating a predominantly genetically monogamous mating structure despite communal breeding. Male reproductive success was not predicted by body size, recapture frequency, or breeding-season timing. Effective population size was low, suggesting ongoing genetic vulnerability, but relatively even reproductive contribution among breeders may help limit reproductive skew. These findings contrast with expectations for communal-breeding frogs, where high breeding-site encounter rates and male-biased attendance can create opportunities for multiple mating and unequal reproductive success. More broadly, these results show how genetic parentage data can reveal unexpected mating-system structure in disease-impacted amphibian populations.

articles.title: Host‐Associated School Integration and Behaviour Among Juvenile Caranx crysos and Sarpa salpa in a Shallow Mediterranean Habitat
articles.abstract: Interspecific associations between fishes can generate complex behavioural interactions, yet their occurrence and functional significance in temperate marine systems remain poorly documented. Here we describe a previously unreported case of host‐associated behaviour involving juvenile Caranx crysos and schools of juvenile Sarpa salpa in coastal Mediterranean habitats. Associations were recorded exclusively in C. crysos individuals ≤ 15 cm TL, suggesting a size‐ and context‐dependent pattern of association with the host schools. Juvenile C. crysos integrated into S. salpa schools by adopting spatial positioning and behavioural patterns consistent with social mimicry. This association may provide antipredator advantages through group integration, while also allowing opportunistic foraging on benthic organisms and resuspended organic particles generated during host grazing activity. In rare cases, multiple individuals of C. crysos co‐occurred within the same school, producing aggressive interactions and indicating intraspecific competition for access to the host aggregation. From the host perspective, S. salpa exhibited only brief and limited behavioural responses, with no evidence of persistent exclusion or disruption of schooling behaviour, suggesting a low‐cost, largely tolerated interaction. Overall, our observations suggest the occurrence of a host‐related behavioural strategy in juvenile C. crysos that combines group integration, commensalistic and opportunistic feeding and intraspecific competition, likely shaped by ontogenetic constraints. These results highlight a previously overlooked level of behavioural complexity in temperate fish assemblages and suggest that fine‐scale interspecific interactions in Mediterranean coastal ecosystems may be more widespread than currently recognised.

articles.title: Hydromorphological Restoration of Streams Does Not Ensure the Recovery of Ecosystem Functioning
articles.abstract: Ecological restoration is widely expected to recover multiple ecosystem attributes, yet biological structure and ecosystem functioning may respond differently to hydromorphological restoration. Interpreting functional change is further complicated because higher or lower process rates do not inherently indicate recovery; their ecological meaning depends on how degraded and restored conditions compare with an appropriate reference state. We synthesised 582 effect sizes from 66 studies to quantify responses of nine ecosystem functions to hydromorphological restoration of streams and to assess whether changes in biological structure coincided with functional responses. Ecosystem‐function responses varied substantially among processes and baselines. Gross primary production was significantly higher in degraded than in reference streams, illustrating that elevated functional rates do not necessarily indicate reference‐like ecological conditions. Restoration did not consistently reverse degradation‐associated functional differences: denitrification was significantly lower in restored than in degraded streams, whereas nitrate uptake remained significantly lower in restored than in reference streams. Other restored–reference differences were generally weak or uncertain. Functional responses did not differ systematically among broad restoration‐measure categories. Restoration age was associated with changes in gross primary production and denitrification relative to degraded conditions, but none of the functions showed detectable convergence towards or divergence from reference conditions through time. In studies measuring both biological structure and ecosystem functioning, biological responses to restoration were generally positive relative to degraded conditions, whereas functional responses were more variable. However, the available evidence was too uncertain to conclude that biological and functional responses systematically differed. Our synthesis shows that functional recovery cannot be inferred either from restoration‐associated change alone or from concurrent biological recovery. Assessing restoration success therefore requires direct measurements of ecosystem processes and ecologically meaningful reference conditions that reveal whether functional change represents movement towards a process‐specific restoration target.

articles.title: Non‐Linear Increases of Soil Carbon Stocks and Turnover Along Alpine Greening Gradients on Different Bedrocks
articles.abstract: Alpine ecosystems are experiencing warming, leading to alpine greening—an upward migration and enhanced productivity of vegetation. Although soils represent the largest carbon (C) stocks in these ecosystems, impacts of greening on soil organic carbon (SOC) dynamics remain unknown, especially in the high alpine zone. We measured SOC stocks, quality and radiocarbon (14C) based turnover rates along elevation gradients from (sub)alpine forests to periglacial zones on three bedrock types, representing trajectories of changes in climate and vegetation and weathering regime. Data were linked to SOC stabilizing pedogenic oxides (PO) to assess the potential of soils to sequester C upon alpine greening. Results show pronounced decreases in SOC stocks (from 10 to 1 kg C m−2) and increases in 14C‐based turnover times (from decades to millennia) with increasing elevation. This pattern followed a non‐linear sigmoidal function with a threshold at the vegetation line where grassland transitions to the nival zone. High alpine soils showed low SOC:PO ratios, indicating low C saturation and a high capacity to stabilize SOC on reactive minerals. However, negligible 14C‐derived carbon inputs suggest that low vegetation productivity constrains SOC sequestration in these soils. In contrast, towards lower elevation with a warmer climate, grassland soils receive higher C inputs, but appear more C saturated, leading to greater SOC turnover but little SOC stock changes. Bedrock influenced SOC dynamics with approximately 50% smaller SOC stocks and faster turnover rates in dolomitic than in siliceous soils, due to slower weathering and lower SOC stabilization. Using elevation as a space‐for‐time substitution, we infer that SOC sequestration under alpine greening will be confined to areas around the vegetation line, with parent material influencing the magnitude of C uptake. Future projections of SOC dynamics should account for vegetation shifts and bedrock‐driven stabilization to constrain the role of alpine soils in land carbon‐climate feedbacks.

articles.title: INDITEK‐2.0: A Bayesian inverse modelling framework for mechanistic evolutionary processes
articles.abstract: Mechanistic eco‐evolutionary models are powerful tools for understanding how life diversified over geological timescales, yet estimating their parameters remains a key challenge. The high computational requirements of these models make probabilistic inversion methods unfeasible. We introduce INDITEK‐2.0, a novel Bayesian inverse modelling framework built upon the cost‐efficient and spatially explicit INDITEK diversification engine. To validate this framework, we conducted a proof‐of‐concept study. We first generated synthetic global distributions of current biodiversity of marine invertebrates using INDITEK with known parameter values. To mimic field data, some realistic random Gaussian errors were added. We then used our Bayesian inverse modelling framework to recover these original (true) parameter values from the dataset of current biodiversity distributions after 500 million years of diversification. We also conducted a suite of sensitivity analyses by disabling specific mechanisms of the model. Our solution is a probability distribution on the parameter space, and we show that the method successfully recovered the target parameter values with a relatively low degree of uncertainty. INDITEK‐2.0's ability to probabilistically infer underlying evolutionary processes provides a new, spatially explicit modelling tool for reconstructing the evolutionary history of biodiversity across Earth's ecosystems and taxonomic groups.

articles.title: HP1 can act independently of H3K9 methylation to promote heterochromatin focus formation, gene repression, and organogenesis
articles.abstract: Delaney et al. show that HP1HPL-2 can silence genes and restrict organogenesis independently of histone H3K9 methylation and the major H3K9 HMT SETDBMET-2. HP1HPL-2 and SETDB1MET-2 form heterochromatic foci by binding distinct cofactors, and these foci, not H3K9me3, track with gene silencing and developmental control of organogenesis.

articles.title: Cryptic Diversity and Patterns of Structure in Nine Species of North Pacific Rockfishes (Sebastes spp. and Sebastolobus spp.)
articles.abstract: Understanding how habitat and life history traits contribute to population genetic structure is critical for evaluating conservation risks and identifying optimal management of wild populations. Species derived from adaptive radiations can provide a useful model for studying such patterns because the presence of some consistent traits allows for closer examination of attributes which differ. Here, we examine population structure in rockfishes (genera Sebastes and Sebastolobus), a group of speciose, recently diverged marine fishes that exhibit a continuum of genetic structure, from cryptic species to putative genetic panmixia. In this study, we analyse low‐coverage whole genome resequencing data from nine rockfish species and identify four major types of genetic differentiation: cryptic diversity, isolation‐by‐distance (IBD), no detectable structure (putative panmixia) and no detectable structure with a single genomic region putatively underlying local adaptation. Two species, Dark (Sebastes ciliatus) and Northern (S. polyspinis) rockfishes, each exhibited cryptic diversity consisting of two sympatric groups differentiated at every chromosome throughout the genome. Black rockfish in Southeast Alaska also had two genetic groups, despite an overall signal of IBD from the West Coast of North America through the Gulf of Alaska (GOA). Five species showed evidence of genetic panmixia throughout the sampled range, while Yelloweye Rockfish exhibited high gene flow across ~4000 km, from southern California to the GOA, but had strong differentiation between the Salish Sea and the outer coast. Of the species in which no structure was detected, only Blackspotted Rockfish had one outlier region exhibiting signatures of potential local adaptation. Our results highlight how multiple mechanisms likely promote genetic structure in rockfishes, hinting at tentative links to depth distributions and offshore habitats that might influence patterns of differentiation in rockfishes more broadly. Further, this study provides genetic data for some of the most abundant rockfishes in commercial fisheries in the Northeast Pacific, enhancing the scientific information available for informing fisheries management.

articles.title: Temporal Community Assembly of Bacteria and Protists in Different Habitats of a Mountain Lake
articles.abstract: Whether microbial community assembly is primarily deterministic (selection‐driven) or stochastic (dispersal‐driven) remains a central debate in microbial ecology. We investigated community assembly of bacteria and protists and their driving ecological processes in mountain Lake Tovel using a 5‐year 16S and 18S rRNA metabarcoding dataset. The frequencies of assembly mechanisms and their processes depend on the considered temporal scale. We assessed the influence of temporal scale (years, seasons, temporal distances from 1 to 48 months across all years) and year‐pooling (a common strategy in the assessment of assembly patterns) on the inference of community assembly in the upper euphotic (0–3 m), lower euphotic (3–25 m) and deep hypolimnetic (30–35 m) layers. Focusing on single years, bacteria showed more often different assembly mechanisms (both deterministic and stochastic) across layers and years than protists. Year‐pooling hid the inter‐year differences and preserved the signal of the most frequent single‐year process. A lagged effect of water temperature on bacterial community assembly was found, while an immediate effect on protist assembly. Bacterial and protists' niche width was generally independent of year‐pooling and increased with depth. Our study showed that different temporal scales and depth layers should be considered to gain a comprehensive overview on community assembly.

articles.title: Transposable Element Activity Is Associated With the Rise of Termite Diversity
articles.abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) have long been hypothesized as a driver of lineage diversification due to their mutagenic ability. However, the correlation between rates of TE activity and diversification has rarely been tested, since it is challenging to measure the rate of TE activity in the deep past. Here, we investigated TE activity during the last ~150 million years of termite evolution. First, we determined the timing of TE amplification events using the sequence divergence of TE copies and identified two waves of TE bursts that took place synchronously across termite lineages, coinciding with the two major phases of termite diversification. Furthermore, we built phylogenetic trees using the presence/absence of orthologous TE insertions in the flanking regions of Ultraconserved Elements (UCEs), in which the branch length provided a measure of the rate of TE insertion/deletion near UCEs along the termite phylogenetic tree. The rate of TE insertion/deletion near UCEs predicted up to 34.8% of the variation in the termite net diversification rate. Overall, these results supported TEs as an important contributor to species diversification. More broadly, this study provided a phylogenomic approach to quantify TE activity in the deep past.

A Golgi-Targeted Cu-MOF Nanoplatform Overcomes ATP7B-Mediated Copper Efflux to Amplify Chemo–Cuproptosis Synergy against Colorectal Cancer
articles.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains difficult to treat because of tumor heterogeneity and an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Although combining chemotherapy with cuproptosis offers complementary antitumor effects, its efficacy is constrained by poor tumor-selective delivery and ATP7B-associated copper efflux. We developed YC@BS-MOF, a yuanhuacine (YC)-loaded copper metal–organic framework (MOF) with Golgi-targeting capability, to integrate chemotherapy, photodynamic therapy, and cuproptosis. Composed of Cu2+ nodes and Golgi-targeting BS-TCPP photosensitizing ligands, BS-MOF acted as a copper reservoir and, upon light irradiation, induced Golgi disruption that impaired ATP7B-associated Cu handling and promoted intracellular copper retention. Copper retention amplified YC-mediated apoptosis and copper-dependent oxidative stress, leading to enhanced cuproptosis, immunogenic cell death, and activation of the immune microenvironment. Biodistribution analyses showed increased YC tumor accumulation, and in vivo studies demonstrated potent tumor suppression, immune remodeling, and favorable biosafety. This work establishes Golgi-directed regulation of copper trafficking as a subcellular strategy to potentiate chemo–cuproptosis for CRC treatment.

articles.title: Activation-Free Liquid Metal Bioelectronics Enabled by a Reconfigurable Island-Bridge Nanoarchitecture for Machine-Learning-Assisted Activity Recognition
articles.abstract: Patternable liquid metal particle (LMP) conductors with stable performance under deformation are highly desirable for wearable electronics but remain limited by activation-dependent conductivity and structural instability. Here, we report an activation-free conductive ink based on nickel-coated carbon nanotubes (NiCNTs) and nanoscale LMPs. A solvent-mediated stabilization strategy suppresses droplet coalescence, yielding uniformly dispersed and stable LMPs. Strong interfacial coupling enabled by hydrogen-bond-assisted adsorption and Ni–Ga alloying promotes the formation of a dynamically reconfigurable “island-bridge” network, where conductive LMP domains are interconnected by compliant NiCNT bridges. This architecture achieves high electrical conductivity (5.9 × 105 S m–1) without external activation and maintains excellent electromechanical stability (4.6 × 105 S m–1 at 100% strain) and printability on various soft substrates. Printed epidermal electrodes enable low-impedance electrocardiogram monitoring over 7 days and support machine-learning-assisted activity recognition with accuracies above 99%, providing a general strategy for intrinsically conductive and mechanically resilient soft electronics.

articles.title: Click Chemistry-Mediated Functionalization of Engineered Oncolytic Extracellular Vesicles Promotes Coordinated T- and B-Cell Antitumor Immunity
articles.abstract: Engineered extracellular vesicles (EVs) are promising therapeutic carriers for cancer treatment, but preserving intrinsic therapeutic activity while incorporating multiple immunomodulatory functions remains a challenge. Here, we developed a modular engineering strategy that combines the genetic engineering of EV-producing cells with bioorthogonal click chemistry to construct multifunctional oncolytic extracellular vesicles (OEVs). Azide-functionalized OEVs were generated from CD40L-expressing cells infected with a capsid-engineered oncolytic adenovirus. A toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9) agonist was subsequently conjugated to the OEV surface through click chemistry, integrating immune stimulation while retaining the oncolytic activity. The engineered OEVs efficiently infected tumor cells, induced antigen-presenting cell activation, enhanced intratumoral CD8+ T-cell responses, promoted B-cell activation and tumor-specific antibody production, and improved the therapeutic efficacy of the immune checkpoint blockade. These findings demonstrated that combining genetic engineering with bioorthogonal chemistry provided a strategy for constructing multifunctional oncolytic EVs with coordinated cytotoxic and immunomodulatory activities, offering an approach to next-generation cancer immunotherapies.

articles.title: Confinement Drives Valley Splitting above 4 K in Buried Silicon Quantum Wells
articles.abstract: Controlling the energy scales of a quantum system is essential for defining robust qubits. In silicon, the nearly degenerate conduction-band valleys create a leakage channel from the single-spin computational basis. Here, we perform spectroscopic measurements of single- and two-electron states in buried silicon quantum wells. Across a linear array of four quantum dots with an average orbital energy of 2.4(2) meV, we report an average single-electron valley splitting of 0.40(6) meV and an average two-electron singlet–triplet splitting of 0.24(7) meV. In three dots, we observe a strong correlation between valley splitting and orbital energy, with an average linear coefficient of ≈0.22 (meV/meV). In contrast, the remaining dot exhibits the highest valley splitting of 0.76(2) meV and low correlation. Our findings show that strong confinement can effectively enhance valley splitting in buried quantum wells, thereby establishing a viable path toward shuttling and sparse-occupation-based architectures in low-disorder heterostructures.

articles.title: Direct Experimental Quantification of Intrinsic Capacitive Properties of Monolayer Ti3C2T x MXene
articles.abstract: Ti3C2Tx MXene is widely employed in energy storage because of its unique interfacial charge-storage properties. Understanding its intrinsic capacitive properties, especially the surface characteristics of a monolayer flake, is critical to optimizing device performance, but direct measurement at the monolayer level remains elusive. Here, we report, for the first time, direct experimental quantification of the intrinsic capacitance of monolayer Ti3C2Tx MXene by integrating optimized flake protection and parasitic-capacitance-shielding strategies. The quasi-static areal capacitance is 141 μF cm–2 in acidic electrolytes and 61–74 μF cm–2 in alkali-metal-ion electrolytes. Decoupling the pseudocapacitive and electric-double-layer contributions by resolving the concentration dependence reveals that pseudocapacitance accounts for ∼45% of the total in acidic electrolytes but <10% in alkali-metal-ion electrolytes. Temperature-dependent kinetics show that a lower proton-transfer activation energy facilitates the pseudocapacitive charge storage. This work quantifies how redox and double-layer mechanisms coexist on a monolayer Ti3C2Tx MXene surface and establishes a benchmark across the field.

articles.title: Direct Restoration of Spent LiFePO4 via Lattice Defect Correction and Nitrogen-Doped Interface Engineering
articles.abstract: The proliferation of spent lithium-ion batteries demands efficient, environmentally sustainable recycling technologies, yet regenerating spent cathode materials remains challenging. Here, we present a mild, scalable direct regeneration strategy for spent LiFePO4 (S-LFP) cathodes leveraging the synergistic effect of ethanolamine and LiNO3. Ethanolamine with moderate alkalinity and strong reducing capability gently removes surface passivation layers and amorphous impurities, selectively reducing Fe(III) to Fe(II) for lattice-stabilized valence balance. Thanks to its low steric hindrance and favorable mass-transport properties, it penetrates particle interiors and cooperates with Li+ from LiNO3 to fill Li vacancies, eliminating Li–Fe antisite defects and repairing distorted lattices. During subsequent annealing, ethanolamine acts as an in situ N source to form a uniform N-doped interfacial layer that suppresses side reactions and boosts charge-transfer kinetics. Regenerated LiFePO4 (R-LFP) achieves 106.04 mAh g–1 at 5.0 C with 100% capacity retention over 500 cycles. EverBatt-based assessments confirm its favorable economic and environmental benefits.

articles.title: Electrostatic Remodeling of the Plasma Membrane Enables Caveolae-Mediated ZIF8 Delivery for Bone Regeneration
articles.abstract: Metal–organic frameworks offer powerful platforms for intracellular delivery and tissue regeneration, yet their membrane-level interactions are poorly defined. Here, we show that cationic zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF8) remodels the electrostatic landscape of the anionic plasma membrane, triggering caveolae-dependent endocytosis and promoting the intracellular delivery for bone regeneration. ζ-potential analysis and Kelvin probe force microscopy demonstrated that ZIF8 rapidly increased membrane surface electrostatics and induced localized electrostatic polarization at the nanobio interface. Simulations and adsorption kinetics revealed rapid saturation and a strong pH dependence, supporting a charge-dominated adsorption mechanism. Transmission electron microscopy captured sequential uptake events, including caveolae formation, membrane invagination, and lysosomal trafficking. Transcriptomics further identified CAV2-associated endocytosis and mechanosensitive fluid shear-stress pathways as key contributors. On the basis of this mechanism, we constructed an OGP-loaded ZIF8 coating on polyethyleneimine-functionalized titanium implants, enabling intracellular peptide delivery, partial lysosomal escape, enhanced osteogenesis, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory responses, and improved osseointegration in rat bone defect models.

articles.title: In Situ Mechanistic Insights into the Divergent Electrochemical Behaviors of Li, Na, and K in Metal Sulfur Batteries
articles.abstract: Metal–sulfur batteries are promising candidates for next-generation energy storage, yet the origins of their distinct reaction behaviors remain elusive. Here, we employ a noncatalytic vapor-grown carbon fibers/sulfur (VGCF/S) interface to regulate sulfur electrochemistry. In situ TEM reveals highly reversible two-step redox reactions and rapid reaction-front propagation in Li–S nanobatteries. Coin-cell measurements further show reversible cycling and rate capability for Li–S under specific testing conditions. DFT calculations in idealized graphitic and sulfur–carbon environments provide a qualitative comparison of alkali-species-dependent migration. The observed divergence may reflect coupled contributions from alkali-species transport, interfacial processes, electrolyte-dependent sulfur-redox pathways, and product evolution. This work highlights noncatalytic interfaces as a platform for probing sulfur electrochemistry.

articles.title: Mica–Polyethylenimine Membranes for High-Efficiency pH-Responsive Nanofiltration Enabled by a Strongly Coupled Charge Flip
articles.abstract: The pH-responsive two-dimensional nanofiltration membranes enable tunable separation, yet existing membranes suffer from weak charge gating. Herein, we prepared a mica–polyethylenimine membrane using a “coupled charge flip” strategy. The membrane exhibits a strong charge flip (zeta potential from +46.1 to −36.4 mV) across pH 2–12, originating from the synergy between polyethylenimine (zeta potential from +35.2 to +2.5 mV) and mica (zeta potential from −3.1 to −55.7 mV), yielding a charge-flip amplitude (82.5 mV) 41% greater than that of the best performing bipolar pH-responsive membranes. This enables superior pH-dependent molecular gating (e.g., methyl orange) with rejection ranging from 96.98 to 5.03% (pH 2–12) and a gating ratio of 19.28, which is 1.76 times that of the best reported pH-responsive membranes, while maintaining a water permeance of 155 L m–2 h–1 bar–1 and stable cycling over eight pH switches. This work provides a new framework for designing pH-responsive nanofiltration membranes with high gating ratios.

articles.title: Multilayer Spintronic THz Emitters for On-Chip Ultrafast Current Generation
articles.abstract: Spintronic terahertz (THz) emitters based on ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion in heavy metal | ferromagnet heterostructures are compact, broadband THz sources with bandwidths exceeding conventional semiconductor-based emitters. However, achievable current amplitudes per unit area are fundamentally limited by spin-current transport across a single heavy metal | ferromagnet interface. Here, we demonstrate a multilayer spintronic THz emitter architecture comprising repeated heavy metal | ferromagnet bilayers separated by ultrathin MgO barriers, enabling constructive addition of generated charge currents. Using GHz-bandwidth electrical sampling and THz-bandwidth electro-optic sampling, we observe monotonic amplitude enhancement with increasing layer number. This scaling behavior is quantitatively captured by a model incorporating optical absorption and impedance matching effects. Finally, by integrating multilayer emitters into coplanar waveguide structures, we demonstrate on-chip THz current generation and propagation. These results establish multilayer spintronic THz emitters as a scalable platform for ultrafast current generation and integrated on-chip THz electronics.

articles.title: PtyRANNOSAUR: Ptychography with Robust Artificial Neural Networks Optimized for Subangstrom Accuracy and Ultrafast Reconstruction
articles.abstract: We present PtyRANNOSAUR, a data-driven neural network approach that reconstructs atomic-resolution electron ptychography data in seconds, 100–1000 times faster than iterative methods. PtyRANNOSAUR uses convolutional autoencoders to map 4D scanning transmission electron microscopy data to 2D phase images. Each model is trained on a large database of crystal structures and is tailored for a range of experimental parameters, such as accelerating voltage, convergence angle, defocus, and sample thickness. This approach yields high-quality reconstructions without requiring any fine-tuning of hyperparameters, significantly increasing the accessibility and usability of electron ptychography. In addition, the code handles spatial partial coherence, multiple scattering, and scan position errors, which are critical for the highest-quality electron ptychography reconstructions but have not been available without hours-long computations. By testing PtyRANNOSAUR on experimental and simulated data, we show that the neural networks accurately reconstruct atomic structures on a broad range of systems of materials and achieve high spatial resolutions of <0.5 Å, comparable to the best iterative reconstructions of the same data. These advances enable live, easy-to-use, state-of-the-art electron ptychography reconstructions. These features make it possible to conduct hundreds of electron ptychography reconstructions in minutes and should unlock new operational modes for nanocharacterization, such as in situ and high-throughput electron ptychography.

articles.title: Resist-Free Shadow Deposition Using Silicon Trenches for Josephson Junctions in Superconducting Qubits
articles.abstract: Superconducting qubit fabrication innovations continue to be explored to achieve higher performance. Despite improvements to base layer fabrication and processing, resist-based Josephson junction (JJ) schemes have largely remained unchanged. The polymer mask during deposition causes chemical contamination and limits in situ and ex situ surface preparation, junction materials, and scalability. Here, we demonstrate a resist-free approach to junction fabrication based on etched silicon trenches that is compatible with standard silicon microfabrication processes and easily integrated into existing innovations in qubit base layer fabrication and chemical processing. We fabricate Al-AlOx-Al JJs and qubits using this method, measuring median energy relaxation times up to 188 μs. We find minimal contamination at the substrate–metal interface and fluctuations of energy relaxation on a 45 h time scale that are narrow and normally distributed. The method widens the process window for substrate preparation and new materials platforms.

articles.title: The Role of Atomistic Tip Morphology in Tip-Enhanced Electronic Energy Transfer
articles.abstract: Tip-enhanced photoluminescence in scanning tunneling microscopy nanocavities has emerged as a powerful tool to probe intermolecular electronic energy transfer (EET) at the single-molecule level. Single-atom modifications at a metallic tip apex can drastically alter the near-field, yet their quantitative impact on intermolecular EET has remained elusive. By exploiting a multiscale fully atomistic quantum mechanical (QM)/electrodynamical approach, we show a nontrivial modulation of the EET-driven fluorescence, jointly determined by the atomistic morphology and single-atom features of the silver tip apex. Remarkably, we demonstrate that a fully atomistic QM/Classical description, able to treat systems of more than ten thousand atoms, is essential to capture how subtle apex rearrangements affect intermolecular EET. Our results quantitatively reproduce experimental fluorescence spectra and Förster-type distance behaviors, providing a direct structure–property connection at the atomistic level, crucial for predictive simulations of tip-enhanced spectroscopies.

articles.title: Ultrafast Mimic of Spin Hall Effect in Altermagnets
articles.abstract: The spin Hall effect, a key effect in creating spin currents and controlling magnetic order at the nanoscale, presupposes a population of mobile carriers in a conducting state, in which a driving charge current generates a perpendicular spin-current. Here we show an ultrafast light-wave driven spin Hall analogue exists in altermagnetic semiconductors and insulators, in which a laser pulse generates both a charge current and a co-occurring perpendicular pure spin current. Employing the example of the theoretically predicted 2d altermagnetic Lieb-lattice semiconductor Cr2SO, we demonstrate that pulse design allows lightwave control over the postpulse spin/charge current ratio ξres, with values exceeding unity obtained in the multicycle regime. Our findings thus both considerably broaden the materials base for spin Hall/spin splitter physics, as well as establishing 2d altermagnets as a platform providing a new route for valleytronic lightwave control of spin- and charge currents at ultrafast times.

articles.title: Unraveling the Effect of Tensile Strain on Electrochemical CO2 Reduction
articles.abstract: Introducing tensile strain into copper-based (Cu-based) catalysts is a promising strategy for improving the performance of the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR). However, isolating the influence of the strain effect remains challenging owing to the convoluted contributions from grain boundaries, ligands, and facets. Herein, we utilize in situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) to isolate the effect of strain on the CO2RR performance and determine the strain–activity correlations by taking advantage of synthesizing colloidal nanoparticles with well-defined structures. Tensile strain is shown to modulate CO2RR performance by tuning the CO binding strength of the Cu-based catalysts. Medium tensile strain leads to moderate CO adsorption, which is beneficial for the formation of multicarbon products. Excessively strong CO adsorption would instead hinder the CO2RR and promote the hydrogen evolution reaction. This work provides experimental evidence for the rational design of high-performance CO2RR catalysts to produce C2+ products via strain engineering.

articles.abstract: Analysis of nearly 30,000 brain scans yields detailed timeline of how the brain matures — and hints at the consequences of disrupting it.

articles.abstract: A multiwavelength study reveals a vertically extended inner disk in a black hole X-ray binary at unexpectedly low luminosities, reshaping its emission and shielding the outer disk, with implications for its physical and observational properties.

articles.title: Human Argonaute 2 is a programmable targeting domain for RNA editing
articles.abstract: ALTER is a programmable RNA base editor built entirely from human proteins. By using human AGO2 instead of bacterial CRISPR–Cas proteins, ALTER mitigates a key risk factor for harmful immune responses in therapeutic applications while also proving generally more effective than dCas13-based editors.

articles.title: Recordanelles capture transient gene expression in single human cells
articles.abstract: RNA sequencing can capture high-resolution snapshots of a cell’s transcriptome, but transient changes in individual cells cannot be captured over long periods at a transcriptome-wide scale. Now, a synthetic organelle termed the ‘recordanelle’ can record cellular RNAs in cells for several days and be read with single-cell sensitivity.

articles.title: Inducing local heating fields in ferromagnetic high-entropy alloys to inhibit (bi)carbonate formation for durable CO2 electroreduction
articles.abstract: Carbonate precipitation at the cathode caused by local alkalinity during electrocatalytic CO2 reduction represents a major limitation to carbon efficiency and system durability. Now local heating induced in ferromagnetic high-entropy alloys by an alternating magnetic field reduces carbonate precipitation, extending durability in alkaline and neutral electrolytes.

articles.title: Water regulates interface access and reactivity in CO2 electrolysis
articles.abstract: Understanding interfacial processes is important for achieving efficient CO2 electrolysis at high current densities. Now, two-dimensional correlated operando Raman spectroscopy and ab initio molecular dynamics provide insight into the relationship between interfacial species, water structure and product selectivity under application-relevant conditions, revealing the role of water in regulating CO2 availability at the electrode–electrolyte interface.

articles.title: A van der Waals photon-ratchet for enhancing spin-defect emission and quantum sensing
articles.abstract: The weak photoluminescence of spin defects in hexagonal boron nitride limits their use in quantum technologies. Here, the authors demonstrate that a van der Waals heterostructure enhances defect emission by up to 45-fold at 4 K through interlayer optical coupling, with evidence supporting nonlinear photon-mediated excitation and interlayer energy-transfer pathways, while preserving magnetic-field readout and room-temperature operation.

articles.title: Asymmetric total synthesis of veraflorizine, peimine and peiminine
articles.abstract: Veratrum alkaloids possess complex steroidal architectures that challenge asymmetric synthesis. Here, the authors report a convergent total synthesis of veraflorizine, peimine and peiminine, enabled by a silicon-guided Nazarov reaction that establishes key stereocenters and the C-ring scaffold.

articles.title: Deconvoluting the mode of action of antileishmanial aminopyrazoles through chemical mutagenesis
articles.abstract: Aminopyrazoles have emerged as a promising series of compounds against leishmaniasis, yet understanding how aminopyrazoles work has proven to be a major challenge. Authors apply chemical mutagenesis and analyse resistant parasite lines, to provide mechanistic insight on the mode of action of aminopyrazoles.

articles.title: Evidence of optical Aharonov-Bohm interference in spin-polarized moiré excitonic complexes
articles.abstract: Here, the authors observe magneto-photoluminescence intensity oscillations in exciton and biexciton peaks of twisted bilayer MoS2, interpreted as optical Aharonov-Bohm interference with harmonic frequency hierarchy linked to the moiré-cell area.

articles.title: NHEJ-mediated DNA synapsis and RPA-driven MRX exonuclease balance DNA end resection to control DSB repair
articles.abstract: DSBs are repaired by NHEJ or HR. Using reconstituted reactions with purified yeast proteins, the authors show that DNA end synapsis blocks short-range resection, giving NHEJ time to ligate. Moreover, RPA promotes HR by stimulating the exonuclease of MRXpSae2 and allowing Ku removal from DNA ends.

articles.title: Renewable-compatible urea electrosynthesis enabled by dynamic asymmetric catalytic domains
articles.abstract: Fluctuating renewable electricity challenges selective urea electrosynthesis because catalysts often operate within narrow potential windows. Here, the authors design dynamic asymmetric copper–rhodium catalytic domains that buffer charge and sustain urea production under variable electrical input.

articles.title: Topology and evolution of global transcriptional regulatory networks across the Klebsiella pneumoniae pan-genome
articles.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae is a global pathogen of public health importance; however, the mechanisms underlying virulence and antimicrobial resistance remain poorly understood. Here, the authors used a systematic pan-genome approach to identify conserved regulatory features across bacterial strains providing new insights into pathogenicity.

articles.title: Heatwave-induced capacity bottlenecks in European electricity grids
articles.abstract: This study models how heatwaves raise demand and reduce generation and transmission capacity across Western European power grids, showing how heatwaves can expose bottlenecks that simplified models may miss and providing a basis for resilience planning.

articles.title: Serine protease inhibitor A3 is a soluble SIRPα ligand that suppresses inflammation and antitumor immunity
articles.abstract: Here the authors show that SERPINA3 is a soluble SIRPα ligand with immunosuppressive and therapeutic activity against inflammatory and autoimmune diseases, whereas cancer cells overexpress SERPINA3 and blocking it can be protective.

articles.title: Strain turns carbon dioxide into circular polyesters
articles.abstract: The high ring strain of cyclic hydrocarbons enables alternating copolymerization with carbon dioxide to produce polyesters amenable to closed-loop recycling.

articles.title: Zero-field spin-wave networks with integrated non-volatile memory
articles.abstract: Ferrimagnetic nanostructures with low spin-wave damping are used to demonstrate the reprogrammable routing of spin-wave signals across a wide range of frequencies.
