articles.title: Milk multi-omics links maternal health to infant growth
articles.abstract: Researchers identify biomarkers that explain how maternal health is linked to mammary gland function, breast milk composition and infant growth, highlighting maternal nutrition as a public health priority.

articles.title: CauTrigger: deciphering biological system state transitions by hierarchical causal decomposition
articles.abstract: CauTrigger is a hierarchical deep latent variable model that can identify potential causal triggers and predict outcomes of perturbation events.

articles.abstract: OpenDVP enables scalable and high-resolution proteomic profiling of cellular neighborhoods.

articles.title: Tracing causal cascades underlying biological state changes
articles.abstract: Maps constructed from omics data to identify the causal mechanisms underlying state transitions have not been established. We developed CauTrigger, which treats state transitions as layered causal cascades rather than isolated molecular changes, effectively separating causal signals from spurious variation. CauTrigger prioritizes potential upstream triggers, predicts perturbation responses and helps turn omics measurements into testable mechanistic hypotheses.

articles.title: Behavioral genomics identifies Creld1 as a cross-modal regulator of somatosensation
articles.abstract: Jiang et al. developed a robust postnatal knockout platform for somatosensory genomics and behavioral screening, identifying Creld1 as a cross-modal regulator of somatosensation through its control of sensory neuron excitability via voltage-gated sodium channels.

articles.title: Network geometry shapes the transformation of task representations across the human cortex
articles.abstract: The dimensionality of intrinsic brain connectivity systematically shapes how task representations compress and expand across the cortex, and activity flow modeling shows the active role of network geometry in generating the transformation.

articles.title: Teleportation transition of surface codes on a superconducting quantum processor
articles.abstract: Quantum teleportation is often discussed for individual quantum systems, but fault-tolerant quantum computers will encode information in multiqubit states. Now teleportation of surface code logical states has been demonstrated.

articles.title: Wigner crystals get dressed
articles.abstract: When repulsion overcomes their tendency to move freely, electrons can arrange into a crystal. Two experiments have now identified Wigner polarons, quasiparticles whose optical signatures reveal the collective response of the electron lattice.

articles.title: Cancer theranostics
articles.abstract: Theranostics integrates diagnostic imaging with targeted therapy to enhance cancer treatment. In this Review, Sofias et al. discuss recent advances in radiotheranostic strategies, advances in nanotheranostic and microtheranostic platforms, and image-guided therapeutic and surgical interventions in oncology.

articles.title: Hit the pause button
articles.abstract: In a recent study, García-Gómez et al. identify an adaptive proliferative pause program that supports the survival of micrometastatic cells during early brain colonization and uncover therapeutic opportunities to target this state.

Durable, highly loaded atomically dispersed catalysts via a reticular coordination strategy
articles.abstract: A reticular coordination strategy is developed in which coordinating one Pt atom per Ce-oxo cluster in a metal–organic framework before calcination yields ceria containing 14.9 wt% atomically dispersed Pt. The resulting lattice confinement inhibits migration and suppresses sintering under harsh reducing conditions.

articles.title: Thianthrenium ylides for safe carbene transfer
Atacicept in IgA Nephropathy — Phase 3 Trial Final Efficacy Analysis
articles.abstract: Atacicept resulted in a significantly greater reduction in the urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo in a previously published analysis of this trial, ORIGIN 3. Final prespecified efficacy results are reported here. We randomly assigned adults with biopsy-confirmed IgA nephropathy to receive weekly subcutaneous atacicept at a dose of 150 mg or placebo. We carried out final analyses of two secondary end points: the change in the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) at week 52 and the annualized eGFR slope through week 104; additional hierarchically tested end points and safety were assessed. Of 431 patients who underwent randomization, 428 received atacicept or placebo (214 per group). At week 52, the mean change in the eGFR was -0.11 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area (95% confidence interval [CI], -1.44 to 1.22) with atacicept and -5.69 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, -7.04 to -4.35) with placebo (mean difference, 5.58 ml per minute per 1.73 m2; 95% CI, 3.68 to 7.48; P<0.001). Through week 104, the mean annualized eGFR slope was -0.60 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, -1.62 to 0.41) with atacicept and -5.60 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, -6.64 to -4.57) with placebo (difference, 5.00 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 per year; 95% CI, 3.55 to 6.45; P<0.001). Composite kidney-disease progression occurred in 11 patients (5.1%) in the atacicept group and in 38 patients (17.8%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.12 to 0.48; P<0.001); no patients in the atacicept group had progression to dialysis, transplantation, or death, as compared with 7 patients in the placebo group. Adverse events occurred in 160 of 214 patients (74.8%) in the atacicept group and in 167 of 214 patients (78.0%) in the placebo group; serious adverse events occurred in 7.0% and 15.4%, respectively. One patient (in the placebo group) died. Atacicept slowed and stabilized the decline in the eGFR as compared with placebo. (Funded by Vera Therapeutics; ORIGIN 3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04716231.).

articles.title: Sibeprenlimab in IgA Nephropathy — Final Phase 3 Trial Analysis
articles.abstract: Sibeprenlimab, a humanized monoclonal antibody, selectively inhibits the cytokine A proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL), a key driver of IgA nephropathy. Preliminary trial results with regard to the primary end point of the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at 9 months after treatment as compared with baseline have been reported, but secondary end points, including outcomes regarding estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), have not. We randomly assigned adults with IgA nephropathy to receive subcutaneous sibeprenlimab (at a dose of 400 mg) or placebo every 4 weeks. The key secondary end point was the annualized slope of the eGFR over 24 months. Other secondary end points included the change in eGFR from baseline to 24 months, a composite kidney end point of kidney-function decline or kidney failure, and pharmacodynamic and safety end points. A total of 510 patients underwent randomization - 259 to receive sibeprenlimab and 251 to receive placebo. The annualized eGFR slope over 24 months was 0.3 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area per year (95% confidence interval [CI], -0.4 to 0.9) with sibeprenlimab and -4.2 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 per year (95% CI, -4.9 to -3.6) with placebo (between-group difference, 4.5 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 per year; 95% CI, 3.6 to 5.4; P<0.001). The least-squares mean treatment difference for the change in eGFR from baseline to 24 months was 9.2 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, 7.1 to 11.4; P<0.001). A composite kidney end-point event occurred in 1 patient (0.4%) in the sibeprenlimab group and in 28 patients (11.2%) in the placebo group (adjusted difference, -10.8 percentage points; hazard ratio, 0.029; 95% CI, 0.004 to 0.214; P<0.001). Adverse events occurred in 235 patients (90.7%) in the sibeprenlimab group and 226 patients (90.0%) in the placebo group; serious adverse events occurred in 21 patients (8.1%) and 32 patients (12.7%), respectively; and serious infections in 5 patients (1.9%) and 10 patients (4.0%). No deaths were reported. Among patients with IgA nephropathy, treatment with sibeprenlimab stabilized the eGFR slope over 24 months, a finding consistent with a reduced risk of kidney-function decline. (Funded by Otsuka Pharmaceutical Development and Commercialization; VISIONARY ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05248646.).

articles.title: Microbial volatile humulene orchestrates plant–microbe alliance to establish disease‐suppressive rhizosphere
articles.abstract: Proposed working model of humulene‐mediated suppression of tomato bacterial wilt. Summary Microbial volatile organic compounds (mVOCs) suppress growth and virulence traits of soil‐borne pathogens, yet their ecological roles in disease suppression remain unclear. Here, we show that the sesquiterpene humulene from Streptomyces acts as a multifunctional regulator that suppresses bacterial wilt through coordinated inhibition of Ralstonia solanacearum, plant metabolic reprogramming, and rhizosphere microbiome modulation. We combined in vitro pathogen assays, pot experiments, microbiota transplantation, rhizosphere 16S rRNA profiling, root‐exudate metabolomics, and plant and pathogen transcriptomics to investigate the direct and microbiome‐mediated effects of humulene. Humulene reduced disease severity and pathogen abundance via a microbiome‐dependent mechanism. Microbiota transplantation confirmed that the humulene‐conditioned microbiome retains transferable disease‐suppressiveness. Humulene also selectively enriched antagonistic Streptomyces, not by direct growth promotion, but by reprogramming tomato root exudation to produce lipid‐derived petroselinic acid, which promoted Streptomyces growth, humulene production, and pathogen suppression. Root transcriptomics further revealed activation of lipid metabolic pathways involving alternative fatty acid desaturation and oxylipin signaling. Together, humulene functions as an ecological signal that integrates pathogen suppression, host lipid metabolism, and microbiome assembly to establish a disease‐suppressive rhizosphere, enabling microbiome‐informed control of bacterial wilt.

articles.title: Altermagnetism in Folded Iron Chain Systems
articles.abstract: Altermagnetism---moment-compensated magnetism with momentum-dependent spin splitting---has so far been realized primarily in N\'eel-type antiferromagnets. Here, we demonstrate altermagnetism in folded iron chain systems with block-type magnetic order (e.g.,$\ensuremath{\uparrow}\ensuremath{\uparrow}\ensuremath{\downarrow}\ensuremath{\downarrow}$). In the strictly one-dimensional (1D) case, altermagnetism is forbidden by the $[{C}_{2}||\mathcal{T}]$ symmetry, but it can emerge when such chains are stacked into a quasi-1D array. To generate altermagnetic spin splitting via this chain-stacking mechanism, two essential ingredients are required: a block-type spin order that spontaneously breaks the combined parity-time reversal symmetry, and the finite interchain hopping. Using first-principles calculations, we identify the ${\mathrm{K}}_{3}{\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}{\mathrm{Se}}_{4}$ family as a promising platform that realizes this mechanism, hosting a $d$-wave altermagnet even without lattice ${C}_{4}$ symmetry. Moreover, owing to its lower symmetry, the block-type folded chain exhibits an isotropic altermagnetic spin splitting, which may manifest as an altermagnetic wrapping effect. Our findings unify real-space block magnetism and reciprocal-space altermagnetism, establishing folded iron chains as a tunable platform for zero-moment spintronic applications.

From these data, transverse-spin-dependent dihadron asymmetries are extracted using pairs of oppositely charged hadrons. These asymmetries ar…

articles.title: Genuine Quantum Strong Mpemba Effect by Eliminating Coherence
articles.abstract: Relaxation does not always reward patience: under certain conditions, a system initially farther from equilibrium can relax faster than one initially closer, a counterintuitive phenomenon known as the Mpemba effect. A conceptually transparent mechanism underlying this effect is the strong Mpemba effect, which commonly requires a unique slowest decay mode. However, for the Davies map, this condition is relaxed: the degenerate slowest modes are purely coherent. This allows the strong Mpemba effect to be realized by strategically eliminating coherence from the initial state. In this Letter, we design and implement a fully controllable optical setup to simulate the Davies map, whose validity is confirmed by verifying the semigroup property of the dynamics. We further demonstrate a genuine quantum strong Mpemba effect in the minimal quantum system, a single qubit. Our results experimentally confirm the key role of quantum coherence in this anomalous thermal relaxation. Moreover, our experimental setup provides a versatile platform for exploring quantum thermodynamics and a wider range of open-system dynamics.

articles.title: Magnon Chern Insulator in Two-Dimensional Fully Compensated Ferrimagnetic Heterostructures
articles.abstract: Achieving intrinsic Chern insulators (CIs) with zero net magnetization remains a long-standing and formidable challenge. Here, motivated by the unique opportunities that topological magnons offer for low-dissipation transport, we propose a general theoretical framework for realizing magnon CIs in filling-enforced fully compensated ferrimagnets with vanishing net magnetization. Moreover, we demonstrate that strong asymmetric intralayer Heisenberg interactions induce a type-III (broken-gap) magnonic band alignment, characterized by nonoverlapping magnon frequency gaps of the two layers, thereby enabling the emergence of magnon CIs. Remarkably, the asymmetric Bose-Einstein occupations of oppositely chiral magnon branches offer a distinct advantage in generating a giant magnon thermal Hall conductivity, which is forbidden in conventional antiferromagnets. Based on the Heisenberg-Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya model and first-principles calculations, we identify the experimentally accessible ${\mathrm{CrI}}_{3}/{\text{CrGeTe}}_{3}$ and ${\mathrm{CrI}}_{3}/{\text{CrSiTe}}_{3}$ heterostructures as ideal material platforms for realizing the proposed magnon CIs with fully compensated ferrimagnetism. These heterostructures host the nonzero magnon Chern numbers and chiral edge states, and remarkably display the strongly enhanced magnon thermal Hall effect comparable to that of ferromagnets, establishing fully compensated ferrimagnets as a promising platform for topological magnon transport without net magnetization.

articles.title: Reflection-Assisted Discrete Achromatic Diffraction

articles.title: Role of Anisotropic Electronic Friction in Laser-Driven Hydrogen Recombination on Copper
articles.abstract: Ultrafast light-driven chemical dynamics at surfaces are governed by energy transfer from excited electrons to vibrational degrees of freedom. When this nonadiabatic energy transfer is anisotropic, it can lead to dynamical steering effects that affect reaction probabilities or nonthermal final energy distributions in molecules. Here, enabled by a machine-learning-based simulation framework, we compare isotropic and anisotropic models of electronic friction during laser-driven hydrogen evolution on the (111) facet of copper. While anisotropic electronic friction determines the rate of energy transfer into the adsorbate and the fluence dependence of desorption probabilities, final translational, vibrational, and rotational energy distributions are mainly governed by the potential energy landscape at the barrier and insensitive to nonadiabatic effects.

articles.title: Twinned Dynamical Decoupling
articles.abstract: Systematic pulse-area errors limit the fidelity of quantum control across many qubit platforms. We introduce twinned dynamical decoupling, an analytic family of sequences $T2n$ in which a pulse sequence is paired with its $\ensuremath{\pi}$-phase-shifted twin. This $\ensuremath{\pi}$-phase step cancels common-mode systematic pulse-area errors to all orders on exact resonance. Then the phases of the pulses in each of the constituent twins are determined in such a manner that detuning errors are suppressed to the highest possible order as well. We have derived a simple analytic formula for these phases applicable to arbitrary sequence length. We demonstrate the sequences with superconducting transmon qubits on the IBM Quantum processor ibm_torino and the IQM Quantum processor Garnet. The measured population plateaus agree closely with theory and show enhanced robustness compared to the most frequently used dynamical decoupling protocols.

articles.title: BAK and BAX form a multiprotein complex to drive mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death
articles.abstract: The apoptotic regulators BAX and BAK, once activated, form homo-oligomers to trigger mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP), activating the apoptosome and caspases. Activation of BAX-BAK without apoptosome activation triggers sustained efflux of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and caspase-independent cell death. However, the molecular basis of mtDNA efflux remains unclear. We purified a macromolecular complex comprising BAK, BAX, activator BH3-only molecules, voltage-dependent anion channels 1 and 2 (VDAC1 and VDAC2), and prohibitins that released mtDNA from mitoplasts. BAX-BAK activation resulted in VDAC closure, mitochondrial calcium influx, and mtDNA efflux. Loss of VDAC1, VDAC2, or prohibitins prevented BAX-BAK activation–induced mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death without affecting MOMP or mitochondrial inner membrane herniation. These findings support differential regulation of cytochrome c and mtDNA efflux by distinct BAX-BAK complexes.

articles.title: Decoupled self-assembled monolayer and perovskite deposition for efficient flexible solar modules
articles.abstract: The power conversion efficiency (PCE) and stability of flexible perovskite solar modules (PSMs) are less than those of their rigid devices because surface hydroxyls desorption on flexible substrates, which disrupts self-assembled monolayer (SAM) anchoring and perovskite crystallization. We developed a decoupled SAM-perovskite codeposition strategy that accelerates SAM anchoring by reducing the SAM-perovskite interaction and ameliorates perovskite crystallization. The certified PCE with phenethylammonium iodide as the passivation molecule was 20.2% on PSMs with device areas of 750 cm 2 . With 1,3-diaminopropane dihydroiodide as the passivator, the PCE of 22.0% for a device area of 14.55 cm 2 decreased by 8% after 1044 hours under maximum power point tracking at 85°C and 65% relative humidity. The devices pass all sequences of an international commercialization assessment standard for flexible portable PSMs.

articles.title: Dynamic functionality–enabled fast and selective transport in nanochannels
articles.abstract: Nanochannels capable of fast and selective mass transport are central to applications in energy, resources, biomedicine, and the environment. However, extreme nanoscale confinement, often coupled with rigid channel environments, imposes substantial frictional and adhesive barriers, causing sluggish transport and constrained selectivity. We identified nanochannel dynamics as a key to addressing these challenges by harnessing the intrinsic mobility (e.g., self-rotation) of confined functionalities to enhance molecular transport. Through a combination of experiments and simulations, we demonstrated that such dynamics reshape transport by promoting kinetic energy transfer and enabling more efficient molecular relays, thereby improving separation performance beyond current benchmarks. Our findings highlight the role of nanochannel dynamics in regulating mass transport under confinement and provide a framework for designing advanced nanochannel systems.

articles.title: Electronic bound states in the continuum in a two-dimensional metal
articles.abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) are quantum states that remain localized despite lying within a continuum of extended, delocalized states. Whereas optical BICs have been realized in photonic systems, achieving electronic bound states embedded in a metallic background remains an ongoing challenge. In this study, we used scanning tunneling microscopy to identify two defect-induced electronic states that remain localized within the metallic continuum of Pd 5 AlI 2 , a two-dimensional van der Waals metal. Our calculations suggest that electron-hopping interference on the decorated checkerboard lattice of Pd 5 AlI 2 gives rise to a (quasi) flat band built from spatially localized eigenstates that are orthogonal to the dispersive continuum. Atomic defects within this frustrated lattice shift the associated flat-band localized states into the metallic continuum, forming robust, symmetry-protected BICs.

articles.title: Imaging electron-hole asymmetry in the quantum melting of generalized Wigner crystals
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional moiré materials provide a versatile platform to explore phase transitions in strongly correlated systems. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we imaged the density-driven melting of generalized Wigner crystals (GWCs) and Mott insulators (MIs) in electron-doped, near-60°–twisted molybdenum diselenide bilayers featuring a triangular moiré superlattice. We observed notable electron-hole asymmetry in GWC melting: Hole-doped GWCs yielded interaction-driven disordered states, whereas electron-doped GWCs melted into delocalized liquid-like states. This asymmetry arose from the broken particle-hole symmetry of the moiré superlattice, which produced electron and hole Fermi pockets with different momentum geometries upon GWC condensation. MI states melted without such asymmetry, consistent with the absence of a symmetry-breaking density modulation. This work provides direct visualization of the emergent phases that appear as GWCs undergo quantum melting transitions.

Intron retention regulates STAT2 function and associates with immunotherapy response in lung cancer
articles.abstract: Immunotherapy with checkpoint inhibitors has revolutionized cancer therapy and enabled considerable therapeutic advances for treating various diseases, including lung cancer. However, the molecular determinants of variable patient outcomes remain unclear. Using long-read RNA sequencing, we mapped the landscape of alternative RNA splicing in human primary lung adenocarcinomas. We identified more than 149,000 full-length messenger RNA (mRNA) isoforms, more than half of which were unannotated and many that occurred in immune-related genes, particularly within the type I interferon response pathway. We functionally characterized retained introns in the STAT2 gene that produced altered protein isoforms that regulated immune signaling and interferon responses and correlated with patient survival after anti–programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunotherapy. These findings position alternative splicing as a regulator of tumor immune responses and reveal intron retention in STAT2 as an interferon regulatory axis that correlates with PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor response.

articles.title: Late Holocene reexpansion of the Laurentide Ice Sheet
articles.abstract: During interglaciations, the Laurentide Ice Sheet (LIS), which is the largest of the Pleistocene ice sheets, retreats to Arctic Canada, where it achieves a minimum configuration. The reexpansion of the LIS following this minimum marks the start of the next glaciation. Here, we show that the last remaining remnant of the most recent LIS, Barnes Ice Cap (Baffin Island, Canada), achieved its minimum interglacial dimensions after ~3.6 thousand years ago, before reexpanding ~2000 years ago, marking the onset of the next glaciation. The new LIS reached maximum dimensions in ~1960 CE, after which anthropogenic summer warming resulted in a negative mass balance, ice margin recession, and the termination of the next glaciation. The demise of the next glaciation, despite the ongoing decline in summer insolation, illustrates the influence of anomalous greenhouse gas forcing on climate.

Natural product biosynthesis by guanidine prenyltransferases in plants and bacteria
articles.abstract: Guanidine exists almost exclusively as a resonance-stabilized cation, making its direct enzymatic functionalization challenging. We identified the cyanobacterial enzyme NosH, which catalyzes direct prenyl transfer to free guanidine. Structural and mechanistic analyses revealed guanidine activation by a two-aspartate clamp coupled to prenyl-donor binding through a distinct catalytic architecture. Guided by these features, we identified a large family of guanidine prenyltransferases across bacteria and plants. Plant enzymes produced guanidine alkaloids such as galegine in vitro and heterologous expression of a plant ortholog in Nicotiana benthamiana produced galegine in planta, providing a direct enzymatic link to plant-specialized metabolism.

articles.title: Sequential diagnosis with language models
articles.abstract: We explored the capabilities of frontier language models in sequential diagnosis, a diagnostic paradigm that captures the iterative nature of clinical reasoning. Given a brief clinical presentation, clinicians selectively acquired information to reach a diagnosis, enabling assessment of diagnostic accuracy and workup cost. We developed an interactive benchmark and an artificial intelligence (AI) system that simulates a panel of physicians, continually revising the differential diagnosis and selecting cost-effective tests. Using this benchmark, the system achieved 83.2% accuracy on New England Journal of Medicine clinicopathological conference cases and 80.3% on MIMIC-IV-ED emergency department admissions, outperforming generalist physicians (36.1 and 46.8%, respectively). Although these findings were obtained in a controlled benchmark setting, they highlight the promise of language models for supporting more accurate, lower-cost diagnoses.

articles.title: The AI debate is missing half the system
articles.abstract: Last month, leading executives of artificial intelligence (AI) companies warned the United Nations Security Council about the risks of losing human control over this rapidly advancing technology. Their recommendations focused heavily on safeguards, evaluation, and governance of AI models and systems, largely overlooking the risks that arise from the interactions of AI with people and institutions. AI safety needs to be addressed at the level of the human–AI system, not the AI model alone.

articles.title: The Monarch Bear
The Virtual Biotech: A multi-agent AI framework for therapeutic discovery and development
articles.abstract: Drug development requires evidence integration across biological scales and modalities, but relevant tools are fragmented. We introduce the Virtual Biotech, an organization of artificial intelligence (AI) agents modeled on a drug-development company, with agentic divisions spanning target discovery, safety assessment, modality selection, and clinical development. We demonstrate its utility at three drug-development decision points. First, more than 37,000 agents annotated outcomes from 55,984 trials and found that drugs targeting cell type–specific genes were 48% more likely to reach market with 32% fewer adverse events. Second, it integrated multimodal evidence to propose a therapeutic strategy in lung cancer. Third, it analyzed a terminated ulcerative colitis trial and inferred potential mechanisms of failure. These results demonstrate that human-guided multi-agent systems can conduct transparent, multiscale analyses to inform therapeutic-development decisions.

articles.title: Thermodynamic origin of the phonon Hall effect in a honeycomb antiferromagnet
articles.abstract: The underlying mechanism of the thermal Hall effect generated by phonons in a variety of insulators is yet to be identified. In this work, we report on a sizable thermal Hall conductivity in nickel phosphorus trisulfide (NiPS 3 ), a van der Waals stack of honeycomb layers with a zigzag antiferromagnetic order. The longitudinal (κ aa ) and the transverse (κ ab ) thermal conductivities peak at the same temperature, and the thermal Hall angle, at this peak, respects a previously identified bound. The amplitude of κ ab is extremely sensitive to the amplitude of magnetization along the b axis but is not correlated with the phonon mean free path, which points to an intrinsic origin.

articles.title: Ultrarapid decision-making in an avian brain
articles.abstract: Perceptual decision-making is well studied in mammals, but its operation in other vertebrates remains unclear. We show that carrion crows ( Corvus corone ) make deliberate decisions in a classic visual motion discrimination task with unprecedented speed, reporting choices in approximately 235 milliseconds on average, which is roughly twice as fast as has been observed in monkeys or humans and without sacrificing accuracy. Recordings from the pallial endbrain reveal that direction-selective neurons encode the upcoming choice as early as about 70 milliseconds after stimulus onset and about 170 milliseconds before the response, with ramping activity scaling with sensory evidence and converging at response onset. These findings highlight the extraordinary efficiency of avian decision-making circuitry, possibly shaped by evolutionary pressures for rapid visuomotor control.

articles.title: Visualizing symmetry-broken Chern insulators and their quantum melting
articles.abstract: In the presence of a magnetic field, electronic states of moiré quantum materials develop a Hofstadter spectrum that provides a distinctive setting for studying the interplay between band topology and strong electron-electron interaction. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we studied Hofstadter’s states in bilayer graphene aligned with hexagonal boron nitride and directly visualized the formation of interaction-driven symmetry breaking Chern insulators. Our measurements revealed the formation of phases that double, triple, or quadruple the moiré unit cell at fractional filling of the Hofstadter bands as well as states with complex intra–unit cell wave functions. We visualized two distinct quantum phenomena in different Chern states, including quantum melting driven by the appearance and proliferation of topological defects and a quantum transition co-occurring with phase competition and separation.

articles.title: Wireless electrocatalytic closed-loop system for drug-free management of diabesity
articles.abstract: Lifestyle-related type 2 diabetes and associated obesity (diabesity) affect >2.5 billion people worldwide and impose nearly $3 trillion in annual health care costs. We developed an implantable, wirelessly powered electrocatalytic closed-loop health optimization (ECHO) device containing platinum-decorated gold nanoclusters embedded in graphite felt that enabled selective, electrically tunable oxidation of blood glucose to renally cleared gluconate. In type 2 diabetic mice, wireless, low-power activation (0.75 volts, 10 milliamperes) restored glucose homeostasis within 1 hour, shifted metabolism from glucose to lipid utilization, reduced body weight and triglycerides, and increased circulating free fatty acids and ketone bodies without detectable hypoglycemia or adverse physiological, inflammatory, or behavioral effects during 6 weeks of treatment. Coupling this ECHO device to a commercial continuous glucose monitoring system enabled autonomous, smartphone-controlled, drug-free closed-loop management of experimental diabesity.

articles.abstract: A person in France has become the first ever human reported to have been infected with Shamonda virus, health authorities have announced.1Until now, the virus had only ever been detected in non-human animals and was considered by officials to be non-transmissible to humans.What happened in France?Details are limited, but what has been announced is that the patient was already receiving treatment for a serious illness that made them susceptible to infection and complications before being infected with Shamonda and dying earlier this month.Investigations into whether the virus caused or contributed to the patient’s death, and how the patient acquired the infection, are ongoing, said the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC).2What is Shamonda?Shamonda virus is a member of a large group of viruses known as bunyaviruses.3Although it was first identified in Nigerian cattle in the 1960s, Shamonda virus was found in European farm animals for the first time...

articles.title: New strategies for enantioselective synthesis of α-stereogenic ketones
articles.abstract: Enantiopure α-stereogenic ketones constitute prevalent scaffolds in numerous natural products and pharmaceuticals while also serving as versatile and valuable building blocks for diverse synthetic transformations. Conventional methods for constructing chiral α-stereogenic ketones typically rely on the reaction of ketone enolates or enamines with electrophiles. However, the need for strong bases to generate these intermediates often limits the substrate scope. Additionally, achieving stereo- and regioselective formation of enolates or enamines from unsymmetrical dialkyl ketones remains a significant challenge. This review provides an overview of recent advances in the enantioselective synthesis of α-stereogenic ketones, highlighting emerging strategies beyond classical chemistry, such as radical reactions, nucleophilic reactions, acyl–nickel-enabled cross-coupling, and enzyme-catalyzed dehalogenation.

articles.title: Selection-for-prediction: rethinking early cognitive development
articles.abstract: For decades, core knowledge accounts have proposed that early cognition is organized by innate, domain-specific conceptual or concept-like representations of objects, physical events, number, and agents. I propose a different starting point: infants’ behaviors may arise from domain-general attentional priors—evolutionarily shaped selection biases—interacting with perceptual mechanisms that organize information and support perceptual prediction, rather than from abstract, postperceptual representations. Attentional priors favor ecologically consequential information, including continuity, contact, and synchrony. When such information is disrupted, perceptual prediction error—rather than conceptual contradiction—may produce violation-of-expectation effects. Grounded in constraints on visual input and neural processing, this framework accounts for early successes and systematic failures, suggesting that development begins with perceptual-attentional mechanisms that shape selection, organization, prediction, and learning.

articles.title: A Universal Constitutive Relation for Static Droplet Retention
articles.abstract: Under applied forcing, static droplet retention is accompanied by contact angle asymmetry, with unequal apparent contact angles on opposite sides. Yet, the relation between the asymmetry and forcing lacks a common constitutive basis. Here, we show that the asymmetry emerges from minimizing the forcing-dependent free energy. The response of the asymmetry to forcing defines a susceptibility whose zero-forcing value yields a universal constitutive relation between the asymmetry and forcing. The constitutive relation is quantitatively validated across liquids, volumes, and forcing levels.

articles.title: A sharp gradient-corrected Lieb--Thirring inequality in one dimension with applications to density functional theory
articles.abstract: We first prove a sharp Lieb-Thirring inequality with semi-classical constant and gradient correction in one dimension. In the periodic setting, the corresponding inequality also includes a parity dependent shell-correction term, which appears to be new. Moreover, we also characterize the optimizers of these inequalities. In particular, the optimizing density profiles form a two-dimensional manifold, which we call here the Poincaré density manifold. We then apply these results to study the Thomas--Fermi--von Weizsäcker (TFW) approximation of the kinetic energy in Density Functional Theory. More precisely, we first obtain an explicit and non-asymptotic bound on the global and local error made by the TFW approximation. These bounds are controlled by the distance of the normalized density profile from the Poincaré density manifold times the number of particles. In particular, these bounds show that the TFW approximation is exact on the Poincaré manifold. We then show that, in the periodic setting, the distance between the Kohn-Sham potential and the inverse TFW potential in the natural dual Sobolev space can also be controlled by explicit density dependent constants times the distance to the Poincaré manifold. As a corollary, we prove that for a fixed density profile, the Kohn-Sham potential converges towards the inverse Thomas--Fermi potential in the high-density limit $N \rightarrow \infty$ with asymptotic rate of order $N^{-2}$. This rate is shown to be optimal.

articles.title: Multireference Polarizable Embedding for Core-Level Spectroscopy in Aqueous Solution: XPS and XAS of Glycine
articles.abstract: Core-level spectra in solution are governed by the interplay of core-hole relaxation, electron correlation, specific solute--solvent interactions, and environmental polarization. We report the first application of RASSCF--RASPT2 combined with the fluctuating-charges polarizable embedding to X-ray photoelectron (XPS) and X-ray absorption (XAS) spectroscopy in aqueous solution. The protocol couples a multireference treatment of core-ionized and core-excited states with molecular-dynamics sampling, and is assessed for the carbon and nitrogen K-edges of glycine in the gas phase and in water. The calculated spectra are compared with experiment and with fixed-charges electrostatic embedding. Gas-phase ionization and absorption features are accurately reproduced. In solution, configurational averaging captures inhomogeneous broadening, while XPS peak positions, relative intensities, and widths depend strongly on the solvent parametrization. The best-performing polarizable model improves the spectral profile, although aqueous ionization energies remain overestimated. For XAS, the carbon K-edge is reproduced close to the experimental energy scale, whereas the nitrogen K-edge line shape is recovered after rigid alignment. These results support multireference polarizable embedding as a promising framework for core-level spectroscopy in solution.

articles.title: Nonadiabatic vibrational dynamics of CO on Pt(111) studied with first-principles many-body perturbation theory
articles.abstract: We investigate the nonequilibrium vibrational dynamics of CO adsorbed on Pt(111), a prototypical adsorbate-surface system for ultrafast vibrational spectroscopy, using a first-principles framework that combines many-body perturbation theory with density functional theory. Within this methodology we explicitly account for electron-hole pair excitations and electron-mediated phonon-phonon coupling. For the latter mechanism, we evaluate the vertex-correction screening, what constitutes a methodological novelty. Our calculations qualitatively reproduce the transient evolution of the internal stretch vibrational mode observed in femtosecond pump-probe experiments, allowing us to identify in the experimental measurements a small transient blueshift after excitation with a femtosecond laser pulse. As predicted in a previous work, the reduction in the number of electronic states available for electron-phonon coupling when the electronic temperature raises at a group 10 transition metal surface, effectively screens the electron-phonon interaction giving rise to an anomalous transient blue-shift.

articles.title: Precise Determination of Electric Dipole Polarizabilities of Sr Clock States Using Linear-Response and Equation-of-Motion Relativistic Coupled-Cluster Methods
articles.abstract: We present accurate values of the electric dipole polarizabilities ($α$) of the ground and excited states of Sr using four-component relativistic coupled-cluster (RCC) theory within the linear-response (LR) and equation-of-motion (EOM) frameworks. We first investigated accuracy of the ground-state polarizability using the LR-RCC method in both spherical and Cartesian coordinate representations. Upon obtaining consistent results for the ground state, we determine the polarizabilities of the excited states using the EOM-RCC method within the finite-field approach. The uncertainties in our results are assessed by examining the completeness of the basis set, higher-order relativistic corrections, and contributions from higher-level excitation configurations beyond the truncation in our RCC method. We also discuss various procedures for extrapolating contributions to the complete basis set limit and examine their respective limitations. Our calculated ground-state polarizability is found to be inconsistent with the latest atomic calculation, but agrees with other calculations and experimental value. Using the differential $α$ value from the EOM-RCC method, we estimate the fractional black-body-radiation-induced frequency shift of the Sr $^{1}$S$_{0}$$\rightarrow$$^{3}$P$_{0}$ clock transition to be $-5.40\times10^{-15}$.

articles.title: Strain Waves Generate Compression and Trigger Buckling in Active Polymers
articles.abstract: Chemical reactions can sustain polymer motion without necessarily generating the compression required for buckling. Theory and simulations show that tension-dependent chemical transitions coupled to bond elasticity generate finite-wavelength traveling strain waves in a semiflexible polymer. In the straight chain at fixed axial span, the waves reduce mean active contraction while leaving mean elastic tension unchanged, generating compression that drives bending above a threshold. Releasing the mean load allows longitudinal waves to persist while transverse perturbations decay.

articles.title: Strontium Titanate Capping Layers as Kinetic Regulators of Redox Phase Transitions in Oxide Heterostructures
articles.abstract: Oxide capping layers are widely used to protect and stabilize thin-film heterostructures, yet their role in governing phase-transition kinetics remains largely unexplored. Here, we uncover the kinetic function of few-nanometer-thick SrTiO$_3$ (STO) capping layers in controlling oxidation and reduction processes, using real-time in situ optical spectroscopic ellipsometry. We show that oxygen diffusion through the nanoscale capping layer constitutes the rate-limiting step, giving rise to diffusion-controlled phase transitions in the underlying materials. As a result, both capping-layer thickness and oxygen partial pressure provide effective handles to tune phase transition temperatures. Quantitative analysis yields an activation energy of $E_A$ = 0.64 $\pm$0.06 eV for oxygen diffusion through STO, highlighting its suitability for precise control of redox reactions in diverse material systems. These results establish oxide capping layers as active kinetic regulators of redox-driven phase transitions and offer a general framework for engineering redox dynamics in complex oxide heterostructures.

articles.title: Unconstrained learning of equivariant atomistic properties
articles.abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have made first-principles accuracy routine for the potential energy surface (PES). Their backbones, often O(3)-equivariant by design, are increasingly used to learn other atomistic properties. Many of these are of high angular order or pseudotensorial character, defined per atom, or expanded on large atom-centered basis sets. Such targets strain equivariant GNNs, whose tensor products grow steeply in cost with angular order and can fail to represent the target if truncated, forcing difficult trade-offs between hyperparameters. Unconstrained models like the Point-Edge Transformer (PET) instead replace explicit O(3) algebra with edge-to-edge attention and learn equivariance from data, so that the same backbone can in principle learn any equivariant property. We demonstrate how to use PET to learn molecular dipoles and polarizabilities, NMR chemical shielding tensors, and auxiliary-basis expansions of the electron density. Increasing the backbone size systematically improves both accuracy and equivariance error, and targeted architectural and training choices reduce the symmetry breaking further. PET matches or improves on the released reference models at lower inference cost and, compared with equivariant models, a smaller memory footprint. The predictions give accurate IR and Raman spectra and isotropic shieldings; the predicted densities accelerate self-consistent field calculations and give one-shot ground-state properties, and pretrained density models transfer to higher levels of theory by fine-tuning on little data. The impact of approximate equivariance is small for most observables, further validating this approach to train fast, accurate, and useful surrogate models for properties beyond the PES.

articles.title: Unifying Time-Independent and Time-Dependent Franck--Condon Pictures in Quantum Mechanochemistry via the Linear Coupling Approximation
articles.abstract: Quantum chemistry has achieved impressive results in modeling and interpreting mechanochemical transformations at the molecular level. An essential question, the time profile of force application, has however attracted less attention. Here, the Franck--Condon theory of quantum mechanochemistry, previously formulated for the sudden-force limit, is generalized to arbitrary time-dependent force profiles using the linear-coupling approximation. Solving the driven harmonic oscillator yields a closed-form, time-dependent effective Huang--Rhys factor: a natural measure of vibrational excitations upon force application. It is governed by the Fourier transform of the force derivative and recovers the sudden- and fixed-force limits. At the conceptual level, this linear coupling picture links mechanochemistry to vibronic spectroscopy and Marcus electron theory. For a shock-front force ramp, vibrational excitation is shown to be suppressed in frequency, only low-frequency modes being excited under realistic laser-shock-peening conditions.

articles.title: Wavenumber-Aware Deep Learning for Robust Analysis of Raman Spectra
articles.abstract: Machine-learning models for spectroscopy usually treat a spectrum as a fixed-grid intensity vector, leaving the physical coordinate implicit in the array index. Such models are tied to a single sampling grid, spectral range and resolution, which limits their use when measurement conditions change. Here we represent each spectral point as a pair of intensity and wavenumber and compute Transformer positional encodings from the wavenumber itself. On Raman spectra of three bacterial species and their synthetic mixtures, this representation remained robust to noise, sparser sampling and partial spectral coverage across convolutional, residual and Transformer networks. In controlled comparisons, wavenumber-based encoding outperformed index-based and learned encodings under partial observation and retained its performance on sampling grids never seen during training, where index-based encoding degraded. These findings were reproduced on a public 30-isolate bacterial benchmark. Explicit physical coordinates offer a simple route to robust spectral analysis under variable measurement conditions.

articles.title: A hormonal message for a longer life
articles.abstract: The steroid hormone dafachronic acid may carry the effects of reduced mTOR activity between tissues to coordinate metabolism and longevity across the body.

articles.title: Motor unit mechanisms of speed control in mouse locomotion
articles.abstract: During locomotion, the coordinated activity of dozens of muscles shapes the kinematic features of each stride, including systematic changes in limb movement across walking speed. Motor units, each of which consists of a single motor neuron and the muscle fibers it innervates, contribute to the total activation of each muscle through their recruitment and firing rate when active. However, it remains unknown how the nervous system controls locomotor speed by changing the firing of individual motor units. To address this, we combined quantitative behavioral analysis of mouse locomotion with single motor unit recordings from the lateral and long heads of the triceps brachii, which drive monoarticular extension of the elbow and biarticular movements of the elbow and shoulder, respectively. In contrast to prior studies employing bulk electromyography (EMG) to examine muscle activity, our recordings revealed the diversity of spike patterning across motor units, as well as systematic differences in motor unit activity across muscles and locomotor speeds. First, motor unit activity differed significantly across the lateral and long heads, suggesting differential control of these two closely apposed elbow extensor muscles. Second, we found that individual units were recruited probabilistically (during only a subset of strides), showing that the highly repeatable bulk EMG signals observed across strides, in fact, reflect varying subsets of individual motor units. Finally, although recruitment probability and firing rate both increased at faster walking speeds, increases in recruitment were proportionally larger than rate changes, and recruitment of individual units accompanied changes in limb kinematics. Together, these results reveal how the firing of individual motor units varies systematically across muscles and walking speeds to produce flexible locomotor behavior.

articles.title: Olfactory combinatorial coding supports risk–reward decision-making in Caenorhabditis elegans
articles.abstract: Olfactory-driven behaviors are essential for animal survival, but mechanisms for decoding olfactory inputs remain poorly understood. We have used whole-network Ca2+ imaging to study olfactory coding in Caenorhabditis elegans. We show that the odorant 1-octanol is encoded combinatorially in the periphery as both an attractant and a repellent. These inputs are integrated centrally, and their relative strengths determine the sensitivity and valence of the behavioral response through modulation of locomotory reversals and speed. The balance of these pathways also dictates the activity of the locomotory command interneurons, which control locomotory reversals. This balance serves as a regulatory node for response modulation, allowing C. elegans to weigh opportunities and hazards in its environment when formulating behavioral responses. Thus, an odorant can be encoded simultaneously as inputs of opposite valence, focusing attention on the integration of these inputs in determining perception, response, and plasticity.

articles.title: Copper-Mediated Valence Tautomerism Enables α -C(sp3)–H Alkylation of 1,3-Dicarbonyl Compounds and Tryptophans via Photocatalysis
articles.abstract: Carbonyl α-C(sp3)–H functionalization is a key approach to access functionalized pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and bioactive peptides. Conventional two-electron enol tautomerization strategies for this transformation often suffer from harsh reaction conditions and limited substrate tolerance. While valence tautomerism (VT) enables radical-type C–H activation, such reactivity has been exclusively realized with nickel catalysis, and copper-mediated VT remains unexplored for α-C(sp3)–H activation of carbonyls. Here, we present a dual photoredox/copper catalytic strategy that exploits copper-mediated VT to generate α-carbonyl alkyl radicals. These radicals undergo radical–radical cross-coupling with nucleophilic radicals generated by photocatalytic decarboxylation, delivering α-carbonyl alkylation products. The protocol features mild conditions and broad functional group tolerance, supporting peptide late-stage modification and gram-scale synthesis. Mechanistic studies and density functional theory (DFT) calculations validate a Cu(III)-mediated VT pathway for radical generation. This work establishes copper as a viable VT catalytic platform, expands the scope of dual photoredox/metal catalysis, and offers a versatile tool for biomolecular derivatization.

articles.title: Liquid Gallium Nanoislands on Zeolite: A Dynamic Confinement Strategy to Break the Catalytic Trade-Off in Hydrodeoxygenation
articles.abstract: Breaking the pervasive activity–selectivity–stability trade-off in catalytic hydrodeoxygenation (HDO) remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a bifunctional nanoisland catalyst (GaNPs-Pt/Beta) that overcomes this limitation by utilizing liquid gallium nanodroplets anchored on Beta zeolite as mobile nanoislands. These islands effectively restrict platinum single-atom migration and agglomeration. Concurrently, Brønsted acid sites provided by the zeolite sea facilitate the dehydration-etherification process. This synergy enables highly efficient transfer hydrogenation at the gallium–platinum interface, achieving selective C–O bond cleavage while preserving C═C bonds under mild conditions. Benefiting from this island-sea architecture, the GaNPs-Pt/Beta catalyst delivers high catalytic activity, achieving >99% cinnamyl alcohol conversion and 93.8% β-methylstyrene selectivity within 6 h at 160 °C, with recyclability demonstrated over nine cycles involving intercycle regeneration. This strategy is scalable to diverse α,β-unsaturated aldehyde/alcohol chemicals, demonstrating that zeolite-based liquid metal nanoislands provide a versatile platform for the sustainable synthesis of high-value chemicals.

articles.title: Nickel-Catalyzed Regiodivergent and Enantioselective Hydrosilylation of Internal Alkenes
articles.abstract: Enantioselective hydrosilylation of alkenes represents a direct and economical route to chiral organosilanes. However, achieving good regio- and enantioselectivity from the same alkene for the divergent synthesis of chiral silanes remains a formidable challenge, particularly for internal alkenes. In this work, we present a ligand-controlled nickel-catalyzed regiodivergent and enantioselective hydrosilylation of 1,2-disubstituted alkenes. This approach provides a direct access to both α- and β-trifluoromethylsilanes with high regio- and enantioselectivity. The resulting enantioenriched silane products are amenable to various stereospecific transformations. Moreover, density functional theory (DFT) calculations elucidate the origin of the observed regio- and enantioselectivity.

articles.title: Photoinduced Enantioselective α-Alkylation of Active Methines with Nonactivated Alkenes Using a Chiral Ytterbium Lewis Acid
articles.abstract: Catalytic enantioselective alkylation is a fundamental strategy for constructing molecular frameworks bearing chiral carbon centers. Herein, we report a photoinduced highly enantioselective catalytic α-alkylation of active methine compounds with nonactivated alkenes to construct chiral quaternary stereocenters. Cooperative catalysis using an organophotocatalyst and a chiral ytterbium Lewis acid bearing an Indapybox ligand efficiently promotes the alkylation of open-chain 2-substituted β-ketoesters, affording the desired products in high yields with high enantioselectivities (up to 96% yield and 96% ee). The reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope with respect to both the alkene and β-ketoesters components. Furthermore, the resulting products can be readily transformed into optically active 5-pyrazolone and 5-isoxazolone derivatives while maintaining high optical purity.

articles.title: Poly(Ionic Liquid)-Engineered Interfacial Water Reorganization for Selective Acidic CO2-to-Formic Acid Electroreduction
articles.abstract: Acidic CO2 electroreduction offers a promising route to improve carbon utilization compared with alkaline or neutral systems. However, maintaining high product selectivity at industrially relevant current densities remains challenging because local CO2 depletion and excessive proton availability intensify the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Herein, we develop a bismuth sulfide (Bi2S3) catalyst modified with a long-chain imidazolium poly(ionic liquid) layer (PIL@BS) for electrocatalytic CO2-to-formic acid conversion at pH 2. In a flow cell containing 3 M KCl, PIL@BS catalyst delivers a high Faradaic efficiency for formic acid (FEFA = 98.4%) at a current density exceeding 300 mA cm–2 and maintains over 80% FEFA after 120 h of continuous operation. Even at low 15 vol % CO2 concentration typical of industrial flue gas, PIL@BS retains higher FA selectivity than unmodified BS, underscoring the effectiveness of PIL in suppressing HER under CO2-limited conditions. Structural characterizations and electrochemical analyses reveal that the PIL backbone creates a hydrophobic interface while preserving CO2 affinity and high ionic conductivity, effectively mitigating the flooding issues and enhancing the local availability of CO2. Operando spectroscopies further show that PIL-regulated interface facilitates access to weakly hydrogen-bonded water. Such interfacial water reorganization disrupts the extended hydrogen-bond network, attenuating the continuous proton-relay pathways that promote the competing HER while maintaining localized proton transfer for CO2 reduction. Combined with theoretical calculations, these findings indicate that the PIL-modified microenvironment enables a direct and energetically favorable hydrogenation pathway toward FA formation. This work highlights the PIL-engineered interfacial microenvironment as a key factor for overriding the intrinsic selectivity of a catalyst and enabling practical CO2 valorization.

articles.title: SIFT-MS Enables Product-Specific Insight into Electrochemical Pulsed CO2 Reduction in Membrane Electrode Assemblies
articles.abstract: Pulsed electrolysis is a promising operating strategy for electrochemical CO2 reduction, but understanding how products form, accumulate, and are released during dynamic operation remains challenging, particularly in membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs). Conventional product analysis methods provide limited time resolution, making them poorly suited for resolving product-specific changes during pulses that are on the timescale of seconds. Here, selected-ion-flow-tube mass spectrometry (SIFT-MS) was used as a quasi-real-time analytical technique to measure the product concentrations during pulsed CO2 electrolysis in a MEA using a copper oxide nanoparticle-derived cathode catalyst. Methodology development for the SIFT-MS technique established the sampling and pulsing criteria required for reliable semi-quantitative analysis of the concentration of reaction products. Applying these methodology developments to pulsed electrolysis experiments unveiled how molecular structure influences product retention within the electrode and subsequent transport into the MEA outlet stream under pulsed CO2R conditions. A comparison of the measured concentrations of ethanol, ethylene, and acetaldehyde provided evidence that the formation of ethanol occurs through multiple contributing reaction pathways. The analysis of the measured concentrations of acetaldehyde, propionaldehyde, and 1-propanol provided evidence for the sequential formation of products through which the formation of aldehydes precedes the formation of 1-propanol. Overall, this work establishes SIFT-MS as a product-specific, quasi-real-time analytical technique for probing pulsed CO2R in membrane electrode assemblies that can unveil crucial information to aid in the development of future MEA electrolyzers and operational strategies.

articles.title: Spatially Decoupled Reaction-Diffusion Microenvironments in Mordenite Enable Highly Selective Methane-to-Methanol Conversion
articles.abstract: The selective oxidation of methane to value-added oxygenates represents a formidable challenge in heterogeneous catalysis, fundamentally limited by the thermodynamic trade-off between activating the reactant and preventing the subsequent overoxidation of fragile products. This vulnerability is deeply tied to the spatial accessibility within the catalytic microenvironment; highly open channels, while facilitating mass transfer, indiscriminately expose the generated products to secondary oxidation. Herein, we develop a site-selective construction strategy to establish spatially decoupled reaction-diffusion microenvironments within mordenite (MOR). By utilizing pyridine as a pore-blocking agent to occupy 12-membered ring (12-MR) channels, we preferentially localize the active Cu species, identified as bent mono-μ-oxo dicopper cores, within the well-defined 8-membered ring (8-MR) side pockets. This architecture induces a profound dual spatial effect. At the reaction level, the 8-MR acts as a nanoscopic kinetic shield by providing a customized local topology that suppresses the reactivity of oxygenated intermediates while retaining sufficient methane activation capability. Crucially, at the mass-transfer level, Cu incorporation into the 12-MR main channels is largely suppressed, allowing these channels to serve as unobstructed diffusion pathways and reducing the probability that desorbed methanol recontacts oxidative Cu sites during outward transport. Furthermore, by eliminating the structural heterogeneity inherent to non-selective synthesis, this spatially defined microenvironment and homogeneous Cu coordination structure enable the elucidation of the intrinsic structure-performance relationship. Under continuous operating conditions, this spatially engineered catalyst exhibits high methanol selectivity and productivity, ranking among the leading Cu-MOR systems for methane-to-methanol conversion. These findings demonstrate that designing a decoupled reaction-diffusion microenvironment can regulate catalytic selectivity beyond electronic-structure modulation, while also offering a generalizable method for the site-selective placement of metal ions within zeolite.

articles.title: Cesium-Triiodide-Mediated Crystallization Regulation of Pure-Iodide Wide-Bandgap Perovskites Enables Perovskite-Silicon Tandem Solar Cells Exceeding 30% Efficiency
articles.abstract: Pure-iodide wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskites (∼1.68 eV) featuring eliminated photoinduced halide segregation are compelling top-cell absorbers for perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells. However, their complex crystallization readily induces heterogeneous composition and structural defects, hindering performance improvements in the resulting devices. Here, we develop a cesium triiodide (CsI3)-mediated strategy to regulate intermediate-phase evolution of pure-iodide WBG perovskites. The CsI3-derived precursor chemistry reconstructs Pb-I coordination networks, suppresses premature organic-dominated intermediate nucleation, and promotes homogeneous phase conversion. The modulated crystallization pathway yields highly crystalline films with improved iodine uniformity and reduced non-radiative recombination losses. Consequently, single-junction solar cells achieve a stabilized power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 22.40%, which retains 95% of its initial efficiency after 1500 h of maximum power point tracking. More importantly, the associated perovskite-silicon solar cells deliver a stabilized PCE of 30.74% along with improved thermal stability, highlighting the great potential of pure-iodide WBG perovskites for efficient and durable tandem photovoltaics.

articles.title: Electrically Enabled Isothermal CeO2 Thermochemical Water Splitting below 900 °C
articles.abstract: Ceria-based thermochemical cycles offer a promising route to solar hydrogen, but require reduction above 1400 °C and large temperature swings. Here, building on electrically assisted CeO2 reduction, we demonstrate repeated isothermal CeO2-based water-splitting cycles at 700–900 °C and 0.5–2.0 V. Porous CeO2−YSZ bilayer pellets with different composition ratios undergo electrically assisted reduction and steam re-oxidation at the same temperature, producing O2 and H2 in separate steps without thermal cycling. The process reaches H2/O2 ratios up to 1.9, reproducible H2 productivity over 10 cycles, and H2 yields up to 49 ± 2 μmol gCeO2−1 cycle−1 after only 20 min of electrically assisted reduction. Extended-reduction experiments show that the best composition remains only ∼0.10 V below the applied bias on an equivalent thermodynamic-voltage basis. Reactor-scale projections based on gas utilization in an existing ceria reactor give a solar-to-H2 efficiency of 5.6% without assuming improvements to the CeO2−YSZ architecture.

articles.title: Rational Ionomer Design Directs Hydrogenation Pathways and Reactant Accessibility in Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction
articles.abstract: Ionomer engineering offers a powerful yet underexplored strategy for electrochemical nitrate reduction (NO3RR), since the polymer tailors the microenvironment at the catalyst surface. Here, we rationally design high-performance ionomers by applying fixed-charge sign and hydration as design criteria. Synthetic anion-exchange ionomers (AEIs) enhance NO3– accessibility, and the highest AEI hydration is accompanied by a shift in the dominant hydrogenation pathway toward a favorable *H-mediated regime. Time-dependent attenuated total reflection surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) coupled with numerical simulation yields a 40.7-fold higher NO3– diffusion coefficient for the AEI than for Nafion. Potential-dependent in situ ATR-SEIRAS combined with kinetic isotope effect measurements and *H scavenging supports a pathway shift arising from a hydrated microenvironment enriched in free and weakly hydrogen-bonded water. The AEI-modified commercial Cu nanoparticle electrode reaches an NH3 yield rate of 13.8 mg h–1cm–2 and 98.0% Faradaic efficiency, positioning the fixed-charge sign and hydration as accessible design descriptors potentially transferable to other electrocatalytic reactions.

articles.title: Chloride-mediated protective bilayer film on magnesium
Intragranular discontinuous precipitation enables exceptional strength and ductility in an additively manufactured high-entropy alloy
Synergistic enhancement of high-temperature strength and uniform plasticity in a Ti-rich refractory high-entropy alloy via strain-rate-modulated dislocation-B2 interactions
Tellurium trioxide as an n-type wide-gap semiconductor with ultrahigh work functions from first principles
A Paradigm Shift Toward Quasi‐Thermodynamically Stable Bulk Heterojunction Morphology Enabled by Controlled Crystallization Kinetics of High Quadrupole Moment Nonfullerene Acceptors
articles.abstract: Recent advances in high quadrupole moment (Q̂$\hat{Q}$) non‐fullerene acceptors (NFAs) have improved exciton diffusion and charge separation in organic photovoltaics (OPVs). However, conventional bulk heterojunctions (BHJs) with a balanced donor‐to‐acceptor ratio often exhibit amorphous mixed domains, introducing energetic disorder and limiting the optoelectronic potential and stability of high‐Q̂$\hat{Q}$ NFAs. Here, a diffusion‐driven 3D crystallization strategy is demonstrated using an NFA‐rich BHJ model (Non‐fullerene Matrix‐BHJ, NM‐BHJ) that suppresses electron trap states and charge localization, thereby reducing energy losses driven by static disorder. Notably, the laterally oriented 3D superstructures significantly enhance thermodynamic stability and improve resistance to morphological changes under thermal stress. OPVs incorporating the optimized NM‐BHJ retain 88.2% of their initial efficiency after 720 h at 65 °C and over 99% after 2400 h at room‐temperature. The obtained T90 of 644 h is, to the best of our knowledge, one of the longest experimentally verified lifetimes reported among Y‐series‐based BHJ systems in the literature, including those employing chemically modified oligomeric derivatives. Combined with its generality across different NFA systems, this study suggests that the NM‐BHJ strategy opens a new era for highly efficient and thermally robust OPV devices by morphologically overcoming the inherent thermal limitations of high‐Q̂$\hat{Q}$ NFAs.

articles.title: Advanced Energy Materials at 15: Advancing the Energy Transition From Fundamental Insights to Practical Technologies
articles.abstract: This Special Issue commemorates the fifteenth anniversary of Advanced Energy Materials and reflects the evolution of energy materials research from fundamental discovery toward practical technologies. Assembled in conjunction with the 2025 Wiley Forum Spring Meeting, the collection brings together 28 Research Articles and 10 Reviews spanning photovoltaics and optoelectronics, electrochemical energy storage and conversion, flexible and distributed energy technologies, and data‐driven materials discovery. Collectively, these contributions demonstrate how advances in materials chemistry, defect and interface control, multiscale characterization, scalable manufacturing, and predictive computation are enabling more efficient, stable, and deployable energy systems. The breadth of the collection underscores the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration and of evaluating innovations under realistic technological constraints. The Special Issue is dedicated to the memory of Professor Taiho Park, whose scientific vision, leadership, and service left a lasting legacy in the field. Sincere appreciation is extended to all contributing authors, reviewers, and the editorial team whose efforts made this anniversary collection possible.

articles.title: Alcohol‐Adduct Mediated Precursor Stabilization Strategies for Conformal SnO2 Layers in Highly Efficient and Stable Perovskite Solar Modules
articles.abstract: Perovskite solar modules (PSMs) attract significant attention for their superior optoelectronic properties, but significant cell‐to‐module (CTM) losses remain a critical issue to be addressed. Among the various factors, the primary reason for CTM losses is the incomplete, non‐conformal coverage of the electron transport layer (ETL) over large‐area, P1‐scribed transparent conductive oxide (TCO) substrates. In this work, we report an alcohol‐adduct mediated precursor stabilization strategy to achieve high‐quality, uniform SnO2 layers via controlled hydrolysis reaction kinetics. We employ a tin isopropoxide isopropanol (TIPI) adduct, which effectively modulates the electrophilicity and stabilizes the Sn center atom, followed by a sequential deposition of SnO2 nanoparticles. This double‐layer (DL) architecture exhibits superior optical properties, improved electron transport, and conformal coverage over large areas. As a result, PSMs fabricated with the TIPI (DL) SnO2 ETL exhibit a maximum power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.6% (reverse/forward average), with a certified PCE of 19.7% (aperture area = 213 cm2). In addition, the PSMs with TIPI (DL) SnO2 ETL demonstrated a wide processing window, maintaining a PCE over 20% regardless of variations in concentration or deposition speed, highlighting potential for in‐line commercialization. Furthermore, the modules exhibited good long‐term stability under damp‐heat and in outdoor field tests.

articles.title: Amorphous π‐Conjugated Passivator Facilitates Widening Process Window for Reliable Perovskite Solar Modules
articles.abstract: Although halide perovskite solar cells have achieved remarkable efficiencies close to their theoretical limits, durability against external factors and reproducible processing remain major barriers to commercialization. Conventional ammonium halide‐based surface passivation strategies enable effective defect passivation and charge selectivity via 2D/3D heterostructure formation, but their metastability and strong sensitivity to processing conditions limit long‐term stability and process window. In this work, we report an amorphous π‐conjugated passivator, (4‐(3‐iodo‐9H‐carbazol‐9‐yl)butyl)phosphonic acid (I–4PACz). The asymmetric iodine substituent enhances the molecular dipole moment while simultaneously altering intermolecular interactions, thereby suppressing ordered molecular packing and enabling the formation of a uniform interfacial layer. The characteristics of I‐4PACz result in efficient charge extraction as well as widening process window. Perovskite solar modules applied to I‐4PACz as passivator between the perovskite and hole transport‐layer show a power conversion efficiency of 21.2% with 24.5 cm2 aperture size, and excellent long‐term stability retaining 85% of the initial efficiency for 884 h under 65°C and 40% relative humidity, and 98.7% of the initial efficiency for 525 h under continous illumination, respectively. Moreover, the minial dependence on blade‐coating speed also reinforces the suitability of this interfacial control strategy for inline and large‐area manufacturing.

articles.title: Amorphous π‐Conjugated Passivator Facilitates Widening Process Window for Reliable Perovskite Solar Modules (Adv. Energy Mater. 39/2026)
articles.abstract: Perovskite Solar Modules In article number e06809, Jaemin Lee, Nam Joong Jeon, Eui Hyuk Jung, and co‐workers demonstrate that an amorphous p‐conjugated passivator enhances performance and improves durability in perovskite solar modules. Treatment of the perovskite surface with the passivator renders a broader processing window to fabricate scalable perovskite solar modules due to diminishing thickness sensitivity.

articles.title: Anisotropic Strain‐Induced Centrosymmetry Breaking in Cubic Formamidinium Lead Iodide (α‐FAPbI3) Thin Films
articles.abstract: Organic–inorganic halide perovskites have emerged as promising materials for next‐generation optoelectronic devices due to their exceptional photophysical properties. Among them, α‐formamidinium lead tri‐iodide (α‐FAPbI3) with a cubic symmetry (space group of Pm3¯m$Pm\bar{3}m$) has garnered attention as a potential absorber in solar cells for its narrow bandgap and superior stability. The fundamental mechanisms governing its high performance have yet to be fully elucidated. In this study, we demonstrate that centrosymmetry breaking in [001] preferentially oriented α‐FAPbI3 thin films (POF) arises from inevitable anisotropic strain during film formation. Using circular polarization‐dependent pump‐probe transient absorption spectroscopy, we observe Rashba‐type band splitting exclusively in POF, indicating symmetry breaking. Angle‐dependent X‐ray diffraction and photoluminescence (PL) reveal significant residual stress in POF compared to randomly oriented films (ROF), confirming strain‐induced lattice distortion. Furthermore, time‐resolved PL and microwave conductivity measurements reveal top‐back inhomogeneous carrier dynamics and anisotropic charge carrier mobility, supporting the presence of the anisotropic strain‐induced symmetry breaking. Our findings provide direct experimental evidence that inevitable strain in POF induces static Rashba effects, offering new insights into strain engineering for high‐performance perovskite optoelectronics and potential quantum applications.

articles.title: Decoupling Chemical and Mechanical Contributions to Capacity Fading in Ni‐Rich Cathodes for Sulfide‐Based All‐Solid‐State Batteries
articles.abstract: All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) promise safer energy storage and the potential to outperform current lithium-ion batteries. Ni-rich cathodes deliver high energy density, whereas sulfide solid electrolytes offer exceptional Li+ conductivity and inherent mechanical compliance, making their combination particularly attractive. Yet their capacity fades rapidly because (electro)chemical and mechanical degradation occur concurrently within the cathode. Here, we propose an approach to decouple these two factors in LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2|Li6PS5Cl0.5Br0.5|Li metal cells by monitoring the state-of-charge window. Uncoated cathodes experience capacity fading primarily due to (electro)chemical degradation: interfacial reactions form resistive interphases consisting of NiO-like rock salt, SO x , PO x , and related species that hinder Li+ extraction, resulting in pronounced charge fading. A conformal LiNbO3 coating on the cathode surface suppresses interfacial reactions, significantly mitigating charge fading but revealing dominant discharge fading arising from mechanical degradation, such as particle cracking and interfacial delamination. While the protective coating stabilizes the interface and improves initial performance, the increased capacity intensifies electrode volume changes, underscoring the need for integrated electro-chemo-mechanical design strategies. Evaluating charge and discharge fading outlines the interplay between (electro)chemical and mechanical degradation and offers a new diagnostic framework to guide the development of more durable, high-energy-density ASSBs.

articles.title: Decoupling Framework and Composition Engineering via Sequential Selenium Source Switching for Efficient Sb2(S,Se)3 Thin Film Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Antimony selenosulfide (Sb2(S,Se)3) has recently attracted intense interest as an earth‐abundant, non‐toxic, and bandgap‐tunable photovoltaic absorber. However, conventional one‐step deposition routes typically produce films with inadequate crystallinity and inhomogeneous elemental distribution through the film thickness, which severely hamper charge transport and limit device performance. Herein, we introduce an innovative selenium‐source switching driven two‐step sequential deposition (SDE) strategy that decouples framework formation from compositional engineering to overcome these limitations. First, a selenourea‐based precursor is used to deposit a thick Sb2(S,Se)3 film serving as a primary light‐harvesting scaffold. Then, a sodium selenosulfate‐based precursor solution is applied for secondary deposition. Owing to the high reactivity of this solution system, selenium species readily penetrate into the as‐deposited film, inducing extensive ion diffusion and recrystallization throughout the bulk Sb2(S,Se)3 material. This SDE strategy simultaneously optimizes the vertical Se/S grading, tailors the bandgap profile, and eliminates bulk deep‐level traps and surface recombination centers. Consequently, the SDE‐Sb2(S,Se)3 device achieves a remarkable efficiency of 10.90%, placing it among the highest efficiencies for this material system. This strategy not only resolves the intrinsic bottlenecks of one‐step techniques but also provides a generalizable route for synthesizing high‐quality multicomponent chalcogenide films and offers new insights into ion‐exchange kinetics during sequential deposition.

articles.title: Degradation Pathways of Silicon‐Based Anodes in Lithium‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Silicon offers high theoretical capacity as an alternative to graphite, yet it undergoes much more severe degradation, resulting in substantially poorer cycle and calendar life. In this context, a mechanistic understanding of degradation pathways is essential for designing silicon‐based anodes with performance comparable to graphite. In this review, we present a comprehensive overview of the degradation mechanisms governing silicon‐based anodes. The mechanisms are organized around active materials degradation at the particle level, which is governed by both intrinsic factors of silicon and extrinsic factors. At the electrode scale, we discuss electrode integrity loss, which arises from the breakdown of mechanical and electrical continuity.
