articles.title: Lithology influences soil microbial functional potential in subtropical forests
articles.abstract: Lithology shapes the Earth’s critical zone, yet its influence on microbial genomic potential in subtropical forests remains unclear. Here, we quantified soil carbon (C), nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and sulfur (S) cycling functional genes across three contrasting lithologies in southwest China using HT-qPCR. We found limestone soils consistently harbored significantly higher gene abundances than dolostone and clasolite soils. Random forest models explained a substantial proportion of the variation in functional gene pools ( R 2 = 0.87–0.92). Based on these identified key drivers, we propose a Nitrogen availability–Microbial resource limitation–Reactive minerals (NMR) framework, where total dissolved nitrogen fuels activity, eco-enzymatic stoichiometry reflects metabolic adaptation, and iron/aluminum oxides regulate substrate accessibility via physical protection. Overall, specific carbonate rock types should be differentiated when modeling biogeochemical cycles.

articles.title: Multi-method non-parametric assessment of river water-quality trends and change-points in the Danshui River basin, metropolitan Taipei (2010–2026)
articles.abstract: The Danshui River drains metropolitan Taipei, where two decades of expanding sewer connection and riparian constructed wetlands have targeted river pollution. Using a continuous monthly record of 1,921 samples from 11 Ministry of Environment stations (2010–2026), we assessed trends and change-points in six measured water-quality variables and the River Pollution Index (RPI), a composite index calculated from four of them, through a multi-method non-parametric design: the Mann–Kendall and seasonal Mann–Kendall tests, a variance-corrected modified test, Theil–Sen slopes, the Pettitt and sequential-Mann–Kendall change-point tests, Innovative Trend Analysis, and a synchronized-permutation Monte Carlo test of field significance. Suspended solids, ammonia, and five-day biochemical oxygen demand declined at 9, 8, and 6 of 11 stations, each field-significant (Monte Carlo p ≤ 0.006); the basin-mean River Pollution Index fell from 3.83 to 3.20 and the severely polluted sample fraction from 11.1% to 2.5% between the early (2010–2012) and late (2023–2025) sub-periods, the incomplete 2026 record excluded. These declines persisted on the 8 complete-record stations, so they are not an artifact of network turnover. Dissolved oxygen did not improve, even as water temperature rose significantly (+0.15 °C yr - ¹), so oxygen conditions merely held against a warming that lowers solubility. Against this improvement, the coliform group rose at most stations, its change-points scattered across 2013–2024 rather than forming a single step; the largest treatment plant’s effluent-coliform log-removal collapsed after 2024, and river coliform was not associated with rainfall, implicating under-disinfected point-source effluent. The basin’s management priority has shifted from organic and nutrient control toward microbial risk and disinfection.

articles.title: Dryland Soil Rewetting Induces Strong Volatile Organic Compound Emissions With Potential to Form Ozone and Aerosols
articles.abstract: Drylands cover nearly half of Earth's terrestrial surface and are expanding under climate change. Biogenic volatile organic compounds (VOCs) significantly influence atmospheric chemistry, yet microbial VOC emissions from dryland soils remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate VOC emissions associated with petrichor—the characteristic scent following rainfall after prolonged drought—across a steep aridity gradient extending into the Negev Desert. Soil rewetting triggered strong VOC fluxes (1–3.5 nmol m−2 s−1 ground area) dominated by sesquiterpenes and benzenoids, with emission patterns and rates linked to climatic regions, soil aridity, and microbial community composition. Petrichor consisted of a complex bouquet of 58 VOCs, and emission fluxes showed a pronounced initial burst. We upscaled the results to Israel and show that petrichor emissions contribute significantly to ozone and secondary organic aerosol formation potentials, comparable in magnitude to those estimated for anthropogenic VOC sources. Soil aridity shaped VOC chemical composition and emission dynamics, indicating strong microbial and environmental controls on the fluxes. As climate change alters precipitation regimes and promotes dryland expansion, these rainfall‐driven bursts of microbial VOCs may represent an overlooked climate‐microbe feedback influencing atmospheric chemistry and radiative forcing at regional and global scales.

articles.title: Context‐dependent unimodal relationships between ectomycorrhizal dominance and tree species diversity in forest ecosystems
articles.abstract: Our study demonstrates that maintaining an asymmetrically mixed mycorrhizal strategy is critical for maximizing forest tree species diversity, rather than dominance by a single type, particularly for diversity metrics emphasizing common species under water‐ and nutrient‐limited or disturbed conditions. This finding advances our understanding of below‐ground symbiosis regulation on forest diversity, which provides a predictive framework for forest management and diversity conservation. Abstract Most trees form mycorrhizal associations with soil fungi, which regulate tree nutrient acquisition and species coexistence. The ectomycorrhizal (EcM) dominance hypothesis predicts that tree species richness decreases with increasing EcM dominance due to positive plant–soil feedback, whereas the mixed mycorrhizal hypothesis suggests that forests with mixed mycorrhizal strategies sustain more species through nutrient complementarity. In fact, the two mechanisms are not mutually exclusive but act jointly to shape diversity as predicted by the asymmetrical unimodal hypothesis. Although this hypothesis has been shown to underlie forest species richness at global scales, whether it consistently favours diversity metrics that differentiate between rare and common species, and how this relationship varies with climate, soil properties and disturbance intensity, remain poorly understood. Using an extensive inventory encompassing 1133 plots in China, we examined the relationships between EcM tree dominance and Hill number‐based diversity metrics. Our results consistently exhibited asymmetrical unimodal relationships, with peak diversity occurring at intermediate EcM dominance (30%–31%), providing robust support for the asymmetrical unimodal relationship hypothesis. Notably, Shannon and Simpson diversities emphasizing common species (i.e. q = 1, 2) showed stronger responses to changes in EcM dominance than species richness (q = 0), a metric more sensitive to rare species. Importantly, these relationships were context‐dependent, being significantly stronger under conditions of lower precipitation and soil nitrogen availability and higher disturbance level. Synthesis. Our study demonstrates that maintaining an asymmetrically mixed mycorrhizal strategy is critical for maximizing forest tree species diversity, rather than dominance by a single type, particularly for diversity metrics emphasizing common species under water‐ and nutrient‐limited or disturbed conditions. This finding advances our understanding of the role of below‐ground symbiosis in regulating forest diversity and provides a predictive framework for forest management and diversity conservation.

articles.title: Functional traits modulate nitrogen addition and climate impacts on growth–mortality trade‐offs in a temperate forest experiment
articles.abstract: Our findings reveal that N enrichment reshapes sapling life‐history strategies by altering trait‐mediated resource allocation and physiological sensitivity to climatic stress, thereby reconfiguring the growth–mortality trade‐off under global change. Abstract The interspecific trade‐off between growth and mortality among tree species is a key dimension of plant life‐history strategies. Atmospheric nitrogen (N) deposition and climate change are transforming forest population dynamics, yet their interactive effects on sapling growth–mortality trade‐offs remain poorly understood. In this study, we used a 5‐year N addition experiment involving 39,366 saplings from 12 temperate tree species in north‐eastern China. We tested how N addition and climate together changed demographic rates and their trade‐off. We implemented a factorial N addition experiment (0, 50 and 100 kg N ha−1 year−1) and assessed how sapling performance was influenced by climate variability, functional traits, soil properties, topography and neighbourhood competition. Low‐N addition increased relative growth rates by 12.5% (plot‐community level), 6.7% (species level) and 13.3% (individual level) without a concomitant increase in mortality, whereas high N addition elevated mortality by up to 23.7% without significantly enhancing growth, indicating a shift in species' positions within the growth–mortality trade‐off space. Notably, we detected non‐additive interactions between N addition and climate: increased precipitation suppressed N‐induced growth gains but amplified mortality, while warming further constrained growth responses under N addition. A realised interspecific growth–mortality trade‐off was observed under all N treatments, but its strength varied among N addition levels, weakening under low‐N addition and partially re‐intensifying under high‐N addition. Functional traits emerged as the primary proximate driver of the growth–mortality trade‐off, mediating part of the indirect effects of N addition and climate on this demographic relationship. Synthesis. Collectively, our findings reveal that N enrichment reshapes sapling life‐history strategies by altering trait‐mediated resource allocation and physiological sensitivity to climatic stress, thereby reconfiguring the growth–mortality trade‐off under global change.

articles.title: Why finer spatial resolutions do not necessarily improve species distribution models
articles.abstract: Seeking the perfect spatial resolution should not be regarded as the holy grail of ecological modelling. In reality, no such universally optimal resolution exists. Progress is more likely to come from explicitly integrating processes operating across multiple resolutions. In particular, incorporating neighbourhood‐scale variables as predictors in SDMs represents an important step in this direction. Abstract In recent years, there has been growing criticism of using too coarse environmental data in species distribution models (SDMs), especially for sessile organisms such as plants. However, we argue that coarse‐resolution environmental predictors are not only conceptually in line with the idea of SDMs, but may often also lead to more robust and realistic models than those with resolutions approaching the sizes of individuals. We explicitly demonstrate this seeming paradox using a virtual ecologist experiment. The main reason behind this is the disequilibrium between a species' fundamental niche and its realised distribution. While this disequilibrium is well‐recognised in biogeography and metapopulation ecology, its impact on fine‐scale SDMs remains rather neglected. Contrary to recent claims, we therefore suggest that the optimal spatial resolution of predictors in SDMs should be guided less by the size of individuals and rather by the spatial extent required to sustain minimum viable populations. Synthesis: Seeking the perfect spatial resolution should not be regarded as the holy grail of ecological modelling. In reality, no such universally optimal resolution exists. Progress is more likely to come from explicitly integrating processes operating across multiple resolutions. In particular, incorporating neighbourhood‐scale variables as predictors in SDMs represents an important step in this direction.

articles.title: Distinguishing pairwise species spatial associations from multi‐species distribution patterns
articles.abstract: To understand species coexistence, measuring between‐species co‐distributional patterns is valuable. In the present study, we distinguished and separated pairwise species spatial associations (including between‐species distribution co‐occurrence and segregation) from multispecies distributional patterns (including aggregation, randomness and overdispersion) by developing and applying statistical methods that are related to the first nearest neighbour distance (NND). The proposed one‐dimensional and two‐dimensional NND metrics allow ecologists to conduct hypothesis testing on empirical biodiversity data collected via spatially constrained line transect sampling and extensive area surveys, respectively. The application of the proposed metrics on the spatial distribution patterns of common wild frogs in SW China showed that amphibian individuals from different species presented co‐occurring distributional aggregation in both suburban and remote hotspot areas. In summary, our study takes a step forward in clarifying and distinguishing between‐species co‐occurrence and segregation effects from multispecies distributional patterns. All statistics for conducting hypothesis testing on interspecific distributional associations versus multispecies distributional aggregation levels using line‐transect sampling‐based or quadrat sampling‐based biodiversity data were available in the R code of the Supporting Information for immediate application.

articles.title: Smoke signals: Measuring wildlife smoke exposure with animal‐borne and stationary sensors
articles.abstract: Wildfires are becoming larger, more frequent and more severe, producing smoke plumes that degrade air quality hundreds of kilometres away and for days to weeks after an active fire. Despite public health and safety concerns regarding wildfire smoke, we know little about how free‐ranging wildlife experience or respond to these exposures. This disconnect reflects a serious data gap in the form of sparse air‐quality monitors in the remote landscapes that wildlife occupy. Animal‐borne sensors have revolutionized wildlife ecology by quantifying how individuals respond to environmental stressors in real time, but an equivalent tool for smoke exposure has been missing. Here, we present the ‘smoke logger’, a low‐cost air‐quality measurement system for monitoring particulate matter ≤2.5 μm (PM2.5) that uses a laser‐scattering sensor and records sub‐hourly measurements throughout entire fire seasons. The unit can be mounted on a GPS collar, pairing air‐quality measurements with animal location, activity and other biologged data, or deployed as a stationary unit within an animal's home range to characterize ambient exposure to particulate matter associated with smoke and vehicle combustion. Within an urban‐to‐rural gradient, GPS‐collared mule deer (Odocoileus hemionus) with attached smoke sensors reported PM2.5 values that varied with proximity to roads, demonstrating the sensor's ability to resolve fine‐scale pollution gradients. In a remote Utah deployment where the nearest regional monitor was 20 km away, collar readings differed from the nearest network sensor by an order of magnitude, demonstrating the limits of using existing networks to estimate exposure for wildlife research. The smoke logger opens a new pathway for wildlife research by resolving individual‐level smoke exposure at spatial and temporal scales that govern behaviour and physiology. Pairing collar‐measured PM2.5 with location, activity and physiological measurements allows ecologists to test mechanisms previously only inferred, including behavioural responses to degraded sensory environments during smoke events and sublethal health effects that persist long after visible smoke clears. The open‐source design extends to additional pollutants and microclimate variables (e.g. temperature, humidity, volatile organic compounds), and disagreement between logger readings and regional smoke products may itself be ecologically informative, flagging candidate smoke refugia invisible to coarser monitoring approaches.

articles.title: Ribosome remodeling drives translation adaptation during viral infection and cellular stress
articles.abstract: Tsai et al. discover that ribosome composition is reprogrammed in response to intrinsic and external cellular perturbations, which supports ribosome remodeling as a conserved mechanism that enables adaptive protein synthesis during pathogen infection and cellular adaptation.

articles.title: Toward interpretable foundation models for molecular biology
articles.abstract: Interpretability must be a first-class design objective for the next generation of foundation models in molecular biology. In this perspective, Varma and Ideker examine the ways in which it can be built into a model, from biological priors to architecture, and provide a checklist for authors and reviewers.

articles.title: When Clades Collide: Genomic Admixture in Blacklegged Ticks (Ixodes scapularis) From the Great Plains
articles.abstract: Ixodes scapularis ticks transmit a number of pathogens important to human health, including Borrelia burgdorferi sensu stricto, the causative agent of Lyme disease. While I. scapularis is found across the Eastern United States, Lyme disease transmission is largely limited to the Northeast and Upper Midwest and is nearly absent in the South. This indicates that differences in northern versus southern clades of I. scapularis are associated with differences in Lyme disease transmission risk. Ixodes scapularis is undergoing range expansion, including into the Great Plains region of the United States. Determining where I. scapularis populations in the Great Plains originated can inform future risk of Lyme disease transmission in this region. In this study, we use a population genomics framework to characterize diversity, structure and B. burgdorferi infection rates of I. scapularis populations in the Great Plains region. We generated whole genome sequence data and single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) datasets from I. scapularis ticks collected in Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska and South Dakota to compare to publicly available data from across the species' range. Our analysis of 200 I. scapularis SNP datasets indicated geographically well‐defined populations that correspond to historical northern and southern ancestral clades of I. scapularis. Ticks from South Dakota, Iowa and northeastern Nebraska are genetically similar populations from the Upper Midwest, while ticks from Kansas are more genetically similar to ticks from the Southeast. Ticks collected in the east central region of Nebraska, however, represent an evenly admixed population of both northern and southern genomic backgrounds. Analysis of B. burgdorferi reads from genomic datasets shows ~50% infection rate in ticks from Iowa and northeastern Nebraska, whereas ticks from Kansas show no evidence of B. burgdorferi infection. Of note, evenly admixed ticks from the east central region of Nebraska also show no evidence of B. burgdorferi infection. These results provide further evidence that tick genomics may influence traits associated with B. burgdorferi infection status, and thus the potential for Lyme disease transmission. As the range of I. scapularis continues to expand, bringing historically isolated populations into contact, there is a clear need to understand the consequence of genomic admixture for B. burgdorferi transmission potential to inform future risk of Lyme disease in the United States.

articles.title: A triple carbonylation cascade converts aldehydes into threofuranoses
articles.abstract: The construction of complex sugars from aldehydes is difficult. Now, a rhodium-catalysed triple-carbonylation cascade is developed that enables the direct conversion of diverse aldehydes into structurally defined 4-carbothreofuranoses in one step. This strategy overcomes long-standing challenges in iterative carbonylation and establishes a modular platform for oxygen-rich scaffold assembly.

articles.title: Controlling reactions via nucleophile sorting
articles.abstract: Controlling the regio-, chemo-, and enantioselectivity of vicinal addition across olefins remains a challenging process. Now, a palladium-catalysed system has been developed, starting from propargylic alcohol precursors, that exploits tiered nucleophilicity between inner- and outer-sphere processes for precise control over the reaction outcome.

articles.title: Evolution of dipole–dipole dynamics in cold ammonia collisions
articles.abstract: Interactions between polar molecules are expected to become increasingly strong at low collision energies through dipole–dipole forces. Now it has been shown that ammonia molecules instead exhibit suppressed dipolar interactions in the cold regime as the dipole moment effectively switches off, as shown by local maxima in the collision cross-sections.

articles.title: Orthogonal nucleophile-ordered assembly for modular access to enantiopure 1,2-amino alcohols
articles.abstract: The selective assembly of multiple chemicals into complex chiral architectures in a single operation is a long-standing challenge. Now a palladium-catalysed orthogonal strategy has been shown to sort and incorporate two native N–H/O–H nucleophiles with similar reactivity, delivering enantioenriched 1,2-amino alcohols and 1,2-diols with high selectivity.

articles.title: Retention and biosynthesis of diverse nitroarenes in Escherichia coli after combinatorial nitroreductase gene deletions
articles.abstract: Nitroarenes are unstable in microbial cultures, limiting the biomanufacturing of these industrially and pharmaceutically important chemicals. Genome engineering of nitroreductase-deficient E. coli strains has now been shown to improve nitroarene retention during fermentation, expanding access to nitro functional group chemistry in whole-cell biocatalysis, metabolic engineering and synthetic biology.

articles.title: All-organic mixed-matrix membranes with single-crystal covalent organic frameworks for carbon capture
articles.abstract: Carbon capture with conventional mixed-matrix membranes is limited by the inability to achieve high packing densities of porous fillers while preserving their intrinsic transport properties. Here the authors develop high-performance membranes based on single-crystal covalent organic framework fillers using a weak-interaction inlaying strategy that enables high filler loadings.

articles.title: Diverse infections transcriptionally reprogram the intestinal epithelium and epithelial–immune cell interactions
articles.abstract: In this Resource, Beiting and colleagues provide an atlas of the mouse ileum and mesenteric lymph nodes under homeostatic conditions and during enteric infection. They also present GutPath, a tool that enables interrogation of the dataset.

articles.title: Chemically moulding intermetallics in two dimensions
articles.abstract: An adsorption–conversion strategy enables the synthesis of ultrathin intermetallics across a broad compositional space, from binaries to high-entropy alloys.

articles.title: Loss-reshaped asymmetric nanolight
articles.abstract: Optical loss is usually treated as a limitation. An electrically tunable carbon-nanotube layer instead uses directional dissipation to reshape nanoscale polariton propagation.

articles.title: Designing rhodamine-binding proteins from scratch
Extracting brain-wide interactions with CURBD
Generalizable perturbation prediction
How to write a rebuttal letter
articles.abstract: The rebuttal letter is a vitally important document when revising a manuscript for a journal. Here we discuss how to communicate about your manuscript revisions in the best possible light.

articles.title: Recording time via brain organoids
The very hungry nanopillar
articles.abstract: Earlier this year, we packed up a small version of our world and headed to Bird Rock Elementary in La Jolla, California, to meet two dozen second graders waiting to do science. We brought with us a plant molecular farming lab, plush virus nanoparticles, and enough curiosity to fill a classroom. We began with wonder.

articles.title: Astrocytes regulate axonal mitochondrial transport deficits in C9ORF72 amyotrophic lateral sclerosis motor neurons
articles.abstract: Disrupted axonal transport and astrocyte dysfunction are implicated in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Here we show these processes are linked—human-induced pluripotent stem-cell-derived astrocytes carrying the C9ORF72 mutation disrupt mitochondrial axonal transport and mitochondrial function in cocultured motor neurons (MNs). Conversely, isogenic gene-corrected astrocytes or boosting astrocytic mitochondrial bioenergetics rescue axonal mitochondrial transport deficits in C9ORF72 MNs. Our results delineate a non-cell-autonomous role for astrocytes in regulating mitochondrial transport along axons in ALS models.

articles.title: Modality-specific reactive and predictive responses in the human superior colliculus
articles.abstract: Chen et al. use 7-Tesla fMRI to show that the human superior colliculus has modality-specific, depth-dependent activity prior to visual or somatosensory events, resembling its response to actual stimulation.

articles.title: A long-sought phase in CuGeO3 traces the full evolution of spin fractionalization
articles.abstract: Neutron spectroscopy measurements combined with tensor network simulations have placed the long-studied quantum spin-chain compound CuGeO3 in a spontaneously dimerized phase predicted in 1982. In this system, fractionalized excitations evolve from nearly free spinons to tightly bound triplons across energy scales within a single spectrum.

articles.title: Clarity on carbon under extreme compression
articles.abstract: Carbon’s high-pressure phase diagram has long been debated. Now shock experiments have tracked diamond through its melting curve, providing a resolution. The findings also serve as a benchmark for first-principles theory.

articles.title: Non-reciprocity in quantum technologies
articles.abstract: Non-reciprocity in the quantum regime promises unidirectional transport and enhanced sensing, but traditional approaches hinder device integration. This Review highlights magnet-free routes for engineering non-reciprocity in quantum systems.

articles.title: Boosting CAR T cell efficacy in cancer with metabolic insights from design to diet
articles.abstract: Although chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy has advanced the treatment of many cancers, it is now apparent that metabolism is a major determinant of CAR T cell fitness, persistence and function. Here, Morgan, MacPherson and Lum examine how metabolism integrates with CAR T cell design, outline possible metabolic engineering solutions, and highlight opportunities to leverage diet to improve CAR T cell efficacy in people with haematological cancers.

articles.title: Molecular glue targets ALK resistance
Next-generation immune cell engagers for B cell depletion in autoimmune diseases
articles.abstract: Immune cell engagers are emerging as a strategy for deep B cell depletion in autoimmune diseases. This Review examines their mechanisms, clinical development and next-generation designs, including T cell, natural killer cell and γδ T cell-engaging formats, and considers lessons from haematological malignancies to improve efficacy, safety and durability of immune modulation.

articles.title: A guide to B cell metabolism
articles.abstract: Metabolic control is an integral component of B cell physiology, shaping fate decisions and effector functions, while also driving maladaptive programmes that contribute to diverse pathologies. This Review provides an overview of the current understanding of B cell metabolism in health and disease.

articles.title: Predicting resistance evolution to guide antibiotic development
articles.abstract: Resistance emergence is a major challenge to antibiotic development, often undermining promising drug candidates and negating years of research and pharmaceutical investment. In this Review, Pál and colleagues propose a resistance-based classification system for antibiotic development that integrates early resistance predictions into the prospective development of new antibiotics.

articles.title: Remediation restores soil carbon
articles.abstract: This study suggests that shifts in bioavailable heavy metals during soil remediation reshape microbial physiological traits, thereby increasing microbial carbon use efficiency and enhancing soil carbon storage.

articles.title: Towards broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals against RNA viruses
articles.abstract: In this Review, Neyts and colleagues discuss the rationale for developing broader-spectrum antivirals against RNA viruses, survey promising antiviral targets and agents, and outline strategies to accelerate clinical development and strengthen outbreak preparedness.

articles.title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qubit Quantum Processors: Simulating Fermions, Bosons, and Gauge Fields
articles.abstract: Researchers develop a hybrid qubit-boson quantum processor framework to simulate interacting fermions, bosons, and lattice gauge fields.

articles.title: Truly three-dimensional lithium-sulfur battery cathodes: A review of materials chemistry, fabrication strategies, and device integration
Poltergeist mechanism: Enhancement of scalar-induced gravitational waves with early matter-dominated era
articles.abstract: Gravitational waves offer a potential window into the first moments of cosmic history. If the Universe underwent and abruptly exited an early matter-dominated phase, as predicted by many particle-physics models involving heavy particles, primordial black holes, or oscillating scalar fields forming Q-balls, the resulting gravitational-wave signal could be amplified via the recently discovered “poltergeist mechanism” discussed in this review. The authors explain the physical origin of this amplification, analyze the mechanism across several cosmological scenarios, and discuss prospects for detecting the resulting signals with current and future gravitational-wave observatories.

articles.title: A multiomic atlas reveals distinct immune landscapes in preterm and term chronic placental inflammation
articles.abstract: Chronic placental inflammation (CPI), an umbrella term encompassing chronic chorioamnionitis, chronic villitis, and chronic deciduitis, is associated with preterm birth (PTB), yet its cellular and molecular determinants across gestation remain poorly defined. Here, we constructed an integrated multiomic atlas of CPI by profiling placental and extraplacental tissues from preterm and term pregnancies using imaging mass cytometry, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire mining. CPI emerged as a gestational age–dependent immune continuum rather than a uniform inflammatory state. Preterm CPI was characterized by infiltration of cytotoxic CD8 + T cells, activated macrophages, and natural killer (NK) cells in the extraplacental membranes. In contrast, term CPI exhibited spatially confined immune niches enriched for homeostatic myeloid cells and regulatory T cells. Multiomic integration revealed active contributions from the developing fetal immune system in preterm CPI, including macrophages, T cells, and mast cells that reshaped maternal-fetal immune cross-talk. Cell-cell–communication analyses uncovered proinflammatory signaling states in preterm CPI and resolution-phase pathways in term CPI, whereas TCR repertoire profiling identified memory clonotypes with viral epitope similarity, consistent with antigen-agnostic activation. Overall, this atlas defines the cellular, spatial, and transcriptional architecture of CPI and provides a framework for translational biomarker discovery and therapeutic intervention development.

articles.title: Aberrant erythrocyte rigidity in JAK2V617F myeloproliferative neoplasms underlies concurrent thrombosis and hemorrhage
articles.abstract: Thrombotic events are the leading cause of death in myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) driven by the JAK2 Val 617 →Phe (JAK2V617F) mutation. We investigated how JAK2V617F alters hemostasis and thrombosis in humans and in lineage-specific knockin mice to test whether red blood cell (RBC) mechanics contribute directly to clot pathology. Jak2 F/+ Vav-Cre knockin mice form structurally aberrant clots characterized by extended clot formation times and unstable hemostatic plug formation. Whole-blood clot contraction in vitro was impaired in humans and mice carrying the JAK2V617F mutation, even when Jak2 V617F erythrocytes were resuspended in normal plasma with normal platelets. Thus, in addition to increasing the hematocrit, the JAK2V617F mutation imparted intrinsic changes in erythrocytes critical for mediating abnormal clot formation. Biophysical analysis showed that Jak2 V617F erythrocytes had stiffened membranes, making them less compressible during clot contraction. Proteomic and lipidomic analysis of Jak2 V617F erythrocytes revealed the loss of key membrane and cytoskeleton proteins, a sparse spectrin cytoskeletal network, increased membrane lipid content, and deep plasma membrane invaginations that were consistent with biaxial cytoskeletal stretching and altered lipid packing. These JAK2V617F-driven changes in erythropoiesis generated intrinsically rigid erythrocytes that impaired clot contraction and produced larger and more occlusive, yet mechanically unstable thrombi. This mechanism may explain the contradictory coexistence of thrombosis and hemorrhage in MPNs and why both complications improve when blood counts are lowered, suggesting that targeting erythrocyte mechanics may provide previously unidentified therapeutic opportunities.

articles.title: Early-life microbiota direct an epithelial S100 program required for neonatal immunity
articles.abstract: Despite appreciation that neonatal immune responses differ markedly from those of adults, the mechanisms that enable early-life immunity remain poorly understood. Here, we find that healthy newborn mice express high concentrations of the S100 calcium-binding protein A8/A9 (S100A8/S100A9) antimicrobial heterodimer calprotectin and that this early up-regulation in the intestine is driven by initial exposure to commensal bacteria. Impaired calprotectin expression or microbiota colonization at birth increased susceptibility of neonatal mice to sepsis and death postinfection; however, calprotectin administration rescued microbiota-depleted pups from infection. Microbiota colonization induced S100A9 expression by intestinal epithelial cells (IECs), and epithelial cells represented the main source of calprotectin in the neonatal intestine. Consistent with a critical role in early-life defense, neonatal IEC-specific S100A9 knockout pups were highly susceptible to infection, phenocopying S100A8/A9 full knockout and antibiotic-exposed neonatal mice. IEC-intrinsic S100A9 expression mediated microbiota-sensitive defense in neonatal mice, and commensal bacteria, such as Lactobacillus , were sufficient to prime this epithelial defense pathway. Mechanistically, indole-3-lactic acid produced by initial colonizers directed IEC intrinsic up-regulation of S100A9 in both mice and human intestinal organoids. Thus, microbiota-epithelial dynamics that occur at birth are essential for programming early-life immunity and suggest that probiotic approaches targeting epithelial cells could prevent neonatal sepsis and death.

articles.title: Erratum for the Research Article “Multifunctional antibody responses from a primate Shigella outbreak inform vaccine design”
Human microglia clear intraneuronal α-synuclein aggregates by GPNMB-mediated trogocytosis
articles.abstract: Microglia are the primary immune cells of the brain, but their role in Parkinson’s disease is not fully understood. Chronic microglial activation is toxic to neurons, but in the early stages of pathology, microglia also exert beneficial functions. We used induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)–derived coculture models to investigate how human microglia respond to α-synuclein aggregates that form de novo inside human dopaminergic neurons with α-synuclein gene triplication or are triggered by fibrils. We found that microglia cleared Ser 129 -phosphorylated α-synuclein aggregates through a contact-dependent mechanism. This process was fine-tuned by sensing (P2RY12) and inhibitory (CD22) signals and involved selective phagocytosis of neuronal subcompartments (trogocytosis), independently of TREM2 or phosphatidylserine. In the presence of intraneuronal α-synuclein aggregates, microglia exhibited morphological and transcriptional changes indicative of activation. Using single-cell sequencing, we identified a cluster of disease-associated microglia (DAM) responsible for this beneficial phenotype and the Parkinson’s disease GWAS candidate glycoprotein nonmetastatic melanoma protein B (GPNMB) as a key effector of aggregate clearance by microglial lysosomes. GPNMB interacted with Ser 129 -phosphorylated α-synuclein in iPSC-derived microglia exposed to aggregate-laden dopaminergic neurons and was up-regulated in substantia nigra microglia of individuals with incidental Lewy bodies or Parkinson’s disease. Microglia-specific GPNMB knockdown using CRISPRi reduced intraneuronal aggregate clearance. GPNMB-mediated trogocytosis was negatively regulated by an autocrine IL-10 signaling loop, whereas IL-10 receptor blockade enhanced the phagocytic response. Together, our study identifies a subtype of human microglia capable of removing intraneuronal aggregates and potential therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Immunoregulatory artificial lymph nodes restore antigen-specific tolerance in advanced multiple sclerosis
articles.abstract: Tolerogenic dendritic cell (tolDC) vaccines are a promising antigen-specific therapy for multiple sclerosis (MS), yet their efficacy is limited by poor homing to secondary lymphoid organs and rapid loss of the tolerogenic phenotype in native inflamed lymph nodes. Here, we developed a 3D-printed tolerogenic artificial lymph node (tol-aLN) that creates a protected immune niche for durable tolerance induction. tolDCs were loaded onto a porous gelatin methacrylate scaffold engineered for sustained C-C motif chemokine ligand 21 (CCL21) release, recruiting naïve CD4 + T cells and shielding tolDCs from an inflammatory lymph node. Geometric optimization of an orthogonal lattice scaffold enhanced spatially confined DC–T cell interactions, promoting robust and stable induction of regulatory T cells (T reg cells). In experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), tol-aLN implantation attenuated disease even at advanced stages by inducing antigen-specific Foxp3 + T reg cells that trafficked to the spleen, lymph nodes, and central nervous system (CNS). Conditional T reg cell depletion abolished therapeutic efficacy, indicating that T reg cells are necessary mediators of tol-aLN–induced protection. Long-term studies revealed sustained remission without impairing systemic immunity. In a myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (amino acids 1 to 125) (MOG 1–125 )–induced EAE model, multivalent tol-aLN also efficiently suppressed inflammatory B cells and autoantibody production, reprogramming CNS B cells toward a regulatory state. Single-cell transcriptomics further revealed a global reduction in interferon-stimulated gene activity and restoration of homeostatic microglial phenotypes. Collectively, tol-aLN offers a scalable, antigen-specific platform for immune tolerance and CNS protection, with translational potential for MS and other autoimmune diseases.

articles.title: Transient receptor potential channel activation targets multiple stages of the schistosome parasite
articles.abstract: Schistosomiasis, a neglected tropical disease caused by infection with parasitic blood flukes of the genus Schistosoma , affects more than 250 million people worldwide. Currently, patients rely on a single medicine, praziquantel (PZQ), discovered half a century ago. To combat drug resistance and reach elimination of the schistosome parasite, alternative drugs to PZQ are required that treat and prevent disease. Here, we describe a drug candidate, M5493, with potent activity against multiple parasite life cycle stages. The target is a parasite transient receptor potential ion channel, distinct from the target of PZQ. To circumvent its limited bioavailability, the active agent was converted to prodrug M5493, which displayed robust activity against the schistosome parasite at doses as low as 5 milligrams per kilogram in mice infected with Schistosoma mansoni . Unlike the benzodiazepine meclonazepam, which displays clinical antihelminthic activity through the same target, M5493 showed no sedating side effects given that it did not engage GABA A receptors. Overall, this compound has the potential to provide single-dose treatment, broad-spectrum efficacy against schistosome parasites at different life cycle stages, and transmission blocking activity.

articles.title: Turning the tables: Repurposing neuroplasticity to defeat cancer
articles.abstract: Instead of asking what nerves do to cancer, my work reveals how cancer injures and reprograms peripheral nerves to drive immune evasion and how targeting this process restores immunotherapy responses.

articles.title: Use of split intein and myotropic AAV vectors enables effective preclinical gene therapy for dysferlinopathy
articles.abstract: Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type R2 (LGMDR2) is a genetic disorder characterized by progressive skeletal muscle weakness and degeneration. It is caused by mutations in the DYSF gene, which prevent dysferlin expression. Dysferlin protein is essential for muscle cell membrane repair. Gene therapy using adeno-associated viral (AAV) vectors to restore full-length dysferlin expression is a promising therapeutic approach for LGMDR2. However, the large size of the dysferlin cDNA (6.2 kilobases) exceeds the ∼4.7-kilobase packaging capacity of AAV vectors, posing a challenge to effective delivery of the full-length protein. Here, we describe the use of split inteins and myotropic AAV vectors for efficient systemic gene delivery and expression of full-length dysferlin in the muscles of an LGMDR2 mouse model. We generated and validated a potent split-intein version of dysferlin that enables reconstitution of scarless full-length dysferlin protein. In vitro assessment of these constructs demonstrated a high capacity of the reconstituted dysferlin to restore membrane repair defects in dysferlinopathic mouse myoblasts. Systemic administration of split-intein and dysferlin dual AAVMYO1 vectors improved muscle strength, increased contractile force, and reduced histopathological abnormalities in the LGMDR2 mouse model at both the presymptomatic stage and late stage of the disease. Compared with the homologous recombination dual–AAV vector strategy, the split-intein technology demonstrated superior efficiency in restoring the full-length dysferlin protein and resulted in greater functional improvements. These findings demonstrate the curative potential of this split intein–based gene therapy approach for LGMDR2.

articles.title: [Seminar] Migraine
articles.abstract: Migraine is a chronic neurovascular disorder characterised by recurrent attacks of moderate-to-severe head pain, accompanied by transient but disabling symptoms such as aura, nausea, vomiting, phonophobia, and photophobia, reflecting the involvement of multiple systems. Migraine affects and disables a large proportion of the global population. The pathogenesis of migraine involves the interplay of genetic and epigenetic factors across complex neurosensory and neurovascular networks. Decades of research have elucidated key components of these pathways, driving the development of mechanism-based therapies that are now transforming clinical practice and substantially improving patients’ lives.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant niraparib monotherapy for unresectable, homologous recombination deficiency-positive, high-grade serous ovarian cancer (NANT): a multicentre, single-arm, phase 2 trial
articles.abstract: BackgroundNeoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval debulking surgery is standard treatment for advanced ovarian cancer that is unlikely to achieve optimal cytoreduction. We aimed to evaluate a chemotherapy-free regimen of neoadjuvant niraparib monotherapy in homologous recombination deficiency (HRD)-positive disease initially unsuitable for primary debulking surgery.MethodsThis single-arm, phase 2 trial was conducted at six tertiary hospitals in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years, had treatment-naïve, FIGO stage III-IV HRD-positive high-grade serous or endometrioid ovarian cancer, an ECOG performance status of 0-2, with a low likelihood of complete primary debulking surgery based on prespecified criteria. Patients received oral niraparib monotherapy for two 28-day cycles with an individualised starting dose of 200 mg or 300 mg. Protocol-permitted supportive care was provided as clinically indicated. Co-primary endpoints were investigator-assessed objective response rate in the response-evaluable population and R0 resection rate after interval debulking surgery in the operated population. Safety was assessed in all patients who received at least one dose of niraparib. The trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04507841), is closed to enrolment, and this report presents the primary analysis.FindingsBetween Jan 8, 2021, and Jul 18, 2023, 127 patients were screened, and 67 were enrolled into the study. All enrolled patients were female and self-identified as Han Chinese (median age 55 years [IQR 50-62]). At the data cutoff (Dec 29, 2025), median follow-up was 37·7 months (IQR 31·8-48·5). Among 48 response-evaluable patients, 30 achieved an objective response, with an objective response rate of 63% (95% CI 47-76). Among 40 operated patients, 32 achieved R0 resection, with an R0 resection rate of 80% (95% CI 64-91). The most common grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events were thrombocytopenia in 32 (48%) of 67 patients, leukopenia in 13 (19%) patients, anaemia in 12 (18%) patients, and neutropenia in nine (13%) patients. Serious adverse events occurred in 19 (28%) patients. No treatment-related deaths occurred.InterpretationNeoadjuvant niraparib showed anti-tumour activity and enabled R0 resection in selected patients with HRD-positive advanced ovarian cancer who were initially unsuitable for primary debulking surgery. This strategy remains investigational and requires randomised validation against standard platinum-taxane neoadjuvant chemotherapy.FundingNational Key Technology Research and Development Program of China, National Natural Science Foundation of China, Natural Science Foundation of Hubei Province, Innovative Drug Research and Development National Science and Technology Major Project, and Zai Lab (Shanghai).TranslationFor the Chinese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

articles.title: Precision before incision: neoadjuvant tumor-agnostic therapies
articles.abstract: The emergence of tumor-agnostic therapies has fundamentally transformed precision oncology. Traditionally developed and approved for metastatic disease, nine therapies spanning immunotherapy, targeted agents, and antibody–drug conjugates now demonstrate a compelling rationale for earlier deployment in the neoadjuvant setting. This review examines the paradigm shift from last-resort to first-consideration approaches. Key advantages of neoadjuvant, biomarker-guided therapy include intervention prior to the development of therapeutic resistance, optimal immune system engagement, and opportunities for organ preservation. Single-agent programmed cell death protein-1 blockade has achieved a 100% complete response rate in mismatch repair-deficient rectal cancer with preserved organ function. Neurotrophic tyrosine receptor kinase (NTRK), rearranged during transfection (RET), and B-Raf proto-oncogene serine/threonine kinase (BRAF) inhibitors have demonstrated substantial responses that enable curative-intent surgery across malignancies. As precision oncology matures, the neoadjuvant tumor-agnostic approach exemplifies optimized therapeutic sequencing, potentially improving patient outcomes and quality of life.

articles.title: Every (slow) breath you take, every choice you make
articles.abstract: Huang and colleagues investigated how slow-paced breathing shapes physiological and brain-related signals during financial decisions under risk. Their findings elucidate neurovisceral pathways linking prolonged exhalation to increased risk-taking, whereby heightened cardiac parasympathetic modulation increases reward sensitivity and neural activity in brain regions involved in valuation and interoception.

articles.title: Dynamic Solvent Participation Drives Sodium Storage in Oxygen Engineered Hard Carbon
articles.abstract: The structural complexity of hard carbon (HC) has sparked persistent debates over its sodium storage mechanisms. To clarify the correlation between these mechanisms and the synthesis process for achieving enhanced electrochemical performance, citric acid was used to in situ engineer the surface oxygen architecture of cellulose-derived hard carbon. The optimized anode achieves a reversible capacity of 400 mAh·g–1 and an initial Coulombic efficiency of 91% in a diglyme-based electrolyte. Systematic in situ and quasi-in situ characterization reveals that charge-transfer resistance evolves cyclically with the sodium storage state, governed by the dynamic formation and attenuation of a solvation layer. These results provide evidence for the involvement of solvent molecules during (de)sodiation, validating the “adsorption–closed pore filling” pathway. This work demonstrates that the interfacial solvation structure is a key determinant of sodium storage kinetics and establishes surface oxygen tailoring as an effective strategy for hard carbon anodes with improved performance.

Effect of Fluvoxamine and Metformin for Fatigue in Patients With Long COVID
articles.abstract: BackgroundPostacute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (long COVID) presents a therapeutic challenge, with fatigue being a common, debilitating symptom.ObjectiveTo assess the efficacy of fluvoxamine and metformin to treat long COVID fatigue.DesignRandomized, placebo-controlled, adaptive trial. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06128967).SettingOutpatient sites in Brazil.Participants399 adults with fatigue 90 days to 24 months after confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection.InterventionParticipants were randomly assigned to fluvoxamine (100 mg twice daily [BID]), extended-release metformin (750 mg BID [n = 71] from October 2023 to April 2024; reduced to 500 mg BID [n = 40] in May 2024 after a protocol amendment until the group was stopped for futility in September 2024), or a matching placebo, each for 60 days with follow-up to day 90.MeasurementsChange in Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS) score.ResultsMedian baseline FSS scores ranged from 5.6 to 5.9 across all study groups. The treatment effect on FSS score for fluvoxamine versus placebo showed a mean difference of -0.43 at day 60 and -0.58 at day 90; both had a posterior probability of superiority of 99%. Fluvoxamine also improved quality-of-life scores with a high posterior probability of superiority. Findings for metformin were inconclusive. Incidence of adverse events was lower for fluvoxamine (24.0%) than for metformin, 750 mg BID (45.1%); metformin, 500 mg BID (42.5%); and placebo (35.5%). Grade 3 or higher adverse events were rare (≤2.7%), with no treatment-related deaths.LimitationsThe results were inconclusive for metformin because of a dose change recommended by the data safety and monitoring committee due to adverse effects causing study withdrawal and early termination. The benefit of fluvoxamine after 90 days is unknown. The trial did not address other long COVID symptoms.ConclusionFluvoxamine shows potential for improving long COVID-associated fatigue and quality of life.Primary funding sourceThe Latona Foundation.

articles.title: Incidence, Process of Care, and Outcomes of In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest in China: A Multicenter Prospective Registry Study
articles.abstract: In-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) is an acute event associated with high mortality. Although survival has improved in high-income countries, contemporary multicenter data from low- and middle-income countries remain scarce, limiting global benchmarking and the identification of system-level opportunities for improvement. This cohort study used data from the BASIC-IHCA (Baseline Investigation of In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest) registry. Adult patients (≥18 years) who experienced IHCA and received cardiopulmonary resuscitation between July 1, 2019, and December 31, 2020, at 37 hospitals across 29 provinces in China were included. The primary outcome was survival to 30 days or hospital discharge. Secondary outcomes included return of spontaneous circulation, 6- and 12-month survival, and favorable neurological outcome (Cerebral Performance Category score 1–2). Process measures focused on the timeliness of resuscitation response and the implementation of postresuscitation interventions. Among 17 602 patients (median age, 66 years; 65.5% male), the annual incidence of adult IHCA was 4.1 per 1000 admissions. Cardiac etiology was identified in 6569 (37.3%) patients, and 2380 (13.5%) presented with initial shockable rhythm. Among all patients, 16 872 (95.9%) received cardiopulmonary resuscitation within 1 minute; timely defibrillation or epinephrine was achieved in 71.4% and 84.4% of patients with initial shockable and nonshockable rhythms, respectively. Sustained return of spontaneous circulation was achieved in 6200 (35.2%) patients, of whom 222 (3.6%) received temperature control therapy and 320 (5.2%) underwent coronary angiography. Overall, 1610 (9.1%) patients survived to 30 days or discharge, with 1241 (7.1%) having a favorable neurological outcome. At 12 months, 1075 (6.1%) patients remained alive, and 986 (5.6%) had a favorable neurological outcome. This multicenter registry highlights a substantial burden of IHCA in China, with markedly low survival rates. Despite prompt initial resuscitation, critical gaps persist in postresuscitation care. Systemic and cultural factors, including the infrequent use of do not attempt cardiopulmonary resuscitation orders, may further contribute to survival disparities. These findings suggest several system-level opportunities to improve IHCA outcomes, including structured response systems, optimized critical care resource allocation, and greater integration of advanced care planning.

articles.title: Global transportation impacts on wildlife mortality and emerging pathways for mitigation
articles.abstract: Terrestrial, freshwater, and marine transportation are fundamental to modern human life, but vehicle collisions with wildlife inadvertently kill hundreds of millions of animals across 2000 vertebrate and invertebrate species annually; however, a comprehensive framework to assess and mitigate these mortalities is missing. We identified and compared the most up‐to‐date information regarding the impacts of transportation on wildlife mortality to determine cross‐cutting solutions to this challenging problem. For example, numerous strategies, such as under‐ or overpasses traversing roads and railways that increase wildlife–habitat connectivity, policies that enforce reduced speed in areas with active wildlife, and passive sensors that detect wildlife to alert nearby ships and vehicles and enable mandatory speed reductions, can reduce wildlife–vehicle collisions. We explored emerging technological advances that could help further reduce future wildlife–vehicle conflicts and provide a path forward for transportation systems. Specifically, we described how the combination of citizen science, artificial intelligence, targeted studies on wildlife demographic impacts, and cost‐effective mitigation efforts will be powerful tools to inform needed future policies to decrease ship speed in areas with threatened whale species and reduce rates of wildlife mortality across ecosystems in a fast‐moving world. Repercusiones del transporte mundial sobre la mortalidad de la fauna silvestre y nuevas vías de mitigación Resumen El transporte terrestre, fluvial y marítimo es fundamental para la vida humana moderna, pero las colisiones de vehículos con fauna silvestre matan inadvertidamente a cientos de millones de animales de 2,000 especies de vertebrados e invertebrados cada año; sin embargo, no existe un marco integral para evaluar y mitigar estas muertes. Hemos identificado y comparado la información más actualizada sobre los impactos del transporte sobre la mortalidad de la fauna silvestre para determinar soluciones transversales a este complejo problema. Por ejemplo, numerosas estrategias —como pasos subterráneos o elevados que cruzan carreteras y vías férreas y que aumentan la conectividad de los hábitats de la fauna silvestre, políticas que imponen la reducción de la velocidad en zonas con presencia de fauna silvestre, y sensores pasivos que detectan a los animales para alertar a los barcos y vehículos cercanos y permitir reducciones obligatorias de la velocidad— pueden reducir las colisiones entre vehículos y fauna silvestre. Analizamos los avances tecnológicos emergentes que podrían contribuir a reducir aún más los futuros conflictos entre la fauna silvestre y los vehículos, y ofrecer una vía a seguir para los sistemas de transporte. En concreto, describimos cómo la combinación de la ciencia ciudadana, la inteligencia artificial, los estudios específicos sobre los impactos demográficos en la fauna silvestre y las medidas de mitigación rentables constituirán herramientas poderosas para fundamentar las políticas futuras necesarias orientadas a reducir la velocidad de los buques en zonas con especies de ballenas amenazadas y a disminuir las tasas de mortalidad de la fauna silvestre en todos los ecosistemas, en un mundo en constante cambio.

articles.title: The Effect of Biogeographic Origin on the Adaptive Trajectories of Plants in Urban Environments
articles.abstract: Parallel adaptation is a hallmark of urban evolution, yet whether plant responses to urbanization are globally consistent or influenced by biogeographic origin remains unclear. We investigated pollinator communities, floral display and reproductive allocation in Trifolium repens along urbanization gradients in 11 European urban areas spanning boreal, continental, and Mediterranean biogeographic regions. We found strong differences, with boreal and continental gradients showing no consistent floral trait shifts, whereas Mediterranean gradients showed parallel reductions in flower and inflorescence size with increased urbanization. This pattern persisted under common‐garden conditions, indicating a genetic basis. Pollinator assemblage, lacking consistent variation along the gradients, did not explain phenotypic changes. Instead, in the Mediterranean, we found an increased asexual investment, suggesting an adaptive trade‐off with floral display. These findings highlight that urban evolutionary trajectories can be modulated by biogeographic origin, with semi‐arid Mediterranean environments emerging as hotspots of urban‐driven adaptation and particularly vulnerable to future urban expansion.

Alternative seed trait strategies are linked to a trade‐off between spatial and temporal dispersal
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Seed dispersal allows plants to seek favourable conditions or spread the risk of unfavourable conditions through space and time. While theory predicts a trade‐off between spatial and temporal dispersal, empirical tests have been stymied by the difficulty of measuring dispersal directly and limited data on seed traits beyond mass. Using hidden Markov models and 20 years of plant community data, we estimated spatial and temporal dispersal probabilities for 60 native and non‐native annual plants and linked them to extensive seed trait measurements. We found a clear spatial–temporal dispersal trade‐off: non‐native grasses showed high spatial dispersal, native forbs high temporal dispersal and non‐native forbs spanned the spectrum. Importantly, the traits underlying these strategies differed by group. For native forbs, spatial dispersal increased with large, elongated seeds, while small, round seeds favoured temporal dispersal. In non‐native forbs, spatial dispersal declined with size, and temporal dispersal was linked to coat thickness and nitrogen content. Seed mass showed little association with either spatial or temporal dispersal. Our results provide empirical support for the spatial–temporal dispersal trade‐off while revealing that multiple distinct trait combinations can achieve similar dispersal strategies, underscoring the need to move beyond seed mass to understand plant life‐history strategies. articles.title: Beyond nutrient concentration: A call for uptake in mycorrhizal research under drought
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) play a critical role in enhancing plant growth and drought resistance by facilitating nutrient (particularly nitrogen [N] and phosphorus [P]) acquisition. However, a widespread methodological issue persists in mycorrhizal research under drought as most studies assess the contributions of AMF solely through plant nutrient concentration, which may lead to erroneous conclusions due to biomass dilution effects. Here, we show that relying on nutrient concentration in plant tissues severely underestimates the contributions of AMF on plant N (47.2%) and P (66.3%) acquisition, and this underestimation is amplified during drought (N: 55.6%; P: 90.9%). Moreover, it may even result in erroneous conclusions in some cases. We strongly advocate that future mycorrhizal research should simultaneously report nutrient uptake, concentration and biomass metrics to more accurately quantify AMF contributions to plant nutrient acquisition. articles.title: Biodiversity effects on ecosystem functioning are driven by resource quality and contamination
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Biodiversity–ecosystem functioning relationships are increasingly explained by species' traits and resource quality differences rather than richness alone, yet cross‐trophic effects and environmental context remain poorly resolved. We experimentally tested how basal resource diversity and chemical stress interact to shape ecosystem functioning in a detritus‐based freshwater system. We manipulated leaf litter diversity (alder, hazel and beech) and selectively contaminated alder with the insecticide imidacloprid, quantifying microbially mediated decomposition, detritivore leaf processing efficiency and detritivore growth. Leaf litter identity was the primary driver of ecosystem functioning. Alder, a nutrient‐rich species, disproportionately enhanced process rates, highlighting the importance of species identity and resource quality. Leaf mixtures combined species differing in resource quality and generated non‐additive effects, with complementarity and dominance enhancing detritivore‐mediated processes, particularly leaf processing efficiency. In contrast, microbial decomposition showed weak or negative diversity effects, suggesting constraints on resource use. Imidacloprid reduced detritivore growth without altering leaf processing efficiency, due to direct toxicity after consumption or indirect effects of imidacloprid on nutritional quality. Contaminated alder acted as an ecological trap, as detritivores preferentially consumed a high‐quality resource despite the negative consequences associated with the imidacloprid treatment, suppressing positive biodiversity effects. Our results demonstrate that leaf species identity, likely reflecting differences in resource quality, and consumer behaviour jointly regulate the transfer of biodiversity effects across trophic levels, while environmental stress can disrupt these mechanisms independently of richness. Foraging energetics reveals late‐summer challenges for pollinators across two British cities
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Foraging bees often work within fine energetic margins, but recent work has shown that foraging conditions can vary markedly across the year. Despite the importance of seasonality for pollinator foraging, most work in this area has relied on indirect approaches. However, energetic efficiency, the ratio of energetic gain to cost during foraging, can be quantified directly to provide a direct comparison of the seasonal foraging conditions experienced by nectar foragers. Here, we provide the first direct measure of seasonal changes in foraging conditions by tracking the energetic efficiency of honeybee nectar forgers across a whole season (April – October) on flower patches that colonies were naturally exploiting. We combined foraging observations, flower nectar sampling and physiological data from the literature to estimate foraging efficiency (ratio of energy net gain to energy expenditure) on 19 study plant species in two locations ~600 km apart in Britain, Brighton and Edinburgh. We found that foraging efficiency was lowest in late summer (mid‐July – August), with predicted foraging efficiency reaching its lowest in mid‐August. As honeybees are generalist foragers and continually monitor foraging conditions, our data suggest that foraging conditions may be challenging during late summer for other flower visitors. Similar patterns of energetic efficiency and energy per flower were observed for both study sites. However, the more urban site was less variable, highlighting the potential importance of land‐use context for influencing seasonal continuity of floral resources. Our results provide the first direct assessment of seasonal variation in foraging efficiency of individual nectar foragers. Our results are relevant to conservation efforts and suggest that efforts to improve nectar general availability in Britain may be most valuable if provided in late summer. articles.title: Functional trait modules link climatic niche geometry to projected range change in global butterflies
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Climate warming is redistributing insects, but species‐level projections alone rarely show which functional strategies are most exposed or how traits are linked to climatic niche structure. We developed a trait‐anchored framework connecting projected range change, functional trait‐space occupancy and climatic niche geometry in global butterflies. We compiled functional traits and georeferenced occurrences for 12,448 butterfly species across six families. Species distribution models estimated current suitable area (Anow) and mid‐century suitable area under SSP5‐8.5 (A2050), from which we derived an expansion index, E = (A2050 − Anow)/Anow. Current suitable cells were projected into a two‐axis climatic harshness space to quantify climatic niche breadth and niche position. We then constructed a global functional trait space, estimated family‐level trait‐space occupancy with trait probability density surfaces, mapped the SDM‐derived expansion index with generalised additive models and tested trait–niche associations with structural equation models. Butterfly functional strategies formed a pronounced core–edge structure. Family core fractions (A50/A99) ranged from 17% to 33%, and standardised total trait‐space extent (A99) varied from 0.12 to 0.85. Projected range change formed a nonlinear, contraction‐dominated trait‐space response surface: mean predicted expansion rates were negative in both functional cores and edges across all families, although contraction intensity and the probability of weakly positive fitted values differed among families. In the pooled SEM, Seasonality was negatively associated with climatic niche breadth (β = −0.14), whereas Environmental affinity (β = 0.21) and Diapause timing (β = 0.13) were positively associated with niche position. Projected climate‐change responses were structured across combinations of functional traits rather than along single traits alone. By linking SDM‐derived range change to functional trait‐space occupancy and climatic niche geometry, this framework shifts vulnerability assessment from species counts toward functional strategy coverage and identifies trait–niche pathways that warrant targeted validation. articles.title: Good days, bad days: Weather patterns driving bryophyte carbon‐exchange dynamics in tropical rainforest canopies
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract The physiology of tropical mosses, liverworts and lichens may be challenged by the daily weather patterns in lowland rainforests. Since these poikilohydric organisms can only photosynthesize and respire when hydrated, unfavourable timing of light and water availability (i.e. desiccation during light hours and hydration during dark hours) may lead to small or negative diel (24‐h) carbon budget, especially in the tree crowns, where desiccation frequently occurs. Here, we tested this ‘unfavourable timing’ hypothesis that explains the low abundance of bryophytes and lichens in tropical lowland forests with a high frequency of weather patterns that limit carbon gain and increase carbon losses. By example of the forest surrounding the Yasuní Scientific Station (YSS) in the Ecuadorian Amazon, our approach consisted of three steps. We used the carbon‐exchange model for poikilohydric organisms PoiCarb (Version 1.1) to simulate diel carbon budgets at a 10‐min temporal resolution for 290 days based on canopy climate data from inside a tree crown and species‐specific physiological parameters. Our simulations explicitly included parameter uncertainty; hence, we were able to discriminate simulations based on their certainty. We implemented a classification tree analysis of the modelled diel carbon budgets for Neckeropsis undulata, the most abundant bryophyte species in the studied canopies. This analysis indicated that limiting light intensities, night‐time hydration and daytime desiccation caused net carbon losses on more than two‐thirds of the modelled days, while net carbon gains occurred only on bright days with rain. We validated these classification rules for an independent subset of days for the same species and for two companion species (Plagiochila raddiana and Symbiezidium transversale). Our validation indicates >70% accuracy in classifying diel carbon budgets. Our findings show that tropical lowlands are a physiologically marginal environment for bryophytes, mainly due to their frequent low‐light cloudy days and, secondarily, due to sunny days with no moisture availability, limiting carbon gain in the studied canopy bryophytes. Our threefold approach constitutes a tool for predicting bryophyte physiological performance under current and changing weather and climate patterns. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Resumen La fisiología de musgos, hepáticas y líquenes puede verse impugnada por los patrones climáticos diarios en los bosques tropicales de tierras bajas. Dado que estos organismos poiquilohídricos pueden fotosintetizar y respirar sólo mientras están hidratados, una sincronización no‐favorable de la disponibilidad de luz y agua (es decir, desecación durante horas de luz e hidratación durante horas de oscuridad) puede provocar balances diarios (24‐horas) de carbono pequeños o negativos, especialmente en las copas de los árboles donde la desecación ocurre con frecuencia. Evaluamos la hipótesis de la “sincronización no‐favorable”, según la cual la alta frecuencia de patrones climáticos que limitan la ganancia de carbono y aumentan las pérdidas de carbono explica la escasa abundancia de briófitos y líquenes en los bosques tropicales de tierras bajas. Tomando como ejemplo el dosel que rodea la Estación Científica Yasuní (YSS) en la Amazonía ecuatoriana, nuestro enfoque consistió en tres pasos. Utilizamos el modelo de intercambio de carbono para organismos poikilohidricos PoiCarb (Versión 1.1) para simular balances de carbono diarios con una resolución temporal de 10 minutos por 290 días, a partir de parámetros climáticos registrados en el dosel y de parámetros fisiológicos especie‐específicos. Nuestras simulaciones incluyeron explícitamente parámetros de incertidumbre, lo que nos permitió discriminar predicciones con base en su nivel de certidumbre.…

articles.title: How do insects pollinate flowers? Behaviour during visitation determines high pollination efficiency by a generalist insect
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Ecosystem services provide essential benefits to human survival and well‐being. Animal behaviour is central to the delivery of many ecosystem services, yet we know little about how behaviour drives services' provision. Pollination is often mediated by insect foraging; however, despite extensive research, our understanding of how pollinators' behaviour during a single flower visit determines plant reproductive success remains limited. Using single visit, pollination efficiency experiments with marmalade hoverflies (Episyrphus balteatus) and strawberries (Fragaria × ananassa), we tested the hypothesis that longer time spent performing behaviours relevant to pollen transfer leads to higher pollination efficiency. To this end we compared fruit weight (g) and the number of fertilised seeds of virgin flowers following a single uninterrupted visit by one fly with that of hand‐pollinated flowers, a measure of maximal pollination efficiency and two negative controls, that is flowers that were not cross‐pollinated. A linear mixed effect model in a Bayesian framework with treatment group as fixed effect and plant identity as random effect revealed that flowers visited by hoverflies produced fruits that were 70–85% heavier and with 64–82% more fertilised seeds than pollinator‐excluded controls, and with as many fertilised seeds as hand‐pollinated flowers. Among all behaviours that flies performed on flowers, pollination efficiency was predicted by the durations of nectar and pollen feeding and stigma‐oriented grooming. The durations of these behaviours were stronger predictors of fruit weight and seed count than total visit duration. We conclude that marmalade hoverflies deliver highly efficient pollination in just a single visit through behaviours that promote stigma contact and pollen transfer, challenging the assumption that these generalist insects contribute significantly to pollination only when abundant. Ultimately, our study reveals how pollinators' behaviour during flower visitation drives service provision and explains why visits are not functionally equivalent. Ultimately, our study shows that specific behaviours during flower visitation determine pollination efficiency and explain why individual visits are not functionally equivalent. Because these behaviours can be altered by anthropogenic stressors, a behavioural perspective will improve predictions of pollination service provision across species and ecological contexts. articles.title: Impact of harvest intensity on ectomycorrhizal and saprotrophic fungal communities in forest soils
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Low‐intensity tree harvesting has been proposed as a sustainable forest management practice to balance and preserve forest productivity, carbon storage and resilience to climate extremes. Soil fungi play a central role in driving tree performance and soil carbon storage, but we have limited knowledge of how soil fungal communities respond to tree harvest intensity. Particularly, ectomycorrhizal fungal biomass and soil fungal community composition have been measured rarely for different tree harvest intensities. Here, we studied the impacts of different tree harvest intensities on the biomass and composition of soil fungal communities, explicitly disentangling effects on ectomycorrhizal and saprotrophic fungi. In a large‐scale forest management experiment covering 15 monospecific stands in the Netherlands, we sampled mineral topsoil near trees and stumps in plots without tree harvest, with 20% or 80% tree basal area reduction, or clearcutting. We determined soil fungal biomass and community composition, as well as ectomycorrhizal fungal biomass in fungal in‐growth bags. Soil fungal biomass near tree stumps in clear‐cut and 80% harvest plots was reduced compared with near trees in the no‐harvest control but did not differ between 20% harvest and no‐harvest control plots. Similarly, soil fungal community composition near stumps in clear‐cut and 80% harvest plots was most different from the no‐harvest control, while shifts in community composition between the 20% and no‐harvest plots were limited. We found larger changes in biomass and community composition for ectomycorrhizal fungi in response to harvesting treatments than for total and saprotrophic fungi. We conclude that responses of the soil fungal community to low‐intensity tree harvesting were relatively small, whereas high‐intensity harvesting and particularly clearcutting impacted fungal communities. High‐intensity harvesting, especially reduced ectomycorrhizal fungal biomass and diversity. Our findings suggest that low‐intensity tree harvesting can potentially provide a good balance between timber production and the preservation of fungal‐mediated soil functions. In addition, distances between remaining trees after harvesting should likely be small (<10 m) to preserve ectomycorrhizal fungi.
